## 7. Agent integration (Harness)

The App Host must drive the Harness **Gateway** surface, not the SDK (see D03 in
`IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`, and `…/strata-work/RECON-HARNESS.md` for the file:line evidence).

Launch and connect:

```sh
dsh web --port 0 --no-open          # prints an authenticated URL
# then: GET /connect?token=<launchToken>&interactions=answer
#   `interactions=answer` is REQUIRED (it defaults to 'none'); without it the peer cannot answer
#   approvals and every ask fails closed as 'unavailable'.
```

| Assertion | What to prove |
| --- | --- |
| A1 (A01/A03) | Prompt → streamed answer, then a controlled read/edit/test tool round trip in a fixture workspace. The tool executes **once**, in Harness — not again in the Strata API. |
| A2 (A04) | Deny a tool: it must not execute, and the agent must receive an explicit denial it can handle. Also test an unavailable answerer and an expired approval. |
| A3 (A05) | `session/cancel` returns `{accepted:true}` immediately; the run is only actually stopped when `api-session/status(sessionId, running:false)` arrives or the durable `turn/end {kind:'aborted'}` is committed. **Wait for quiescence before reporting Stopped.** |
| A4 (A08) | Two sessions run independently; cancelling one must not disturb the other. |
| A5 (A06/A07) | A session started in Desktop resumes in Terminal with the same history, model and workspace, and **without replaying completed tool effects**. |
| A6 (A09) | Subagents are real child sessions, bounded by `maxDepth`/`maxActiveSubagents`, cancellable. |
| A7 (A10) | A bounded goal (`maxGoalRounds`) stops at its limit with `round-limit`; resume re-arms it explicitly. |

## 8. Time-skip

Time-skip is **implemented** (`strata_control/time_skip.py`, `strata timeskip`). The state machine,
the non-regression gate and the apply/restore safety are covered by 24 tests that pass on this Mac.
What those tests cannot show is whether a *real model* produces a candidate worth keeping, which is
what this section qualifies.

### 8.1 The command

```sh
# Declare checks for the workspace first: .strata/checks.json
cat > .strata/checks.json <<'JSON'
{"checks": [
  {"id": "tests",  "command": "python -m pytest -q", "timeout_s": 900},
  {"id": "lint",   "command": "ruff check .",       "timeout_s": 300},
  {"id": "readme", "file": "README.md", "sha256": "<expected hex>"}
]}
JSON

strata timeskip run --workspace "$PWD" --prompt "make the failing test pass" \
    --attempts 2 --revise-command "<python> <repo>/integrations/harness/revise_once.py --deadline 300"
strata timeskip status <run-id>
strata timeskip apply  <run-id> --dry-run
strata timeskip apply  <run-id>            # refuses if the workspace changed; exit 6
strata timeskip apply  <run-id> --restore
```

`--revise-command` is what makes the revision a real agent turn. **Exit 0 from it means an attempt
was made, not that it succeeded** — the checks decide that. Omit it and the run is inconclusive by
construction.

### 8.2 Observations to record

| ID | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| S01 | The baseline and candidate are real files on disk with recorded digests, and the retained checkpoint is identified by hash, not by the word "updated". |
| S02 | Run it against a workspace with a genuinely failing check: the candidate that fixes it is **kept**, and `decision.outcome` is `accepted`. |
| S03 | Break a previously passing check in the candidate: it is **rejected**, `decision.regressions` names it, and the workspace still holds the original. |
| S04 | Run with a check whose command does not exist: `outcome` is `unknown`, `decision.outcome` is `inconclusive`, and `needs_user_review` is true. It must **not** read as a pass. |
| S05 | Run twice with an unchanged workspace: the second run must not report an improvement. |
| S06 | `strata timeskip apply <id> --dry-run` writes nothing; the real apply keeps a rollback copy; a subsequent apply after you edit a file yourself exits **6** and leaves your edit alone. |
| S07 | Send SIGINT during the `generating` phase: the run ends `cancelled`, the baseline stays selected, and the workspace is unchanged. |
| S08 | Kill the Harness mid-attempt: the run ends `failed`, the baseline stays selected, and the reason is recorded. |
| S09 | Compare cost honestly: report the baseline's and the revision's token or time cost and the total wall-clock latency. **Do not infer a speed or quality gain from the name "Time-skip."** |

**Fixture results do not qualify a model.** Every S-row above must be run with the real local model
selected, and the run id, digests and raw `run.json` retained as evidence.

## 9. Engine tuning

The job contract is implemented (`strata_control/tuning.py`, `strata tune`), with 31 tests covering
the selection rule, failure recording, the exclusive lease and the exported-configuration retest.
**The measurement harness is not written**, so no sweep has run against a real model — on this Mac
there is no runnable workload, and inventing one would defeat the point. This section is what to do
on a machine that has one.

### 9.1 See what a sweep would search, and why not

Always start here. The plan is the review surface, and it is safe to run anywhere:

```sh
strata tune plan --engine /path/to/strata --backend metal \
    --model qwen3.8-flash-next --objective generation --trials 16 --repeats 3
```

It reads the engine's own `--help` to decide which dimensions are real. **Assertion T00:** every
dimension in `searches:` names a flag the binary accepts, and every entry in `excluded:` gives a
reason. A dimension silently missing is a defect. For reference, on the Metal engine built here the
answer is `ple_io`, `kv`, `kv_grow`, `spec_min_p` searched, and seven dimensions excluded with
reasons (`vram_reserve`, `pcie_frac`, `expert_cache` are not Apple Silicon concepts; `host_core`,
`pool_affinity`, `pool_workers` parse but their kernels are unported, per
`metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`; `prompt_cache_tail` is CUDA/HIP-only).

### 9.2 Wire the measurement harness

One callable, `measure(candidate) -> dict`, must boot the engine with `candidate.args`, run the
declared workload, and return at least `tokens_per_s`, optionally `ttft_ms`,
`prefill_tokens_per_s`, `decode_tokens_per_s`, `memory_mib`, `power_w`, and `correct`. Raising means
the candidate could not be measured; the message becomes its recorded status. `correct` must come
from a **task check**, not from a comparison against the baseline's text.

### 9.3 Observations to record

| ID | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| T01 | The tuner is optional: with it removed, serving and manual settings still work. |
| T02 | Every candidate's argv contains only flags the engine accepts; the sweep never mutates the active profile (`strata-<model>.json` is byte-identical before and after). |
| T03 | Trigger a boot failure, an OOM, a timeout and a cancellation. All four are retained in the report with their status; only the sweep's own devices are affected. |
| T04 | At least three paired repeats per candidate plus a baseline rerun. The report's `drift` section shows the baseline's two medians. Include the decode, a prompt-heavy and a multi-turn/tool workload. |
| T05 | Take a winner whose advantage came from `prompt_cache_tail`; confirm it is **not** in the exported args and that the exported configuration is re-measured before the recommendation stands. |
| T06 | Change the model file or the driver and confirm the previous history is not reused as if comparable. |
| T07 | Applying is separate: it revalidates the report and profile digests, snapshots, reloads, verifies, and rolls back on failure. Cancel before apply leaves the saved config unchanged. |
| T08 | Repeat the whole qualification per advertised backend. **Stub-engine or fixture results are labelled as such and never count as a backend qualification.** |

### 9.4 The HyperCore-Tune position, for whoever qualifies CUDA

HyperCore-Tune is not the optimizer; it was evaluated at pin `4f9ab7fa` and is documented in
`IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md` §1.12 as a *candidate* adapter behind the Strata job. If you qualify it on
CUDA, it supplies the search and the per-candidate boot; the Strata job still owns the lease, the
evidence, the dimension validation and the exported retest. Two things to check first: its
`strata_env.py` locates Strata by walking up from its own directory (pass `--strata-root` instead),
and it writes `max_run_<model>.{json,sh,bat}` next to that root — make sure that is not your active
profile.

## 10. Reading a result: would this pass if the feature did nothing?

This section exists because of a specific class of mistake made repeatedly during Phase A, and it is
written as an instruction rather than an anecdote because a Phase B run will meet it again.

**Three separate checks in this build passed for reasons unrelated to the feature they named.** Each
printed plausible output and asserted something that was *also* true when the feature was absent:

* the tuning sweep reported "trials 4 of 4" out of 96 combinations, so "no candidate beat the
  baseline" read as a conclusion when it was an artefact of stopping early;
* the cancellation check passed while the scripted turn finished in milliseconds, so Stop arrived
  after the turn had already ended;
* the approval-denial check passed while the tool failed for an unrelated reason — a malformed
  scripted call — and the launch-URL parameter it relied on turned out to be decorative.

All three were green. None of them exercised what they claimed to.

**So, for every check in this kit, answer one question before recording a pass:**

> Would this assertion also hold if the feature did nothing at all?

If the answer is yes, the check is not evidence. The usual causes, in the order they were met here:

1. **An assertion about an absence.** "The tool did not run", "no file was created", "no candidate
   won" are all satisfied by a run that never got that far. Pair every absence with a positive
   control: the same setup where the feature *does* act, asserting that it acted (A03 beside A04).
2. **A window that is too short to be tested.** A cancellation test against a turn that finishes in
   milliseconds proves nothing. Make the window real — a token delay, a held lock — and *assert that
   the window was open* before acting, not merely that the action succeeded.
3. **A parameter that is inert.** Read where a flag is actually parsed before relying on it. The
   launch-URL `interactions` parameter was read only on `/connect`, so on `GET /?token=` it did
   nothing; the check passed for a reason that had nothing to do with the code under test.
4. **A count that does not say what it counted.** "4 of 4" without the size of the space is not a
   completion claim. Report the denominator and whether the sample was the whole space or a prefix.

**And for the harness around a check, not just the check:** three of the defects found in Phase A were
in the *test* rather than the product — a stale worker answering on the port a profile hardcoded, a
client that followed a redirect and discarded the credential carried on it, and a client that posted
a request without the envelope the gateway requires. Each produced a run that looked normal. When a
result is surprising, suspect the harness first: it is the part that has not been exercised before.

## AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md

Strata runs the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next mixture-of-experts model (and its Coder, Swift 1.5, Unsloth, Gyro and NVFP4
variants, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) on a normal PC: one NVIDIA or AMD graphics card plus system RAM on Windows or Linux,
or an Apple Silicon Mac. Version 0.2.3, engine 0.1.48. It has three parts:

- **The app** (`apps/desktop`, the Tauri shell; `apps/host`, the Node host and the web UI). It is for people who do
  not want a terminal. The installer has the engine inside.
- **The Terminal** (`strata.py`, `strata_cli/`, `strata_control/`): the `strata` command. It sets up a model, serves
  it and watches it. Agents use this part.
- **The engine and the server** (`src/`, `include/`, `metal/`, `sycl/` for the C++/CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal engine;
  `serve/` for the Python server with an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API and a web page). `setup.py`, started by
  `START-HERE.bat` or `setup.sh`, is the older one-click installer from source.

## Installing Strata for a user

Follow **[docs/AI_SETUP.md](docs/AI_SETUP.md)**. For an agent that has a shell, the short version is:

1. Install the Terminal. It needs no administrator rights.

   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh                  # Linux, Mac
   irm https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex                         # Windows PowerShell
   ```

   On Windows, open a new terminal afterwards so that `strata` is on the PATH.
2. Check what would happen. Nothing is changed:

   ```sh
   strata launch --plan --model q2_0
   ```

3. Set up and serve without questions. It downloads the engine for the card and the model (tens of GB), starts the
   server, prints the addresses and returns. The server keeps running.

   ```sh
   strata launch --model q2_0 --yes --no-tui
   ```

   Useful flags (all of them: `strata launch --help`): `--family`, `--model-path` (files the user already has),
   `--data-dir`, `--context 32k|64k|128k`, `--vision off|on|gpu|cpu`, `--parallel N`, `--gpu 0,1`,
   `--access local|lan|cloudflare|tailscale`, `--port`, `--api-key-env NAME`, `--new-key`, `--save-preset NAME`,
   `--output json`. `strata launch --status` shows what is serving, `strata launch --stop` stops it, and
   `strata launch --show-key` prints the API key.
4. Connect the user's apps: `strata connect` lists them, `strata connect <app> --check` sends one prompt and one tool
   call the way that app does.

Keep the server on `127.0.0.1` unless the user asks for more. Beyond it an API key is recommended: `--access lan` makes one for you, and `--no-api-key` serves without one (a warning, never a refusal; on a public tunnel the warning is stronger). The old route (clone
the repository and run `START-HERE.bat --yes` or `./setup.sh --yes`) still works and is the fallback when the
Terminal cannot run. Strata's MCP server ([docs/MCP_SERVER.md](docs/MCP_SERVER.md)) offers the same steps as tools.

## Working on the code

- How the engine works, every measured number, the API and all settings: [docs/DETAILS.md](docs/DETAILS.md) and
  the [paper](docs/paper/Strata-Paper.pdf).
- The Terminal: [docs/TERMINAL.md](docs/TERMINAL.md) and [docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md](docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md). The app,
  the packages and the update feed: [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md) and [packaging/UPDATES.md](packaging/UPDATES.md).
- AMD (HIP) build and validation: [docs/AMD_HIP.md](docs/AMD_HIP.md); multi-GPU: [docs/MULTI_GPU.md](docs/MULTI_GPU.md);
  Mac (Metal): [docs/MAC.md](docs/MAC.md).
- Tests: the Terminal and Control tests are in `tests/terminal` (`python -m pytest tests/terminal`). The app's UI
  tests run with `npm test` in `apps/host`. Setup's own tests run without a GPU or downloads:
  `python tools/test_setup_<name>.py` (for example `tools/test_setup_amd.py`, `tools/test_setup_choices.py`).
- Keep the docs' style: plain words, short sentences, written for non-technical users first. Give measured numbers
  with what they were measured on. Make no claim without a measurement.

## Contributing a change or report

The rules are in **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)**. Read it before you open an issue or a pull request, and
follow it whether a person or an agent writes the text. The short version:

- Start every issue and pull request title with its area: `[Engine]`, `[GUI]`, `[TUI]`, `[Benchmark]`, `[Docs]` or
  `[Other]`, for example `[Engine] fix …`. A check on GitHub fails a pull request whose title has no area.
- Search the open and closed issues and pull requests first, and add to a thread that already covers your point.
- Agree the scope in an issue before a large feature, a refactor or a change to a default.
- One problem per pull request. Lead with the problem and the result, then the approach, then the validation
  (passed, failed and not run, kept apart) and the limits.
- A new feature is opt-in, and the default path stays byte-identical to the last release. Say how you checked.
- Build every backend a file touches (CUDA, HIP, SYCL) before asking for review.
- Change a default only where you measured it faster, and show the numbers with what they were measured on.
- Never submit measurements, logs or reproduction steps you did not produce. Mark a finding from reading code as
  unconfirmed static analysis.
- A report from hardware the maintainers do not have is welcome. Follow
  [docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md](docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md), compare against a same-day run of the build you are
  testing, and say what you did not test.
- Open test requests and the hardware that is wanted are listed in [docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md](docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md).


## CODER-9060XT-OPTIMIZATION.md

# Coder on the RX 9060 XT 16 GB (9700X, 32 GB RAM) — optimization playbook

Written from the tuning work done on the RTX 3060 laptop Swift config in October 2026, plus Strata's own
measured notes (docs/AMD_HIP.md, AMD_HIP_PERFORMANCE.md, bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt).
Target: the Coder engine built for ROCm 10.2 ("hipBLASLt 100500"), gfx1200.

Current baseline on that machine: prefill ~1200–1400 tok/s, decode ~70–40 tok/s with the Coder.

## Applied to `~/Documents/Strata-v02x` (Oct 21 2026)

The whole tuned set above was ported from `~/Documents/Strata-v021` after a fresh engine build (0.2.1.x):
`gfx1200-hipblaslt-100401.txt` into `tools/hip/` (67 rows), a new `strata-coder-iq1_m.json` with the Oct 18
env slate (100401 table · RESIDENT_PIN=1 · HIP_WMMA=1 · PF_FUSED=1 · PF_GEMM=1 · PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=4096 ·
PREFILL_MMQ=1 · ADAPT_OVERLAP(+_RESIDENT)=1 · EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1) and the setup-generated coder args
(expert-cache auto, prefill auto, spec 4 / min-p 0.5, MTP, 180000 ctx, kv int8, resident-experts — no vision
section, #1322), the Swift config's two lost keys restored (`STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING`,
`STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1`; kept arms 1+2+4 and the arm-7b `--adapt-swaps 0 --resident-experts` form were
already in it), `start-strata.sh` / `stop-strata.sh` / `run-coder-iq1_m.sh` / `strat_coder.sh` /
`strat_swift.sh` re-generated for this tree (same-tree cwd guard), and the
`STRATA_BENCH_KEY` Authorization patch applied to `tools/agent_turns_bench.py`. Rejected arms (spec 6,
HEADROOM_GIB=6, adapt-async, DENSE_MMQ, SH_STREAM, 100500 table, 10.1 native stack, MTP side stream,
GFX12_CHUNK=1, pool-workers) deliberately NOT applied. Memlock limits entry is system-level, still in place.

Verification chain on the first start passed every check: exe = this tree's engine, maps = system
`libhipblaslt.so.1.4` (matches the 100401 table), env table line correct, banner `tuning enabled
(67 rows, gfx1200, version 100401)` (tail the file, not the first match — the log appends across restarts),
pin `resident 18.56 GiB, pinned 18.56 GiB`, `FileExpertSource: 1425 of 1425`, rotation 96 buffers,
keyed API answer and MTP drafting live.

## Coder ring / side-stream sweep (Oct 21, v02x tree, strata_bench medians, fresh restart per arm)

From upstream #3480 ("gfx1200 prompt speed", same card): tested `STRATA_PREFILL_RING=384` and
`STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=1` on the Coder. Four arms, one restart each (NOT interleaved — start-to-start
roulette is visible in the table; treat the pooled picture as the verdict):

| arm (fresh start) | 4K prompt | 16K prompt | chat decode (n=9) | agent decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ring 96 (default), start 1 | 1,514.9 (1171–1517) | 1,678.6 (1645–1694) | 47.0 (35.7–62.3) | 49.3 |
| ring 384, start 1 | 1,604.8 (1576–1605) | 1,721.0 (1688–1724) | 45.9 | 49.8 |
| ring 384 + side stream | 1,609.0 | 1,682.6 | 48.6 | 45.5 |
| ring 384, start 2 (confirm) | 1,446.0 (1361–1541) | 1,638.1 | 43.6 | 47.4 |
| ring 96 (default), start 2 | **1,641.7 (1466–1647)** | **1,738.6 (1735–1741)** | 45.8 | 44.4 |

- **`STRATA_PREFILL_RING=384`: NO reproducible gain on the Coder.** 4K pooled medians tie
  (ring-384's two starts straddle the default's), and 16K pooled slightly favors the default. The +22%
  in #3480 came from a different config shape (IQ2_XS fused pack, their own queue-capping and batching)
  — not this desk's. **Rejected; the Coder keeps engine default (96).**
- **`STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=1`: tie on prompt, decoder-leaning on agent medians. The playbook's
  default-off now has a same-card measurement, not just the R9700 one. Might differ under batching or
  capped `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES`, which we do not use.**
- Today's best Coder readings came from the untouched default config (4K 1,641.7 / 16K 1,738.6 /
  chat 45.8–47.0 / agent 44.4–49.3) — the Oct 18 slate stays the tuned optimum for this box.
- Ring 384 is not refused for other packs: Swift (q4_0 KV, x4_0 chunk) pays the 96-slot ring for a WMMA
  path that never runs there, so the Swift arm is still worth its own sweep — different shape from the
  Coder's result (recorded before the Swift arms run, so the Coder's null doesn't prejudice them).



## Priority order (biggest expected gains first)

1. **hipBLASLt tuning table — CONFIRMED PRESENT on the machine (Oct 2026).**
   Upstream only ships `gfx1200-hipblaslt-100202.txt`; the machine's repo (`~/Documents/Strata`, commit
   `bc25718` "local working") carries locally generated `gfx1200-hipblaslt-100401.txt` and
   `gfx1200-hipblaslt-100500.txt`. **HTTP A/B correction (Oct 19–20): the live config runs the 100401
   table with the system hipBLASLt 1.4.1 (banner: `tuning enabled (67 rows, gfx1200, version 100401)`);
   an earlier note here saying the config wires 100500 was stale.** Measured A/B (same engine v0.1.45,
   same day, strata_bench medians, 4K/16K/decode):

   | pair | 4K prompt | 16K prompt | chat decode | agent decode |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 100401 (system lib 1.4.1, `/opt/rocm/core`) | **1,651** (1,373–1,652) | **1,734** | 47.0 | **50.7** |
   | 100500 (bundle 1.5 lib, llama dir LD swap) | 1,468 | 1,711 | 49.0 | 49.0 |

   **Keep 100401**; 100500 measured −11% at 4K, flat at 16K, within noise on decode. The 100500 pair
   validated at load (mixed stack: ROCm 10.0 runtime + hipBLASLt 1.5 transplant works, worth revisiting
   ONLY as part of a full ROCm 10.2 move). Note: "100500" is a hipBLASLt version tag (1.5.0 per the
   table-name scheme "1.2.0 is 100200"), NOT a ROCm version; ROCm 10.2 wheels are not published for
   gfx120X (the family's nightly index caps at 7.14.0a20260612) — a native ROCm 10.2 + 1.5 pairing needs
   the system ROCm upgraded (sudo), or the desk stays on 10.0. Guard rails:
   - after any ROCm/hipBLASLt update, re-check the installed version against the table name — a version
     mismatch means the engine silently falls back to plain hipBLAS: measured **~45% slower** for a 131K
     prompt;
   - if regenerating ever becomes necessary, build and run the tuner (`tools/hip/tune_hipblaslt.cpp`) on
     the card (it measures kernels in place; takes a while).

2. **`STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 STRATA_PF_GEMM=1 STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=4096`** — measured +18%
   (925 → 1,092 tok/s) on an RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100); nothing ICMP-specific in it, valid to try on gfx1200.

3. **`--prefill auto:32768`** — +23% at 74K prompts on the same 7900 XTX report. Chunk above 32768 was
   measured flat. The community 9060 XT run kept `--prefill 8192` (their context was 122880 with INT8 KV).
   With the Coder's ~23.4 GB arena in 32 GB RAM and a 180K context, hold to the chunk the free VRAM allows;
   confirm with "the prompt path allocates its own buffers" / borrow lines in the log.

4. **`STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=1`** — opt-in HIP MMQ for the prompt's dense GGUF projections: +12–18%
   on RDNA2 (6900 XT, 0.1.40.1) for 4K prompts; RDNA4 untested (it is newer, expect similar or better).
   Measure A/B; answers stay within measured MMQ error bounds.

5. **`--resident-experts` (prompt path borrows the expert-cache slots).** On the 7900 XTX this took
   prompts 1,092 → 2,503 tok/s. Two checks after the first request of each start:
   - reply keeps authors: log line `FileExpertSource: N of M of the prompt path's lendable slots keep their
     experts in RAM too` — N must equal M; if short, lower `STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB` (default 4.0; on
     a 32 GB box try 3.0–3.5) and restart; check the line again after every ROCm update (the runtime's own
     host-RAM share shifts the optimum);
   - with 32 GB RAM + 23.4 GB arena there is little slack — watch the `memory guard` line.

6. **`--vram-reserve-mib 2048`** — the community 9060 XT 16 GB value (used with INT8 KV at 122,880 ctx).
   Raise it only if the engine's start-of-request paging WARNING ("below 512 MiB free") appears; that
   warning means Windows/drivers could page the card under load and drop decode.

7. **`--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`** at large contexts — the measured community combo; INT8 KV halves
   the cache versus fp32 and 32768 resident cells keep attention local. At 180K context this is what makes
   the window affordable at all (the Qwen3.6 path, by contrast, has NO kv quant/stream — see the
   earlier conversation for that comparison).

8. **`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`** — flat above 4, measured. Decode comes from the MTP drafter; keep it on.

9. **Small knobs, test only if the big ones land:**
   - `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` (Linux, RDNA2 numbers went either way: RX 6800 Windows slower, R9- fork faster);
     answer-identical, purely scheduling — quick A/B on this RDNA4 card adds a data point.
   - `STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM`: do NOT force `=1` — on gfx120x the engine's default (off) is right; the
     R9700 lost prompt speed with it created. Only gfx103x creates it by default.
   - `--pool-workers 15` on the 16-thread 9700X matches the Flash-Next pattern (workers + host thread ≤
     logical CPUs; keep 1 for the host callback).
   - GDN parallel/split path: `STRATA_GDN_PARALLEL=1` is unmerged upstream (#108) — skip.

## Measured on the machine (Oct 18 2026, v0.1.45 engine, system ROCm / hipBLASLt 1.4.1, RX 9060 XT 16 GB)

Bench: tools/hip/bench_prefill.py (140/280-line code prompts, 128-token gens, temp 0, fresh prompts).

| Arm | 8.8K fresh prefill | 4.2K fresh prefill | Decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1.45 stock | 1450 / 1441 | 1508 | 49.7–52.2 |
| + PF_FUSED/GEMM/SWITCH_MIN_T 4096 | **1485 / 1503** | **1592** | 48.3–53.5 |
| + STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=1 | identical (within noise) — keeper, no cost | | |
| + STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=6 | rejected: same speed but lend coverage broke (1152/1426 slots, ~26% long-prompt penalty warned) | | |

Old engine (re-rooted tree, hipBLASLt 1.5.0 wheels): remembered ~1200–1400 prefill — v0.1.45 + fused is faster on the
same-day bench. MTP kept (spec 4, min-p 0.5, ~65% acceptance on the bench).

Notes the engine itself printed:
- prompt chunk stays at 8192: 16384 would not fit the 30 GB RAM budget with 20.3 GiB resident experts (#2090) — do not force STRATA_GFX12_CHUNK=1 on this box
- KV streaming off (KV stays fully in VRAM at 180K INT8; ~560 MiB VRAM free) — do not add --kv-resident here without re-measuring
- prompt path borrows VRAM cache slots for intent routing; "FileExpertSource: N of N" must hold or long prompts re-read the pack

## Candidate queue from the docs sweep (Oct 18 2026) — ordered, with what the docs measured

Decode levers (no pin needed):
1. `--adapt-async 1` (engine arg, resident-RAM mode; BATCHING.md/DETAILS.md: x1.07-1.11 decode solo, 12/12 prompts,
   RTX 3090 + 5600X community report) — the adaptive tier's copies advance between windows on a helper thread.
   Falls back to blocking when buffers are not page-locked (watch the log to say which tier it took).
2. `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` (+ `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP_RESIDENT=1` in the resident RAM mode, 0.1.43): the adaptive
   tier's copies land while the next decode window runs (generate.cpp #1389). Try if (1) logs a blocking tier.
3. `--draft-vocab en` (engine arg; DETAILS.md): English/code draft subset, ~110 MiB less VRAM head, English
   answers 1-2% faster, frees VRAM for a few more expert cache slots. Harmless for a code box; loses CJK draft speed.

Prefill levers (no pin needed):
4. `STRATA_DENSE_MMQ=1` (HIP opt-in, AMD_HIP.md #820): dense GGUF projections through int8 MMQ instead of
   dequantize+hipBLAS — RX 6900 XT measured 4K prompt 436 -> 757 tok/s. May be redundant here because the hipBLASLt
   tuned GEMM path already handles dense (test before keeping).
5. `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` (opt-in): 16-bit prompt GEMMs FP16 in/out (gfx103x tip at bench/results/2026-10-04-rdna2-fp16-prompt);
   answers not bit-identical to BF16 path — A/B quality before keeping.
6. `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` (Linux): answer-identical scheduling; RDNA2 went both ways (6800 Windows slower, fork
   forks faster) — quick A/B, adds an RDNA4 data point.
7. `STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=1`: measured +35-45% prompt on RX 6800 Windows (#1240) but the R9700 LOST prompt speed
   with it — RDNA4 default is off; low priority, test isolation only.

The pin endgame (needs one-time sudo on the box: memlock soft+hard are 8 MiB, so STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1 silently
stays pageable — the OLD engine did too, "pinned 0.00 GiB" in its logs):
- raise memlock (e.g. `/etc/security/limits.d/strata.conf: kareem soft memlock unlimited / hard memlock unlimited`
  + re-login, or a systemd user unit with LimitMEMLOCK=infinity), then set `STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1` and re-check
  `pinned 18.x GiB` in the log;
- then `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1` (removes the last host copy of every adaptive swap; requires fully pinned,
  GPU-mapped complement — docs/EXCHANGE_ROTATION.md) and re-test `--adapt-async 1` on the pinned tier.

Not applicable on this box: KV streaming / STRATA_KV_PREFETCH (KV fully in VRAM), 16K prompt chunks (RAM math in
#2090 forbids it), PREFILL CPU_SHARE on AMD (measured slower on one AMD box, and HIP keeps it opt-in).

## Sweep results (Oct 18 2026, after the migration — measured, one arm at a time)

| Arm | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `--adapt-async 1` | decode flat (47.3–53.1) — the x1.07-1.11 report was arena-mode on an RTX 3090/5600X | **removed** |
| `--draft-vocab en` | no-op: this pack's shipped `draft_vocab.bin` IS the 40,525-id English/code subset (head 81.2 MiB); setup now records `"draft_vocab": "en"` | keep (cosmetic) |
| `STRATA_DENSE_MMQ=1` | flat (1500/1504/1599) — the model's dense runs in native IQ kernels, not dequantize+hipBLAS | **removed** |
| `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` | clearly worse on RDNA4 Linux: decode 41.0–43.8, prefill 1378–1470 | **removed** (engine default right) |
| `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` + `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP_RESIDENT=1` | decode 48.9–54.5 (best single reading), prefill 1505/1508 | **kept** |

### Desk forensics + update pull (Oct 19–20)

- **The server takeover trap, found live:** the desk's 8080 server since Oct 19, 16:12 was the **old
  `~/Documents/Strata` tree's engine** (v0.1.39-era exe + old config + its own .venv ROCm wheels), not
  the tuned v0.1.45 tree. The v0145 `stop-strata.sh` only matches processes whose cmdline contains
  `Strata-v0145*`, so cross-tree stop silently no-ops and same-port dup-guards make the start echo
  "already running". Any tree-hopping on the desk must kill BOTH trees' `serve/server.py` +
  `engine/strata` explicitly (pgrep with bracket-escaped patterns) and verify with `readlink
  /proc/<pid>/exe` before trusting numbers. Corrected same-day v0145 baselines: 4K 1,651 / 16K 1,734 /
  chat 47.0 / agent decode 50.7.
- **Verification chain that worked each restart:** `exe` path → `libhipblaslt` kind of
  `/proc/PID/maps` → `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING` from `/proc/PID/environ` → `grep` the LAST "tuning
  enabled" line in the log (`grep -m2 ... | tail` returns the FIRST two matches of the file — stale
  entries; tail the file instead).
- **Update state:** upstream at **v0.2.1** (engine 0.1.46; releases 0.2.0-beta + 0.2.1 carry the gfx12
  prompt WMMA/fused defaults with identity gates, RX 9000 two-queue start priming, worker-plan change,
  drive probe, config `user_args` protection). `~/Documents/Strata` git fetched; **worktree**
  `~/Documents/Strata-v021` created from tag `v0.2.1`; setup running against the system ROCm 10.0.0
  with the recorded coder recipe (`--family coder --context 180000 --kv int8 --no-start --no-browser
  --yes`), so files come from the existing `~/Documents/Strata-data`. v015 stays installed and serving;
  switch only after 0.2.1 measures equal-better. The 7.14-wheel runtime arm and the cache purge (pip
  cache 3.0 GB reclaimed, disk 36 GB free) recorded en route.

### v0.2.1 bring-up onto the desk (Oct 20)

- **Incident: the compile OOM-killed the v0145 engine** (nothing was serving mid-build). The engine
  page-locks ~18 GiB and is the biggest RSS on the 30 GB box; ninja's parallel HIP compiles took RAM
  over and the OOM killer took the engine. **Lesson: stop the server before compiling a new engine.**
- Compile itself was clean against the system ROCm 10.0.0 (`/opt/rocm`), engine 0.1.46 in
  `~/Documents/Strata-v021/engine/strata`. Setup recipe reused v0.1.45's: `./setup.sh --family coder
  --context 180000 --kv int8 --no-start --no-browser --yes` over the shared `~/Documents/Strata-data`
  (no model re-downloads; setup validates existing files).
- **Bring-up deltas 0.1.45 → 0.2.1** (each cost a re-restart to reach parity):
  - no gfx1200 hipBLASLt table ships (`[!] no tuning table for gfx1200 … have: 100202`) → copied the
    locally generated `gfx1200-hipblaslt-100401.txt` from v0145 into v021's `tools/hip/`.
  - `STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN` default flipped to `0` → set `1` (the Oct 18 memlock raise makes pin safe).
  - `host` is gone from the generated config and **a non-loopback bind now refuses to start without
    an API key** (0.2.x security design, server.py preflight; 0.1.45 served 0.0.0.0 keyless). Set
    `api_key: "strata"`: **LAN clients must now send `Bearer strata` to reach the desk on 0.2.1.**
  - `--vision` appended by default with a `"vision"` config section; the server **re-adds `--vision`**
    if the section exists without it (#1322), so dropping the args entry is not enough — for A/B
    parity (v0145 ran images off) the whole `"vision"` section must be deleted (it also spawns a
    second process, `engine/strata-vision`). Vision stays available in 0.2.1 (CPU reader) when wanted.
  - `draft_vocab: "en"` in the v0145 config was **dead config**: the 0.1.45 engine rejected
    `--draft-vocab` on its very first start (Oct 18 log, `unknown argument: --draft-vocab`), so the
    desk always ran the CJK MTP draft subset. Not ported; v0.2.1's identical default needs nothing.
  - `expert-profile-coder.bin` md5-identical between trees (both shipped, no learned drift yet).
- **Bench tool gotchas on a keyed server** (first v021 arm had 18/18 failed requests, all metrics 0 —
  discarded): `strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` needs `--api-key strata` because `--url`
  skips config loading (it reads `api_key` from the config otherwise); `tools/agent_turns_bench.py`
  sends **no Authorization header at all** (breaks against any keyed server — upstream report
  candidate), patched locally to take `Authorization: Bearer $STRATA_BENCH_KEY`.
- Verified serving state before the A/B: single engine process (`readlink /proc/PID/exe` =
  `v021/engine/strata`), system hipBLASLt 1.4 mapped, env table = v021's 100401 copy, banner
  `tuning enabled (67 rows, gfx1200, version 100401)`, 476 MiB VRAM free (v0145 ~560 — slightly more
  in use on 0.1.46, same order).
- **Same-day A/B verdict (strata_bench medians, n=3 runs, 9700X + RX 9060 XT): v0.2.1 is dead even
  with the tuned v0.1.45 on this card.**

  | metric | v0.1.45 (arm A') | v0.2.1 (arm C') |
  |---|---|---|
  | 4K prompt tok/s | 1,651 (1,373–1,652) | 1,647.8 (1,340–1,648) |
  | 16K prompt tok/s | 1,734 | 1,679.7 (1,668–1,745) |
  | chat decode tok/s | 47.0 | 47.9 (41.0–64.4) |
  | agent decode tok/s | 50.7 | 47.2 (40.1–55.1) |

  Ranges overlap throughout; nothing regressed beyond noise. The 0.2.1 prizes that motivated the move
  (queue priming at fresh start, worker-plan fix, drive probe, download speed) are structural, the

### Swift decode/prefill optimization arms (Oct 20 night, same-session probes)

Setup pre-warned the structural cost: 40 GB experts, page cache ~26 GiB, "79 GB read from the drive
per 32K prompt" at chunk 16384. User-reported symptom: erratic slow sessions. Baseline bench (killed
early at the user's request): decode legs wildly bouncy — 2.5 / 15.3 / 24.5 / 27.1 / 30.7 / 38.5 /
41.2 / 53.3 tok/s, first-token 0.6–5.6 s.

- **Mechanism found twice**: (1) engine warning — "only 474 MiB VRAM free … driver can page GPU
  memory to system RAM, decode falls to a few tok/s" (#2065); (2) slow-request autopsies —
  "OS read 22.9 GB from storage (15.8k major faults) for 37.9 GB of expert reads": a 4K prefill sweep
  evicts the decode hot pages, the next small-prompt decode re-reads cold. Ping-pong between the
  prefill set and the decode set inside a 26 GiB cache is the box's structural cost.
- **Arms (same-session probe = 2× 3,255-tok prefill + 100-tok decodes, fresh restart each arm):**

  | Arm | change | cold 4K | warm 4K | decode runs |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 (partial bench) | untouched swift config + laptop env | — | — | 2.5–53.3, huge cliffs |
  | 1 | + coder PF slate (PREFILL_MMQ/PF_FUSED/PF_GEMM/PF_SWITCH_MIN_T/EXCHANGE_ROTATE/ADAPT_OVERLAP_RESIDENT=1) + profile-save | 285 | 5,538 | 22–34 |
  | 2 | + STRATA_GFX12_CHUNK=0 (8192) | 310 | 6,694 | 24/50/45 |
  | 3 | + --pool-workers 16 | 318 | 5,467 | 16/30/34 — **rejected** (8-core default better; log said "7 workers by default" = default honors every physical core) |
  | 4 | −pool-workers, + --vram-reserve-mib 768 (engine's own prescription) | 300 | **8,294** | 25/38/37, then second probe 24/**5.8**/10.2 — cliff persists (that leg: 22.9 GB cold) |
  | 5 | chunk 4096 | 228 | 2,471 | — **rejected**: more passes than savings; plan line: chunk 8192 = "136 GB read per 32K (4 chunks); fewest passes win" — chunk 16384 = 79 GB but worse short-prompt resonance |
  | 6 | + STRATA_COLD_OVERLAP=1 | 314 | 5,384 | first probe fine, second probe **3.1/6.4/9.4** — **rejected** (streaming mode defeats the cache reuse warm-up) |
  | final | **arms 1+2+4 kept**, chunk reverted to "0" | 261 | 4,772–8,294 | warms 9→29→46 within 2–3 requests |

- **Kept (all measured, none Reggie):** coder PF slate on Swift, chunk 8192, `--vram-reserve-mib 768`,
  `--expert-profile-save expert-profile-learned-swift.bin --expert-profile-save-every 10` (zero-cost,
  the adaptive tier compounds placement with real use).
- **Re-equilibriing rule for users:** the first 1–2 requests after a domain flip (big prompt ↔ new
  conversation) run cold on this RAM size; within a conversation decode is warm-stable. Fundamental
  to 40 GB experts / 26 GiB cache; more RAM or smaller expert set are the only real fixes.
- Not tuned (engine auto-picks and its plan is measured sane): STRATA_IO_PF_GATE=1, HC_Q8 (already
  Q8_0), route-tail skip (108k entries skipping), STRATA_SSD_KEEPALIVE. The "drive 1.50 GB/s
  (assumed)" plan input matches the boot PLE probe (~91k rows/s), not an error.

### "Use both RAM and NVMe" — the pinned-tier arms (Oct 20 night, direct answer)

User question: can't we keep a RAM copy AND stream from the NVMe? That mode exists —
`--resident-experts` (= `--mmap-experts --resident-cpu-experts`, adaptive page-locked RAM copy +
file streaming, the docs' low-RAM-PC resident mode). Setup chose plain streaming for this box; both
pin sizes were then measured here:

| Arm | state | cold 4K prefill | warm 4K | decode | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | `--resident-experts` (23.05 GiB page-locked, 4 GiB headroom) | **79 tok/s (41.5 s)** | 689 | 503 under load | pinned tier starves prefill; setup was right; user's later trial: warm 4K decays to ~7 tok/s all-in (90.3 s/pass) from exchange churn, decode itself healthy (41.7 tok/s by engine monitor) |
| 8 | + `STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=9` (17.86 GiB pinned, ~9 GiB cache) | **24 tok/s (135 s!)** | 5,676–6,284 | ~20 flat | adaptive-swap thrash: 4,293 blob file re-reads/request, 2.8–3k exchanges/request; **in user's hands: crash loop — 19 engine restarts; engine pinned 17.5 GiB with "8.85 GiB really free" (its own line) → dies under way; reborn in streaming mode** |
| 7b | `--adapt-swaps 0` + `--expert-profile` → `expert-profile-learned-swift.bin` (22.61 GiB pin after the solver clamps to avail−4) | **292 tok/s** (user's own 4K request, while a second probe co-loaded) | 425 | 41.7→42.1 (ctx 88), 34.6 (ctx 4,007, user) | adaptive tier OFF: monitor shows `0 exchanged with the VRAM tier`, 90–92% decode expert hits; cold-4K prefill = streaming's disk-bound band (same SSD); profile save disabled while tier off; survived user traffic + probes without a single restart | 
| final | plain `--mmap-experts` (the winner, arms 1+2+4) | ~261–300 | 5,400–8,294 | warms 22→46 | OS page-cache LRU beats the engine's adaptive tier at this workload |

**Why the OS cache wins:** the desk's traffic mix (big prefill sweeps ↔ decode doors) doesn't match
the pin tier's decay model; the LRU adapts for free, and every pinned byte shrinks a cache that
was already the bottleneck. More RAM (or a smaller expert set) remains the only real fix for the
ping-pong. Memlock infrastructure on the desk is proven working either way (23 GiB page-locked
without complaint, from the Oct 18 pin endgame).

**Arm 7b — the pin's working form (Oct 20 late).** Arm 7's instability was never the pin; it was the
adaptive exchange tier: 96-expert memcpy churn per adaptive round that turned a warm 4K prefill into
90 s and left the engine dancing on the cold prefill too. Two changes fix it: `--adapt-swaps 0`
(misses fall straight through to file reads — monitor counts exactly 0 exchanges), and loading the
learned expert profile so the 22.61 GiB pin and the 6,063 GPU slots are placed by tonight's traffic
instead of the ship default. Result: cold-4K prefill lands in the streaming form's disk-bound band
(292 tok/s), warm 4K 425 tok/s (90–92% expert hits), decode unchanged from the pin's own best
(34.6–42.1 tok/s). The solver clamps the pin to available−4 GiB whatever the model asks (30.15 GiB
wanted → 22.61 given), so the pin size breathes with the desktop's free RAM — a fresh boot with
RAM free pins more, a busy boot pins less, both run. Costs: profile learning is frozen while the
tier is off (`--expert-profile-save` needs it), and 22.6 GiB stays committed to the pin. Streaming
still beats it on warm prefill (8,294 vs 425) and keeps all RAM free; 7b is the form to run when
the user wants the pin held.

### ROCm 10.1.0 native-stack arm (Oct 20 evening)

- **What "genuine 10.2+1.5" turned out to be:** no ROCm 10.2 exists in any public Linux channel (the
  v2 nightly families/deb/staging all freeze at `7.14.0a20260612`; `whl-multi-arch` tops at
  `10.1.0a20260822`; repo.radeon.com apt last touched May 2026; PyPI has stub packages; the GitHub
  TheRock releases attach no binaries — the released 10-line is **10.1.0**, Oct 5). The closest
  genuine version-matched native stack obtainable without sudo is therefore the
  **10.1.0 line**, built from the 2026-08-22 snapshot (`10.1.0~20260822-32539019050`), which is the
  same state that became the 10.1.0 release.
- **The no-sudo recipe that worked** (recorded for future re-tests; ~2 GB kept in
  `~/Documents/rocm10-native-stack/wheels`):
  1. pip install the TheRock wheels into an isolated target:
     `pip install --target ~/Documents/rocm10-native-stack/wheels --index-url
     https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/whl-multi-arch/ rocm-sdk-core==10.1.0a20260822
     rocm-sdk-libraries==10.1.0a20260822`
  2. the wheels carry loose `.so`s (runtime 7.16, comgr 3.4, hipblaslt/rocblas/hipblas) but
     **arch-agnostic only**: rocBLAS needs its per-arch Tensile data and hipBLASLt its gfx1200
     library dirs, which live in the era's per-arch `.deb`s
     (`amdrocm-blas10.1-gfx1200`, 266 MB) — downloaded from
     `.../packages-multi-arch/deb/20260822-32539019050/pool/main/`, extracted with **bsdtar**
     (the desk is CachyOS: no dpkg-deb; `ar x` + `tar -xJf data.tar.xz`), and the dirs
     `lib/{hipblaslt,rocblas,.kpack}` grafted into the wheel's `lib/`.
  3. desk quirks: CachyOS + fish (always `bash -lc`), `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` must be set at process start
     (Python's os.environ change inside a running process does nothing for dlopen).
- **Engine wiring:** `lib_dirs = [wheels/_rocm_sdk_core/lib, wheels/_rocm_sdk_libraries/lib,
  /opt/rocm/lib]` — the loader then resolves the engine's own deps onto the 10.1 stack (verified via
  `/proc/PID/maps`) and 10.1's stack pages in the engine's already-built kernels fine.
- **Version compat surprise:** the 10-line's `libhipblaslt.so.1` reports **compatibility version
  100401 to the engine** (log: `hipBLASLt version mismatch: file=100500 runtime=100401`) — the
  locally tuned **100401 table matches the 10.1 native lib unchanged**; no regeneration needed.
  (A ctypes probe of `hipblasLtGetVersion` from this shim returns 0 — the engine's own query is the
  trustworthy one.)
- **Arm G + G2 (same-day, each after a fresh restart, 100401 table everywhere):**

  | | 10.0 system pair (2 runs) | 10.1.0 native wheel stack (G, G2) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 4K | 1,647.8 / 1,645.0 | 1,651.7 / 1,634.5 |
  | 16K | 1,679.7 / 1,670.8 | 1,744.5 / 1,599.3 (leg 1,743.8 beside ~1,557) |
  | chat | 47.9 / 46.2 | 45.7 / 42.5 |
  | agent decode | 47.2 / 47.5 | 50.2 / 46.2 |

  **Verdict: tie on means (4K, 16K, agent each within a percent or two), the 10-line swings widely
  between fresh starts while the 10.0 pair reproduced within 0.3% all day. REJECTED for serving.**
  The 10.1 stack is kept on disk (3.3 GB, one config line away) strictly as a re-test bench for the
  day a genuine 10.2/1.5 pairing appears (sudo ROCm install or a new wheel channel).
- Scratch cleaned: the deb/extraction temps deleted (re-downloadable), merged data verified inside
  the wheel tree first. Disk 29 GB free.

### Post-0.2.1 tuning arms on the desk (Oct 20)

Base for all: the v0.2.1 arm above (4K 1,647.8 / 16K 1,679.7 / chat 47.9 / agent 47.2, same day).

- **Arm D — `STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=6` (setup's own tip for 30 GB boxes, #834): REJECTED.**
  Measured: 4K **1,398.9** (491.9–1,468.2 — a −15% median with a badly slow leg), 16K 1,649.3 (−2%),
  chat 44.6 (−7%), agent 47.0 (flat). The tip's community box is not this box; the larger headroom
  measurably starved prompts here. Reverted to the default (env key removed; default stays 4).
  Lesson: setup prints tips that need a local A/B like everything else.
- **Arm E — `--spec 4 → 6` (the config ran setup defaults; MTP draft depth never swept on the desk):
  REJECTED.** Measured: 4K 1,429.3 (−13%), 16K 1,534.1 (−9%), chat 42.9 (−10%), agent 46.2 (flat),
  and wider variance (agent re-read legs up to 124 tokens). Deeper drafts cost more than they give
  on this model/box. Reverted to `--spec 4`.
- **Sweep conclusion: both candidate levers from the 0.2.1 release notes measured worse on this machine;
  the deployed v0.2.1 config stays exactly at the shipped defaults + the Oct 18 env slate (100401
  table, RESIDENT_PIN=1, WMMA/PF/PREFILL/ADAPT/EXCHANGE) — which is itself the tuned optimum for
  this box as of Oct 20. Nothing else in 0.2.1 applies (display reserve stays on the 9060 XT because
  it drives the desktop; KV streaming needs RAM the box lacks; ROCm 10.2 pairs need sudo).**
- **Base re-confirmed after the reverts (same-day third run): 4K 1,645.0 (1,305–1,647) / 16K 1,670.8 /
  chat 46.2 / agent 47.5 — dead on the first base arm at 4K/16K. The rejected arms' low 4K medians
  were change-caused, not time-of-day drift.**
- **Arm F — 100500 re-test on the new engine (hipBLASLt 1.5 from the llama bundle + 100500 table,
  banner `version 100500`; v0.2.1): TIE with 100401, the v0.1.45-era "-11% at 4K" verdict did NOT
  carry over.** Measured: 4K 1,654.2 vs 1,647.8/1,645.0 (tie), 16K 1,710.5 vs 1,679.7/1,670.8 (+2%,
  ranges overlap), chat 47.5 (tie), agent 45.4 (−4% vs 47.2/47.5). **Keep 100401**: prompts equal,
  decode favors it, and it is the version-matched system stack (100500 depends on the llama-b1337
  bundle dir staying put). The 100500 question is closed on v0.2.1's engine too — now as a tie
  instead of a loss; a re-test is only due after a genuine ROCm 10.2/1.5 native pairing (sudo).

## The pin endgame (DONE Oct 18 2026 - memlock raised, levers measured)

One-time fix applied: /etc/security/limits.d/strata-memlock.conf with
"kareem soft memlock unlimited" + "kareem hard memlock unlimited"
(fish: printf "%s\n" "kareem soft memlock unlimited" "kareem hard memlock unlimited" | sudo tee
/etc/security/limits.d/strata-memlock.conf). Before that memlock soft+hard were 8 MiB, so
STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1 silently stayed pageable - the OLD engine did too ("pinned 0.00 GiB" in its logs).

| Arm (measured same-day) | Decode | Prefill | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1 | 48.9-56.8 (best 56.8, lowest decode_ms 2254) | 1571-1575 top | keep - "mapped pinned cache complement ready: resident 18.35 GiB, pinned 18.35 GiB" verified |
| + STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1 | 49.7-58.8 (best 58.8 all day) | 1591-1638 top | keep - "exchange buffer rotation enabled: 96 buffers ... no host commit memcpy" |
| + --adapt-async 1 re-test on pinned tier | 52.1-54.9, same median | 1563-1641 | removed - no gain vs rotate-only, and not bit-identical run to run |

## Same levers tried on the laptop (RTX 3060 6 GB, Swift IQ3_XXS CUDA, Oct 18 2026)

Bench: tools/hip/bench_prefill.py (4.2K/8.8K fresh code prompts, 128-token gens). Baseline same-day:
prefill 322–328 tok/s, decode 29.7–29.9 tok/s.

| Arm | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` | identical to baseline; NO fused-activation log line — the fused batch wants a whole layer's ~460 experts in the ring and this card's cache has 326 slots (#136) | **removed** |
| `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` | decode 30.7–31.2 (+2–4%), prefill flat; active in mapped mode (no resident variant needed) | **kept** |
| `--resident-experts` (+overlap displaced) | engine built a 39.56 GiB page-locked complement (47 GiB RAM used); decode FELL to 27.0–28.4 (23.6 worst); overlap auto-disabled in resident mode | **removed** — whole-blob PCIe exchanges cost more than mapped mode's page-cache reads on this card |

Laptop final env: STRATA_KV_PREFETCH=1, STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1 — decode ~30.7–31.2, prefill ~320–326.
The laptop cannot host the pinned/rotate endgame usefully: its mapped mode already reads experts from RAM
page cache, and its 6 GB card does not have the VRAM for a big exchange-buffer set.

Role swap per user: Ornith stopped, Swift serving on **8080** (the phantom 8080 listener cleared itself —

**Expert-residency arms (probe = /tmp/opencode/swift-probe.py, 256-token planning prompts; metric band =

| Arm | slots / VRAM free | decode tok/s | hit rate | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (auto, 64K) | 390 / 446 MiB | 29.3–30.1 | 32.1–33.5% | — |

Why flat: decode is CPU-pool-bound (64–68% of routed experts computed on the pool), so VRAM hits move PCIe
share (7.6% → 6.8–7.5%) but not the pool drain. Exhaust-online: engine-container games are done — the docs'
twice-measured collapse is at 0 MiB free (RTX 4080S: 102 → 13.7 tok/s at higher hit rates; RTX 5080:
reserve 770→0 bought +333 slots, decode 40.9 → 16.6 — "the slack is worth more than the extra slots").
**Dead ends with doc/help citation on this build:** `--kv-grow` needs whole-KV-in-VRAM mode — stays off with
KV streaming (help text); `--kv-resident` floors at 20480 cells (config's 4096 clamped); `--vram-reserve-mib`
doesn't exist in this (pre-0.1.44) checkout — the arm that helped others isn't available here.

**Kept: `--expert-profile-save` persistence.** `--expert-profile P` pre-fills 392/392 slots from the shipped
profile in 0.1 s (11.9 GB/s); adding `--expert-profile-save /home/kareem/strata/data/expert-profile-learned.bin
--expert-profile-save-every 10` persists what the adaptive tier learns about real planner traffic (written on
QUIT and every 10 min; the next start starts from it). Zero-cost, compounds with use — re-probe hit rates in
a few days of real work. Untried, next-arms list: `--adapt-async 1` (swaps between verify windows, not
bit-exact), smaller `--prefill` chunk (borrow path borrows 240 slots during prefill — prefill-phase hits).


## Do NOT re-litigate (measured flat or worse)
- prefill chunk > 32768 (flat), `--spec` > 4 (flat), `--kv-resident` changes at small contexts (flat).
- MTP side stream on gfx1200 (see #9).

## Measurement protocol (keep it honest, per the repo's docs style)
- Bench with fresh prompts (no prefix reuse) for A/B arms; note prompt-n and the `reading the prompt`
  rate lines; one warmup + 3 trials, medians.
- Focused script: `tools/hip/bench_prefill.py` exists in this repo for the HIP prefill path.
- Compare against a same-day run of the current config (the repo's CONTRIBUTING rule: every claim needs
  numbers + what they were measured on).
- After each ROCm or driver update: re-check (5) and (1) — the tuning table version must match the
  library exactly or the engine silently pre-fills ~45% slower.

## One-line config sketch (as measured deployed Oct 18 2026, for a fresh-session handoff)
```
env: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=<path>/gfx1200-hipblaslt-100401.txt (match the installed hipBLASLt!), STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1,
     STRATA_PF_FUSED=1, STRATA_PF_GEMM=1, STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=4096, STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=1,
     STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1, STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP_RESIDENT=1, STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=1, STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1
args: --expert-profile expert-profile-coder.bin --expert-cache auto --resident-experts
      --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5
      --kv int8 --max-context 180000
      (everything else setup-generated for coder IQ1_M)
```
Requires the memlock limits.d entry above, or RESIDENT_PIN/EXCHANGE_ROTATE silently stay off.
`STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=6` was measured NEGATIVE here (broke lend coverage 1152/1426 → ~26% long-prompt
penalty warned); HEADROOM was 4 by engine default and correct on this 30 GB box.

inode; next start takes it), restarted via the control server, benched (bench/results/2026-10-22-coder-v022-engine):

4K 1509.0 vs 1514.9 (-0.4%), 16K 1644.9 vs 1678.6 (-2.0%), chat dec 46.0 vs 47.0, agent dec 49.1 vs 49.3 —
all inside the ring sweep's start-to-start roulette band: no regression, no gain, deployed as the new base.
Ops note: the control node server's /start /stop had an inverted isRunning branch (start refused while idle,
stop ran with nothing running) — fixed Oct 22, /status verified.

## Coder MTP / adaptive-swaps decomposition + victory combo (Oct 22, v0.2.2 engine, 4 arms, strata_bench medians)
Question after the Oct 21 drift-audit: what is --adapt-swaps 0 worth on the Coder, and what does MTP cost?
Four arms, fresh start each, same-day baseline = v0.2.2 engine from the engine A/B (1509.0/4K, 1644.9/16K,

## Conversation cache (Oct 22): cap set, floor governs
Defaults were slot-4/prompt-cache-6 (~118 MB each)/min-free 2560 MiB; zero park events had ever fired
(single-session use). Added `--conversation-cache-mib 4096` (bench-neutral: a cap, no reservation) so
parallel-session parking is permitted up to 4 GiB total. At the recorded RAM state (MemAvailable ~4.4-5.4 GiB)
the 2560 MiB floor still limits actual parking to ~2-3 GiB; a true 4 GiB multi-session cache would require

Park events and skipped parks are visible in the engine log ("conversation cache: parked|skipped ... bytes=").

## CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to Strata

**AI assistance is welcome. The contributor is responsible for understanding the change and supplying real evidence.**

These rules apply to issues, pull requests, benchmark reports, and the agents helping prepare them.
You should be able to explain every changed line and answer review questions about it.

## Before starting

1. Search [issues](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues) and
   [pull requests](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pulls), including closed discussions. Add new evidence to an
   existing thread when it covers your problem.
2. Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the documentation for the component you want to change.
3. Get maintainer agreement on scope before substantial features, refactors, architecture changes, or changes to
   defaults. Describe the user problem, proposed behavior, and tradeoffs in an issue first. Agreement on scope
   does not guarantee a merge. Focused fixes and benchmark reports can go straight to a PR.
4. Keep one problem per PR. Update that PR after feedback; do not open competing attempts for the same change.

Do not resubmit a declined proposal under a different title or through another agent. If new evidence changes
the situation, bring it to the original discussion and let a maintainer decide whether to reopen it.

## Report a problem people can investigate

Use the matching [issue form](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/new/choose). A bug report should include:

- The smallest steps or command that reproduce the problem, and the expected and actual behavior.
- Strata version or commit, OS, GPU and VRAM, and relevant model, quantization, and configuration.
- The exact error and relevant logs, with credentials and private content removed.
- Whether you reproduced it yourself. Label a finding based only on reading code or a scanner as
  **unconfirmed static analysis**, and explain the suspected path without presenting it as an observed failure.

Do not invent reproduction steps, errors, affected hardware, or severity. If you cannot reproduce something,
say what you inspected and what would verify the hypothesis. Feature requests should explain a concrete user
need and the current workaround. Questions should say what you tried and where you got stuck.

Example structure, with placeholders to replace with actual observations:

```text
Problem: <one observed behavior>
Environment: <commit, OS, GPU/VRAM, model/quant, relevant settings>
Reproduce: <exact command or short sequence>
Expected: <documented or intended behavior>
Actual: <observed behavior and exact error>
Evidence: <sanitized log attachment>
Reproduction status: <reproduced locally OR unconfirmed static analysis>
```

## Titles

Every issue and pull request title starts with its area in square brackets, then a short description: `[Engine]`, `[GUI]`, `[TUI]`,
`[Benchmark]`, `[Docs]` or `[Other]`. For example `[Engine] fix decode stop on long prompts` or `[GUI] keep the model list after a tab
switch`. The issue forms ask for the area and a check on the title fails when the prefix is missing.

## Prepare a focused pull request

Lead with the problem and resulting behavior. Explain why the approach is needed, the important limits, and
any compatibility effects. Link the issue and scope agreement when applicable. A file-by-file narration or
an AI-generated summary of the diff is not a substitute for this explanation.

- Keep unrelated formatting, cleanup, dependency changes, and speculative abstractions out of the PR.
- Add documentation where it changes what a user or developer needs to know. Avoid repeated summaries,
  speculative roadmaps, and generated documentation with no actionable information.
- Preserve existing behavior outside the intended change. New features are opt-in; follow the default-path
  and performance requirements in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
- Read the complete diff, including generated files, before submitting. Remove debugging output, secrets,
  private paths, and accidental files.
- Prefer a small relevant regression check over tests that only restate the implementation. Documentation-only
  changes need link, example, and consistency checks; they do not require GPU builds.

## Show the validation you actually performed

List exact commands, the revision and environment tested, and observed outcomes. Keep **passed**, **failed**,
and **not run** separate. Include relevant output or a log attachment. A command you suggest running is not
evidence that it passed; a CI run on a different revision is not validation of the submitted code.

Build every backend a code change touches, including CUDA, HIP, and SYCL where applicable, before requesting
review. For changes that need hardware execution, report that execution separately from compilation. A mock,
static check, or successful build does not establish hardware correctness. If you lack a required environment,
keep the PR as a draft, identify the missing checks, and ask for targeted help in the same thread. Do not claim
compatibility you have not tested.

Performance claims need before/after runs on the same hardware and workload, with every changed setting
identified. Preserve the individual runs, failures, and variability. Follow the
[community measurement guide](docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md); standard submissions will use the
[benchmark protocol](docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md) once it is activated. One fast run does not justify changing a
default or claiming a speedup for other machines.

Example PR body; placeholders are not test results:

```text
Problem and result: <trigger; behavior before and after the change>
Related discussion: <issue URL and scope agreement, when required>
Approach: <why this fix; relevant compatibility effects>
Validation:
  Passed: <exact command, revision/environment, observed result, log>
  Failed: <exact command and failure, or none observed>
  Not run: <check, reason, and what remains unverified>
Limits: <known limitations or remaining work>
```

## Rules for AI-assisted work

Use agents to help investigate, implement, and explain work that you can review. Before submitting, verify
their claims against the source, actual command output, or a cited primary reference.

Never submit fabricated measurements, invented test results, fake logs, or copied claims you have not checked.
Do not turn a repository scan into a batch of speculative issues or PRs. Consolidate related findings, establish
their effect, and submit the useful evidence. Do not present an agent's confidence or another model's approval
as validation. Keep review replies concise and address the requested change or evidence directly.

Maintainers may request a smaller change, return a PR to draft, or close a submission that lacks evidence,
duplicates existing work, or ignores agreed scope. A smaller, understandable contribution with honest limits
is easier to review and maintain.

## Share a benchmark

A results-only PR should contain the human report, raw measurements, sanitized configuration, and supporting
logs. Keep it separate from engine changes and include poor results and failed requests.

The [current community benchmark guide](docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md) remains available for measurements made
with today's tools. The [new protocol](docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md) defines the draft standard and future approval
workflow. Its draft status must remain visible: existing reports are not automatically standard or approved.


## HAND_OFF.md

# HAND_OFF.md — MTP tuning, stage 3 (2026-10-28, late session)

Continues the stage-1/2 sweep written earlier today. **Stage 3 reverses stage 1's
conclusion**: the `--spec-min-p 0.25` winner was a measurement artifact, and the
live profile is now back on the shipped default `--spec-min-p 0.5`, with evidence.

## State of the machine (unchanged, verified)

- Terminal 0.2.7, Control 0.1.53, engine 0.1.52 (`linux-x86_64-hip-rx9070`) at
  `~/.local/share/strata/components/engine/0.1.52-linux-x86_64-hip-rx9070/strata`.
- Card: RX 9060 XT-class (gfx1200), hip, hipBLASLt table
  `tools/hip/gfx1200-hipblaslt-100500.txt` active ("67 rows, gfx1200, version 100500").
- Live profile `/home/kareem/Documents/strata-start-stop-server/coder-dflash2-15.json`:
  `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--mtp-q4 all`, `--max-context 179000`, `--kv int8`,
  `--resident-experts`. Rollback copies in the same folder:
  `.bak-20261028` (pre-stage-1, exe already repointed to 0.1.52).
- 8080 server is the profile's own (started 15:46 by `start-strata.sh`), verified by
  the engine line in `strata-coder-iq1_m-dflash2-15.log` and live requests.
- `--draft dflash2 ...` stays inert under `--serve` (engine drafts with MTP). Unchanged.

## Two facts stage 1/2 missed

1. **`--spec 4` does not run as 4.** `src/program/generate.cpp:3208` — because
   `--suffix-draft` defaults to 3, the engine sets `mtp_max_t = spec` and raises
   `spec` to `spec+2` (capped 8). So stage 1's arms compared *effective* windows
   6 (from 4), 7 (from 5), 8 (from 6): "`--spec 4` is the right depth" really means
   "effective 6 with MTP capped at 4 beats effective 7 and 8". Untested levers that
   follow from this: `--suffix-draft 0`, `--mtp-max-t M`, `--lookup-chain-min M`,
   `--mtp-hnorm stream`, and **`--mtp-window`** (draft layer attends to the last N
   cells, default 32768, `src/program/generate.cpp:681`; it is in `--help`'s shadow —
   it parses at `generate.cpp:1922` — and docs/STRIX_HALO.md:144 measured +3.5% at
   8192 on 64K output). At this profile's 179k window it is the biggest untested knob.
2. **`spec_min_p` can be overridden per request** —
   `serve/server.py:1427` forwards `"strata_tune": {"spec_min_p": P}` into the engine's
   GEN line (`generate.cpp:12351`), so the lever can be A/B-tested **inside one running
   server, with no restart and no downtime**. That is what made stage 3 possible. It
   cannot be set as a shared default through `POST /settings` (not in `SHARED_KEYS`,
   `serve/server.py:7749`); only the run config's `sampling.strata_tune` block
   (`server.py:7952`) carries it, and that needs a restart like an engine flag.

## Why stage 1's numbers misled

Stage 1 compared medians of 6 rounds across **separate process restarts**. Within an
arm the round-to-round spread was sd ≈ 5-6 tok/s on a base of ~48 (min 42, max 62), so
the standard error of a median of 6 is ≈ ±6% — about the size of every "winner" it
reported. The four base repeats (49.7/49.5/49.7/49.8, and one at 52.1) sit inside that
band too.

Stage 3 fixes it: one process, the same cached document, value order rotated so each
`spec_min_p` occupies each slot once per question (Latin square), 3 passes × 5 values ×
6 questions = 90 requests per context size, and the statistic is the **paired difference
against min-p 0.25 within the same (pass, question) cell** — drift cancels.

## Stage 3 — paired, greedy (temperature 0), 18 pairs per value

`mtp-tune/runner4.py`, evidence `mtp-tune/evidence/stage3-117k.jsonl`,
`stage3-155k.jsonl`, summaries `summary-stage3-117k.txt`, `summary-stage3-155k.txt`.

| min-p | 117k tok/s | paired vs 0.25 | 155k tok/s | paired vs 0.25 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| 0.05 | 46.0 | −3.41% (se 2.10) tie | 45.8 | −1.96% (se 1.86) tie |
| 0.15 | 47.8 | −1.83% (se 2.08) tie | 45.5 | −4.56% (se 1.39) **loses** |
| **0.25** | 48.9 | base | 47.5 | base |
| 0.35 | 48.1 | +0.82% (se 2.48) tie | 47.7 | +2.48% (se 1.27) tie |
| 0.50 | 48.6 | −0.21% (se 1.28) tie | 49.2 | +0.72% (se 1.46) tie |

Acceptance does move with the floor (0.49 at 0.05 → 0.71 at 0.5, `draft_n` 394 → 217),
but on this card it does not move decode speed: greedy is a flat plateau, and **0.25 is
not better than 0.5 anywhere**. Below 0.25 starts to cost.

## Stage 3 — paired, sampled (temperature 0.7 + the model card's top_p 0.8 / top_k 20)

`mtp-tune/runner5.py` → `probe_5b`, evidence `evidence/stage5b-temp07.jsonl`,
`runner5b.out`. This is the setting the user's apps actually send (the stage-1/2/3-greedy
workloads were greedy-only, the handoff's own stated limit).

| min-p | median tok/s | accept | paired vs 0.25 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **0.25** (was live) | 44.2 | 0.49 | base |
| **0.50** (now live) | 47.1 | 0.67 | **+4.77% (se 1.73) — beats** |
| 0.75 | 43.7 | 0.81 | −2.00% (se 1.36) — loses |

## Decision applied

`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5` — the shipped default — is the best of everything measured
so far: a tie or a small win over 0.25 greedy at both context sizes, and +4.8% on
sampled traffic, which is the real workload. The profile is edited, the server was
restarted at 15:46, and the running engine line reads `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`.
Post-restart spot check (one question each, no statistics): 61.6 tok/s sampled and
63.0 tok/s greedy on a cache-hit 117k prefix.

## Stage 4 — `--mtp-window` at 154,545 tokens (later the same day)

`mtp-tune/runner6.py`, evidence `evidence/stage4-mtpwindow.jsonl`, summary
`summary-stage4-mtpwindow.txt`, run logs `runner6.out` / `runner6c.out`.
Each arm is a fresh serve on 8091 (8080 stopped: one engine fits in GPU+RAM); greedy,
18 paired rounds vs the base arm, plus the arm's own cold prefill rate.
Base = no flag = the engine default 32,768 cells (`src/program/generate.cpp:681`).

| arm | median decode | accept | cold prefill | paired decode vs base |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| base 32,768 | 48.5 | 0.74 | 1597.6 tok/s | — |
| 16384 | 49.7 | 0.73 | 1590.9 | +0.08% (se 1.04) tie |
| 8192 | 49.0 | 0.73 | 1591.7 | −0.46% (se 1.54) tie |
| **4096** | 52.1 | 0.74 | 1600.4 | **+3.18% (se 1.31) beats** |
| **0 = every cell** | 46.0 | 0.73 | 1578.7 | **−6.98% (se 1.47) loses** |
| base repeat (6 rounds) | 47.9 | 0.72 | 1584.3 | −1.68% (se 4.29) — drift band |

- The `0` arm is what makes the rest readable: on this card the draft layer's attention
  window **does** cost real time (every-cell is ~7% slower), so the 8192/16384 ties are
  genuine nulls, not an inert flag. Strix Halo's `--mtp-window 8192` +3.5%
  (docs/STRIX_HALO.md:144) does not transfer.
- `4096` is the one claim, and it is **applied but not confirmed**: it was the last arm
  measured, in a later process than base. The base repeat inside this session differed
  from the base arm by −1.68% ±4.29 (n=6), which is too wide to rule out drift of that
  size. Acceptance did not move (0.74), so the win is pure verify-time saving; that is
  the shape that would be real.
- Prefill did not improve with any window, including 4096 (1578-1600 tok/s, all one
  sample each): the draft-KV truncation in `src/core/mtp.cpp:1426` is not a first-token
  lever here.
- Changing the window invalidates the parked conversation cache
  (`src/core/conversation_file.cpp:885`, checked by `conversation_file_test.cpp:378`),
  which was observed: the first 117k request after the restart re-prefilled (81 s wall,
  `cache_n 0`).

Applied at 16:46: `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp-window 4096` in the live profile,
server restarted, engine argv confirmed, warm 117k cache-hit rounds at 49.1 / 49.8 tok/s
(accept 0.72-0.78). To undo it, delete the two `--mtp-window 4096` lines from
`coder-dflash2-15.json` and restart.

## Stage 5 — `--mtp-hnorm stream` (17:00, restart-based A/B, item 4)

`--mtp-hnorm pooled|stream` changes only the draft layer's hidden-input norm: `pooled`
(default) takes one RMS over all four hyper-connection streams, `stream` normalizes each
stream on its own, which is what llama.cpp's own MTP graph does
(`include/strata/core/mtp.hpp:59-62`, `docs/DETAILS.md:394`, `third_party/llama.cpp/src/models/qwen3next.cpp:678`).
Drafts only — the verifier decides every token — so a change here can only move speed,
never answer quality.

Protocol: `mtp-tune/runner7.py`, the generalized version of stage 4 (any extra flag or
`ENV:KEY=VAL` per arm, first arm is the reference). Three fresh `strata serve` processes
on port 8091, 8080 down for the whole run: 154,545-token cached document, greedy, 320
tokens, 3 passes x 6 questions = 18 rounds per arm, plus a 1-pass base repeat at the end
to see how far the machine moved between processes.

```
base = base: median 50.7 tok/s (n=18), prefill 1584.6 tok/s
hnorm-stream  n=18 median=52.9 accept=0.78 | paired +5.59% (se 1.66) BEATS | prefill 1591.0
base-repeat   n= 6 median=48.8 accept=0.72 | paired -0.46% (se 2.65) tie
```

Read it as: +5.6% decode with the drift check at −0.5% (a tie), and the acceptance rate
going 0.72 → 0.78 is the mechanism, not a side effect — the pooled norm was feeding the
draft layer a distorted hidden state. Prefill is flat (1584.6 → 1591.0, inside stage 4's
1578.7-1600.4 spread).

Applied at 17:11: `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp-hnorm stream --mtp-window 4096` in the
live profile, engine argv confirmed on the running process, a short greedy request
returning at 66.6 tok/s. Undo: delete the two `--mtp-hnorm stream` lines from
`coder-dflash2-15.json` and restart. Pre-change state: `coder-dflash2-15.json.bak-20261028-hnorm`.

Not tested: whether `stream` interacts with `--mtp-q4 all` or the 4096 window (both were
on in both arms, so the win is the win for this combination only), and whether the
acceptance gain holds at temperature 0.7 (stage 6 measures that as a by-product, since
every arm of that scan now runs on `stream`).

## Greedy output is not reproducible here — measured, and documented behavior

At temperature 0 the reply text changed between min-p values **and between two identical
requests** (probe 5a, `runner5.py` → `probe_5a`, `evidence/determinism-5a.json`): each of
4 settings produced 2 different replies; passing a `seed` did not pin the text either.
Cause is in the repo's own code and docs, not speculation about it:
`src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp:243-260` (`native_gu_mt_min`, issue #152) — one token
uses ggml's `vec_dot`, two or more use the multi-token AVX kernels, and how many tokens
share an expert row depends on how many drafts a verify window held, so the last bits and
near-ties at temperature 0 depend on the drafting. `docs/DETAILS.md:99-104` documents it
and the opt-in fix `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` (config `env`), measured −1..−3% decode on a
Ryzen 7600. Verification itself stays exact (`generate.cpp:16646`, strict argmax
equality; rollback of K/V and GDN state is exact, `include/strata/core/verify.hpp:13-18`),
so this is arithmetic, not a wrong accept.
Consequence: the docs' "byte-identical greedy answers" claims
(`docs/RADEON_780M.md:110`, `docs/MULTI_GPU.md:199`) hold only across runs with the same
window widths, not across `spec_min_p` settings, unless `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` is set.
**Not tested on this card**: what `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` costs here (it needs a restart).

## What is left

1. **Confirm or drop `--mtp-window 4096`** (it is live but unconfirmed, see stage 4): one
   fresh session, base arm first then 4096, 18 paired rounds each, ~10 min with 8080
   down: `python3 runner6.py base-32k` then `python3 runner6.py 4096`, or edit the arm
   list. If it does not hold, delete the flag.
   Still unmeasured process-level levers, same restart cost each:
   `--suffix-draft 0` (true `--spec 4`, no lookup windows), `--mtp-max-t`,
   `--lookup-chain 4 --lookup-chain-min 5` (stage 1's chain combo failed with the default
   min 3), `--mtp-hnorm stream`, and `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` (reproducible greedy output,
   expected −1..−3% but unmeasured on this card).
2. Prefill / time-to-first-token has never been swept at all — every stage measured
   decode only. At a 179k window the first-token wait is the number the user feels.
   Knobs: `--prefill auto`, `--prefill-pipe` (settable per request via `pipe=`),
   `--ple-io ram` (docs/DETAILS.md:2500 measured −18% prompt at 4K on another card),
   `--short-read`, the `STRATA_PF_*` env already in the profile.
3. Concurrency: everything here is one slot. `--batch-mtp` measured identical to base
   because there was no second slot.

## Limits of the stage-3 measurement (say these with any claim)

- One card, one profile, one model (coder IQ1_M), one fixed repo-text document, 6 fixed
  questions, 320-token answers, single slot.
- Context sizes 117,284 and 154,545 prompt tokens — not the exact 179k cap.
- Greedy stage: 18 pairs per value; sampled stage: 18 pairs per value but the replies
  differ text-to-text, so its pairing is by (pass, question) cell, not by identical work.
- Stage 1/2's per-arm medians (54.2 / 50.7 tok/s etc.) are NOT comparable with stage 3's
  numbers: different protocol, and stage 1/2 unpaired. Only stage 3's paired differences
  carry a standard error.
- Nothing here tested `--spec` depth against the effective-window rewrite in fact 1, so
  "`--spec 4` is right" is only "effective 6 is right" as measured.
