        r[i] = bfly(r[i], _mm512_shuffle_f32x4(r[i], r[i], 0b10110001), (__mmask16) 0xF0F0);   // h = 4
        r[i] = bfly(r[i], _mm512_shuffle_f32x4(r[i], r[i], 0b01001110), (__mmask16) 0xFF00);   // h = 8
    }
    for (int h = 1; h < 8; h <<= 1)   // h = 16, 32, 64: whole registers
        for (int i = 0; i < 8; i += 2 * h)
            for (int j = i; j < i + h; ++j) {
                const __m512 a = r[j], b = r[j + h];
                r[j] = _mm512_add_ps(a, b);
                r[j + h] = _mm512_sub_ps(a, b);
            }
    const __m512 s = _mm512_set1_ps(0.088388347648f);
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) _mm512_storeu_ps(v + 16 * i, _mm512_mul_ps(r[i], s));
}

// exl3_cpu_prepare_block / exl3_cpu_band_out with the FP16 scales converted 16 at a time (vcvtph2ps: exact, as
// f32_from_f16) and the block's sum in eight double lanes
EXL3_AVX512 float prepare_block_avx512(const uint16_t* suh, const float* x, float* xh) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 16) {
        const __m512 sc = _mm512_cvtph_ps(_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*) (suh + i)));
        _mm512_storeu_ps(xh + i, _mm512_mul_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(x + i), sc));
    }
    had128_avx512(xh);
    __m512d s0 = _mm512_setzero_pd(), s1 = _mm512_setzero_pd();
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 16) {
        s0 = _mm512_add_pd(s0, _mm512_cvtps_pd(_mm256_loadu_ps(xh + i)));
        s1 = _mm512_add_pd(s1, _mm512_cvtps_pd(_mm256_loadu_ps(xh + i + 8)));
    }
    return (float) _mm512_reduce_add_pd(_mm512_add_pd(s0, s1));
}
EXL3_AVX512 void band_out_avx512(const float* acc, float ki, float kz, const uint16_t* svh, float* y) {
    const __m512 vk = _mm512_set1_ps(ki), vz = _mm512_set1_ps(kz);
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 16) _mm512_storeu_ps(y + i, _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(acc + i), vk, vz));
    had128_avx512(y);
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 16) {
        const __m512 sc = _mm512_cvtph_ps(_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*) (svh + i)));
        _mm512_storeu_ps(y + i, _mm512_mul_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(y + i), sc));
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- AVX2
// The AVX-512 tier on 8-lane registers, a tile row's 16 columns as two halves of 8 (after exllamav3's AVX2 tier).
// Column c' of a half reads the tile's words K c' + base (mod 8K) - its 8 words lie in one residue class of the word
// index mod K, and its funnel shift is the same for all 8 (the layout's row-shift invariant).  So each tile's K
// registers are regrouped once into its K classes, and every half's gather is then ONE vpermd of a class register
// (none where the lanes are in order already) instead of a permute and a blend per register the half reads: odd K
// takes each class lane from exactly one register (blends only), K 2 / 4 / 8 are shuffles / a 4x4 / an 8x8 transpose,
// K 6 a permute and a blend per register.  exllamav3 gets the same single permute from a planar order repacked at load
// (`_copy_repacked`); here the regrouping costs a few register ops a tile and the RAM tier and the GPUs keep the
// tiles as they are.  The shifts are immediates, and the byte sum and the FMA are the AVX-512 tier's, lane for lane
// in the same (slice, row) order: the two tiers give the same bits.

// the lane of tile word w in its class register (class w % K; avx2_classes builds them)
constexpr int avx2_slot(int K, int w) {
    return (K & 1)    ? (w & 7)
           : K == 2   ? (w & 4) | ((w >> 2) & 2) | ((w >> 1) & 1)
           : K == 4   ? (w >> 3) + 4 * ((w >> 2) & 1)
           : K == 8   ? (w >> 3)
                      : w / K;
}

// per row and half: the right shift, whether the 16-bit windows sit in one word (no second gather), and for the
// window's first and last word the class register and the vpermd lanes that put its 8 words in column order
template <int K>
struct Avx2Tab {
    int sh[16][2] = {};
    bool one[16][2] = {};
    int cls[16][2][2] = {};
    bool ident[16][2][2] = {};
    int32_t idx[16][2][2][8] = {};
    bool ok = true;   // the invariants above hold for every row and half
};
template <int K>
constexpr Avx2Tab<K> make_avx2tab() {
    Avx2Tab<K> t{};
    const RowTab<K> rt = make_rowtab<K>();
    for (int r = 0; r < 16; ++r)
        for (int h = 0; h < 2; ++h) {
            const int c0 = 8 * h;
            t.sh[r][h] = rt.sr[r][c0];
            t.one[r][h] = true;
            for (int c = c0; c < c0 + 8; ++c) {
                if (rt.sr[r][c] != t.sh[r][h]) t.ok = false;
                if (rt.i0[r][c] != rt.i1[r][c]) t.one[r][h] = false;
            }
            if (t.one[r][h] != (t.sh[r][h] <= 16)) t.ok = false;
            for (int wd = 0; wd < 2; ++wd) {
                const auto& ix = wd == 0 ? rt.i0 : rt.i1;
                t.cls[r][h][wd] = ix[r][c0] % K;
                t.ident[r][h][wd] = true;
                for (int c = 0; c < 8; ++c) {
                    if (ix[r][c0 + c] % K != t.cls[r][h][wd]) t.ok = false;
                    t.idx[r][h][wd][c] = avx2_slot(K, ix[r][c0 + c]);
                    if (t.idx[r][h][wd][c] != c) t.ident[r][h][wd] = false;
                }
            }
        }
    return t;
}
template <int K>
inline constexpr Avx2Tab<K> kAvx2Tab = make_avx2tab<K>();

// odd K: lane l of class rho is register j's, the one j with (8 j + l) % K == rho
template <int K, int RHO, int J>
constexpr int avx2_odd_mask() {
    int m = 0;
    for (int l = 0; l < 8; ++l)
        if ((8 * J + l) % K == RHO) m |= 1 << l;
    return m;
}
template <int K, int RHO, int J = 1>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE __m256i avx2_odd_class(const __m256i (&R)[K], __m256i acc) {
    if constexpr (J == K) {
        return acc;
    } else {
        constexpr int m = avx2_odd_mask<K, RHO, J>();   // (clang's _mm256_blend_epi32 is a macro: no template commas)
        return avx2_odd_class<K, RHO, J + 1>(R, _mm256_blend_epi32(acc, R[J], m));
    }
}
template <int K, int... RHO>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_odd_classes(const __m256i (&R)[K], __m256i (&C)[K], std::integer_sequence<int, RHO...>) {
    ((C[RHO] = avx2_odd_class<K, RHO>(R, R[0])), ...);
}
// any K (used for K 6): class rho's word rho + K s at lane s - each register's words permuted there, then blended
template <int K, int RHO, int J>
constexpr int avx2_gen_mask() {
    int m = 0;
    for (int s = 0; s < 8; ++s)
        if ((RHO + K * s) / 8 == J) m |= 1 << s;
    return m;
}
template <int K, int RHO, int J, int S>
constexpr int avx2_gen_lane() {
    return (RHO + K * S) / 8 == J ? (RHO + K * S) % 8 : 0;
}
template <int K, int RHO, int J = 0>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE __m256i avx2_gen_class(const __m256i (&R)[K], __m256i acc) {
    if constexpr (J == K) {
        return acc;
    } else if constexpr (avx2_gen_mask<K, RHO, J>() == 0) {
        return avx2_gen_class<K, RHO, J + 1>(R, acc);
    } else {
        const __m256i p = _mm256_permutevar8x32_epi32(
            R[J], _mm256_setr_epi32(avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 0>(), avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 1>(),
                                    avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 2>(), avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 3>(),
                                    avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 4>(), avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 5>(),
                                    avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 6>(), avx2_gen_lane<K, RHO, J, 7>()));
        constexpr int m = avx2_gen_mask<K, RHO, J>();   // (a macro under clang, as above)
        return avx2_gen_class<K, RHO, J + 1>(R, _mm256_blend_epi32(acc, p, m));
    }
}
template <int K, int... RHO>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_gen_classes(const __m256i (&R)[K], __m256i (&C)[K], std::integer_sequence<int, RHO...>) {
    ((C[RHO] = avx2_gen_class<K, RHO>(R, _mm256_setzero_si256())), ...);
}
// a 4x4 transpose in each 128-bit half: o[q] = lanes q and q + 4 of r0..r3
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_t4(__m256i r0, __m256i r1, __m256i r2, __m256i r3, __m256i (&o)[4]) {
    const __m256i t0 = _mm256_unpacklo_epi32(r0, r1), t1 = _mm256_unpackhi_epi32(r0, r1);
    const __m256i t2 = _mm256_unpacklo_epi32(r2, r3), t3 = _mm256_unpackhi_epi32(r2, r3);
    o[0] = _mm256_unpacklo_epi64(t0, t2);
    o[1] = _mm256_unpackhi_epi64(t0, t2);
    o[2] = _mm256_unpacklo_epi64(t1, t3);
    o[3] = _mm256_unpackhi_epi64(t1, t3);
}
// a tile's 8K words as its K class registers (word w in C[w % K] at lane avx2_slot(K, w))
template <int K>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_classes(const uint32_t* w, __m256i (&C)[K]) {
    __m256i R[K];
    for (int j = 0; j < K; ++j) R[j] = _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*) (w + 8 * j));
    if constexpr (K == 1) {
        C[0] = R[0];
    } else if constexpr (K % 2 == 1) {
        avx2_odd_classes<K>(R, C, std::make_integer_sequence<int, K>{});
    } else if constexpr (K == 2) {
        const __m256 a = _mm256_castsi256_ps(R[0]), b = _mm256_castsi256_ps(R[1]);
        C[0] = _mm256_castps_si256(_mm256_shuffle_ps(a, b, 0x88));   // words 0 2 8 10 | 4 6 12 14
        C[1] = _mm256_castps_si256(_mm256_shuffle_ps(a, b, 0xDD));   // words 1 3 9 11 | 5 7 13 15
    } else if constexpr (K == 4) {
        avx2_t4(R[0], R[1], R[2], R[3], C);
    } else if constexpr (K == 8) {
        __m256i A[4], B[4];
        avx2_t4(R[0], R[1], R[2], R[3], A);
        avx2_t4(R[4], R[5], R[6], R[7], B);
        for (int q = 0; q < 4; ++q) {
            C[q] = _mm256_permute2x128_si256(A[q], B[q], 0x20);
            C[q + 4] = _mm256_permute2x128_si256(A[q], B[q], 0x31);
        }
    } else {
        avx2_gen_classes<K>(R, C, std::make_integer_sequence<int, K>{});
    }
}

// the 8 words (first or last of each window) of row R's half H, in column order
template <int K, int R, int H, int WD>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE __m256i avx2_gather(const __m256i (&C)[K]) {
    constexpr const Avx2Tab<K>& T = kAvx2Tab<K>;
    if constexpr (T.ident[R][H][WD]) {
        return C[T.cls[R][H][WD]];
    } else {
        return _mm256_permutevar8x32_epi32(C[T.cls[R][H][WD]],
                                           _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i*) T.idx[R][H][WD]));
    }
}

struct Avx2Consts {
    __m256i mult, ones8, ones16, low16;
};
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE Avx2Consts avx2_consts() {
    return {_mm256_set1_epi32((int) kMul1), _mm256_set1_epi8(1), _mm256_set1_epi16(1), _mm256_set1_epi32(0xffff)};
}

// row R's half H: its 8 states, and their codebook byte sums as F32
template <int K, int R, int H>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE __m256 avx2_sums(const __m256i (&C)[K], const Avx2Consts& k) {
    constexpr const Avx2Tab<K>& T = kAvx2Tab<K>;
    constexpr int sh = T.sh[R][H];
    const __m256i b = avx2_gather<K, R, H, 1>(C);
    __m256i st;
    if constexpr (T.one[R][H] && sh == 16) {
        st = _mm256_srli_epi32(b, 16);
    } else if constexpr (T.one[R][H]) {
        st = _mm256_and_si256(_mm256_srli_epi32(b, sh), k.low16);
    } else {
        const __m256i a = avx2_gather<K, R, H, 0>(C);
        st = _mm256_and_si256(_mm256_or_si256(_mm256_srli_epi32(b, sh), _mm256_slli_epi32(a, 32 - sh)), k.low16);
    }
    return _mm256_cvtepi32_ps(
        _mm256_madd_epi16(_mm256_maddubs_epi16(_mm256_mullo_epi32(st, k.mult), k.ones8), k.ones16));
}

template <int K, int R>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_rows(const __m256i (&C)[K], const float* xk, __m256& lo, __m256& hi, const Avx2Consts& k) {
    if constexpr (R < 16) {
        const __m256 xv = _mm256_broadcast_ss(xk + R);
        lo = _mm256_fmadd_ps(avx2_sums<K, R, 0>(C, k), xv, lo);
        hi = _mm256_fmadd_ps(avx2_sums<K, R, 1>(C, k), xv, hi);
        avx2_rows<K, R + 1>(C, xk, lo, hi, k);
    }
}

template <int K>
EXL3_AVX2 void band_avx2(const Exl3Part& m, const float* xh, int tc0, int ks0, int ks1, float* out /* 128 */) {
    static_assert(kAvx2Tab<K>.ok, "EXL3 tile layout: a half row's words must share a residue class and a shift");
    constexpr int W = 8 * K;
    const int ld = m.n / 16;
    const size_t row_words = (size_t) ld * W;
    const Avx2Consts k = avx2_consts();
    __m256 acc[8][2];   // the band's 8 tiles (16 registers: in memory, a tile's two taken at a time)
    for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t) acc[t][0] = acc[t][1] = _mm256_setzero_ps();
    const uint32_t* row = m.trellis + (size_t) ks0 * row_words + (size_t) tc0 * W;
    for (int ks = ks0; ks < ks1; ++ks, row += row_words) {
        // the band's 8 tiles of this slice are contiguous; the next slices' are one row of tiles on
        const char* pf = (const char*) (row + 4 * row_words);
        for (int l = 0; l < 8 * W * 4; l += 64) _mm_prefetch(pf + l, _MM_HINT_T0);
        const float* xk = xh + ks * 16;
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t) {
            __m256i C[K];
            avx2_classes<K>(row + t * W, C);
            __m256 lo = acc[t][0], hi = acc[t][1];
            avx2_rows<K, 0>(C, xk, lo, hi, k);
            acc[t][0] = lo;
            acc[t][1] = hi;
        }
    }
    for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t) {
        _mm256_storeu_ps(out + t * 16, acc[t][0]);
        _mm256_storeu_ps(out + t * 16 + 8, acc[t][1]);
    }
}

// band_avx2 for N activations at once, as band_avx512_n: a half row's states summed once, then one FMA per
// activation - activation i's FMAs are band_avx2's for it alone, in its order, so out[i] is the same bit for bit.
// Up to 3 activations both halves of a tile at once (2N accumulators, one broadcast a row and activation); more, a
// tile's halves one after the other (N accumulators, not 2N: 16 registers) - 2 activations 1.55 -> 1.34 ms an
// expert-token on one Zen 3 core, 3: 1.18 -> 1.11
template <int N, int... I>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_fma_n(__m256 f, const float* const (&xk)[N], int r, __m256 (&a)[N],
                                 std::integer_sequence<int, I...>) {
    ((a[I] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(f, _mm256_broadcast_ss(xk[I] + r), a[I])), ...);
}
template <int K, int N, int H, int R>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_rows_n(const __m256i (&C)[K], const float* const (&xk)[N], __m256 (&a)[N],
                                  const Avx2Consts& k) {
    if constexpr (R < 16) {
        avx2_fma_n<N>(avx2_sums<K, R, H>(C, k), xk, R, a, std::make_integer_sequence<int, N>{});
        avx2_rows_n<K, N, H, R + 1>(C, xk, a, k);
    }
}
template <int N, int... I>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_fma_n2(__m256 f0, __m256 f1, const float* const (&xk)[N], int r, __m256 (&lo)[N],
                                  __m256 (&hi)[N], std::integer_sequence<int, I...>) {
    ((lo[I] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(f0, _mm256_broadcast_ss(xk[I] + r), lo[I]),
      hi[I] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(f1, _mm256_broadcast_ss(xk[I] + r), hi[I])),
     ...);
}
template <int K, int N, int R>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_rows_n2(const __m256i (&C)[K], const float* const (&xk)[N], __m256 (&lo)[N],
                                   __m256 (&hi)[N], const Avx2Consts& k) {
    if constexpr (R < 16) {
        avx2_fma_n2<N>(avx2_sums<K, R, 0>(C, k), avx2_sums<K, R, 1>(C, k), xk, R, lo, hi,
                       std::make_integer_sequence<int, N>{});
        avx2_rows_n2<K, N, R + 1>(C, xk, lo, hi, k);
    }
}
template <int K, int N>
EXL3_AVX2 void band_avx2_n(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int tc0, int ks0, int ks1,
                           float* const* out /* N x 128 */) {
    static_assert(kAvx2Tab<K>.ok, "EXL3 tile layout: a half row's words must share a residue class and a shift");
    constexpr int W = 8 * K;
    const int ld = m.n / 16;
    const size_t row_words = (size_t) ld * W;
    const Avx2Consts k = avx2_consts();
    __m256 acc[8][2][N];
    for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t)
        for (int h = 0; h < 2; ++h)
            for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) acc[t][h][i] = _mm256_setzero_ps();
    const uint32_t* row = m.trellis + (size_t) ks0 * row_words + (size_t) tc0 * W;
    for (int ks = ks0; ks < ks1; ++ks, row += row_words) {
        const char* pf = (const char*) (row + 4 * row_words);
        for (int l = 0; l < 8 * W * 4; l += 64) _mm_prefetch(pf + l, _MM_HINT_T0);
        const float* xk[N];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) xk[i] = xh[i] + ks * 16;
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t) {
            __m256i C[K];
            avx2_classes<K>(row + t * W, C);
            if constexpr (N <= 3) {
                __m256 lo[N], hi[N];
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) lo[i] = acc[t][0][i], hi[i] = acc[t][1][i];
                avx2_rows_n2<K, N, 0>(C, xk, lo, hi, k);
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) acc[t][0][i] = lo[i], acc[t][1][i] = hi[i];
            } else {
                __m256 a[N];
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) a[i] = acc[t][0][i];
                avx2_rows_n<K, N, 0, 0>(C, xk, a, k);
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) acc[t][0][i] = a[i], a[i] = acc[t][1][i];
                avx2_rows_n<K, N, 1, 0>(C, xk, a, k);
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) acc[t][1][i] = a[i];
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i)
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t) {
            _mm256_storeu_ps(out[i] + t * 16, acc[t][0][i]);
            _mm256_storeu_ps(out[i] + t * 16 + 8, acc[t][1][i]);
        }
}

// #188's split-K piece (rows_avx512_n) on the AVX2 tier: slices [ks0, ks1) of EVERY column for N activations, the
// tile rows in memory order, a tile's sums in acc between slices; each row's decode and FMAs are band_avx2's, so acc[i]
// is the band kernel's for its columns and xh[i] alone, bit for bit (and rows_avx512_n's)
template <int K, int N>
EXL3_AVX2 void rows_avx2_n(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int ks0, int ks1, int t0, int t1,
                           float* const* acc) {
    static_assert(kAvx2Tab<K>.ok, "EXL3 tile layout: a half row's words must share a residue class and a shift");
    constexpr int W = 8 * K;
    const int ld = m.n / 16;
    const size_t row_words = (size_t) ld * W;
    const Avx2Consts k = avx2_consts();
    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i)
        for (int c = 16 * t0; c < 16 * t1; c += 8) _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[i] + c, _mm256_setzero_ps());
    const int span = t1 - t0;
    const uint32_t* row = m.trellis + (size_t) ks0 * row_words;
    for (int ks = ks0; ks < ks1; ++ks, row += row_words) {
        const float* xk[N];
        for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) xk[i] = xh[i] + ks * 16;
        for (int t = t0; t < t1; ++t) {
            const uint32_t* w = row + (size_t) t * W;
            const uint32_t* pf = t + 16 < t1 || span == ld ? w + 16 * W : row + row_words + (size_t) (t + 16 - span) * W;
            for (int l = 0; l < W * 4; l += 64) _mm_prefetch((const char*) pf + l, _MM_HINT_T0);
            __m256i C[K];
            avx2_classes<K>(w, C);
            if constexpr (N == 1) {
                __m256 lo = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[0] + t * 16), hi = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[0] + t * 16 + 8);
                avx2_rows<K, 0>(C, xk[0], lo, hi, k);
                _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[0] + t * 16, lo);
                _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[0] + t * 16 + 8, hi);
            } else if constexpr (N <= 3) {
                __m256 lo[N], hi[N];
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i)
                    lo[i] = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16), hi[i] = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16 + 8);
                avx2_rows_n2<K, N, 0>(C, xk, lo, hi, k);
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i)
                    _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16, lo[i]), _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16 + 8, hi[i]);
            } else {
                __m256 a[N];
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) a[i] = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16);
                avx2_rows_n<K, N, 0, 0>(C, xk, a, k);
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16, a[i]), a[i] = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16 + 8);
                avx2_rows_n<K, N, 1, 0>(C, xk, a, k);
                for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[i] + t * 16 + 8, a[i]);
            }
        }
    }
}

// #188's band GEMM (decode_chunk + gemm_tile) on the AVX2 tier: a chunk of a band's byte sums decoded once into F32,
// then TB activations x 32 columns a pass, the sums in registers (12 of the 16 with TB 3) - each column's FMAs in the
// band kernel's order (k ascending; x w + a as band_avx2's s x + a), so the same bits as gemm_tile on AVX-512
template <int K, int R>
EXL3_AVX2_INLINE void avx2_decode_rows(const __m256i (&C)[K], float* wr, int t, const Avx2Consts& k) {
    if constexpr (R < 16) {
        _mm256_store_ps(wr + R * 128 + t * 16, avx2_sums<K, R, 0>(C, k));
        _mm256_store_ps(wr + R * 128 + t * 16 + 8, avx2_sums<K, R, 1>(C, k));
        avx2_decode_rows<K, R + 1>(C, wr, t, k);
    }
}
template <int K>
EXL3_AVX2 void decode_chunk_avx2(const Exl3Part& m, int tc0, int ks0, int ks1, float* wc /* (ks1 - ks0) 16 x 128 */) {
    constexpr int W = 8 * K;
    const size_t row_words = (size_t) (m.n / 16) * W;
    const Avx2Consts k = avx2_consts();
    const uint32_t* row = m.trellis + (size_t) ks0 * row_words + (size_t) tc0 * W;
    for (int ks = ks0; ks < ks1; ++ks, row += row_words) {
        const char* pf = (const char*) (row + 4 * row_words);
        for (int l = 0; l < 8 * W * 4; l += 64) _mm_prefetch(pf + l, _MM_HINT_T0);
        float* wr = wc + (size_t) (ks - ks0) * 16 * 128;
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; ++t) {
            __m256i C[K];
            avx2_classes<K>(row + t * W, C);
            avx2_decode_rows<K, 0>(C, wr, t, k);
        }
    }
}
// acc[t][0..128) += sum_{k < kr} x[t][k] wc[k][..] for TB activations
template <int TB>
EXL3_AVX2 void gemm_tile_avx2(const float* wc, int kr, const float* const* x, float* const* acc) {
    for (int cb = 0; cb < 128; cb += 32) {
        __m256 a[TB][4];
        for (int t = 0; t < TB; ++t)
            for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) a[t][j] = _mm256_loadu_ps(acc[t] + cb + j * 8);
        const float* w = wc + cb;
        for (int q = 0; q < kr; ++q, w += 128) {
            const __m256 w0 = _mm256_load_ps(w), w1 = _mm256_load_ps(w + 8), w2 = _mm256_load_ps(w + 16),
                         w3 = _mm256_load_ps(w + 24);
            for (int t = 0; t < TB; ++t) {
                const __m256 xv = _mm256_broadcast_ss(x[t] + q);
                a[t][0] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(xv, w0, a[t][0]);
                a[t][1] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(xv, w1, a[t][1]);
                a[t][2] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(xv, w2, a[t][2]);
                a[t][3] = _mm256_fmadd_ps(xv, w3, a[t][3]);
            }
        }
        for (int t = 0; t < TB; ++t)
            for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) _mm256_storeu_ps(acc[t] + cb + j * 8, a[t][j]);
    }
}
template <int K>
EXL3_AVX2 void band_gemm_avx2(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int tc0, int nb, float* const* acc,
                              float* wc) {
    constexpr int KS = kGemmK / 16;
    constexpr int TB = 3;   // 12 sums + 4 weights of the 16 registers
    for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) std::memset(acc[t], 0, (size_t) nb * 128 * sizeof(float));
    std::vector<float*> ab((size_t) n);
    for (int ks0 = 0; ks0 < m.k / 16; ks0 += KS) {
        const int ks1 = std::min(m.k / 16, ks0 + KS), kr = (ks1 - ks0) * 16;
        for (int bb = 0; bb < nb; ++bb) {
            decode_chunk_avx2<K>(m, tc0 + 8 * bb, ks0, ks1, wc);
            for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) ab[(size_t) t] = acc[t] + bb * 128;
            float* const* ap = ab.data();
            int t = 0;
            for (; t + TB <= n; t += TB) {
                const float* xp[TB];
                for (int i = 0; i < TB; ++i) xp[i] = xh[t + i] + ks0 * 16;
                gemm_tile_avx2<TB>(wc, kr, xp, ap + t);
            }
            if (t < n) {
                const float* xp[TB];
                for (int i = 0; i < n - t; ++i) xp[i] = xh[t + i] + ks0 * 16;
                if (n - t == 1) gemm_tile_avx2<1>(wc, kr, xp, ap + t);
                else gemm_tile_avx2<2>(wc, kr, xp, ap + t);
            }
        }
    }
}

// had128 on 16 registers (exllamav3's hadamard_128_avx2): every butterfly takes the scalar loop's operands (a lane's
// partner by a permute; the lower lane a + b, the upper t - r = a - b), so the result is had128's bit for bit
EXL3_AVX2 void had128_avx2(float* v) {
    __m256 r[16];
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) r[i] = _mm256_loadu_ps(v + 8 * i);
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
        __m256 t = _mm256_permute_ps(r[i], 0b10110001);   // h = 1
        r[i] = _mm256_blend_ps(_mm256_add_ps(r[i], t), _mm256_sub_ps(t, r[i]), 0b10101010);
        t = _mm256_permute_ps(r[i], 0b01001110);          // h = 2
        r[i] = _mm256_blend_ps(_mm256_add_ps(r[i], t), _mm256_sub_ps(t, r[i]), 0b11001100);
        t = _mm256_permute2f128_ps(r[i], r[i], 0x01);     // h = 4
        r[i] = _mm256_blend_ps(_mm256_add_ps(r[i], t), _mm256_sub_ps(t, r[i]), 0b11110000);
    }
    for (int h = 1; h < 16; h <<= 1)   // h = 8 .. 64: whole registers
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; i += 2 * h)
            for (int j = i; j < i + h; ++j) {
                const __m256 a = r[j], b = r[j + h];
                r[j] = _mm256_add_ps(a, b);
                r[j + h] = _mm256_sub_ps(a, b);
            }
    const __m256 s = _mm256_set1_ps(0.088388347648f);
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) _mm256_storeu_ps(v + 8 * i, _mm256_mul_ps(r[i], s));
}

// prepare_block_avx512 / band_out_avx512 on the AVX2 tier, the same operations in the same order: the FP16 scales by
// vcvtph2ps (exact), the block's sum in the same eight double lanes (lanes 0-7 of the 16-float steps' first half, 8-15
// of the second, added) and reduced as GCC's _mm512_reduce_add_pd does (upper four + lower four, then the two pairs,
// then the last two), band_out's FMA - the same bits as the AVX-512 tier
EXL3_AVX2 float prepare_block_avx2(const uint16_t* suh, const float* x, float* xh) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 8) {
        const __m256 sc = _mm256_cvtph_ps(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i*) (suh + i)));
        _mm256_storeu_ps(xh + i, _mm256_mul_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(x + i), sc));
    }
    had128_avx2(xh);
    __m256d s0a = _mm256_setzero_pd(), s0b = _mm256_setzero_pd(), s1a = _mm256_setzero_pd(), s1b = _mm256_setzero_pd();
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 16) {
        s0a = _mm256_add_pd(s0a, _mm256_cvtps_pd(_mm_loadu_ps(xh + i)));
        s0b = _mm256_add_pd(s0b, _mm256_cvtps_pd(_mm_loadu_ps(xh + i + 4)));
        s1a = _mm256_add_pd(s1a, _mm256_cvtps_pd(_mm_loadu_ps(xh + i + 8)));
        s1b = _mm256_add_pd(s1b, _mm256_cvtps_pd(_mm_loadu_ps(xh + i + 12)));
    }
    const __m256d lo = _mm256_add_pd(s0a, s1a), hi = _mm256_add_pd(s0b, s1b);   // the 8 lanes of s0 + s1
    const __m256d t3 = _mm256_add_pd(hi, lo);
    const __m128d t6 = _mm_add_pd(_mm256_extractf128_pd(t3, 1), _mm256_castpd256_pd128(t3));
    return (float) (_mm_cvtsd_f64(t6) + _mm_cvtsd_f64(_mm_unpackhi_pd(t6, t6)));
}
EXL3_AVX2 void band_out_avx2(const float* acc, float ki, float kz, const uint16_t* svh, float* y) {
    const __m256 vk = _mm256_set1_ps(ki), vz = _mm256_set1_ps(kz);
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 8) _mm256_storeu_ps(y + i, _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(acc + i), vk, vz));
    had128_avx2(y);
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; i += 8) {
        const __m256 sc = _mm256_cvtph_ps(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i*) (svh + i)));
        _mm256_storeu_ps(y + i, _mm256_mul_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(y + i), sc));
    }
}

// AVX-512 F and BW with FMA, the OS saving the state (STRATA_FORCE_AVX2 is the tier choice's, below)
bool cpu_avx512_exl3() {
    unsigned r[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
    auto cpuid = [&](unsigned leaf, unsigned sub) {
#if defined(_MSC_VER)
        int x[4];
        __cpuidex(x, (int) leaf, (int) sub);
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) r[i] = (unsigned) x[i];
#else
        __cpuid_count(leaf, sub, r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3]);
#endif
    };
    cpuid(0, 0);
    if (r[0] < 7) return false;
    cpuid(1, 0);
    if (!((r[2] >> 27) & 1u) || !((r[2] >> 12) & 1u)) return false;   // OSXSAVE, FMA
#if defined(_MSC_VER)
    const unsigned long long xcr0 = _xgetbv(0);
#else
    unsigned lo = 0, hi = 0;
    __asm__ volatile("xgetbv" : "=a"(lo), "=d"(hi) : "c"(0));
    const unsigned long long xcr0 = ((unsigned long long) hi << 32) | lo;
#endif
    if ((xcr0 & 0xE6) != 0xE6) return false;   // the OS saves the AVX-512 state
    cpuid(7, 0);
    return ((r[1] >> 16) & 1u) && ((r[1] >> 30) & 1u);   // AVX-512F, AVX-512BW
}
// F16C (the AVX2 tier's FP16 scale conversions; every AVX2 CPU has it, asked anyway)
bool cpu_f16c() {
    unsigned r[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
#if defined(_MSC_VER)
    int x[4];
    __cpuidex(x, 1, 0);
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) r[i] = (unsigned) x[i];
#else
    __cpuid_count(1, 0, r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3]);
#endif
    return ((r[2] >> 29) & 1u) != 0;
}
#endif

// the tiers this CPU runs (bit t: tier t - 0 scalar, 1 AVX2 + FMA + F16C, 2 AVX-512 F/BW), and the one the lane takes:
// the widest, but AVX2 on an AVX-512 CPU with STRATA_FORCE_AVX2=1 (to compare the two vector tiers)
int tier_mask() {
    static const int mask = [] {
        int t = 1;
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
        if (cpu_avx2_ok() && cpu_f16c()) t |= 2;
        if (cpu_avx512_exl3()) t |= 4;
#endif
        return t;
    }();
    return mask;
}
int detect_tier() {
    const int t = tier_mask();
    const char* f = std::getenv("STRATA_FORCE_AVX2");
    if ((t & 4) && !(f != nullptr && f[0] == '1')) return 2;
    return (t & 2) ? 1 : 0;
}

template <int K>
void band_on(int tier, const Exl3Part& m, const float* xh, int tc0, int ks0, int ks1, float* acc) {
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
    if (tier == 2) {
        band_avx512<K>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc);
        return;
    }
    if (tier == 1) {
        band_avx2<K>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc);
        return;
    }
#endif
    band_scalar<K>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc);
}

// n activations (1..kExl3CpuMaxN) on one band
template <int K>
void band_on_n(int tier, const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int tc0, int ks0, int ks1,
               float* const* acc) {
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
    if (tier == 2 && n > 1) {
        switch (n) {
            case 2: band_avx512_n<K, 2>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 3: band_avx512_n<K, 3>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 4: band_avx512_n<K, 4>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 5: band_avx512_n<K, 5>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 6: band_avx512_n<K, 6>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 7: band_avx512_n<K, 7>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            default: band_avx512_n<K, 8>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
        }
    }
    if (tier == 1 && n > 1) {
        switch (n) {
            case 2: band_avx2_n<K, 2>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 3: band_avx2_n<K, 3>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 4: band_avx2_n<K, 4>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 5: band_avx2_n<K, 5>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 6: band_avx2_n<K, 6>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            case 7: band_avx2_n<K, 7>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
            default: band_avx2_n<K, 8>(m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); return;
        }
    }
#endif
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) band_on<K>(tier, m, xh[i], tc0, ks0, ks1, acc[i]);
}

// a split-K piece's tile columns [t0, t1) for n activations (1..kExl3CpuMaxN); the scalar loop: each band's
// band_scalar (t0, t1 multiples of 8 there)
template <int K>
void rows_on_n(int tier, const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int ks0, int ks1, int t0, int t1,
               float* const* acc) {
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
    if (tier == 2) {
        switch (n) {
            case 1: rows_avx512_n<K, 1>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 2: rows_avx512_n<K, 2>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 3: rows_avx512_n<K, 3>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 4: rows_avx512_n<K, 4>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 5: rows_avx512_n<K, 5>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 6: rows_avx512_n<K, 6>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 7: rows_avx512_n<K, 7>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            default: rows_avx512_n<K, 8>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
        }
    }
    if (tier == 1) {
        switch (n) {
            case 1: rows_avx2_n<K, 1>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 2: rows_avx2_n<K, 2>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 3: rows_avx2_n<K, 3>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 4: rows_avx2_n<K, 4>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 5: rows_avx2_n<K, 5>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 6: rows_avx2_n<K, 6>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            case 7: rows_avx2_n<K, 7>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
            default: rows_avx2_n<K, 8>(m, xh, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc); return;
        }
    }
#endif
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for (int c0 = 16 * t0; c0 < 16 * t1; c0 += 128) band_scalar<K>(m, xh[i], c0 / 16, ks0, ks1, acc[i] + c0);
}

void band_acc_tier(int tier, const Exl3Part& m, const float* xh, int c0, int ks0, int ks1, float* acc) {
    const int tc0 = c0 / 16;
    switch (m.K) {
        case 1: band_on<1>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 2: band_on<2>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 3: band_on<3>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 4: band_on<4>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 5: band_on<5>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 6: band_on<6>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 7: band_on<7>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        case 8: band_on<8>(tier, m, xh, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc); break;
        default:
            for (int i = 0; i < 128; ++i) acc[i] = 0.0f;
    }
}

void band_acc_n_tier(int tier, const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int c0, int ks0, int ks1,
                     float* const* acc) {
    const int tc0 = c0 / 16;
    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < n; i0 += kExl3CpuMaxN) {
        const int c = std::min(kExl3CpuMaxN, n - i0);
        switch (m.K) {
            case 1: band_on_n<1>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 2: band_on_n<2>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 3: band_on_n<3>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 4: band_on_n<4>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 5: band_on_n<5>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 6: band_on_n<6>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 7: band_on_n<7>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            case 8: band_on_n<8>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, tc0, ks0, ks1, acc + i0); break;
            default:
                for (int i = 0; i < c; ++i)
                    for (int j = 0; j < 128; ++j) acc[i0 + i][j] = 0.0f;
        }
    }
}

}  // namespace

int exl3_cpu_tier() {
    static const int tier = detect_tier();
    return tier;
}

bool exl3_cpu_vector() { return exl3_cpu_tier() > 0; }

float exl3_cpu_prepare_block(const uint16_t* suh, const float* x, float* xh) {
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
    if (exl3_cpu_tier() == 2) return prepare_block_avx512(suh, x, xh);
    if (exl3_cpu_tier() == 1) return prepare_block_avx2(suh, x, xh);
#endif
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; ++i) xh[i] = x[i] * f32_from_f16(suh[i]);
    had128(xh);
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; ++i) sum += xh[i];
    return (float) sum;
}

float exl3_cpu_prepare(const Exl3Part& m, const float* x, float* xh) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int b = 0; b < m.k; b += 128) sum += exl3_cpu_prepare_block(m.suh + b, x + b, xh + b);
    return (float) sum;
}

void exl3_cpu_band_acc(const Exl3Part& m, const float* xh, int c0, int ks0, int ks1, float* acc) {
    band_acc_tier(exl3_cpu_tier(), m, xh, c0, ks0, ks1, acc);
}

void exl3_cpu_band_acc_n(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int c0, int ks0, int ks1,
                         float* const* acc) {
    band_acc_n_tier(exl3_cpu_tier(), m, xh, n, c0, ks0, ks1, acc);
}

bool exl3_cpu_band_acc_on(int tier, const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int c0, int ks0, int ks1,
                          float* const* acc) {
    if (tier < 0 || tier > 2 || ((tier_mask() >> tier) & 1) == 0 || n < 1) return false;
    if (n == 1) band_acc_tier(tier, m, xh[0], c0, ks0, ks1, acc[0]);
    else band_acc_n_tier(tier, m, xh, n, c0, ks0, ks1, acc);
    return true;
}

void exl3_cpu_rows_acc_cols_n(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int ks0, int ks1, int c0, int c1,
                              float* const* acc) {
    const int tier = exl3_cpu_tier();
    const int t0 = c0 / 16, t1 = c1 / 16;
    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < n; i0 += kExl3CpuMaxN) {
        const int c = std::min(kExl3CpuMaxN, n - i0);
        switch (m.K) {
            case 1: rows_on_n<1>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 2: rows_on_n<2>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 3: rows_on_n<3>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 4: rows_on_n<4>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 5: rows_on_n<5>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 6: rows_on_n<6>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 7: rows_on_n<7>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            case 8: rows_on_n<8>(tier, m, xh + i0, c, ks0, ks1, t0, t1, acc + i0); break;
            default:
                for (int i = 0; i < c; ++i)
                    for (int j = c0; j < c1; ++j) acc[i0 + i][j] = 0.0f;
        }
    }
}

void exl3_cpu_rows_acc_n(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int ks0, int ks1, float* const* acc) {
    exl3_cpu_rows_acc_cols_n(m, xh, n, ks0, ks1, 0, m.n, acc);
}

size_t exl3_cpu_gemm_scratch() { return (size_t) kGemmK * 128; }

void exl3_cpu_band_gemm(const Exl3Part& m, const float* const* xh, int n, int c0, int nb, float* const* acc,
                        float* wc) {
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
    if (exl3_cpu_tier() == 2) {
        switch (m.K) {
            case 1: band_gemm_avx512<1>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 2: band_gemm_avx512<2>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 3: band_gemm_avx512<3>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 4: band_gemm_avx512<4>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 5: band_gemm_avx512<5>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 6: band_gemm_avx512<6>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 7: band_gemm_avx512<7>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 8: band_gemm_avx512<8>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            default: break;
        }
    }
    if (exl3_cpu_tier() == 1) {
        switch (m.K) {
            case 1: band_gemm_avx2<1>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 2: band_gemm_avx2<2>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 3: band_gemm_avx2<3>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 4: band_gemm_avx2<4>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 5: band_gemm_avx2<5>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 6: band_gemm_avx2<6>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 7: band_gemm_avx2<7>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            case 8: band_gemm_avx2<8>(m, xh, n, c0 / 16, nb, acc, wc); return;
            default: break;
        }
    }
#endif
    (void) wc;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for (int b = 0; b < nb; ++b) exl3_cpu_band_acc(m, xh[i], c0 + 128 * b, 0, m.k / 16, acc[i] + 128 * b);
}

void exl3_cpu_rows_acc(const Exl3Part& m, const float* xh, int ks0, int ks1, float* acc) {
    exl3_cpu_rows_acc_n(m, &xh, 1, ks0, ks1, &acc);
}

void exl3_cpu_band_out(const Exl3Part& m, const float* acc, float xsum, int c0, float* y) {
    const float ki = k_inv(), kz = k_zero() * xsum;
#if defined(EXL3_X86)
    if (exl3_cpu_tier() == 2) {
        band_out_avx512(acc, ki, kz, m.svh + c0, y);
        return;
    }
    if (exl3_cpu_tier() == 1) {
        band_out_avx2(acc, ki, kz, m.svh + c0, y);
        return;
    }
#endif
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; ++i) y[i] = acc[i] * ki + kz;
    had128(y);
    for (int i = 0; i < 128; ++i) y[i] *= f32_from_f16(m.svh[c0 + i]);
}

void exl3_cpu_band(const Exl3Part& m, const float* xh, float xsum, int c0, float* y) {
    float acc[128];
    exl3_cpu_band_acc(m, xh, c0, 0, m.k / 16, acc);
    exl3_cpu_band_out(m, acc, xsum, c0, y);
}

}  // namespace strata::dsv41k::cpu


## src/kernels/b6_mmvq_bench.cpp

// src/kernels/b6_mmvq_bench.cpp - B6: what a verify row costs in the dense projections, per kernel, per card.
//
//     build/b6_mmvq_bench [reps] [device, -1 = all] [B rows mode: 1 = 2 rows, or 2 / 4 / 8]
//
// The decode's dense projections at the model's own shapes and formats (qwen3.8-flash-next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS:
// GDN qkv / gate / out, QSA q / out, shared expert, the head; the BF16 router), called with ncols = 1..5 and 8 as a
// verify window of that many rows calls them.  Per call: CUDA events around each launch, every launch queued back to
// back (no host gap inside a measurement), the median of `reps` (default 500) after a warm-up.  The weights rotate
// over enough copies to exceed the L2, as the decode reads each layer's weights cold.  Synthetic bytes with sane
// block scales (as mmvq_multi_parity): the time does not depend on the values.
//
// Two layouts side by side: the default exact layout (A) and STRATA_B6_MMVQ_ROWS (B, native_mmvq_set_b6_rows).  For
// every case and ncols: B's output against A's, bit for bit (memcmp), and both against ncols single-column calls.
// Exit code 1 if any comparison differs.  GPU time only: immune to the host and to any generated text.
#include "strata/kernels/bf16_gemv.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/iq_kernels.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/native_mmvq.hpp"

#include <cuda_runtime.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <random>
#include <vector>

namespace K = strata::kernels;

namespace {

struct Case {
    const char* name;
    int type;          // GGML type id; 30 = BF16 (bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf_multi)
    int n_in, n_out;
    int block_elems, block_bytes;
    int scale_at[2];   // byte offsets of the fp16 scales in a block; -1 = none
};

const Case CASES[] = {
    {"gdn qkv Q6_K", 14, 2560, 10240, 256, 210, {208, -1}},
    {"gdn qkv Q4_K", 12, 2560, 10240, 256, 144, {0, 2}},
    {"gdn qkv Q5_K", 13, 2560, 10240, 256, 176, {0, 2}},
    {"gdn qkv IQ4_XS", 23, 2560, 10240, 256, 136, {0, -1}},
    {"gdn gate Q6_K", 14, 2560, 6144, 256, 210, {208, -1}},
    {"gdn out Q6_K", 14, 6144, 2560, 256, 210, {208, -1}},
    {"gdn out IQ4_XS", 23, 6144, 2560, 256, 136, {0, -1}},
    {"gdn out Q4_K", 12, 6144, 2560, 256, 144, {0, 2}},
    {"qsa q IQ4_XS", 23, 2560, 12288, 256, 136, {0, -1}},
    {"qsa q Q6_K", 14, 2560, 12288, 256, 210, {208, -1}},
    {"shexp up IQ3_S", 21, 2560, 640, 256, 110, {0, -1}},
    {"shexp gate Q4_K", 12, 2560, 640, 256, 144, {0, 2}},
    {"shexp down IQ4_NL", 20, 640, 2560, 32, 18, {0, -1}},
    {"router BF16", 30, 2560, 512, 1, 2, {-1, -1}},
    {"head Q5_K", 13, 2560, 248320, 256, 176, {0, 2}},
};
const int WIDTHS[] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8};

bool ck(cudaError_t e, const char* what) {
    if (e == cudaSuccess) return true;
    std::printf("CUDA: %s: %s\n", what, cudaGetErrorString(e));
    return false;
}

uint16_t sane_half(std::mt19937& rng) {
    const uint32_t r = rng();
    return (uint16_t) (((r >> 31) << 15) | ((5u + (r >> 10) % 5u) << 10) | (r & 0x3ffu));
}
uint16_t bf16(float x) {
    uint32_t u;
    std::memcpy(&u, &x, 4);
    return (uint16_t) ((u + 0x7fff + ((u >> 16) & 1)) >> 16);
}

struct Buf {
    std::vector<void*> w;   // weight copies
    std::size_t wbytes = 0;
    void* xq = nullptr;     // Q8_1 of 8 columns
    float* xf = nullptr;    // the float activations (BF16 path)
    float* y = nullptr;     // 8 columns of output
};

// one call of the case at `ncols` on weight copy `k` into y
void call(const Case& c, const Buf& b, int k, int ncols, float* y, cudaStream_t s) {
    if (c.type == 30)
        K::bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf_multi(b.xf, c.n_in, (const uint16_t*) b.w[(size_t) k], y, c.n_out, c.n_in, c.n_out, ncols, s);
    else
        K::native_mmvq(c.type, b.w[(size_t) k], b.xq, y, c.n_in, c.n_out, ncols, s);
}
// column j alone (ncols = 1), into y + j * n_out
void call_col(const Case& c, const Buf& b, int j, float* y, cudaStream_t s) {
    if (c.type == 30)
        K::bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf_multi(b.xf + (size_t) j * c.n_in, c.n_in, (const uint16_t*) b.w[0],
                                     y + (size_t) j * c.n_out, c.n_out, c.n_in, c.n_out, 1, s);
    else
        K::native_mmvq(c.type, b.w[0], (const uint8_t*) b.xq + K::native_q8_1_bytes(c.n_in, 1) * (size_t) j,
                       y + (size_t) j * c.n_out, c.n_in, c.n_out, 1, s);
}

double median_ms(const Case& c, const Buf& b, int ncols, int reps, cudaStream_t s, std::vector<cudaEvent_t>& ev) {
    const int nk = (int) b.w.size();
    for (int r = 0; r < 30; ++r) call(c, b, r % nk, ncols, b.y, s);   // warm-up
    for (int r = 0; r < reps; ++r) {
        cudaEventRecord(ev[(size_t) 2 * r], s);
        call(c, b, r % nk, ncols, b.y, s);
        cudaEventRecord(ev[(size_t) 2 * r + 1], s);
    }
    cudaStreamSynchronize(s);
    std::vector<float> t((size_t) reps);
    for (int r = 0; r < reps; ++r) cudaEventElapsedTime(&t[(size_t) r], ev[(size_t) 2 * r], ev[(size_t) 2 * r + 1]);
    std::nth_element(t.begin(), t.begin() + reps / 2, t.end());
    return t[(size_t) reps / 2];
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    setvbuf(stdout, nullptr, _IONBF, 0);
    const int reps = argc > 1 ? std::max(50, std::atoi(argv[1])) : 500;
    int n_dev = 0;
    if (!ck(cudaGetDeviceCount(&n_dev), "device count")) return 1;
    const int only = argc > 2 ? std::atoi(argv[2]) : -1;
    const int bmode = argc > 3 ? std::atoi(argv[3]) : 1;
    long long bad = 0;
    for (int dev = 0; dev < n_dev; ++dev) {
        if (only >= 0 && dev != only) continue;
        cudaSetDevice(dev);
        cudaDeviceProp pr{};
        cudaGetDeviceProperties(&pr, dev);
        std::printf("\n=== device %d: %s (sm_%d%d, L2 %d KB), %d reps, median ms per call, B = rows mode %d ===\n", dev, pr.name,
                    pr.major, pr.minor, pr.l2CacheSize / 1024, reps, bmode);
        std::printf("%-18s %4s %9s %9s %8s %8s  %s\n", "case", "cols", "A ms", "B ms", "A +col", "B +col",
                    "bitwise B=A, A=1col, B=1col");
        cudaStream_t s;
        if (!ck(cudaStreamCreate(&s), "stream")) return 1;
        std::vector<cudaEvent_t> ev((size_t) 2 * reps);
        for (auto& e : ev) cudaEventCreate(&e);
        for (const Case& c : CASES) {
            if (c.type != 30 && !K::native_mmvq_supported(c.type)) {
                std::printf("%-18s unsupported type %d\n", c.name, c.type);
                continue;
            }
            std::mt19937 rng(77u + (unsigned) c.type * 131u + (unsigned) c.n_out);
            Buf b;
            b.wbytes = c.type == 30 ? (size_t) c.n_in * c.n_out * 2 : K::native_mmvq_weight_bytes(c.type, c.n_in, c.n_out);
            std::vector<uint8_t> w(b.wbytes);
            if (c.type == 30) {
                std::normal_distribution<float> nd(0.f, 0.05f);
                auto* p = (uint16_t*) w.data();
                for (size_t i = 0; i < b.wbytes / 2; ++i) p[i] = bf16(nd(rng));
            } else {
                for (auto& x : w) x = (uint8_t) (rng() & 0xff);
                const size_t nb = (size_t) c.n_out * (size_t) (c.n_in / c.block_elems);
                for (size_t k = 0; k < nb; ++k)
                    for (int at : c.scale_at)
                        if (at >= 0) {
                            const uint16_t h = sane_half(rng);
                            std::memcpy(&w[k * (size_t) c.block_bytes + (size_t) at], &h, 2);
                        }
            }
            const size_t copies = std::max<size_t>(1, std::min<size_t>(8, (96u << 20) / b.wbytes + 1));
            bool ok = true;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < copies && ok; ++k) {
                void* d = nullptr;
                ok = ck(cudaMalloc(&d, b.wbytes), "malloc w") && ck(cudaMemcpy(d, w.data(), b.wbytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice), "copy w");
                b.w.push_back(d);
            }
            std::vector<float> x((size_t) 8 * c.n_in);
            std::normal_distribution<float> nx(0.f, 1.f);
            for (auto& v : x) v = nx(rng);
            const size_t ybytes = (size_t) 8 * c.n_out * 4;
            ok = ok && ck(cudaMalloc(&b.xf, x.size() * 4), "malloc x") &&
                 ck(cudaMemcpy(b.xf, x.data(), x.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice), "copy x") &&
                 ck(cudaMalloc(&b.y, ybytes), "malloc y");
            if (ok && c.type != 30) {
                ok = ck(cudaMalloc(&b.xq, K::native_q8_1_bytes(c.n_in, 8)), "malloc xq");
                if (ok) K::quantize_q8_1_rows(b.xf, 8, c.n_in, b.xq, s);
            }
            float *ya = nullptr, *yb = nullptr, *y1 = nullptr;
            ok = ok && ck(cudaMalloc(&ya, ybytes), "ya") && ck(cudaMalloc(&yb, ybytes), "yb") && ck(cudaMalloc(&y1, ybytes), "y1");
            if (!ok) return 1;
            double a1 = 0, b1 = 0;
            for (int T : WIDTHS) {
                std::vector<uint32_t> ha((size_t) T * c.n_out), hb(ha.size()), h1(ha.size());
                K::native_mmvq_set_b6_rows(0);
                const double ta = median_ms(c, b, T, reps, s, ev);
                call(c, b, 0, T, ya, s);
                for (int j = 0; j < T; ++j) call_col(c, b, j, y1, s);
                K::native_mmvq_set_b6_rows(bmode);
                const double tb = median_ms(c, b, T, reps, s, ev);
                call(c, b, 0, T, yb, s);
                K::native_mmvq_set_b6_rows(0);
                if (!ck(cudaStreamSynchronize(s), "run")) return 1;
                cudaMemcpy(ha.data(), ya, ha.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
                cudaMemcpy(hb.data(), yb, hb.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
                cudaMemcpy(h1.data(), y1, h1.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
                const bool ba = std::memcmp(ha.data(), hb.data(), ha.size() * 4) == 0;
                const bool a_1 = std::memcmp(ha.data(), h1.data(), ha.size() * 4) == 0;
                const bool b_1 = std::memcmp(hb.data(), h1.data(), hb.size() * 4) == 0;
                long long nonfinite = 0;
                for (uint32_t u : ha) { float f; std::memcpy(&f, &u, 4); if (!std::isfinite(f)) ++nonfinite; }
                if (!ba || !b_1 || nonfinite) ++bad;
                if (T == 1) { a1 = ta; b1 = tb; }
                std::printf("%-18s %4d %9.4f %9.4f %8.4f %8.4f  %s %s %s%s\n", c.name, T, ta, tb,
                            T > 1 ? (ta - a1) / (T - 1) : 0.0, T > 1 ? (tb - b1) / (T - 1) : 0.0, ba ? "ok" : "DIFF",
                            a_1 ? "ok" : "diff", b_1 ? "ok" : "DIFF", nonfinite ? " NONFINITE" : "");
            }
            for (void* d : b.w) cudaFree(d);
            cudaFree(b.xq); cudaFree(b.xf); cudaFree(b.y); cudaFree(ya); cudaFree(yb); cudaFree(y1);
        }
        for (auto& e : ev) cudaEventDestroy(e);
        cudaStreamDestroy(s);
    }
    std::printf("\nb6_mmvq_bench: %s (%lld case/width comparisons failed)\n", bad ? "FAILED" : "ok", bad);
    return bad ? 1 : 0;
}


## src/kernels/batch_rows_parity.cpp

// src/kernels/batch_rows_parity.cpp - the batch window's one-launch-for-all-rows kernels (#2234, STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS /
// STRATA_BATCH_GDN_GROUPS) against the per-row launches they replace, bitwise (GPU, synthetic, no model).
//
//   1. qsa_block_scores_rows   == qsa_block_scores, one call per row, each row with its OWN indexer keys;
//   2. qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows == qsa_decode_attn_batch, one call per row, each row over its OWN K/V pools
//      (int8 codes + scales, and fp16);
//   3. gdn_step_norm_groups    == gdn_step_norm_multi, one call per slot group, in the window (all outputs, the state
//      untouched) and in the 1-row commit (the state written after `keep` tokens).
// Every case compares with memcmp, not a tolerance. Usage: batch_rows_parity
#include "strata/kernels/qsa.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/qsa_decode_attn.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/verify_kernels.hpp"

#include <cuda_fp16.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <random>
#include <vector>

namespace k = strata::kernels;

namespace {
void ck(cudaError_t e, const char* w) {
    if (e != cudaSuccess) { std::fprintf(stderr, "%s: %s\n", w, cudaGetErrorString(e)); std::exit(2); }
}
template <typename T> T* up(const std::vector<T>& h) {
    T* d = nullptr;
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d, h.size() * sizeof(T) + 64), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMemcpy(d, h.data(), h.size() * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice), "upload");
    return d;
}
template <typename T> std::vector<T> down(const T* d, size_t n) {
    std::vector<T> h(n);
    ck(cudaMemcpy(h.data(), d, n * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), "download");
    return h;
}
uint16_t f2h(float f) { __half h = __float2half(f); return *reinterpret_cast<uint16_t*>(&h); }

int bad = 0;
void report(const char* what, bool same) {
    std::printf("  %-64s %s\n", what, same ? "bitwise" : "*** DIFFERS ***");
    if (!same) ++bad;
}

// ---- 1. the block scores ----
void scores_case(int rows) {
    const k::QsaShapes s = k::qsa_real_shapes();
    const int64_t max_blocks = 3000;
    std::mt19937 rng(11 + rows);
    std::normal_distribution<float> nd(0.f, 1.f);
    k::QsaScoreRows sr;
    sr.n = rows;
    std::vector<const float*> pooled(rows), dead(rows);
    std::vector<float> q((size_t) rows * s.idx_n_head * s.idx_dim);
    for (auto& x : q) x = nd(rng);
    std::vector<int32_t> steps((size_t) rows * k::kStepCount);
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
        std::vector<float> p((size_t) max_blocks * s.idx_dim), d((size_t) s.idx_dim);
        for (auto& x : p) x = nd(rng);
        for (auto& x : d) x = nd(rng);
        pooled[r] = up(p);
        dead[r] = up(d);
        sr.pooled[r] = pooled[r];
        sr.dead[r] = dead[r];
        const int64_t pos = 700 + 997 * r + (r % 3) * 5;   // different lengths, and an incomplete block at the tail
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepPos] = (int32_t) pos;
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepNKv] = (int32_t) (pos + 1);
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepNBid] = (int32_t) ((pos + 1) / s.idx_block);
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepWidth] = (int32_t) k::qsa_selection_width(pos + 1, s);
    }
    const float* d_q = up(q);
    const int32_t* d_steps = up(steps);
    float *d_rows = nullptr, *d_ref = nullptr;
    const size_t n = (size_t) rows * max_blocks;
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d_rows, n * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d_ref, n * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMemset(d_rows, 0, n * 4), "memset");
    ck(cudaMemset(d_ref, 0, n * 4), "memset");
    k::qsa_block_scores_rows(sr, d_q, d_steps, rows, max_blocks, s, d_rows, nullptr);
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r)
        k::qsa_block_scores(pooled[r], dead[r], d_q + (size_t) r * s.idx_n_head * s.idx_dim, d_steps + (size_t) r * k::kStepCount, 1,
                            max_blocks, s, d_ref + (size_t) r * max_blocks, nullptr);
    ck(cudaDeviceSynchronize(), "sync");
    const std::vector<float> a = down(d_rows, n), b = down(d_ref, n);
    char name[96];
    std::snprintf(name, sizeof name, "qsa_block_scores_rows, %d rows (own keys each)", rows);
    report(name, std::memcmp(a.data(), b.data(), n * 4) == 0);
    // the window selects with one top-k launch over all rows (row-independent) where the per-row path ran one per row
    const int64_t cap = k::qsa_selection_width(k::kTopkMaxCells, s);
    int32_t *i_rows = nullptr, *i_ref = nullptr;
    ck(cudaMalloc(&i_rows, (size_t) rows * cap * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMalloc(&i_ref, (size_t) rows * cap * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMemset(i_rows, 0, (size_t) rows * cap * 4), "memset");
    ck(cudaMemset(i_ref, 0, (size_t) rows * cap * 4), "memset");
    k::qsa_block_topk(d_ref, d_steps, rows, max_blocks, cap, s, i_rows, nullptr);
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r)
        k::qsa_block_topk(d_ref + (size_t) r * max_blocks, d_steps + (size_t) r * k::kStepCount, 1, max_blocks, cap, s,
                          i_ref + (size_t) r * cap, nullptr);
    ck(cudaDeviceSynchronize(), "sync");
    const std::vector<int32_t> ta = down(i_rows, (size_t) rows * cap), tb = down(i_ref, (size_t) rows * cap);
    bool tsame = true;
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
        const int64_t w = steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepWidth];
        tsame = tsame && std::memcmp(ta.data() + (size_t) r * cap, tb.data() + (size_t) r * cap, (size_t) w * 4) == 0;
    }
    std::snprintf(name, sizeof name, "qsa_block_topk over %d rows == one call per row", rows);
    report(name, tsame);
}

// ---- 2. the decode attention ----
void attn_case(int rows, bool int8) {
    const k::QsaShapes s = k::qsa_real_shapes();
    const int64_t HD = s.head_dim, NKV = s.n_head_kv, NH = s.n_head, PS = s.page_size;
    const int64_t ctx_max = 5000, pages = (ctx_max + PS - 1) / PS, prow = pages * NKV * PS;
    const int64_t cap = k::qsa_selection_width(ctx_max, s);
    std::mt19937 rng(23 + rows + int8);
    std::normal_distribution<float> nd(0.f, 1.f);
    std::uniform_int_distribution<int> code(-127, 127);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> sc(0.005f, 0.03f);
    k::QsaAttnPoolsRows pr;
    pr.n = rows;
    std::vector<float> q((size_t) rows * NH * HD);
    for (auto& x : q) x = nd(rng) * 2.0f;
    std::vector<int32_t> ids((size_t) rows * cap, 0), steps((size_t) rows * k::kStepCount, 0);
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
        k::QsaAttnPools& pl = pr.p[r];
        if (int8) {
            std::vector<int8_t> kq((size_t) prow * HD), vq((size_t) prow * HD);
            std::vector<uint16_t> ks((size_t) prow * (HD / 64)), vs(ks.size());
            for (auto& x : kq) x = (int8_t) code(rng);
            for (auto& x : vq) x = (int8_t) code(rng);
            for (auto& x : ks) x = f2h(sc(rng));
            for (auto& x : vs) x = f2h(sc(rng));
            pl.k_q = up(kq); pl.v_q = up(vq); pl.k_scale = up(ks); pl.v_scale = up(vs);
        } else {
            std::vector<uint16_t> kh((size_t) prow * HD), vh(kh.size());
            for (auto& x : kh) x = f2h(nd(rng) * 1.5f);
            for (auto& x : vh) x = f2h(nd(rng));
            pl.k_pool = up(kh); pl.v_pool = up(vh);
        }
        std::vector<int32_t> table(pages);
        for (int64_t i = 0; i < pages; ++i) table[i] = (int32_t) i;
        std::shuffle(table.begin(), table.end(), rng);   // each row's pool has its own page order
        pl.page_table = up(table);
        const int64_t nkv = 900 + 641 * r + (r % 2) * 3;
        const int64_t w = k::qsa_selection_width(nkv, s);
        std::vector<int32_t> all((size_t) nkv);
        for (int64_t c = 0; c < nkv; ++c) all[c] = (int32_t) c;
        std::shuffle(all.begin(), all.end(), rng);
        std::sort(all.begin(), all.begin() + w);
        std::copy(all.begin(), all.begin() + w, ids.begin() + (size_t) r * cap);
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepPos] = (int32_t) (nkv - 1);
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepNKv] = (int32_t) nkv;
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepNBid] = (int32_t) (nkv / s.idx_block);
        steps[(size_t) r * k::kStepCount + k::kStepWidth] = (int32_t) w;
    }
    const float* d_q = up(q);
    const int32_t* d_ids = up(ids);
    const int32_t* d_steps = up(steps);
    const int64_t scr = (int64_t) k::qsa_decode_attn_scratch_floats(cap, s);
    float *scratch = nullptr, *d_rows = nullptr, *d_ref = nullptr;
    ck(cudaMalloc(&scratch, (size_t) rows * scr * 4), "malloc");
    const size_t n = (size_t) rows * NH * HD;
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d_rows, n * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d_ref, n * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMemset(d_rows, 0, n * 4), "memset");
    ck(cudaMemset(d_ref, 0, n * 4), "memset");
    k::qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows(d_q, pr, d_ids, d_steps, cap, s, scratch, d_rows, rows, nullptr);
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r)
        k::qsa_decode_attn_batch(d_q + (size_t) r * NH * HD, pr.p[r], d_ids + (size_t) r * cap, d_steps + (size_t) r * k::kStepCount, cap,
                                 s, scratch + (size_t) r * scr, d_ref + (size_t) r * NH * HD, 1, nullptr);
    ck(cudaDeviceSynchronize(), "sync");
    const std::vector<float> a = down(d_rows, n), b = down(d_ref, n);
    char name[96];
    std::snprintf(name, sizeof name, "qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows, %d rows, %s pools (own pools each)", rows, int8 ? "int8" : "fp16");
    report(name, std::memcmp(a.data(), b.data(), n * 4) == 0);
}

// ---- 3. the GDN recurrence ----
void gdn_case(const std::vector<int>& ntok, bool commit) {
    const int S = 128, h_k = 16, h_v = 48;   // the artifact's geometry
    const int qk = S * h_k, C = 2 * qk + S * h_v, vd = S * h_v;
    const float eps = 1e-6f;
    int T = 0;
    for (int n : ntok) T += n;
    const int G = (int) ntok.size();
    std::mt19937 rng(31 + T * 7 + G + commit);
    std::normal_distribution<float> nd(0.f, 1.f);
    std::vector<float> h((size_t) T * C), gate((size_t) T * h_v), beta((size_t) T * h_v), z((size_t) T * vd), gamma(S);
    for (auto& v : h) v = nd(rng) * 0.1f;
    for (auto& v : gate) v = -(0.5f + 3.0f * (float) (rng() % 100) / 100.0f);
    for (auto& v : beta) v = (float) (rng() % 100) / 100.0f;
    for (auto& v : z) v = nd(rng);
    for (auto& v : gamma) v = 1.0f + 0.1f * nd(rng);
    const size_t st_n = (size_t) S * h_v * S;
    std::vector<std::vector<float>> st0(G);
    std::vector<float*> st_g(G), st_r(G);
    std::vector<int32_t*> keep(G);
    k::GdnGroups gg;
    gg.n = G;
    int first = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < G; ++i) {
        st0[i].resize(st_n);
        for (auto& v : st0[i]) v = nd(rng) * 0.1f;
        st_g[i] = up(st0[i]);
        st_r[i] = up(st0[i]);
        const int32_t kp = commit ? ntok[i] : 0;   // a commit group keeps all of its rows here
        keep[i] = up(std::vector<int32_t>{kp});
        gg.state[i] = st_g[i];
        gg.keep[i] = commit ? keep[i] : nullptr;
        gg.first[i] = first;
        gg.ntok[i] = ntok[i];
        first += ntok[i];
    }
    const float* d_h = up(h);
    const float* d_gate = up(gate);
    const float* d_beta = up(beta);
    const float* d_z = up(z);
    const float* d_gm = up(gamma);
    float *d_y = nullptr, *d_yr = nullptr;
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d_y, (size_t) T * vd * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMalloc(&d_yr, (size_t) T * vd * 4), "malloc");
    ck(cudaMemset(d_y, 0, (size_t) T * vd * 4), "memset");
    ck(cudaMemset(d_yr, 0, (size_t) T * vd * 4), "memset");
    k::gdn_step_norm_groups(gg, d_h, C, d_gate, d_beta, d_z, d_gm, eps, d_y, h_k, h_v, commit, nullptr);
    for (int i = 0; i < G; ++i) {
        const int f = gg.first[i];
        // the engine's per-slot call: a window group runs its rows with all outputs; a commit group (1 row) keeps them
        k::gdn_step_norm_multi(st_r[i], d_h + (size_t) f * C, C, d_gate + (size_t) f * h_v, d_beta + (size_t) f * h_v,
                               d_z + (size_t) f * vd, d_gm, eps, d_yr + (size_t) f * vd, h_k, h_v, ntok[i],
                               commit ? keep[i] : nullptr, nullptr, 0);
    }
    ck(cudaDeviceSynchronize(), "sync");
    bool same = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < G; ++i) {
        const std::vector<float> a = down(st_g[i], st_n), b = down(st_r[i], st_n);
        same = same && std::memcmp(a.data(), b.data(), st_n * 4) == 0;
        if (!commit) same = same && std::memcmp(a.data(), st0[i].data(), st_n * 4) == 0;   // a window leaves the state alone
    }
    if (!commit) {
        const std::vector<float> a = down(d_y, (size_t) T * vd), b = down(d_yr, (size_t) T * vd);
        same = same && std::memcmp(a.data(), b.data(), a.size() * 4) == 0;
    }
    char name[96], rows[64] = "";
    for (int i = 0; i < G && i < 8; ++i) std::snprintf(rows + std::strlen(rows), sizeof rows - std::strlen(rows), "%s%d", i ? "," : "", ntok[i]);
    std::snprintf(name, sizeof name, "gdn_step_norm_groups %s, groups of %s rows", commit ? "commit" : "window", rows);
    report(name, same);
}
}  // namespace

int main() {
    std::printf("batch rows parity (#2234 kernels against the per-row launches)\n");
    for (int r : {1, 2, 4, 8}) scores_case(r);
    for (int r : {1, 3, 8}) {
        attn_case(r, true);
        attn_case(r, false);
    }
    gdn_case({1}, false);
    gdn_case({1, 1, 1, 1}, false);
    gdn_case({2, 2, 2, 2}, false);
    gdn_case({1, 3, 2, 1, 1}, false);
    gdn_case({1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1}, false);
    gdn_case({1}, true);
    gdn_case({1, 1, 1, 1}, true);
    gdn_case({1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1}, true);
    std::printf("%s\n", bad ? "batch_rows_parity: FAILED" : "batch_rows_parity: ok");
    return bad ? 1 : 0;
}


## src/kernels/bf16_bits_test.cpp

// src/kernels/bf16_bits_test.cpp - `bf16_bits.hpp` against ggml's rule, over EVERY f32 bit pattern (CPU only).
//
// the rounding add `i + 0x7FFF + bit16` carries out of the mantissa for a NaN, so 0x7FFFFFFF came back as
// -0 and 0x7F800001 as +inf - an upstream NaN was masked instead of propagated.  `ggml_compute_fp32_to_bf16`
// (ggml-impl.h at the pinned llama.cpp) tests the NaN first and returns `(i >> 16) | 64`.  Three checks, all
// exhaustive (2^32 inputs, a few seconds):
//
//   1. the header equals ggml's function, transcribed below, on every input;
//   2. on every NON-NaN input it equals the previous rounding, so the change cannot move a finite value or an
//      infinity by a single bit;
//   3. every NaN input gives a quiet NaN of the same sign.
//
// And the round trip over all 65,536 bf16 patterns: a non-NaN bf16 survives f32 and back unchanged.
#include "strata/kernels/bf16_bits.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>

namespace {

/// ggml_compute_fp32_to_bf16, ggml/src/ggml-impl.h (MIT, the ggml authors), on raw bits.
uint16_t ggml_bf16(uint32_t u) {
    if ((u & 0x7fffffffu) > 0x7f800000u) return (uint16_t) ((u >> 16) | 64);
    return (uint16_t) ((u + (0x7fffu + ((u >> 16) & 1u))) >> 16);
}

/// The rule before this fix, kept only to prove the change is confined to NaN inputs.
uint16_t previous_bf16(uint32_t u) {
    u = (u + ((u >> 16) & 1u) + 0x7FFFu) & 0xFFFF0000u;
    return (uint16_t) (u >> 16);
}

bool is_nan_bits(uint32_t u) { return (u & 0x7fffffffu) > 0x7f800000u; }

}  // namespace

int main() {
    unsigned long long vs_ggml = 0, vs_previous = 0, nan_lost = 0, nan_inputs = 0, previous_masked = 0;
    uint32_t first_bad = 0;
    bool have_bad = false;
    for (uint64_t k = 0; k <= 0xFFFFFFFFull; ++k) {
        const uint32_t u = (uint32_t) k;
        float f;
        std::memcpy(&f, &u, 4);
        const uint16_t got = strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32(f);
        if (got != ggml_bf16(u)) {
            ++vs_ggml;
            if (!have_bad) { first_bad = u; have_bad = true; }
        }
        if (is_nan_bits(u)) {
            ++nan_inputs;
            const uint32_t back = (uint32_t) got << 16;
            // a quiet NaN (bit 22 of the f32) with the input's sign
            if (!is_nan_bits(back) || (back & 0x00400000u) == 0 || (back >> 31) != (u >> 31)) ++nan_lost;
            if (!is_nan_bits((uint32_t) previous_bf16(u) << 16)) ++previous_masked;
        } else if (got != previous_bf16(u)) {
            ++vs_previous;
            if (!have_bad) { first_bad = u; have_bad = true; }
        }
    }
    std::printf("  f32 -> bf16 over 2^32 inputs: %llu differ from ggml, %llu non-NaN differ from the previous rule\n",
                vs_ggml, vs_previous);
    std::printf("  NaN inputs: %llu, not a quiet same-sign NaN now: %llu (the previous rule masked %llu of them)\n",
                nan_inputs, nan_lost, previous_masked);
    if (have_bad) std::printf("    first mismatch at input 0x%08x\n", first_bad);

    unsigned long long trip_bad = 0;
    for (uint32_t h = 0; h <= 0xFFFFu; ++h) {
        const float f = strata::kernels::f32_from_bf16((uint16_t) h);
        const uint16_t back = strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32(f);
        const bool nan = is_nan_bits(h << 16);
        if (back != (nan ? (uint16_t) (h | 64u) : (uint16_t) h)) ++trip_bad;
    }
    std::printf("  bf16 -> f32 -> bf16 over 65536 patterns: %llu wrong\n", trip_bad);

    const bool ok = vs_ggml == 0 && vs_previous == 0 && nan_lost == 0 && trip_bad == 0 && previous_masked > 0;
    std::printf("\nbf16_bits_test %s\n", ok ? "OK" : "FAILED");
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}


## src/kernels/bf16_gemv_parity.cpp

// src/kernels/bf16_gemv_parity.cpp - P2.S5's test for the BF16 GEMV.
//
// THREE THINGS ARE CHECKED, and the third is the one the engine's correctness rests on:
//
//   1. both kernels against a host reference that reads the SAME bf16 bits - so what is under test is the
//      reduction, not the conversion, and the tolerance is set by summation order and nothing else;
//   2. the naive and the split kernel agree with each other, because the naive one is the reference the
//      split one exists to be checked against and a disagreement there means one of them is wrong;
//   3. **THE ACTIVATION CONTRACT IS OBSERVABLE.**  A BF16 weight sees a BF16 activation; feeding it fp16 or
//      f32 instead is a 2^-9 = 1.95e-03 relative change, which is above any 1e-3 tolerance.  An fp16
//      activation is the rival reading, computed and required to differ, because it is what the engine did
//      before `docs/activation-contract.md` settled the question and it produces perfectly plausible output.
#include "strata/kernels/bf16_bits.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/bf16_gemv.hpp"
#include "strata/kernels/f16_bits.hpp"

#include <cuda_runtime.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <random>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace {

using strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32;
using strata::kernels::f32_from_bf16;

void check(cudaError_t e, const char* what) {
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "%s: %s\n", what, cudaGetErrorString(e));
        std::exit(1);
    }
}

double rel_l1(const std::vector<float>& a, const std::vector<float>& b) {
    double d = 0, m = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) {
        d += std::fabs((double) a[i] - (double) b[i]);
        m += std::fabs((double) a[i]);
    }
    return d / (m > 1e-30 ? m : 1e-30);
}

/// The host reference, in DOUBLE, over the same bf16 bits.
void reference(const std::vector<uint16_t>& x, const std::vector<uint16_t>& w, long long n_in, long long n_out,
               std::vector<float>& y) {
    y.assign((size_t) n_out, 0.0f);
    for (long long o = 0; o < n_out; ++o) {
        double acc = 0;
        for (long long i = 0; i < n_in; ++i)
            acc += (double) f32_from_bf16(x[(size_t) i]) * (double) f32_from_bf16(w[(size_t) (o * n_in + i)]);
        y[(size_t) o] = (float) acc;
    }
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    bool selftest = false;
    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {
        if (std::string(argv[i]) == "--selftest") selftest = true;
        else { std::fprintf(stderr, "usage: bf16_gemv_parity [--selftest]\n"); return 2; }
    }
    int bad = 0;

    // THE REAL SHAPES, because a kernel that only works on a square toy is not a kernel this engine can use.
    // `ssm_alpha` is [2560, 48] - a wide reduction and 48 outputs - and `indexer.k_proj` is [2560, 128].
    struct Shape { long long n_in, n_out; const char* what; };
    const Shape shapes[] = {
        {2560, 48, "ssm_alpha.weight  [2560, 48]"},
        {2560, 128, "indexer.k_proj   [2560, 128]"},
        {2560, 512, "indexer.q_proj   [2560, 512]"},
        {2560, 2560, "ple_value        [2560, 2560]"},
    };

    for (const Shape& s : shapes) {
        std::mt19937 rng(4242);
        std::normal_distribution<float> g(0.0f, 1.0f);
        std::vector<float> fx((size_t) s.n_in), fw((size_t) (s.n_in * s.n_out));
        for (auto& v : fx) v = g(rng);
        // a realistic weight scale: these are projections, not embeddings
        for (auto& v : fw) v = g(rng) * 0.05f;

        // THE ACTIVATION IS ROUNDED TO BF16 FIRST, which is the contract, and the WEIGHT is already bf16 in
        // the pack - the loaded bytes ARE the high 16 bits of an f32.
        std::vector<uint16_t> x((size_t) s.n_in), w((size_t) (s.n_in * s.n_out));
        for (size_t i = 0; i < fx.size(); ++i) x[i] = bf16_from_f32(fx[i]);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < fw.size(); ++i) w[i] = bf16_from_f32(fw[i]);

        std::vector<float> want;
        reference(x, w, s.n_in, s.n_out, want);

        uint16_t *d_x = nullptr, *d_w = nullptr;
        float *d_y = nullptr;
        check(cudaMalloc(&d_x, x.size() * 2), "x");
        check(cudaMalloc(&d_w, w.size() * 2), "w");
        check(cudaMalloc(&d_y, (size_t) s.n_out * 4), "y");
        check(cudaMemcpy(d_x, x.data(), x.size() * 2, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice), "cx");
        check(cudaMemcpy(d_w, w.data(), w.size() * 2, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice), "cw");

        std::vector<float> naive((size_t) s.n_out), warp((size_t) s.n_out), split((size_t) s.n_out);
        strata::kernels::bf16_gemv(d_x, d_w, d_y, s.n_in, s.n_out, nullptr);
        check(cudaMemcpy(naive.data(), d_y, naive.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), "cy1");
        strata::kernels::bf16_gemv_split(d_x, d_w, d_y, s.n_in, s.n_out, 32, nullptr);
        check(cudaMemcpy(warp.data(), d_y, warp.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), "cy2");
        strata::kernels::bf16_gemv_split(d_x, d_w, d_y, s.n_in, s.n_out, 256, nullptr);
        check(cudaMemcpy(split.data(), d_y, split.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), "cy3");

        const double rn = rel_l1(want, naive), rw = rel_l1(want, warp), rs = rel_l1(want, split);
        std::printf("  %-34s naive %.2e  warp %.2e  split256 %.2e\n", s.what, rn, rw, rs);
        // The products are EXACT - both sides are bf16-valued, so f32 represents each product exactly - and
        // the only difference is the order the 2560 terms are added.  A tight bound is therefore meaningful.
        if (!(rn <= 1e-5 && rw <= 1e-5 && rs <= 1e-5)) { std::printf("    *** over 1e-5 ***\n"); ++bad; }

        // ---- 3. THE ACTIVATION CONTRACT.  The rival: an fp16 activation instead of bf16, which is what the
        // engine did before the contract was settled.  It must be observable, or check 1 above would pass
        // against either and the contract would be untested.
        {
            std::vector<float> fp16_as_f32((size_t) s.n_in);
            std::vector<uint16_t> x16((size_t) s.n_in);
            for (size_t i = 0; i < fx.size(); ++i) {
                x16[i] = strata::kernels::f16_from_f32(fx[i]);
                fp16_as_f32[i] = strata::kernels::f32_from_f16(x16[i]);
            }
            // Round the fp16 value to bf16 - i.e. give the kernel a bf16 activation whose VALUES came through
            // fp16.  That is the whole difference between the two contracts at this call site.
            for (size_t i = 0; i < fp16_as_f32.size(); ++i) x[i] = bf16_from_f32(fp16_as_f32[i]);
            check(cudaMemcpy(d_x, x.data(), x.size() * 2, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice), "cx2");
            std::vector<float> rival((size_t) s.n_out);
            strata::kernels::bf16_gemv(d_x, d_w, d_y, s.n_in, s.n_out, nullptr);
            check(cudaMemcpy(rival.data(), d_y, rival.size() * 4, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), "cy4");
            const double r = rel_l1(want, rival);
            const bool visible = r > 1e-4;
            std::printf("      %-30s %s (%.4f%% apart)\n", "bf16 vs fp16 activation",
                        visible ? "yes" : "*** NO ***", r * 100);
            if (!visible) ++bad;
        }
        cudaFree(d_x); cudaFree(d_w); cudaFree(d_y);
    }

    std::printf("\nbf16_gemv: %d failures\n", bad);
    if (bad) return 1;
    if (selftest) std::printf("bf16_gemv_parity OK\n");
    return 0;
}


## src/kernels/cpu/expert.cpp

// src/kernels/cpu/expert.cpp - P2.S3: the Q2_0 expert kernel, promoted from bench/micro/cpu_s2.cpp.
//
// The body is the validated kernel, moved rather than rewritten: it carries the P0.T2 parity result
// (rel 1.461e-06 against the ggml formula) and the three performance findings recorded in
// include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert.hpp.  Read that header first; it says why each piece is shaped this way.
#include "strata/kernels/cpu/expert.hpp"

#include <immintrin.h>
#if defined(_MSC_VER)
#include <intrin.h>
#else
#include <cpuid.h>
#endif

#include <cmath>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

namespace strata::kernels::cpu {
namespace {

/// fp16 -> fp32, written out rather than using `_cvtsh_ss`, because the F16C intrinsic's behaviour on
/// subnormals is the one place the two can differ and the scales in this artifact are small.
inline float h2f(const uint8_t* p) {
    uint16_t h;
    std::memcpy(&h, p, 2);
    const uint32_t sign = (uint32_t) (h >> 15) & 1u;
    uint32_t exp = (h >> 10) & 0x1Fu, man = h & 0x3FFu, f;
    if (exp == 0) {
        if (man == 0) {
            f = sign << 31;
        } else {
            exp = 127 - 15 + 1;
            while (!(man & 0x400u)) { man <<= 1; --exp; }
            man &= 0x3FFu;
            f = (sign << 31) | (exp << 23) | (man << 13);
        }
    } else if (exp == 31) {
        f = (sign << 31) | 0x7F800000u | (man << 13);
    } else {
        f = (sign << 31) | ((exp - 15 + 127) << 23) | (man << 13);
    }
    float out;
    std::memcpy(&out, &f, 4);
    return out;
}

// The x86 Q8_0 quantization and generic Q2_0 dot sequences are adapted from llama.cpp
// 3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d,
// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c: quantize_row_q8_0 and
// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/quants.c: ggml_vec_dot_q2_0_q8_0_generic.
//
// MIT License
// Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors
//
// Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
// of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
// in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
// to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
// copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
// furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:
//
// The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
// copies or substantial portions of the Software.
//
// THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
// IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
// FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
// AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
// LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
// OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
// SOFTWARE.
void quantize_oracle_q8_0(const float* x, int n, ActQ& a) {
    a.nchunks = n / QKA;
    for (int chunk = 0; chunk < a.nchunks; ++chunk) {
        const float* xb = x + chunk * QKA;
        __m256 v0 = _mm256_loadu_ps(xb);
        __m256 v1 = _mm256_loadu_ps(xb + 8);
        __m256 v2 = _mm256_loadu_ps(xb + 16);
        __m256 v3 = _mm256_loadu_ps(xb + 24);
        const __m256 sign = _mm256_set1_ps(-0.0f);
        __m256 maximum = _mm256_andnot_ps(sign, v0);
        maximum = _mm256_max_ps(maximum, _mm256_andnot_ps(sign, v1));
        maximum = _mm256_max_ps(maximum, _mm256_andnot_ps(sign, v2));
        maximum = _mm256_max_ps(maximum, _mm256_andnot_ps(sign, v3));
        __m128 max4 = _mm_max_ps(_mm256_extractf128_ps(maximum, 1), _mm256_castps256_ps128(maximum));
        max4 = _mm_max_ps(max4, _mm_movehl_ps(max4, max4));
        max4 = _mm_max_ss(max4, _mm_movehdup_ps(max4));
        const float amax = _mm_cvtss_f32(max4);
        const float d = amax / 127.0f;
