        old = {**first, "args": first["args"] + CVEC}                                      # 0.2.0-beta: no copy of what was written
        code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--context", "131072", configs=[("strata-q2_0.json", old)])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertEqual(cfg["user_args"], CVEC)
        self.assertEqual(cfg["args"][-len(CVEC):], CVEC)

    def test_3215_a_reserve_of_zero_is_kept(self):
        first = self.first()
        written = list(first["args"])
        edited = [*written]
        edited[edited.index("--vram-reserve-mib") + 1] = "0"
        for old in ({**first, "args": edited, "args_written": written},                    # with the copy of what was written
                    {**first, "args": edited}):                                           # a 0.2.0-beta file
            code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--context", "131072", configs=[("strata-q2_0.json", old)])
            self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
            self.assertEqual(value(cfg["args"], "--vram-reserve-mib"), "0")
            self.assertEqual(cfg["user_args"], ["--vram-reserve-mib", "0"])

    def test_3270_a_lowered_reserve_is_not_reset(self):
        first = self.first()
        written = list(first["args"])
        for mib in ("1024", "256"):
            edited = [*written]
            edited[edited.index("--vram-reserve-mib") + 1] = mib
            code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--context", "131072", configs=[("strata-q2_0.json", {**first, "args": edited, "args_written": written})])
            self.assertEqual(value(cfg["args"], "--vram-reserve-mib"), mib)

    def test_the_vision_default_is_not_taken_for_a_choice(self):
        first = self.first()                                                               # pictures on the GPU write 700 themselves
        self.assertEqual(value(first["args"], "--vram-reserve-mib"), "700")
        code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--context", "131072", "--vision", "cpu", configs=[("strata-q2_0.json", first)])
        self.assertNotIn("user_args", cfg)
        self.assertNotIn("--vram-reserve-mib", cfg["args"])                                # the CPU reader needs no reserve

    def test_an_option_given_on_the_command_line_wins_and_is_kept(self):
        first = self.first()
        old = {**first, "args": first["args"] + ["--vram-reserve-mib", "0"], "user_args": ["--vram-reserve-mib", "0"]}
        code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--context", "131072", "--vram-reserve-mib", "256", configs=[("strata-q2_0.json", old)])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertEqual(cfg["user_args"], ["--vram-reserve-mib", "256"])
        self.assertEqual(value(cfg["args"], "--vram-reserve-mib"), "256")

    def test_a_first_install_with_a_reserve_records_it(self):
        code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--vram-reserve-mib", "300")
        self.assertEqual(cfg["user_args"], ["--vram-reserve-mib", "300"])

    def test_setup_writes_args_written_and_a_rerun_with_no_edit_makes_no_user_args(self):
        first = self.first()
        code, out, cfg, _ = self.run_setup("--context", "131072", configs=[("strata-q2_0.json", {**first, "args_written": first["args"]})])
        self.assertNotIn("user_args", cfg)


class Start(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_start_puts_the_persons_options_over_the_generated_ones(self):
        cfg = {"args": ["--pack", "/p", "--vram-reserve-mib", "1536", "--spec", "4"],
               "user_args": ["--vram-reserve-mib", "0"] + CVEC}
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            args = engine_args(cfg)
        self.assertEqual(value(args, "--vram-reserve-mib"), "0")
        self.assertEqual(args.count("--vram-reserve-mib"), 1)
        self.assertEqual(args[args.index("--control-vector-scaled"):][:9], CVEC)
        self.assertEqual(cfg["args"][3], "1536")                                           # the config in memory is untouched

    def test_the_settings_page_records_the_reserve_as_the_persons(self):
        cfg = {"args": ["--pack", "/p", "--vram-reserve-mib", "1536"], "args_written": ["--pack", "/p", "--vram-reserve-mib", "1536"]}
        new, changed = runconfig.apply(cfg, {"vram_reserve_mib": 0})
        self.assertEqual(changed, ["vram_reserve_mib"])
        self.assertEqual(new["user_args"], ["--vram-reserve-mib", "0"])
        self.assertEqual(new["args_written"], new["args"])
        back, _ = runconfig.apply(new, {"vram_reserve_mib": None})
        self.assertNotIn("user_args", back)
        self.assertNotIn("--vram-reserve-mib", back["args"])

    def test_a_tuning_replaces_only_the_flags_it_sets(self):
        cfg = {"args": ["--pack", "/p", "--vram-reserve-mib", "0", *CVEC], "args_written": ["--pack", "/p"],
               "user_args": ["--vram-reserve-mib", "0", *CVEC]}
        out = tune_apply.apply_args_to_config(cfg, ["--vram-reserve-mib", "512", "--pcie-frac", "0.5"])
        self.assertEqual(value(out["args"], "--vram-reserve-mib"), "512")
        self.assertEqual(out["user_args"], CVEC)                                           # the tuned flag is no longer the old pin
        self.assertEqual(out["args_written"], out["args"])


class DisplayCards(unittest.TestCase):
    """The app keeps the safety reserve for a card that drives a display and less on one that does not (#3215)."""

    def test_nvidia_by_nvidia_smi(self):
        gpus = [{"vendor": "nvidia", "index": 0}, {"vendor": "nvidia", "index": 1}, {"vendor": "nvidia", "index": 2}]
        strata_mcp.mark_display(gpus, {0: False, 1: True}, [])
        self.assertIs(gpus[0]["drives_display"], False)
        self.assertIs(gpus[1]["drives_display"], True)
        self.assertNotIn("drives_display", gpus[2])                                        # not told: unknown

    def test_amd_by_the_windows_adapter_with_a_desktop(self):
        amd = {"vendor": "amd", "index": 1, "pci_id": 0x744C}
        gpus = [{"vendor": "amd", "index": 0, "pci_id": 0x164E}, amd]
        strata_mcp.mark_display(gpus, {}, ["PCI\\VEN_1002&DEV_164E&SUBSYS_1"])
        self.assertIs(gpus[0]["drives_display"], True)
        self.assertIs(amd["drives_display"], False)
        twins = [{"vendor": "amd", "pci_id": 0x744C}, {"vendor": "amd", "pci_id": 0x744C}]
        strata_mcp.mark_display(twins, {}, ["PCI\\VEN_1002&DEV_744C"])
        self.assertNotIn("drives_display", twins[0])                                       # two of one model: not told apart
        strata_mcp.mark_display(gpus[:1] + [{"vendor": "amd", "pci_id": 0x1}], {}, [])
        self.assertTrue(True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tools/test_vision_reader.py

"""The picture reader choice for an AMD engine folder (strata_control/vision_reader.py) and the server's fallback from the GPU
reader to the CPU reader (serve/server.py, Vision._start): hip present, hip missing, hip start failure, then cpu.

    python -m unittest tools.test_vision_reader
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest import mock

from strata_control import vision_reader as VR
import serve.server as server


def folder(*names: str) -> Path:
    d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="vr-"))
    for n in names:
        (d / n).write_bytes(b"x")
    return d


class Choose(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_default_reader_by_card_memory_is_one_rule_for_every_make(self):
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(12), "cpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(16), "cpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(23.5), "gpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(24), "gpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(32), "gpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(None), "gpu")                  # memory unknown: the GPU reader falls back by itself
        for asked, vram, want in ((None, 16, "cpu"), ("yes", 12, "cpu"), ("on", 32, "gpu"), ("gpu", 12, "gpu"), ("cpu", 32, "cpu"),
                                  ("no", 32, "none"), ("off", 12, "none")):
            self.assertEqual(VR.wanted(asked, vram), want, (asked, vram))

    def test_an_intel_arc_keeps_the_cpu_reader_by_default_and_gpu_is_asked_for(self):
        """The one exception to the 24 GB rule: the SYCL reader has run on a 8 GB A750 only (INTEL_GPU_READER_BY_DEFAULT)."""
        self.assertFalse(VR.INTEL_GPU_READER_BY_DEFAULT)
        for vram in (8, 16, 24, 32):
            self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(vram, "intel"), "cpu")
            self.assertEqual(VR.wanted("yes", vram, "intel"), "cpu")
            self.assertEqual(VR.wanted("gpu", vram, "intel"), "gpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.wanted("yes", 32), "gpu")                        # other makes: unchanged
        with mock.patch.object(VR, "INTEL_GPU_READER_BY_DEFAULT", True):
            self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(32, "intel"), "gpu")
            self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(8, "intel"), "cpu")              # with the exception off, the 24 GB rule is the same as for every make

    def test_the_sycl_reader_is_the_gpu_reader_of_an_intel_folder(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-sycl")
        r = VR.choose(d, "gpu", windows=False)
        self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name, r.cpu_exe.name), ("gpu", "strata-vision-sycl", "strata-vision"))
        self.assertEqual(VR.vision_section(r, {"mmproj": "m"})["gpu"], True)
        r = VR.choose(folder("strata-vision"), "gpu", windows=False)         # no SYCL reader built: the CPU one, said
        self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name), ("cpu", "strata-vision"))
        self.assertIn("no GPU picture reader", r.note)
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(d, "cpu", windows=False).exe.name, "strata-vision")

    def test_hip_present_gives_the_gpu_reader_with_the_cpu_one_to_fall_back_on(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-hip")
        for ask in ("yes", "on", "gpu"):
            r = VR.choose(d, ask, windows=False, gpu_arch="gfx1201", archs=["gfx1200", "gfx1201"])
            self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name, r.cpu_exe.name), ("gpu", "strata-vision-hip", "strata-vision"), ask)
            self.assertEqual(r.note, "")

    def test_hip_missing_gives_the_cpu_reader(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision")
        r = VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False, gpu_arch="gfx1201")
        self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name, r.cpu_exe), ("cpu", "strata-vision", None))
        self.assertEqual(r.note, "")                               # "yes" never asked for the GPU in particular
        self.assertIn("no GPU picture reader", VR.choose(d, "gpu", windows=False).note)   # --vision gpu: said once

    def test_card_not_in_the_build_gives_the_cpu_reader(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-hip")
        r = VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False, gpu_arch="gfx1100", archs=["gfx1200", "gfx1201"])
        self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name), ("cpu", "strata-vision"))
        self.assertIn("gfx1100", r.note)

    def test_unknown_card_tries_the_gpu_reader(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-hip")
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False, gpu_arch="", archs=["gfx1201"]).mode, "gpu")
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False, gpu_arch="gfx1100", archs=None).mode, "gpu")

    def test_gcn_arch_names_with_features_match(self):
        self.assertEqual(VR.gfx_of("gfx1201:sramecc-:xnack-"), "gfx1201")
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-hip")
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False, gpu_arch="gfx1151:sramecc+:xnack-", archs=["gfx1151"]).mode, "gpu")

    def test_cpu_asked_and_off(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-hip")
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(d, "cpu", windows=False).exe.name, "strata-vision")
        for ask in ("no", "none", "off", None):
            self.assertEqual(VR.choose(d, ask, windows=False).mode, "none")

    def test_no_reader_at_all(self):
        d = folder("strata")
        for ask in ("yes", "cpu", "gpu"):
            r = VR.choose(d, ask, windows=False)
            self.assertEqual(r.mode, "none", ask)
            self.assertIn("no picture reader", r.note)

    def test_windows_names(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision.exe", "strata-vision-hip.exe")
        r = VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=True, gpu_arch="gfx1201", archs=["gfx1201"])
        self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name, r.cpu_exe.name), ("gpu", "strata-vision-hip.exe", "strata-vision.exe"))
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(folder("strata-vision-hip"), "yes", windows=True).mode, "none")   # a Linux name on Windows

    def test_run_config_section(self):
        d = folder("strata-vision", "strata-vision-hip")
        base = {"mmproj": "m.gguf", "model": "t.gguf", "max_tokens": 1024}
        sec = VR.vision_section(VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False), base)
        self.assertTrue(sec["gpu"])
        self.assertEqual(Path(sec["exe"]).name, "strata-vision-hip")
        self.assertEqual(Path(sec["cpu_exe"]).name, "strata-vision")
        cpu = VR.cpu_fallback(sec)
        self.assertFalse(cpu["gpu"])
        self.assertEqual(Path(cpu["exe"]).name, "strata-vision")
        self.assertNotIn("cpu_exe", cpu)
        self.assertEqual(cpu["mmproj"], "m.gguf")
        cpu_only = VR.vision_section(VR.choose(folder("strata-vision"), "yes", windows=False), base)
        self.assertFalse(cpu_only["gpu"])
        self.assertNotIn("cpu_exe", cpu_only)
        self.assertIsNone(VR.cpu_fallback(cpu_only))
        self.assertIsNone(VR.cpu_fallback({**sec, "cpu_exe": ""}))
        self.assertIsNone(VR.cpu_fallback({"exe": "strata-vision", "gpu": True}))   # an NVIDIA config has no fallback


class MacReader(unittest.TestCase):
    """A Mac has one picture program, strata-vision with Metal built in: --gpu reads on the GPU, without it on the CPU."""

    def test_a_mac_reads_on_the_gpu_by_default_whatever_its_memory(self):
        for ram in (16, 32, 64, 128, None):
            self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(ram, unified=True), "gpu", ram)
            self.assertEqual(VR.wanted(None, ram, unified=True), "gpu", ram)
            self.assertEqual(VR.wanted("yes", ram, unified=True), "gpu", ram)
        self.assertEqual(VR.wanted("cpu", 32, unified=True), "cpu")             # asked for: kept
        self.assertEqual(VR.wanted("off", 32, unified=True), "none")
        self.assertEqual(VR.default_mode(16), "cpu")                           # a 16 GB card of a PC still follows the 24 GB rule

    def test_the_one_program_is_both_readers_and_its_own_fallback(self):
        d = folder("strata", "strata-vision")
        for ask in ("yes", "on", "gpu"):
            r = VR.choose(d, ask, windows=False, mac=True)
            self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name, r.cpu_exe.name, r.note), ("gpu", "strata-vision", "strata-vision", ""), ask)
        sec = VR.vision_section(VR.choose(d, "yes", windows=False, mac=True), {"mmproj": "m.gguf", "model": "t.gguf", "max_tokens": 1024})
        self.assertTrue(sec["gpu"])
        self.assertEqual(sec["exe"], sec["cpu_exe"])
        fallback = VR.cpu_fallback(sec)
        self.assertFalse(fallback["gpu"])
        self.assertEqual(fallback["exe"], sec["exe"])

    def test_cpu_asked_is_kept_with_the_time_it_takes(self):
        r = VR.choose(folder("strata-vision"), "cpu", windows=False, mac=True)
        self.assertEqual((r.mode, r.exe.name, r.cpu_exe), ("cpu", "strata-vision", None))
        self.assertIn("50 seconds", r.note)
        self.assertFalse(VR.vision_section(r, {})["gpu"])

    def test_an_engine_without_the_reader_gets_pictures_off(self):
        for ask in ("yes", "gpu", "cpu"):
            r = VR.choose(folder("strata"), ask, windows=False, mac=True)
            self.assertEqual(r.mode, "none", ask)
            self.assertIn("no picture reader", r.note)
        self.assertEqual(VR.choose(folder("strata-vision"), "off", windows=False, mac=True).mode, "none")

    def test_a_hip_program_is_not_a_mac_reader(self):
        r = VR.choose(folder("strata-vision-hip"), "yes", windows=False, mac=True)
        self.assertEqual(r.mode, "none")


class FakeProc:
    def __init__(self, first_line: str):
        self.stdin, self.stdout = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO(first_line)
        self.killed = False

    def kill(self):
        self.killed = True

    def wait(self, timeout=None):
        return 0

    def poll(self):
        return None


def make_vision(cfg: dict) -> "server.Vision":
    with mock.patch.object(server.Vision, "work_dir", staticmethod(lambda: Path(tempfile.gettempdir()))):
        return server.Vision(cfg, lazy=True)


class Fallback(unittest.TestCase):
    CFG = {"exe": "/e/strata-vision-hip", "cpu_exe": "/e/strata-vision", "gpu": True, "mmproj": "/m/mm.gguf",
           "model": "/m/t.gguf", "max_tokens": 1024, "threads": 6}

    def run_start(self, answers: dict, cfg: dict | None = None):
        """answers: exe name -> its first stdout line, or an exception to raise from popen."""
        started = []

        def popen(what, args, **kw):
            name = Path(args[0]).name
            started.append(args)
            a = answers[name]
            if isinstance(a, Exception):
                raise a
            return FakeProc(a)

        v = make_vision(cfg or self.CFG)
        out = io.StringIO()
        with mock.patch.object(server, "popen", popen), mock.patch("builtins.print", lambda *a, **k: out.write(" ".join(map(str, a)) + "\n")):
            err = None
            try:
                v._start()
            except RuntimeError as e:
                err = e
        return v, started, out.getvalue(), err

    def test_hip_present_and_starts(self):
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": "READY 2048\n"})
        self.assertIsNone(err)
        self.assertEqual([Path(a[0]).name for a in started], ["strata-vision-hip"])
        self.assertIn("--gpu", started[0])
        self.assertEqual(log, "")
        self.assertFalse(v.stopped)

    def test_hip_start_failure_falls_back_to_cpu_with_one_line(self):
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": "ERR this GPU (gfx1100) is not in the picture reader's build (gfx1200,gfx1201)\n",
                                               "strata-vision": "READY 2048\n"})
        self.assertIsNone(err)
        self.assertEqual([Path(a[0]).name for a in started], ["strata-vision-hip", "strata-vision"])
        self.assertNotIn("--gpu", started[1])
        self.assertIn("--threads", started[1])
        self.assertEqual(log.count("\n"), 1)
        self.assertIn("gfx1100", log)
        self.assertIn("CPU", log)
        self.assertFalse(v.stopped)
        self.assertIsNone(v.fallback)

    def test_hip_process_that_dies_silently_falls_back(self):                  # a GPU runtime that aborts: stdout closes empty
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": "", "strata-vision": "READY 2048\n"})
        self.assertIsNone(err)
        self.assertEqual(len(started), 2)
        self.assertEqual(log.count("\n"), 1)

    def test_hip_missing_file_falls_back(self):                               # popen raises (exe gone, not executable)
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": FileNotFoundError("strata-vision-hip"),
                                               "strata-vision": "READY 2048\n"})
        self.assertIsNone(err)
        self.assertEqual(len(started), 2)

    def test_restart_after_a_fallback_stays_on_the_cpu_reader(self):
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": "ERR nope\n", "strata-vision": "READY 2048\n"})
        started.clear()
        with mock.patch.object(server, "popen", lambda what, args, **kw: started.append(args) or FakeProc("READY 2048\n")):
            v.restart()
        self.assertEqual([Path(a[0]).name for a in started], ["strata-vision"])

    def test_cpu_failure_after_the_fallback_is_an_error(self):
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": "ERR nope\n", "strata-vision": "ERR cannot load the vision encoder\n"})
        self.assertIsNotNone(err)
        self.assertIn("cannot load", str(err))

    def test_a_config_without_cpu_exe_has_no_fallback(self):                  # NVIDIA: the error is shown as before
        cfg = {k: v for k, v in self.CFG.items() if k != "cpu_exe"}
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision-hip": "ERR nope\n"}, cfg)
        self.assertIsNotNone(err)
        self.assertEqual(len(started), 1)
        self.assertEqual(log, "")

    def test_cpu_config_is_unchanged(self):
        cfg = {"exe": "/e/strata-vision", "gpu": False, "mmproj": "/m/mm.gguf", "model": "/m/t.gguf"}
        v, started, log, err = self.run_start({"strata-vision": "READY 2048\n"}, cfg)
        self.assertIsNone(err)
        self.assertNotIn("--gpu", started[0])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tools/test_windows_amd_gpu.py

"""#1587: a Windows PC with only an AMD card - the server's hardware_static names the card from the registry's display
class, and strata_bench no longer labels the run "CPU only".  No GPU, no registry needed (a fake winreg).

    python -m unittest tools.test_windows_amd_gpu
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import types
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
from serve import telemetry as T  # noqa: E402

GB = 1 << 30


def fake_winreg(adapters):
    """A winreg with the display class holding `adapters` (dicts of value name -> value) under 0000, 0001, ..."""
    w = types.ModuleType("winreg")
    w.HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE = "HKLM"
    keys = {f"{i:04d}": a for i, a in enumerate(adapters)}
    subs = list(keys) + ["Properties"]

    def OpenKey(root, sub):
        if root == "HKLM":
            return "CLASS"
        if root == "CLASS" and sub in keys:
            return keys[sub]
        raise OSError("denied")

    def EnumKey(k, i):
        if i >= len(subs):
            raise OSError("no more")
        return subs[i]

    def QueryValueEx(k, name):
        if name not in k:
            raise OSError("no value")
        return k[name], 1
    w.OpenKey, w.EnumKey, w.QueryValueEx = OpenKey, EnumKey, QueryValueEx
    return w


IGPU = {"DriverDesc": "AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics", "ProviderName": "Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.",
        "DriverVersion": "32.0.13066.12", "HardwareInformation.qwMemorySize": 512 << 20}
CARD = {"DriverDesc": "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT", "ProviderName": "Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.",
        "DriverVersion": "32.0.21001.9024", "HardwareInformation.MemorySize": (16 * GB).to_bytes(8, "little")}
GEFORCE = {"DriverDesc": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070", "ProviderName": "NVIDIA", "DriverVersion": "32.0.16.1047",
           "HardwareInformation.qwMemorySize": 12 * GB}


class Adapters(unittest.TestCase):
    def read(self, adapters, vendor=None):
        with mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, {"winreg": fake_winreg(adapters)}), mock.patch.object(T.os, "name", "nt"):
            return T.windows_display_adapters(vendor)

    def test_reads_names_vram_and_drivers(self):
        a = self.read([IGPU, CARD, GEFORCE])
        self.assertEqual([x["name"] for x in a], ["AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics", "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT", "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070"])
        self.assertEqual(a[1]["vram_bytes"], 16 * GB)       # the binary form of the memory size
        self.assertEqual(a[2]["vram_bytes"], 12 * GB)
        self.assertEqual([x["name"] for x in self.read([IGPU, CARD, GEFORCE], "amd")],
                         ["AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics", "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT"])

    def test_the_integrated_radeon_is_left_out_beside_a_card(self):
        self.assertEqual([c["name"] for c in T.windows_amd_cards(self.read([IGPU, CARD], "amd"))], ["AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT"])
        self.assertEqual([c["name"] for c in T.windows_amd_cards(self.read([IGPU], "amd"))], ["AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics"])

    def test_off_windows_nothing(self):
        with mock.patch.object(T.os, "name", "posix"):
            self.assertEqual(T.windows_display_adapters(), [])

    def test_hardware_static_names_the_card(self):
        cards = [{"name": "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT", "provider": "AMD", "driver": "x", "vram_bytes": 16 * GB}]
        with mock.patch.object(T.os, "name", "nt"), mock.patch.object(T, "windows_amd_cards", return_value=cards), \
                mock.patch.object(T, "gpu_reader", return_value=mock.Mock(ok=lambda: False)), \
                mock.patch.object(T, "_CpuRamFallback"), mock.patch.object(T, "_cpu_name", return_value="cpu"), \
                mock.patch.object(T.threading, "Thread"):
            t = T.Telemetry(amd=True)
        self.assertEqual(t.static["gpu_name"], "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT")
        self.assertEqual(t.static["gpu_vram_total_mib"], 16384)

    def test_bench_labels_the_card(self):
        import strata_bench as B
        cards = [{"name": "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT", "provider": "AMD", "driver": "32.0.21001.9024", "vram_bytes": 16 * GB}]
        with mock.patch.object(B, "run_cmd", return_value=""), mock.patch.object(B.os, "name", "nt"), \
                mock.patch.object(T, "windows_amd_cards", return_value=cards):
            info = B.gpu_info_local()
        self.assertEqual(info["gpus"], [{"name": "AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT", "vram_mib": 16384, "driver": "32.0.21001.9024"}])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tools/tqenc.py

"""tqenc.py - Python side of the trellis encoder (tools/trellis/tqenc.cpp, built to libtqenc.so by
`sh tools/trellis/build.sh lib`): encode / decode blocks of TQ2_T, TQK6, TQK7 and the experimental TQK5X / TQK4X, the
input-only block Hadamard of the DeepSeek plan, and error metrics.

Rows of a tensor are blocks of 128 consecutive weights along the INPUT dimension (the GGUF fastest axis), exactly as the
decoders read them.  A tensor of shape [rows, n] (n a multiple of 128) is encoded row by row; the output has
rows * n/128 * block_bytes bytes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import pathlib

import numpy as np

TQ2_T, TQK6, TQK7, TQK5X, TQK4X, TQK5T, TQK4T = 144, 145, 146, 224, 225, 226, 227
# TQK5X / TQK4X: experimental version 2, the computed (LUT-free) codebook (src/kernels/cpu/tq_computed.hpp);
# TQK5T / TQK4T: version 1, the fork's point table (what the first pilots and the Gyro-S checks used for K5 / K4)
TYPE_NAMES = {TQ2_T: "TQ2_T", TQK6: "TQK6", TQK7: "TQK7", TQK5X: "TQK5X", TQK4X: "TQK4X", TQK5T: "TQK5T", TQK4T: "TQK4T"}
TYPE_BY_NAME = {v: k for k, v in TYPE_NAMES.items()}
KBITS = {TQ2_T: 8, TQK6: 6, TQK7: 7, TQK5X: 5, TQK4X: 4, TQK5T: 5, TQK4T: 4}
COMPUTED = (TQK5X, TQK4X)
BLOCK = 128


def block_bytes(t: int) -> int:
    return 2 + 4 * KBITS[t]


def bpw(t: int) -> float:
    return block_bytes(t) * 8 / BLOCK


_lib = None


def lib() -> ctypes.CDLL:
    global _lib
    if _lib is None:
        cands = [os.environ.get("TQENC_LIB", ""),
                 str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "build-tqenc" / "libtqenc.so"),
                 "libtqenc.so"]
        last = None
        for c in cands:
            if not c:
                continue
            try:
                _lib = ctypes.CDLL(c)
                break
            except OSError as e:
                last = e
        if _lib is None:
            raise RuntimeError("libtqenc.so not found (sh tools/trellis/build.sh lib): %s" % last)
        _lib.tqe_encode.restype = ctypes.c_double
        _lib.tqe_encode.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.c_void_p,
                                    ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int,
                                    ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p]
        _lib.tqe_decode.restype = None
        _lib.tqe_decode.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.c_void_p]
    return _lib


_hip = None


class _gpu_lock:
    """TQENC_GPU_LOCK=<card number>: take the box locks (shared /data/gpu.lock, exclusive ~/locks/gpu<N>.lock) around every GPU
    call and release them in between, so a long job that is mostly host work does not keep the card from other users.
    TQENC_GPU_WAIT=<seconds> (default: wait for ever): give up after that long; `ok` is then False and encode() uses the CPU."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.fds = []
        self.ok = True

    def __enter__(self):
        card = os.environ.get("TQENC_GPU_LOCK")
        if card is None:
            return self
        import fcntl
        import time
        wait = float(os.environ.get("TQENC_GPU_WAIT", "1e9"))
        t0 = time.time()
        while os.path.exists(os.path.expanduser("~/locks/EXCL_WAIT")):   # a writer is waiting for the box
            if time.time() - t0 > wait:
                self.ok = False
                return self
            time.sleep(2)
        for path, mode in (("/data/gpu.lock", fcntl.LOCK_SH), (os.path.expanduser("~/locks/gpu%s.lock" % card), fcntl.LOCK_EX)):
            fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT)
            while True:
                try:
                    fcntl.flock(fd, mode | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                    break
                except BlockingIOError:
                    if time.time() - t0 > wait:
                        os.close(fd)
                        self.ok = False
                        for f in reversed(self.fds):
                            os.close(f)
                        self.fds = []
                        return self
                    time.sleep(0.2)
            self.fds.append(fd)
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *a):
        for fd in reversed(self.fds):
            os.close(fd)
        return False


def hip_lib() -> ctypes.CDLL:
    """libtqenc_hip.so (sh tools/trellis/build.sh hip; run under the box GPU locks, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES picks the card)."""
    global _hip
    if _hip is None:
        cands = [os.environ.get("TQENC_HIP_LIB", ""),
                 str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "build-tqenc" / "libtqenc_hip.so")]
        last = None
        for c in cands:
            if not c:
                continue
            try:
                _hip = ctypes.CDLL(c)
                break
            except OSError as e:
                last = e
        if _hip is None:
            raise RuntimeError("libtqenc_hip.so not found: %s" % last)
        _hip.tqh_encode.restype = ctypes.c_double
        _hip.tqh_encode.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int64, ctypes.c_void_p,
                                    ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p,
                                    ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int]
    return _hip


def encode(w: np.ndarray, t: int, h: np.ndarray | None = None, iters: int = 1, ncand: int = 1, exact: int = 0,
           scale_tries: int = 1, threads: int = 0, gpu: bool = False):
    """w: float32 array whose last axis is a multiple of 128.  Returns (packed uint8 [nblocks, block_bytes],
    per-block error float64 [nblocks], total error, stats dict).  Error = sum h (w - decoded)^2 (h = 1 if None)."""
    w = np.ascontiguousarray(w, dtype=np.float32)
    if w.shape[-1] % BLOCK:
        raise ValueError("last axis %d is not a multiple of 128" % w.shape[-1])
    nb = w.size // BLOCK
    out = np.zeros((nb, block_bytes(t)), dtype=np.uint8)
    err = np.zeros(nb, dtype=np.float64)
    stats = np.zeros(2, dtype=np.int64)
    hp = None
    if h is not None:
        h = np.ascontiguousarray(h, dtype=np.float32)
        if h.shape != w.shape:
            raise ValueError("importance weights must have the shape of w")
        hp = h.ctypes.data
    if gpu:
        if exact or t == TQ2_T:
            raise ValueError("the GPU encoder has no exact search and no TQ2_T")
        with _gpu_lock() as gl:
            if gl.ok:
                tot = hip_lib().tqh_encode(t, w.ctypes.data, hp, nb, out.ctypes.data, iters, ncand, scale_tries, 0,
                                           err.ctypes.data, stats.ctypes.data, None, 0)
                return out, err, tot, {"nonfinite_blocks": int(stats[0]), "zero_blocks": int(stats[1])}
        threads = int(os.environ.get("TQENC_CPU_THREADS", threads or 24))   # the card stayed busy: the CPU encoder, same blocks
    tot = lib().tqe_encode(t, w.ctypes.data, hp, nb, out.ctypes.data, iters, ncand, exact, scale_tries, threads,
                           err.ctypes.data, stats.ctypes.data)
    return out, err, tot, {"nonfinite_blocks": int(stats[0]), "zero_blocks": int(stats[1])}


def decode(packed: np.ndarray, t: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """packed: uint8 array of whole blocks.  Returns float32 [nblocks * 128] (d * codebook)."""
    packed = np.ascontiguousarray(packed, dtype=np.uint8)
    bb = block_bytes(t)
    if packed.size % bb:
        raise ValueError("%d bytes is not a whole number of %s blocks" % (packed.size, TYPE_NAMES[t]))
    nb = packed.size // bb
    out = np.zeros(nb * BLOCK, dtype=np.float32)
    lib().tqe_decode(t, packed.ctypes.data, nb, out.ctypes.data)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Hadamard

def hadamard_matrix(n: int = BLOCK) -> np.ndarray:
    """The normalized Sylvester-Walsh-Hadamard matrix (entry (-1)^popcount(r & c) / sqrt(n)); symmetric, orthonormal."""
    h = np.array([[1.0]])
    while h.shape[0] < n:
        h = np.block([[h, h], [h, -h]])
    return (h / np.sqrt(n)).astype(np.float32)


def make_signs(width: int, seed: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A reproducible +1/-1 vector (the plan's D).  The vector itself, not the seed, is what a file must store."""
    r = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return (r.integers(0, 2, size=width) * 2 - 1).astype(np.float32)


def pack_signs(signs: np.ndarray) -> bytes:
    return np.packbits((signs > 0).astype(np.uint8), bitorder="little").tobytes()


def unpack_signs(b: bytes, width: int) -> np.ndarray:
    bits = np.unpackbits(np.frombuffer(b, dtype=np.uint8), bitorder="little")[:width]
    return bits.astype(np.float32) * 2 - 1


def rotate(w: np.ndarray, signs: np.ndarray | None) -> np.ndarray:
    """The input transform U = H D on the last axis, per 128-block: Wrot = W U^T, i.e. each row w -> H (signs * w).
    The same function applied to an activation x gives U x."""
    w = np.asarray(w, dtype=np.float32)
    if signs is not None:
        w = w * signs
    shp = w.shape
    return (w.reshape(-1, BLOCK) @ hadamard_matrix()).reshape(shp)   # H is symmetric


def unrotate(w: np.ndarray, signs: np.ndarray | None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Inverse of rotate (H is its own inverse: orthonormal and symmetric; then the signs)."""
    shp = w.shape
    x = (np.asarray(w, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1, BLOCK) @ hadamard_matrix()).reshape(shp)
    return x * signs if signs is not None else x


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- metrics

def sqnr_db(ref: np.ndarray, approx: np.ndarray) -> float:
    ref = np.asarray(ref, dtype=np.float64).ravel()
    e = np.sum((ref - np.asarray(approx, dtype=np.float64).ravel()) ** 2)
    return float("inf") if e == 0 else float(10 * np.log10(np.sum(ref ** 2) / e))


def rel_mse(ref: np.ndarray, approx: np.ndarray) -> float:
    ref = np.asarray(ref, dtype=np.float64).ravel()
    return float(np.sum((ref - np.asarray(approx, dtype=np.float64).ravel()) ** 2) / max(np.sum(ref ** 2), 1e-300))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- .tqx container
# A small versioned file for ONE encoded matrix (research artifacts; not a GGUF).  Little endian:
#   "TQXP" | u32 version (1) | u32 type id | u32 rows | u32 cols | u32 flags (bit 0: input Hadamard, 128-blocks)
#   | u32 n_sign_bytes | sign bits (1 = +1, LSB first, one per input column) | u32 hadamard block (128) | packed blocks
# An unknown version or type is refused before any data is read.
TQX_MAGIC = b"TQXP"
TQX_VERSION = 2   # 2: types 224 / 225 are the computed codebook; a version 1 file means the point table (226 / 227)


def write_tqx(path, t: int, rows: int, cols: int, packed: np.ndarray, signs: np.ndarray | None) -> None:
    import struct
    sb = pack_signs(signs) if signs is not None else b""
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(TQX_MAGIC + struct.pack("<IIIIII", TQX_VERSION, t, rows, cols, 1 if signs is not None else 0, len(sb)))
        f.write(sb)
        f.write(struct.pack("<I", BLOCK))
        f.write(np.ascontiguousarray(packed, dtype=np.uint8).tobytes())


def read_tqx(path):
    import struct
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    if data[:4] != TQX_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError("not a TQXP file")
    ver, t, rows, cols, flags, nsb = struct.unpack_from("<IIIIII", data, 4)
    if ver == 1 and t in (TQK5X, TQK4X):
        t += 2   # a version 1 file: the point table
    elif ver != TQX_VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported TQXP version %d (this reader handles %d, and 1 for the point-table K5 / K4)" % (ver, TQX_VERSION))
    if t not in KBITS:
        raise ValueError("unknown trellis type %d" % t)
    at = 4 + 24
    signs = unpack_signs(data[at:at + nsb], cols) if flags & 1 else None
    at += nsb
    (blk,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, at)
    at += 4
    if blk != BLOCK:
        raise ValueError("unsupported Hadamard block %d" % blk)
    nb = rows * (cols // BLOCK)
    packed = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.uint8, count=nb * block_bytes(t), offset=at).reshape(nb, block_bytes(t))
    return t, rows, cols, packed, signs


## tools/_paths.py

"""tools/_paths.py - where the tools find llama.cpp's gguf-py (for the MTP packer and the fixtures).

Order: $STRATA_GGUF_PY, then <engine>/third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py (what setup.py clones), then the development
tree's ../../.ref/llama.cpp/gguf-py, then (#3269) the install folders: in the Control package setup.py writes third_party/
to the per-user install folder ($STRATA_INSTALL_DIR, else the app's folder, the Terminal's remembered installs), not
beside the tools, so a tool run by hand from the package finds it there.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ENGINE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def _install_dirs() -> list[Path]:
    """The per-user install folders a Control-mode setup.py writes third_party/ into. Best effort: never raises."""
    out: list[Path] = []
    raw = os.environ.get("STRATA_INSTALL_DIR")
    if raw:
        out.append(Path(raw).expanduser())
    try:
        if str(ENGINE) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.append(str(ENGINE))
        from strata_control import discovery
        out.append(discovery.app_install_dir())
        out += [pl.path for pl in discovery.places(here=ENGINE)]
    except Exception:
        pass
    return out


def gguf_py() -> str:
    cands = [os.environ.get("STRATA_GGUF_PY"), ENGINE / "third_party" / "llama.cpp" / "gguf-py",
             ENGINE.parents[min(1, len(ENGINE.parents) - 1)] / ".ref" / "llama.cpp" / "gguf-py"]   # the dev tree; a shallow install (G:\Strata) has no grandparent
    cands += [d / "third_party" / "llama.cpp" / "gguf-py" for d in _install_dirs()]
    for c in cands:
        if c and (Path(c) / "gguf").is_dir():
            return str(c)
    sys.exit("llama.cpp's gguf-py was not found. Set STRATA_GGUF_PY to the gguf-py folder of any llama.cpp checkout "
             "(<llama.cpp>/gguf-py), or run setup.py once (it downloads llama.cpp into third_party/ of the install "
             "folder; in the desktop app or the Terminal package that folder is STRATA_INSTALL_DIR, which this tool also "
             "looks in)")


def add_gguf_py() -> None:
    p = gguf_py()
    if p not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, p)


## tools/ab_engine.py

"""A/B two engine builds or environments on one config: restart the server per arm, alternate arms over rounds.

    python tools/ab_engine.py strata-q2_0.json A:exe=/path/a B:exe=/path/b,STRATA_EXP_MODE=0 [--rounds 3]

An arm is NAME:key=value,...; `exe` replaces the config's engine, `xargs` appends ';'-separated engine arguments,
every other key is set in the engine's environment.  Each round starts the server once per arm (the arms' order alternates), warms it up with one short
answer, then sends the same requests: greedy, fixed prompts, a short chat set and one long prompt.  Prints the
server's own timings (llama.cpp's `timings`: decode and prompt tokens per second) per request and the per-arm
medians.  Decode numbers move run to run (the adaptive expert tier, the OS), so compare medians over rounds.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROMPTS = (
    "Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists into one sorted list, with a docstring and two tests.",
    "Explain in two paragraphs how a refrigerator moves heat from inside to outside.",
    "List ten practical tips for learning a new language as an adult, one sentence each.",
)


def long_prompt(words: int) -> str:
    rng = random.Random(7)
    vocab = ("river stone market lantern copper winter garden signal harbor needle orbit velvet canyon ember "
             "ledger quartz meadow anchor violet thunder").split()
    body = " ".join(rng.choice(vocab) for _ in range(words))
    return f"Here is a list of words:\n{body}\n\nSummarize what kinds of words appear in the list, in five sentences."


def post(port: int, prompt: str, max_tokens: int) -> dict:
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": max_tokens,
                         "temperature": 0, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read())


def wait_ready(port: int, proc: subprocess.Popen, timeout: float = 1800) -> None:
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"server exited with {proc.returncode}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/models", timeout=5) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    post(port, "Say hi.", 8)
                    return
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(3)
    raise TimeoutError("server not ready")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("config")
    ap.add_argument("arms", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8090)
    ap.add_argument("--max-new", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--long-words", type=int, default=6000)
    ap.add_argument("--log", default="ab_engine.jsonl")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    base = json.loads(Path(a.config).read_text())
    arms = []
    for s in a.arms:
        name, _, kv = s.partition(":")
        env = dict(x.split("=", 1) for x in kv.split(",") if x)
        arms.append((name, env))
    reqs = [(f"chat{i}", p) for i, p in enumerate(PROMPTS)] + [("long", long_prompt(a.long_words))]
    out = open(a.log, "a")
    res: dict = {n: {} for n, _ in arms}
    for rnd in range(a.rounds):
        order = arms if rnd % 2 == 0 else arms[::-1]
        for name, env in order:
            cfg = dict(base)
            e = dict(env)
            if "exe" in e:
                cfg["exe"] = e.pop("exe")
            if "xargs" in e:                       # extra engine arguments, ';'-separated
                cfg["args"] = list(base["args"]) + e.pop("xargs").split(";")
            cfg["port"] = a.port
            cfg["log"] = str(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"ab_{name}_r{rnd}.log")
            cpath = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"ab_{name}.json"
            cpath.write_text(json.dumps(cfg, indent=1))
            penv = dict(os.environ, **e)
            proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "serve" / "server.py"), "--engine", "strata", "--config",
                                     str(cpath), "--port", str(a.port)], cwd=str(ROOT), env=penv,
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            try:
                t0 = time.time()
                wait_ready(a.port, proc)
                print(f"round {rnd} {name}: ready in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s", flush=True)
                for tag, p in reqs:
                    r = post(a.port, p, a.max_new)
                    t = r.get("timings", {})
                    row = {"round": rnd, "arm": name, "req": tag, "decode": t.get("predicted_per_second"),
                           "prompt": t.get("prompt_per_second"), "prompt_n": t.get("prompt_n"),
                           "n": r.get("usage", {}).get("completion_tokens"),
                           "text": r["choices"][0]["message"].get("content", "")[:80]}
                    out.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
                    out.flush()
                    res[name].setdefault(tag, []).append(row)
                    print(f"  {tag:6s} decode {row['decode']} tok/s  prompt {row['prompt']} tok/s ({row['prompt_n']})  "
                          f"n {row['n']}", flush=True)
            finally:
                proc.terminate()
                try:
                    proc.wait(60)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    proc.kill()
                time.sleep(5)
    print("\nmedians over rounds:")
    for tag, _ in reqs:
        cells = []
        for name, _ in arms:
            rows = res[name].get(tag, [])
            d = statistics.median([x["decode"] for x in rows if x["decode"]]) if rows else float("nan")
            pr = statistics.median([x["prompt"] for x in rows if x["prompt"]]) if rows else float("nan")
            cells.append(f"{name}: decode {d:6.1f}  prompt {pr:7.1f}")
        print(f"  {tag:6s} | " + " | ".join(cells))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())


## tools/agent_turns_bench.py

"""Decode A/B on coding-agent turns over this repository: arms restarted per round, per-turn ratios.

    python tools/agent_turns_bench.py strata-iq2_xs.json base: hcq8:STRATA_HC_Q8=2 [--rounds 2]

The workload is five simulated coding-agent sessions over this repository's own files (README, serve/, setup.py, the
expert cache, the hyper-connection kernels, the tokenizer): a system prompt, four tools, a task (three in English, two
in French), then tool calls whose results are the real files, at most 2,000 lines per read as agents' read tools
return them.  Every point right after a tool result is one turn the model continues - 23 turns from ~2.5K to ~100K
tokens with the repository as of 0.1.41, consecutive turns sharing their prefix as in a real session.  Nothing
personal and nothing downloaded: anyone with this checkout gets the same requests.

Arms are given as ab_engine.py takes them (NAME:key=value,...; `exe` replaces the engine, `xargs` appends
';'-separated engine arguments, any other key goes to the engine's environment).  The rounds mirror the arm order
(A B, B A, ...), each arm on a fresh server.  Sampling is the agent's (temperature 1, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, a fixed
seed), 256 new tokens per turn.  The result is the server's own decode tok/s per turn and, per arm, the median of the
per-turn ratios to the first arm with the number of turns it won: a whole-session median hides which turns moved.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from ab_engine import wait_ready  # noqa: E402

SYSTEM = ("You are an autonomous coding agent working in the user's repository. You can read files, search the code, "
          "edit files and run commands with the tools below. Work step by step: read the code you need before changing "
          "it, make small and correct edits, keep the existing style, and explain briefly what you did. Never invent "
          "file contents: read them. When the task is done, give a short summary of the changes and how to test them.")

TOOLS = [
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "read_file", "description": "Read a file of the repository (UTF-8 text).",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string", "description": "path from the repository root"}},
                       "required": ["path"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "grep", "description": "Search the repository for a regular expression; returns matching lines.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"pattern": {"type": "string"}, "path": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["pattern"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "edit_file", "description": "Replace an exact string in a file with a new one.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "old": {"type": "string"},
                                                        "new": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path", "old", "new"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "run", "description": "Run a shell command in the repository and return its output.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["command"]}}},
]

# (name, task, [(tool, argument, what the assistant says before the call)])
SESSIONS = [
    ("server-option",
     "Add a `--max-queue N` option to the HTTP server that rejects new chat requests with HTTP 503 when N requests are "
     "already waiting, document it in the README's settings section, and add a test.",
     [("read_file", "README.md", "I'll start with the README to see how settings are documented."),
      ("grep", "add_argument", "Now let me find where the server parses its options."),
      ("read_file", "serve/server.py", "The options are in serve/server.py; reading it."),
      ("read_file", "serve/frontend.py", "Requests go through the frontend; let me read it too."),
      ("read_file", "docs/DETAILS.md", "Checking DETAILS.md for the existing API documentation style.")]),
    ("expert-cache",
     "Explain precisely how the expert cache decides which experts stay in VRAM during decode, then propose and "
     "implement a small improvement to its eviction policy with a measurement plan.",
     [("read_file", "docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md", "Let me read the design overview first."),
      ("read_file", "include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp", "Now the cache's interface."),
      ("read_file", "src/core/expert_cache.cpp", "And its implementation."),
      ("grep", "adapt_every", "Searching for the adaptive swap logic."),
      ("read_file", "src/core/expert_source.cpp", "The dispatch that consults the cache is in expert_source.cpp.")]),
    ("installer-fr",
     "Dans l'installateur, la détection de la RAM disponible se trompe parfois sous Windows quand un autre programme "
     "réserve beaucoup de mémoire. Trouve où elle est faite, corrige-la, ajoute un test et explique la correction en "
     "français.",
     [("read_file", "setup.py", "Je commence par lire l'installateur."),
      ("grep", "def .*ram", "Je cherche les fonctions qui mesurent la RAM."),
      ("read_file", "docs/INSTALL.md", "Je vérifie ce que la documentation promet sur la RAM."),
      ("read_file", "docs/MODELS.md", "Le choix du modèle dépend de la RAM ; je lis cette page aussi.")]),
    ("cuda-kernel",
     "The hyper-connection read kernels are latency bound on small batches. Read them, explain where the time goes, "
     "and write a faster variant for 1-4 tokens that keeps the same results bit for bit.",
     [("read_file", "include/strata/kernels/fused_gr.hpp", "First the kernel interface."),
      ("read_file", "src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu", "Now the kernels themselves."),
      ("grep", "fused_gr_read_multi", "Where are they called from?"),
      ("read_file", "src/core/verify.cpp", "The verify window calls them; reading it.")]),
    ("tokenizer-fr",
     "Écris une suite de tests pytest pour le tokenizer Python (encodage, décodage, tokens spéciaux, texte multilingue, "
     "cas limites), puis corrige les bugs que les tests révèlent. Réponds en français.",
     [("read_file", "tools/strata_tokenizer.py", "Je lis d'abord le tokenizer."),
      ("grep", "strata_tokenizer", "Je cherche qui l'utilise."),
      ("read_file", "serve/frontend.py", "Le frontend l'appelle ; je le lis pour voir les usages réels."),
      ("read_file", "serve/chat_template.jinja", "Je regarde aussi le modèle de conversation."),
      ("read_file", "chat.py", "Et le client en ligne de commande.")]),
]


def tool_result(tool: str, arg: str) -> str:
    if tool == "read_file":
        lines = (ROOT / arg).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
        text = "\n".join(lines[:2000])
        return text + (f"\n... (truncated: lines 1-2000 of {len(lines)})" if len(lines) > 2000 else "")
    if tool == "grep":
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "grep", "-n", "-I", "-E", arg], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        lines = r.stdout.splitlines()
        return "\n".join(lines[:200]) + (f"\n... ({len(lines) - 200} more lines)" if len(lines) > 200 else "")
    raise ValueError(tool)


def turns() -> list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]:
    """[(tag, messages)]: one entry per point right after a tool result."""
    out = []
    for name, task, steps in SESSIONS:
        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": task}]
        for i, (tool, arg, before) in enumerate(steps):
            cid = f"call_{name}_{i}"
            args = {"path": arg} if tool == "read_file" else {"pattern": arg}
            msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": before,
                         "tool_calls": [{"id": cid, "type": "function",
                                         "function": {"name": tool, "arguments": json.dumps(args)}}]})
            msgs.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": cid, "content": tool_result(tool, arg)})
            out.append((f"{name}.{i}", [dict(m) for m in msgs]))
    return out


def post(port: int, messages: list[dict], max_tokens: int, seed: int) -> dict:
    body = {"messages": messages, "tools": TOOLS, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95,
            "top_k": 20, "seed": seed, "reasoning_effort": "high"}
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ.get("STRATA_BENCH_KEY", "")})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=3600) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read())


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("config")
    ap.add_argument("arms", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8090)
    ap.add_argument("--max-new", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--max-turns", type=int, default=0, help="only the first N turns (0: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1234)
    ap.add_argument("--log", default="agent_turns_bench.jsonl")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    base = json.loads(Path(a.config).read_text())
    arms = []
    for s in a.arms:
        name, _, kv = s.partition(":")
        arms.append((name, dict(x.split("=", 1) for x in kv.split(",") if x)))
    work = turns()
    if a.max_turns:
        work = work[:a.max_turns]
    out = open(a.log, "a")
    res: dict = {n: {} for n, _ in arms}
    for rnd in range(a.rounds):
        for name, env in (arms if rnd % 2 == 0 else arms[::-1]):
            cfg = dict(base)
            e = dict(env)
            if "exe" in e:
                cfg["exe"] = e.pop("exe")
            if "xargs" in e:
                cfg["args"] = list(base["args"]) + e.pop("xargs").split(";")
            cfg["port"] = a.port
            cfg["log"] = str(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"agent_turns_{name}_r{rnd}.log")
            cpath = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"agent_turns_{name}.json"
            cpath.write_text(json.dumps(cfg, indent=1))
            proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "serve" / "server.py"), "--engine", "strata", "--config",
                                     str(cpath), "--port", str(a.port)], cwd=str(ROOT), env=dict(os.environ, **e),
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            try:
                t0 = time.time()
                wait_ready(a.port, proc)
                print(f"round {rnd} {name}: ready in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s", flush=True)
                for tag, msgs in work:
                    r = post(a.port, msgs, a.max_new, a.seed)
                    t = r.get("timings", {})
                    row = {"round": rnd, "arm": name, "turn": tag, "decode": t.get("predicted_per_second"),
                           "prompt_n": t.get("prompt_n"), "prompt": t.get("prompt_per_second"),
                           "n": r.get("usage", {}).get("completion_tokens")}
                    out.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
                    out.flush()
                    res[name].setdefault(tag, []).append(row)
                    print(f"  {tag:16s} decode {row['decode']} tok/s  prompt {row['prompt_n']} tokens", flush=True)
            finally:
                proc.terminate()
                try:
                    proc.wait(60)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    proc.kill()
                time.sleep(5)
    first = arms[0][0]

    def per_turn(name: str, tag: str) -> float:
        v = [x["decode"] for x in res[name].get(tag, []) if x["decode"]]
        return statistics.mean(v) if v else float("nan")

    print(f"\nper-turn decode ratio to {first} (mean over rounds per turn, then the median over turns):")
    for name, _ in arms:
        med = statistics.median([per_turn(name, t) for t, _ in work])
        if name == first:
            print(f"  {name:10s} median decode {med:6.1f} tok/s")
            continue
        r = [per_turn(name, t) / per_turn(first, t) for t, _ in work]
        print(f"  {name:10s} median decode {med:6.1f} tok/s   x{statistics.median(r):.3f} (x{min(r):.2f} to "
              f"x{max(r):.2f}), {sum(x > 1 for x in r)}/{len(r)} turns faster")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())


## tools/batch_groups_cache_test.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""#1604: with --batch N --batch-groups N on a layer split, two long conversations that alternate must reuse their slot
(or the conversation cache) on every later turn instead of reading their prompt from token 0.

  python3 tools/batch_groups_cache_test.py CFG OUT.json
  STRATA_EXTRA_ARGS="--batch 2 --batch-groups 2 --prompt-cache 4 --conversation-cache-mib 4096 --conversation-cache-slots 3"

Three rounds; each round runs conversation A and conversation B at the same time (so both go through the batch slots),
the next round continues each one (prompt + its answer + a new user turn).  The engine log says per request how many
prompt tokens were reused.  PASS when every request of rounds 2 and 3 reused at least 90 % of the previous round's
prompt.  The answers (token ids) are written to OUT.json to compare two runs.
"""
import json, os, re, sys, threading
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(os.environ.get("STRATA_REPO", Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "tools")); sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
import strata_tokenizer as ST
from serve.server import StrataEngine, child_env, engine_args

cfg = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
tp = Path(cfg["tokenizer"])
vocab = json.loads((tp / "vocab.json").read_text())
toks = [None] * len(vocab)
for t, i in vocab.items():
    toks[i] = t
tok = ST.Tokenizer(toks, (tp / "merges.txt").read_text().split("\n"), json.loads((tp / "token_type.json").read_text()))
if os.environ.get("GPUS"):   # e.g. GPUS=0,1: a layer split over those cards (SPLIT=auto)
    cfg["gpu"] = [int(x) for x in os.environ["GPUS"].split(",")]
    cfg["layer_split"] = os.environ.get("SPLIT", "auto")
args = engine_args(cfg) + os.environ.get("STRATA_EXTRA_ARGS", "").split()
log = os.environ.get("SMOKE_LOG", cfg["log"])
eng = StrataEngine(os.environ.get("STRATA_EXE", cfg["exe"]), args, cwd=cfg.get("cwd"), log=log, env=child_env(cfg))
GEN = "<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n"


def enc(text):
    return tok.encode(text, parse_special=True)


def first(tag, n):
    return enc(f"<|im_start|>user\n[{tag}] " + " ".join(f"Entry {i} of {tag}: value {i * 13 % 97}." for i in range(n))
               + "\nCount from 1 to 80 separated by commas." + GEN)


conv = {"A": first("alpha", 250), "B": first("bravo", 250)}
answers = {"A": [], "B": []}
prev_len = {}
rounds = []


def one(name, ids, out):
    res = [t for t in eng.generate(ids, 80, {"temperature": 0}, threading.Event()) if t is not None]
    out[name] = res


for rnd in range(3):
    lens = {k: len(v) for k, v in conv.items()}
    out = {}
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=one, args=(k, conv[k], out)) for k in ("A", "B")]
    for t in ts:
        t.start()
    for t in ts:
        t.join()
    rounds.append({"prompt_lens": lens, "answers": out})
    print(f"round {rnd + 1}: prompts {lens}, answers {[len(v) for v in out.values()]}", flush=True)
    for k in conv:
        answers[k].append(out[k])
        conv[k] = conv[k] + out[k] + enc(f"<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nNow count from {rnd + 2} to {rnd + 60}." + GEN)
eng.proc.stdin.close()
try:
    eng.proc.wait(60)
except Exception:
    eng.proc.kill()
json.dump(rounds, open(sys.argv[2], "w"))

text = open(log, errors="replace").read()
reqs = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in re.findall(r"strata serve: prompt (\d+) tokens = (\d+) reused", text)]
print("requests (prompt tokens, reused):", reqs)
print("slot gave back lines:", len(re.findall(r"gave back", text)), " conversation cache restores:",
      len(re.findall(r"conversation cache: restored", text)))
# rounds 2 and 3 are the last 4 requests of the log
ok = len(reqs) >= 6
for p, r in reqs[2:]:
    if r < 0.9 * (p - 140):   # the previous prompt + answer is ~all of it but the new turn
        ok = False
print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


## tools/batch_interleave_test.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Batch slots, the parts batch_test.py does not reach (#465): a long prompt read WHILE other slots decode (its
chunks interleaved with their windows), and a conversation's next turn continued from the slot that holds it.

  1. solo references (GEN): A, then A's next turn (from the live session), B, C (a long prompt)
  2. the same in the slots: A in slot 0, B in slot 1 next to it, then C in slot 2 while A and B decode - every slot's
     tokens must equal its solo tokens
  3. A's next turn (BGEN into slot 0, which still holds A): read from the slot, its tokens must equal the solo next turn
  4. a long prompt D gives way (BYIELD) at its first chunk boundary, a short E is admitted, D goes on from its slot
     while E decodes: both equal their solo tokens.  On a pipelined batch (a layer split, more than one group) a read
     never gives way: D is then read whole into slot 2 and E admitted into slot 1 beside it; both must still equal
     solo, only the give-way is not required (--yield auto; --yield expect requires it anyway)
  6. A in a slot, stopped after 50 tokens and continued on the solo path (GEN of A + its tokens, from the slot): the
     whole equals solo A (what the server does with a request left alone in a slot)
  5. (a measurement) a solo next turn continued from a slot: the drafts accepted
  7. F, A's history as a client sends it back without the reply's thinking, from slot 1's turn checkpoint: equal to
     F solo (which continues from the same checkpoint of the live chain)
     (after step 6 the solo path holds A's start, so F's start comes from the live chain or the prompt cache here)
  7b. A in slot 1 to its end, --flush unrelated solo GENs, then F2 (A's question, another reply) into slot 2: its
     start can only come from slot 1's turn checkpoint; equal to F2 solo.  The engine log line says which source was used.

Exact comparisons need the same settings as batch_test.py (this script sets STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1):
  python tools/batch_interleave_test.py --exe build/strata --config strata-<model>.json \\
      --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000 --no-prefill-borrow"
Without --no-prefill-borrow the slots decoding during C's read see the expert cache without the slots C's prompt
borrowed (those experts run on the CPU, which rounds differently): A's and B's text may then drift from solo.
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from batch_test import Engine, tokenizer  # noqa: E402

LONG = ("The history of mathematics is long and full of surprising turns. Early civilizations counted with tally marks, "
        "then with symbols, and later with place-value systems that made arithmetic far easier. ")


def run(eng, out, line, slot=None):
    """Send one GEN/BGEN; returns (tokens of the request line, the BADM flag) - BT/BDONE of other slots are kept."""
    eng.send(line)
    got = []
    for l in out:
        if l.startswith("T "):
            got.append(int(l.split()[1]))
        elif l.startswith(("BT ", "BDONE ")):
            eng.pending.append(l)
        elif l.startswith("ERR"):
            raise SystemExit("engine: " + l)
        elif slot is None and l.startswith("DONE"):
            return got, None
        elif slot is not None and l.startswith("BADM "):
            return got, l.split()[2] == "1"
    raise SystemExit(f"the engine ended during: {line[:40]} (see {eng.log_path})")


def engine_pipelined(eng, extra):
    """Does the engine run the batch in pipelined groups (a layer split, more than one group)?  Then a BYIELD is
    dropped: a pipelined read never gives way."""
    if "--batch-groups" in extra:
        v = extra[extra.index("--batch-groups") + 1] if extra.index("--batch-groups") + 1 < len(extra) else ""
        if v.isdigit():
            return int(v) > 1
    eng.log.flush()
    m = re.search(r"--batch-groups auto: (\d+) groups? of", Path(eng.log_path).read_text(errors="replace"))
    return bool(m) and int(m.group(1)) > 1


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--exe", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--max-new", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--long", type=int, default=5000, help="tokens of the long prompt C (several prompt chunks)")
    ap.add_argument("--extra", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--yield", dest="yield_mode", choices=("auto", "expect", "skip"), default="auto",
                    help="step 4's give-way: auto = expect a YIELDED unless the batch is pipelined (the engine log "
                         "says '--batch-groups auto: N groups' with N > 1, or --extra has --batch-groups N > 1), "
                         "where a read never gives way; expect = always required; skip = never required")
    ap.add_argument("--flush", type=int, default=8,
                    help="7b: unrelated solo GENs between A in slot 1 and F, so only the slot holds A's start (0: off)")
    ap.add_argument("--dump", default="", help="write every solo and slot token list as JSON: an A/B of two builds")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cfg = json.loads(Path(a.config).read_text())
    tok = tokenizer(cfg["tokenizer"])

    def chat(q):
        return tok.encode(f"<|im_start|>user\n{q}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n",
                          parse_special=True)
    body = LONG * (a.long // max(1, len(tok.encode(LONG))) + 1)
    A = chat("Write a Python function that merges overlapping intervals, then explain it.")
    B = chat("Compare TCP and QUIC: handshake, congestion control, multiplexing.")
    C = chat(body + "\nSummarize the text above in three sentences.")
    D = chat(body + "\nWhat are the three most important ideas in the text above?")
    E = chat("Describe the life cycle of a star like the Sun.")
    print(f"prompts: A {len(A)}, B {len(B)}, C {len(C)} tokens", flush=True)
    eng = Engine(a.exe, cfg, 3, {"STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN": "1"}, a.extra.split())
    eng.pending = []
    out = eng.lines()
    ids = lambda v: ",".join(map(str, v))
    M = a.max_new

    # 1. solo
    sA, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(A)}")
    A2 = A + sA + chat("Now do the same in Rust.")
    sA2, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(A2)}")
    # F: A's history as a client sends it back WITHOUT the reply's thinking - it shares A only up to A's last turn
    # boundary (the checkpoint there); solo it continues from that checkpoint of the live chain
    turn_at = max(i for i, t in enumerate(A) if t == A[0])          # A[0] is <|im_start|>
    F = A[:turn_at] + tok.encode("<|im_start|>assistant\nA short answer.<|im_end|>\n", parse_special=True) + \
        chat("Now in Go.")
    sF, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(F)}")
    # F2 (step 7b): another reply to A's question - it too shares A only up to A's turn checkpoint
    F2 = A[:turn_at] + tok.encode("<|im_start|>assistant\nAnother short answer.<|im_end|>\n", parse_special=True) + \
        chat("Now in C.")
    sF2, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(F2)}") if a.flush > 0 else ([], None)
    sB, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(B)}")
    sC, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(C)}")
    sD, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(D)}")
    sE, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M} {ids(E)}")
    print(f"solo: A {len(sA)}, A2 {len(sA2)}, B {len(sB)}, C {len(sC)}, D {len(sD)}, E {len(sE)} tokens", flush=True)

    # 2. the slots: A, B, then the long C while they decode
    got = {0: [], 1: [], 2: []}
    done = {}
    t0 = time.time()
    for s, P in ((0, A), (1, B), (2, C)):
        first, cont = run(eng, out, f"BGEN {s} {M} {ids(P)}", slot=s)
        got[s] += first
        if not cont:
            done[s] = True
    t_admit = time.time() - t0
    during_c = sum(1 for l in eng.pending if l.startswith("BT "))   # windows the slots ran while C was admitted

    def drain():
        while eng.pending or len(done) < 3:
            l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
            if l.startswith("BT "):
                _, s, y = l.split()
                got[int(s)].append(int(y))
            elif l.startswith("BDONE "):
                done[int(l.split()[1])] = True
            elif l.startswith("ERR"):
                raise SystemExit("engine: " + l)
    drain()
    print(f"slots: admissions {t_admit:.1f}s; {during_c} slot tokens arrived while the admissions read their prompts",
          flush=True)
    ok = True
    for s, ref, name in ((0, sA, "A"), (1, sB, "B"), (2, sC, "C")):
        same = got[s] == ref
        ok &= same
        d = next((k for k in range(min(len(got[s]), len(ref))) if got[s][k] != ref[k]), None)
        print(f"slot {s} ({name}): {len(got[s])} tokens, solo {len(ref)}: "
              f"{'IDENTICAL' if same else f'DIFFERS at {d}'}", flush=True)

    # 3. A's next turn from slot 0 (the engine's log says "slot 0 gave back ...")
    first, cont = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 0 {M} {ids(A2)}", slot=0)
    got2, done = first, {}
    if cont:
        while True:
            l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
            if l.startswith("BT 0 "):
                got2.append(int(l.split()[2]))
            elif l.startswith("BDONE 0 "):
                break
    same = got2 == sA2
    ok &= same
    d = next((k for k in range(min(len(got2), len(sA2))) if got2[k] != sA2[k]), None)
    print(f"A's next turn from its slot: {len(got2)} tokens, solo {len(sA2)}: "
          f"{'IDENTICAL' if same else f'DIFFERS at {d}'}", flush=True)
    # 4. a long prompt D gives way (BYIELD) to a short E at its first chunk boundary, then goes on from its slot.
    # On a pipelined batch (a layer split with more than one group) a read never gives way (generate.cpp: the BYIELD
    # is dropped): D is then admitted whole into slot 2 and E goes into the free slot 1 while D decodes - both must
    # still equal solo, only the give-way itself is not checked (--yield)
    pipelined = engine_pipelined(eng, a.extra.split())
    expect_yield = a.yield_mode == "expect" or (a.yield_mode == "auto" and not pipelined)
    eng.send(f"BGEN 2 {M} {ids(D)}")
    eng.send("BYIELD 2")
    yielded, firstD, contD = None, [], None
    for l in out:
        if l.startswith("T "):
            firstD.append(int(l.split()[1]))
        elif l.startswith("YIELDED "):
            yielded = l
        elif l.startswith(("BT ", "BDONE ")):
            eng.pending.append(l)
        elif l.startswith("ERR"):
            raise SystemExit("engine: " + l)
        elif l.startswith("BADM 2 "):
            contD = l.split()[2] == "1"
            break
    if yielded is not None:
        print(f"D gave way: {yielded}", flush=True)
    elif expect_yield:
        print(f"D gave way: None (expected a YIELDED: batch {'pipelined' if pipelined else 'not pipelined'})",
              flush=True)
        ok = False
    else:
        print(f"D gave way: None - the batch is pipelined ({pipelined}), where a read never gives way; D stays in "
              f"slot 2 ({len(firstD)} first tokens, {'continues' if contD else 'done'}), E goes into slot 1 beside it",
              flush=True)
    got4 = {1: [], 2: []}
    first, cont1 = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 1 {M} {ids(E)}", slot=1)
    got4[1] += first
    if yielded is not None:
        first, cont2 = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 2 {M} {ids(D)}", slot=2)
        got4[2] += first
    else:   # D never left slot 2: its tokens so far are the read's first ones plus the BT 2 lines kept in pending
        got4[2] += firstD
        cont2 = contD
    done4 = {s for s, c in ((1, cont1), (2, cont2)) if not c}
    while len(done4) < 2:
        l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
        if l.startswith("BT "):
            _, s, y = l.split()
            if int(s) in got4 and int(s) not in done4:
                got4[int(s)].append(int(y))
        elif l.startswith("BDONE "):
            done4.add(int(l.split()[1]))
        elif l.startswith("ERR"):
            raise SystemExit("engine: " + l)
    for s, ref, name in ((1, sE, "E (short, admitted while D waited)"), (2, sD, "D (gave way, then went on)" if yielded else "D (read whole, E admitted beside it)")):
        same = got4[s] == ref
        ok &= same
        d = next((k for k in range(min(len(got4[s]), len(ref))) if got4[s][k] != ref[k]), None)
        print(f"slot {s} {name}: {len(got4[s])} tokens, solo {len(ref)}: "
              f"{'IDENTICAL' if same else f'DIFFERS at {d}'}", flush=True)
    # 6. back to the solo path (what the server does with a request left alone in a slot): A in slot 1, BSTOP after
    # 50 tokens, then GEN of A + what it produced - the engine continues from the slot with MTP drafts again
    first, cont = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 1 {M} {ids(A)}", slot=1)
    got6, sent = list(first), False
    while cont:
        l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
        if l.startswith("BT 1 "):
            got6.append(int(l.split()[2]))
            if len(got6) >= 50 and not sent:
                eng.send("BSTOP 1")
                sent = True
        elif l.startswith("BDONE 1 "):
            break
    tail6, _ = run(eng, out, f"GEN {M - len(got6)} {ids(A + got6)}") if len(got6) < M else ([], None)
    same = got6 + tail6 == sA
    ok &= same
    both = got6 + tail6
    d = next((k for k in range(min(len(both), len(sA))) if both[k] != sA[k]), None)
    print(f"A in a slot, then solo again after {len(got6)} tokens: {len(both)} tokens, solo {len(sA)}: "
          f"{'IDENTICAL' if same else f'DIFFERS at {d}'}", flush=True)

    # 5. (a measurement, not a check) a SOLO next turn continued from slot 0: its tokens are exact either way, but the
    # draft layer's own K/V was built for another conversation, so fewer drafts may be accepted than in a solo next
    # turn whose drafter read the conversation (A2 in step 1)
    A3 = A2 + got2 + chat("Now in Go.")
    eng.send(f"GEN {M} {ids(A3)}")
    for l in out:
        if l.startswith(("BT ", "BDONE ")):
            eng.pending.append(l)
        elif l.startswith("DONE"):
            f = l.split()
            print(f"solo next turn from a slot: drafts accepted {f[6]} of {f[7]} ({f[1]} tokens in {f[4]} ms)",
                  flush=True)
            break
    # 7. F, A's history without the reply's thinking, into slot 2 (its start comes from the live chain or the prompt
    # cache: step 6's solo continuation took slot 1's contents back; 7b below makes a slot the only source)
    first, cont = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 2 {M} {ids(F)}", slot=2)
    got7 = list(first)
    while cont:
        l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
        if l.startswith("BT 2 "):
            got7.append(int(l.split()[2]))
        elif l.startswith("BDONE 2 "):
            break
    same = got7 == sF
    ok &= same
    d = next((k for k in range(min(len(got7), len(sF))) if got7[k] != sF[k]), None)
    print(f"F (A's history without the reply's thinking) in slot 2: {len(got7)} tokens, solo "
          f"{len(sF)}: {'IDENTICAL' if same else f'DIFFERS at {d}'}", flush=True)
    # 7b. step 7 where only a SLOT can give the start: after step 6 the solo path took slot 1's contents back, so the
    # live chain (or the prompt cache) held A's start in step 7 and F came from there.  Here A runs to its end in
    # slot 1, then --flush unrelated solo GENs push A out of the live session and the prompt cache's checkpoints; F2
    # (A's question, another reply) into slot 2 can then only start from slot 1's turn checkpoint (slot 2 holds F,
    # which shares no more with F2 than A does; the engine log line is printed) - its tokens must equal F2 solo
    got7b = []
    if a.flush > 0:
        first, cont = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 1 {M} {ids(A)}", slot=1)
        gotA = list(first)
        while cont:
            l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
            if l.startswith("BT 1 "):
                gotA.append(int(l.split()[2]))
            elif l.startswith("BDONE 1 "):
                break
        same = gotA == sA
        ok &= same
        print(f"7b: A in slot 1 to its end: {len(gotA)} tokens, solo {len(sA)}: {'IDENTICAL' if same else 'DIFFERS'}",
              flush=True)
        for k in range(a.flush):
            run(eng, out, f"GEN 8 {ids(chat(f'Unrelated question {k}: name one prime number above {100 * k}.'))}")
        eng.log.flush()
        mark = len(Path(eng.log_path).read_text(errors="replace"))
        first, cont = run(eng, out, f"BGEN 2 {M} {ids(F2)}", slot=2)
        got7b = list(first)
        while cont:
            l = eng.pending.pop(0) if eng.pending else next(out)
            if l.startswith("BT 2 "):
                got7b.append(int(l.split()[2]))
            elif l.startswith("BDONE 2 "):
                break
        tail = Path(eng.log_path).read_text(errors="replace")[mark:]
