## tests/terminal/test_gpu_roles.py

"""strata_control/gpu_roles.py: Main / Helper / Off for every graphics card (the rules the app, `strata launch`, setup and the server share)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from strata_control import gpu_roles as R

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
V = json.loads((ROOT / "tests" / "data" / "gpu_roles_vectors.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def roles(d):
    return None if d is None else {int(k): v for k, v in d.items()}


class Vectors(unittest.TestCase):
    """tests/data/gpu_roles_vectors.json is also run by apps/host/tests/gpu-roles.test.mjs against gpu-roles.ts."""

    def test_recommend(self):
        for c in V["recommend"]:
            with self.subTest(c["hw"]):
                r = R.recommend(V["hw"][c["hw"]])
                self.assertEqual(r["roles"], roles(c["roles"]))
                self.assertEqual((r["main"], r["why"]), (c["main"], c["why"]))

    def test_set_role(self):
        for c in V["set_role"]:
            with self.subTest(c):
                out, note = R.set_role(roles(c["roles"]), V["hw"][c["hw"]], c["card"], c["role"])
                self.assertEqual(out, roles(c["after"]))
                self.assertEqual(note, c["note"])

    def test_order(self):
        for c in V["order"]:
            with self.subTest(c):
                self.assertEqual(R.order(roles(c["roles"]), V["hw"][c["hw"]]), c["gpu"])

    def test_warnings(self):
        for c in V["warnings"]:
            with self.subTest(c):
                w = R.warnings(roles(c["roles"]), V["hw"][c["hw"]], spill_gb=c.get("spill_gb", 0.0))
                self.assertEqual([x["code"] for x in w], c["codes"])
                if c.get("fix"):
                    self.assertEqual(w[0]["fix"], c["fix"])

    def test_saved(self):
        for c in V["saved"]:
            with self.subTest(c):
                got, problem = R.saved_roles(c["cfg"])
                self.assertEqual(got, roles(c["roles"]))
                if c.get("problem"):
                    self.assertIn(c["problem"], problem or "")

    def test_legacy(self):
        for c in V["legacy"]:
            with self.subTest(c):
                self.assertEqual(R.from_legacy(c["gpu"], V["hw"][c["hw"]], c.get("gpu_order")), roles(c["roles"]))


class Words(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_warnings_are_one_short_line_and_say_only_what_a_person_cannot_know(self):
        two = V["hw"]["two"]
        # a slower card as Main is NOT warned about: people understand it (owner rule)
        self.assertEqual(R.warnings({0: "main", 1: "helper"}, two), [])
        for case in V["warnings"]:
            for w in R.warnings(roles(case["roles"]), V["hw"][case["hw"]], spill_gb=case.get("spill_gb", 0.0)):
                self.assertLess(len(w["text"]), 90, w["text"])
                self.assertNotIn("slower", w["text"].replace("is slow as Main", ""))

    def test_cpu_only_line(self):
        w = R.warnings({0: "off", 1: "off"}, V["hw"]["two"], engine_runs_cpu_only=True)
        self.assertEqual(w[0]["text"], "Performance is degraded on CPU only.")
        w = R.warnings({0: "off", 1: "off"}, V["hw"]["two"])
        self.assertEqual(w[0]["text"], R.NO_CARD_LINE)

    def test_sentence_and_describe(self):
        self.assertEqual(R.sentence(V["hw"]["one"]), "Strata will use your RTX 4070 Ti.")
        s = R.sentence(V["hw"]["three"])
        self.assertIn("RTX 4070 Ti is Main: it is faster.", s)
        self.assertIn("RTX 2060 starts Off: 8 GB or less.", s)
        self.assertEqual(R.describe({0: "helper", 1: "main"}, V["hw"]["two"]), "Main: GPU 2 RTX 4070 Ti. Helper: GPU 1 RTX 3060.")

    def test_cards_with_8_gb_or_less_start_off_but_a_lone_8_gb_card_is_main(self):
        self.assertEqual(R.recommend([{"index": 0, "name": "RTX 4060", "vram_gb": 8}])["roles"], {0: "main"})
        r = R.recommend([{"index": 0, "name": "A", "vram_gb": 12, "speed": 9}, {"index": 1, "name": "B", "vram_gb": 8, "speed": 5}, {"index": 2, "name": "C", "vram_gb": 10, "speed": 5}])
        self.assertEqual(r["roles"], {0: "main", 1: "off", 2: "helper"})


class MirrorAndParse(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_mirror_writes_roles_and_the_legacy_fields_with_main_last(self):
        m = R.mirror({0: "helper", 1: "main"}, V["hw"]["two"])
        self.assertEqual(m["gpu_roles"], {"0": "helper", "1": "main"})
        self.assertEqual((m["gpu"], m["gpu_order"]), ([0, 1], "as_given"))
        self.assertNotIn("gpu_none", m)
        one = R.mirror({0: "off", 1: "main"}, V["hw"]["two"])
        self.assertEqual(one["gpu"], 1)                                   # one card is a number, never a list (#3203)
        none = R.mirror({0: "off", 1: "off"}, V["hw"]["two"])
        self.assertEqual((none["gpu"], none["gpu_none"]), ([], True))

    def test_parse_roles(self):
        cards = V["hw"]["three"]
        self.assertEqual(R.parse_roles("1=main, 0=helper,2=off", cards), {1: "main", 0: "helper", 2: "off"})
        self.assertEqual(R.roles_from_text("1=main,0=helper", cards), {0: "helper", 1: "main", 2: "off"})      # unnamed cards are Off
        self.assertEqual(R.roles_from_text("0=helper", cards), {0: "main", 1: "off", 2: "off"})                 # a lone card on is Main
        for bad in ("", "1", "1=boss", "x=main", "0=main,1=main", "7=main"):
            with self.subTest(bad), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                R.parse_roles(bad, cards)

    def test_normalize(self):
        two = V["hw"]["two"]
        self.assertEqual(R.normalize({0: "helper", 1: "helper"}, two), {0: "helper", 1: "main"})
        self.assertEqual(R.normalize({0: "main", 1: "main"}, two), {0: "main", 1: "helper"})
        self.assertEqual(R.normalize({0: "helper", 1: "off"}, two), {0: "main", 1: "off"})

    def test_spill_uses_the_cards_that_are_on(self):
        two = [{"index": 0, "name": "A", "vram_gb": 12}, {"index": 1, "name": "B", "vram_gb": 12}]
        a = R.spill_for({0: "main", 1: "helper"}, two, 44.0, 32.0)
        b = R.spill_for({0: "main", 1: "off"}, two, 44.0, 32.0)
        self.assertLess(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(R.spill_for({0: "main", 1: "off"}, two, None, 32.0), 0.0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_handover.py

"""`strata update` installs a newer Control; the Terminal on PATH hands over to it (it used to keep running the old one)."""

import json
import os
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from strata_cli import handover

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WINDOWS = os.name == "nt"


def make_control(components: Path, version: str, folder: str | None = None, whole: bool = True, point: bool = True) -> Path:
    folder = folder or version
    d = components / "control" / folder
    (d / "strata_control").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (d / "VERSION").write_text(version + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (d / "strata.py").write_text("print('control', %r)\n" % version, encoding="utf-8")
    if whole:
        py = handover.bundled_python(d)
        py.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        py.write_text("stub", encoding="utf-8")
    if point:
        (components / "control" / "active.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": version, "folder": folder}), encoding="utf-8")
    return d


class Handover(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="strata-handover-")
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.comp = Path(self.temp.name) / "components"
        self.comp.mkdir()
        self.env = {"STRATA_COMPONENTS_DIR": str(self.comp), handover.ENV_CHECKOUT: "1"}
        self.calls, self.warnings = [], []

    def go(self, running="0.1.46", env=None, argv=("status",)):
        def fake(*args, **kwargs):
            self.calls.append((args, kwargs))
            return 7
        env = {**self.env, **(env or {})}
        return handover.maybe_hand_over(list(argv), environ=env, running=running, execv=fake, run=fake, warn=self.warnings.append)

    def test_a_source_checkout_never_hands_over(self):
        make_control(self.comp, "0.1.46.1")
        env = {k: v for k, v in self.env.items() if k != handover.ENV_CHECKOUT}
        original = handover.running_from_checkout
        handover.running_from_checkout = lambda: True
        try:
            result = handover.maybe_hand_over(["status"], environ=env, running="0.1.46", execv=None,
                                              run=lambda *a, **k: self.fail("handed over"), warn=self.warnings.append)
        finally:
            handover.running_from_checkout = original
        self.assertIsNone(result)
        self.assertEqual(self.warnings, [])

    def test_a_newer_control_takes_over_with_its_own_interpreter_and_the_same_arguments(self):
        d = make_control(self.comp, "0.1.46.1")
        result = self.go(argv=("serve", "--port", "1"))
        self.assertEqual(len(self.calls), 1)
        args, kwargs = self.calls[0]
        python, command = (args[0], args[1]) if not WINDOWS else (args[0][0], args[0])
        self.assertEqual(Path(python), handover.bundled_python(d))
        self.assertEqual(command[1:], [str(d / "strata.py"), "serve", "--port", "1"])
        env = kwargs.get("env") or args[2]
        self.assertEqual(env["STRATA_HANDOVER"], "1")
        if WINDOWS:
            self.assertEqual(result, 7, "the exit code of the newer Control is passed through")
        self.assertEqual(self.warnings, [])

    def test_no_loop_when_already_handed_over(self):
        make_control(self.comp, "0.1.46.1")
        self.assertIsNone(self.go(env={"STRATA_HANDOVER": "1"}))
        self.assertIsNone(self.go(env={"STRATA_NO_HANDOVER": "1"}))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls, [])

    def test_a_broken_target_falls_back_with_one_warning(self):
        make_control(self.comp, "0.1.46.1", whole=False)
        self.assertIsNone(self.go())
        self.assertEqual(self.calls, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.warnings), 1)
        self.assertIn("0.1.46.1", self.warnings[0])
        self.assertIn("running 0.1.46 instead", self.warnings[0])

    def test_a_target_that_fails_to_start_falls_back(self):
        make_control(self.comp, "0.1.46.1")

        def boom(*a, **k):
            raise OSError(8, "Exec format error")
        result = handover.maybe_hand_over(["status"], environ=self.env, running="0.1.46", execv=boom, run=boom, warn=self.warnings.append)
        self.assertIsNone(result)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.warnings), 1)

    def test_an_older_or_equal_target_is_ignored(self):
        make_control(self.comp, "0.1.45")
        self.assertIsNone(self.go(running="0.1.46"))
        make_control(self.comp, "0.1.46")
        self.assertIsNone(self.go(running="0.1.46"))
        self.assertIsNone(self.go(running="0.1.46.1"))
        self.assertEqual((self.calls, self.warnings), ([], []))

    def test_the_version_in_the_folder_counts_not_the_pointers_claim(self):
        d = make_control(self.comp, "0.1.45")
        (self.comp / "control" / "active.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "9.9.9", "folder": "0.1.45"}), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIsNone(self.go(running="0.1.46"))
        self.assertTrue(d.is_dir())

    def test_a_pointer_cannot_leave_the_control_folder(self):
        outside = Path(self.temp.name) / "etc"
        (outside / "strata_control").mkdir(parents=True)
        (outside / "VERSION").write_text("9.0.0", encoding="utf-8")
        (outside / "strata.py").write_text("print('evil')", encoding="utf-8")
        py = handover.bundled_python(outside)
        py.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        py.write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.comp / "control").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        for folder in ("../../etc", "..", "../etc", "a/b", "/etc", "..\\etc", ""):
            (self.comp / "control" / "active.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "9.0.0", "folder": folder}), encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIsNone(self.go(), folder)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls, [])

    @unittest.skipIf(WINDOWS, "needs a symlink")
    def test_a_folder_that_is_a_link_out_of_the_control_folder_is_refused(self):
        real = make_control(Path(self.temp.name) / "elsewhere", "9.0.0", point=False)
        (self.comp / "control").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (self.comp / "control" / "9.0.0").symlink_to(real, target_is_directory=True)
        (self.comp / "control" / "active.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "9.0.0", "folder": "9.0.0"}), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIsNone(self.go())
        self.assertEqual(self.calls, [])

    def test_no_pointer_or_garbage_means_nothing_happens(self):
        self.assertIsNone(self.go())
        (self.comp / "control").mkdir()
        for text in ("{", "[]", "null", json.dumps({"folder": "x"})):
            (self.comp / "control" / "active.json").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIsNone(self.go(), text)
        self.assertEqual((self.calls, self.warnings), ([], []))

    @unittest.skipIf(WINDOWS, "a shell stub stands in for the bundled interpreter")
    def test_end_to_end_the_real_entry_point_hands_over_and_does_not_loop(self):
        newer = make_control(self.comp, "99.0.0")
        py = handover.bundled_python(newer)
        py.write_text('#!/bin/sh\nexec "%s" "$@"\n' % sys.executable, encoding="utf-8")
        py.chmod(py.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR)
        (newer / "strata.py").write_text("import os,sys\nprint('control 99', os.environ.get('STRATA_HANDOVER'), sys.argv[1:])\nraise SystemExit(3)\n",
                                         encoding="utf-8")
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "strata.py"), "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              env={**os.environ, "STRATA_COMPONENTS_DIR": str(self.comp), handover.ENV_CHECKOUT: "1"})
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 3, done.stderr)
        self.assertIn("control 99 1 ['--version']", done.stdout)
        # with the guard set the current Control runs, and says its own version
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "strata.py"), "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              env={**os.environ, "STRATA_COMPONENTS_DIR": str(self.comp), "STRATA_HANDOVER": "1"})
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 0, done.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(done.stdout.startswith("strata "), done.stdout)

    def test_the_entry_point_falls_back_when_the_target_is_broken(self):
        make_control(self.comp, "99.0.0", whole=False)
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "strata.py"), "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              env={**os.environ, "STRATA_COMPONENTS_DIR": str(self.comp), handover.ENV_CHECKOUT: "1"})
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 0, done.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(done.stdout.startswith("strata "), done.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(len(done.stderr.strip().splitlines()), 1, done.stderr)
        self.assertIn("99.0.0", done.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_hipblaslt_tuning.py

"""The hipBLASLt tuning tables in the AMD engine packages: what a package holds per card family, and the one rule that decides at a start
whether a table is used (strata_control/hipblaslt_tuning.py). Folders are throwaways; no GPU tool is run.

The packages' hipBLASLt versions below are the ones the 0.2.x release packages bundle (docs/AMD_HIP.md, Ready-made packages): Windows ROCm
10.2.0a20260930 carries 1.5.0 (100500), the Linux 7.10.0a20251120 wheels 1.2.0 (100200), Linux Strix Halo's 7.14.1 1.4.1 (100401)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from strata_control import hipblaslt_tuning as ht

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TABLES = ROOT / "tools" / "hip"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "packaging"))
import package_engine  # noqa: E402
import stage_tuning  # noqa: E402

#: (platform, variant) -> (archs of the package, hipBLASLt version it bundles, architectures that must carry a table)
PACKAGES = {
    ("windows-x86_64", "rx9070"): (("gfx1200", "gfx1201"), 100500, {"gfx1201"}),
    ("windows-x86_64", "rdna3"): (("gfx1100", "gfx1101", "gfx1102", "gfx1151"), 100500, {"gfx1100", "gfx1151"}),
    ("linux-x86_64", "rx9070"): (("gfx1200", "gfx1201"), 100200, set()),                    # no table for 1.2.0 on RDNA4 (docs/AMD_HIP.md)
    ("linux-x86_64", "rx7900"): (("gfx1100", "gfx1101", "gfx1102"), 100200, {"gfx1100"}),
    ("linux-x86_64", "halo"): (("gfx1151",), 100401, {"gfx1151"}),
    # 0.2.2 RX 6000 packages: hipBLASLt ships no gfx1030 / gfx1031 kernels at any version, so no table, plain hipBLAS
    ("windows-x86_64", "rdna2"): (("gfx1030", "gfx1031"), 100500, set()),
    ("linux-x86_64", "rx6000"): (("gfx1030", "gfx1031"), 100400, set()),
}


ON = {ht.SWITCH: "on"}            # the switch that uses a matching table whatever "auto" does
AUTO = {}


def fake_table(folder: Path, arch: str, version: int, *, header: str | None = None) -> Path:
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = folder / ht.table_name(arch, version)
    path.write_text(f"# solution ids are scoped to this hipBLASLt version and device architecture\n"
                    f"{header or f'{ht.HEADER} {arch} {version}'}\nbf16 128 2560 128 4096 73754\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return path


def fake_package(root: Path, *, version: int | None = 100500, tables=(("gfx1201", 100500),), build=True) -> Path:
    folder = root / "0.2.1-pkg"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    meta = {"version": "0.2.1", "backend": "hip"}
    if version is not None:
        meta["hipblaslt_version"] = version
    if build:
        (folder / "BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta), encoding="utf-8")
    for arch, ver in tables:
        fake_table(folder / ht.TABLE_DIR, arch, ver)
    return folder


class TempDir(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.dir.name)


class Decision(TempDir):
    """Match, mismatch, switch, the person's own choice."""

    def test_a_table_for_this_card_and_this_hipblaslt_is_used(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON)
        self.assertEqual(d.path, pkg / "tuning" / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt")
        self.assertIn("gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt", d.message)
        self.assertIn(ht.SWITCH, d.message)               # the line tells how to turn it off
        self.assertEqual(d.level, "info")

    def test_a_table_for_another_hipblaslt_version_is_not_used_and_the_log_says_why(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root, version=100200, tables=(("gfx1201", 100500),))
        d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON)
        self.assertIsNone(d.path)
        self.assertEqual(d.level, "warn")
        self.assertIn("100200", d.message)
        self.assertIn("100500", d.message)
        self.assertIn("plain hipBLAS", d.message)

    def test_a_card_without_a_table_in_the_package_gets_plain_hipblas_and_one_line(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1200"], environ=ON)
        self.assertIsNone(d.path)
        self.assertIn("none for gfx1200", d.message)

    def test_the_card_that_has_a_table_is_found_among_several(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root, tables=(("gfx1100", 100500), ("gfx1151", 100500)))
        self.assertEqual(ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1101", "gfx1151"], environ=ON).path.name, "gfx1151-hipblaslt-100500.txt")

    def test_a_package_that_does_not_say_its_hipblaslt_is_not_guessed_at(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root, version=None)
        d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON)
        self.assertIsNone(d.path)
        self.assertEqual(d.level, "warn")
        self.assertIn("hipblaslt_version", d.message)

    def test_an_unreadable_card_is_a_note_not_a_guess(self):
        d = ht.resolve(fake_package(self.root), [], environ=ON)
        self.assertIsNone(d.path)
        self.assertIn("could not be read", d.message)

    def test_a_table_whose_header_disagrees_with_its_name_is_not_used(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root, tables=())
        fake_table(pkg / "tuning", "gfx1201", 100500, header=f"{ht.HEADER} gfx1201 100401")
        d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON)
        self.assertIsNone(d.path)
        self.assertIn("header", d.message)

    def test_the_switch_turns_it_off_in_the_environment_and_in_the_run_config(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        for word in ("off", "OFF", "0", "no", "false", "none"):
            d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ={ht.SWITCH: word})
            self.assertIsNone(d.path, word)
            self.assertIn("off", d.message)
        self.assertIsNone(ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=AUTO, cfg={"hipblaslt_table": False}).path)
        self.assertIsNotNone(ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=AUTO, cfg={"hipblaslt_table": True}).path)
        self.assertIsNone(ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ={ht.SWITCH: "off"}, cfg={"hipblaslt_table": True}).path)   # the environment wins
        for word in ("on", "ON", "1", "yes", "true"):
            self.assertIsNotNone(ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ={ht.SWITCH: word}).path, word)

    def test_auto_follows_the_one_constant_and_says_what_is_available(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        with mock.patch.object(ht, "AUTO_USES_TABLE", False):
            d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=AUTO)
            self.assertIsNone(d.path)
            self.assertIn("gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt", d.message)
            self.assertIn(f"{ht.SWITCH}=on", d.message)
            self.assertEqual(ht.mode(AUTO), "auto")
        with mock.patch.object(ht, "AUTO_USES_TABLE", True):
            d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=AUTO)
            self.assertEqual(d.path, pkg / "tuning" / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt")
            self.assertIsNone(ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ={ht.SWITCH: "off"}).path)

    def test_the_default_is_the_owners_decision(self):
        """A table changes the bits of the prompt's dense GEMMs (notes-021-hip.md); the owner chose: on by default for Strix Halo only."""
        self.assertFalse(ht.AUTO_USES_TABLE)
        self.assertEqual(ht.AUTO_ARCHS, ("gfx1151",))

    def test_auto_uses_the_table_on_strix_halo_only(self):
        for arch, used in (("gfx1151", True), ("gfx1201", False), ("gfx1100", False)):
            root = self.root / arch
            root.mkdir()
            pkg = fake_package(root, tables=((arch, 100500),))
            d = ht.resolve(pkg, [arch], environ=AUTO)
            self.assertEqual(d.path is not None, used, (arch, d.message))
            self.assertIsNone(ht.resolve(pkg, [arch], environ={ht.SWITCH: "off"}).path)

    def test_a_table_the_person_set_is_never_replaced(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        mine = str(self.root / "mine.txt")
        for environ, cfg in (({ht.ENGINE_VAR: mine}, {}), ({}, {"env": {ht.ENGINE_VAR: mine}})):
            d = ht.resolve(pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=environ, cfg=cfg)
            self.assertIsNone(d.path)
            self.assertIn(mine, d.message)
            out = ht.apply({"backend": "hip", **cfg}, pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=environ, say=lambda line: None)
            self.assertEqual((out.get("env") or {}).get(ht.ENGINE_VAR, mine), mine)


class Apply(TempDir):
    def test_apply_puts_the_table_in_a_copy_of_the_config_and_says_so_once(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        cfg = {"backend": "hip", "env": {"STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN": "0"}}
        lines = []
        out = ht.apply(cfg, pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON, say=lines.append)
        self.assertEqual(out["env"][ht.ENGINE_VAR], str(pkg / "tuning" / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt"))
        self.assertEqual(out["env"]["STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN"], "0")
        self.assertNotIn(ht.ENGINE_VAR, cfg["env"])        # the caller's config is untouched
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 1)
        self.assertTrue(lines[0].startswith("[strata] hipBLASLt tuning table"))

    def test_apply_with_a_mismatch_leaves_the_config_alone_and_warns(self):
        pkg = fake_package(self.root, version=100200)
        cfg = {"backend": "hip"}
        lines = []
        self.assertIs(ht.apply(cfg, pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON, say=lines.append), cfg)
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 1)
        self.assertIn("note", lines[0])

    def test_other_backends_and_packages_without_tables_are_silent(self):
        lines = []
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        cfg = {"backend": "cuda"}
        self.assertIs(ht.apply(cfg, pkg, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON, say=lines.append), cfg)
        bare = self.root / "cuda-pkg"
        bare.mkdir()
        (bare / "BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "0.2.1"}), encoding="utf-8")
        out = ht.apply({"backend": "hip"}, bare, ["gfx1201"], environ=ON, say=lines.append)
        self.assertNotIn("env", out)
        self.assertEqual(lines, [])

    def test_the_server_start_applies_it_for_a_component_engine(self):
        from serve import server
        pkg = fake_package(self.root)
        (pkg / "strata").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        cfg = {"exe": "component:strata-engine", "backend": "hip"}
        out = io.StringIO()
        with mock.patch.object(server.engine_component, "expand", return_value=str(pkg / "strata")), \
                mock.patch.object(ht, "present_archs", return_value=["gfx1201"]), \
                mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=False), contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
            os.environ.pop(ht.SWITCH, None)
            os.environ.pop(ht.ENGINE_VAR, None)
            self.assertNotIn(ht.ENGINE_VAR, server.child_env(server.with_component_engine(cfg)))     # "auto" is off by default
            os.environ[ht.SWITCH] = "on"
            started = server.with_component_engine(cfg)
            env = server.child_env(started)
            self.assertEqual(env[ht.ENGINE_VAR], str(pkg / "tuning" / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt"))
            os.environ[ht.SWITCH] = "off"
            self.assertNotIn(ht.ENGINE_VAR, server.child_env(server.with_component_engine(cfg)))
        self.assertIn("hipBLASLt tuning table", out.getvalue())

    def test_present_archs_picks_the_configured_card_on_linux(self):
        with mock.patch("strata_control.engine_component.hip_archs_present", return_value=["gfx1100", "gfx1201"]):
            if os.name != "nt":
                self.assertEqual(ht.present_archs({"gpu": 1}), ["gfx1201"])
                self.assertEqual(ht.present_archs({"gpu": [1, 0]}), ["gfx1201", "gfx1100"])
            self.assertEqual(ht.present_archs({}), ["gfx1100", "gfx1201"])


class PackageContents(TempDir):
    """What each package of the release matrix carries, from the real tables of tools/hip."""

    def test_every_release_package_carries_the_tables_its_cards_have(self):
        for (platform, variant), (archs, version, wanted) in PACKAGES.items():
            stage = self.root / f"{platform}-{variant}"
            stage.mkdir()
            copied = ht.stage_tables(stage, archs, version, TABLES)
            self.assertEqual({n.split("-")[0] for n in copied}, wanted, (platform, variant))
            on_disk = {p.name for p in (stage / "tuning").glob("*.txt")} if (stage / "tuning").is_dir() else set()
            self.assertEqual(on_disk, set(copied), (platform, variant))
            for arch in wanted:                           # the file the engine start will pick is there and its own header agrees
                self.assertTrue(ht.header_ok(stage / "tuning" / ht.table_name(arch, version), arch, version), (platform, arch))

    def test_the_missing_report_names_the_architectures_without_a_table(self):
        left = ht.missing_report(("gfx1100", "gfx1101", "gfx1102"), 100200, TABLES)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(left), ["gfx1101", "gfx1102"])
        self.assertEqual(ht.missing_report(("gfx1201",), 100200, TABLES), {"gfx1201": [100202, 100500]})

    def test_every_table_in_the_repo_has_a_header_that_matches_its_name(self):
        tables = ht.tables_in(TABLES)
        self.assertGreater(len(tables), 8)
        for (arch, version), path in tables.items():
            self.assertTrue(ht.header_ok(path, arch, version), path.name)

    def test_version_from_header_reads_the_rocm_tree(self):
        inc = self.root / "include" / "hipblaslt"
        inc.mkdir(parents=True)
        (inc / "hipblaslt-version.h").write_text("#define HIPBLASLT_VERSION_MAJOR 1\n#define HIPBLASLT_VERSION_MINOR 5\n"
                                                 "#define HIPBLASLT_VERSION_PATCH 0\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(ht.version_from_header(self.root), 100500)
        self.assertIsNone(ht.version_from_header(self.root / "nowhere"))

    def test_stage_tuning_writes_the_version_and_the_tables(self):
        stage = self.root / "stage"
        stage.mkdir()
        (stage / "BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "0.2.1", "archs": ["gfx1151"]}), encoding="utf-8")
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            self.assertEqual(stage_tuning.main(["--stage", str(stage), "--archs", "gfx1151", "--version", "100401"]), 0)
        meta = json.loads((stage / "BUILD.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(meta["hipblaslt_version"], 100401)
        self.assertEqual(meta["archs"], ["gfx1151"])      # what was there stays
        self.assertTrue((stage / "tuning" / "gfx1151-hipblaslt-100401.txt").is_file())

    def test_stage_tuning_can_demand_a_table(self):
        stage = self.root / "stage"
        stage.mkdir()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as caught:
            stage_tuning.main(["--stage", str(stage), "--archs", "gfx1201", "--version", "100200", "--expect", "gfx1201"])
        self.assertIn("gfx1201", str(caught.exception))

    def test_stage_tuning_refuses_a_rocm_whose_version_it_cannot_read(self):
        stage = self.root / "stage"
        stage.mkdir()
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
            stage_tuning.main(["--stage", str(stage), "--archs", "gfx1201", "--rocm", str(self.root / "no-rocm")])


class PackagedAndHashed(TempDir):
    """packaging/package_engine.py: the tables are files of the package (hashed, so signed with it) and a bad AMD stage is refused."""

    def stage(self, **kw):
        src = self.root / "src"
        src.mkdir()
        (src / "strata").write_bytes(b"engine" * 100)
        (src / "libamdhip64.so.7").write_bytes(b"hip" * 100)
        (src / "BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "0.2.1", **kw}), encoding="utf-8")
        return src

    def build(self, src, archs=("gfx1201",), tree=False):
        out = self.root / "out"
        out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        with mock.patch.object(package_engine, "_bundle_missing_libraries", return_value=[]):
            return package_engine.build(src, "hip", "0.2.1", "linux-x86_64", out, entry="strata", archs=archs, build_id="t", tree=tree,
                                        variant="rx9070")

    def test_the_tables_are_listed_and_hashed_in_the_manifest_even_without_tree(self):
        src = self.stage(hipblaslt_version=100500)
        fake_table(src / "tuning", "gfx1201", 100500)
        folder = self.build(src)
        listed = {f["path"]: f for f in json.loads((folder / "engine-component.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["files"]}
        self.assertIn("tuning/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt", listed)
        self.assertEqual(len(listed["tuning/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt"]["sha256"]), 64)
        (folder / "tuning" / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt").write_text("changed", encoding="utf-8")   # a swapped table fails the start's hash check
        from strata_control import engine_component as ec
        with self.assertRaises(ec.ComponentProblem):
            ec.verify(ec.read_manifest(folder), full=True)

    def test_an_amd_stage_without_a_hipblaslt_version_is_refused(self):
        src = self.stage()
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as caught:
            self.build(src)
        self.assertIn("hipblaslt_version", str(caught.exception))

    def test_a_table_for_another_version_or_card_than_the_package_is_refused(self):
        src = self.stage(hipblaslt_version=100500)
        fake_table(src / "tuning", "gfx1201", 100202)
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as caught:
            self.build(src)
        self.assertIn("100202", str(caught.exception))
        other = self.root / "other"
        other.mkdir()
        src2 = other / "src"
        src2.mkdir()
        (src2 / "strata").write_bytes(b"e")
        (src2 / "BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps({"hipblaslt_version": 100500}), encoding="utf-8")
        fake_table(src2 / "tuning", "gfx1100", 100500)
        with mock.patch.object(package_engine, "_bundle_missing_libraries", return_value=[]), self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as caught:
            package_engine.build(src2, "hip", "0.2.1", "linux-x86_64", other / "out", entry="strata", archs=("gfx1201",), build_id="t")
        self.assertIn("gfx1100", str(caught.exception))

    def test_a_cuda_package_needs_no_hipblaslt_version(self):
        src = self.stage()
        out = self.root / "out"
        out.mkdir()
        with mock.patch.object(package_engine, "_bundle_missing_libraries", return_value=[]):
            package_engine.build(src, "cuda", "0.2.1", "linux-x86_64", out, entry="strata", archs=("sm_86",), build_id="t")


class SetupFindsThePackageTable(TempDir):
    """setup.py outside the app (a git checkout, or the old Windows zip that START-HERE unpacks): the engine folder's own tuning/ comes first."""

    def load_setup(self):
        import importlib.util
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("setup_hipblaslt_copy", ROOT / "setup.py")
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
        return module

    def test_the_engine_folders_table_wins_over_tools_hip_and_the_switch_turns_it_off(self):
        setup = self.load_setup()
        pkg = self.root / "engine"
        fake_table(pkg / "tuning", "gfx1201", 100500)
        seen = []
        with mock.patch.object(setup, "ok", seen.append), mock.patch.object(setup, "say", seen.append), \
                mock.patch.object(setup, "warn", seen.append), mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=False):
            os.environ.pop(ht.SWITCH, None)
            self.assertEqual(setup.hipblaslt_table("gfx1201", [], 100500, [pkg / "tuning"]), pkg / "tuning" / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt")
            self.assertEqual(setup.hipblaslt_table("gfx1201", [], 100500), TABLES / "gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt")
            self.assertIsNone(setup.hipblaslt_table("gfx1201", [], 100200, [pkg / "tuning"]))      # no table for 1.2.0: warned, plain
            os.environ[ht.SWITCH] = "off"
            self.assertIsNone(setup.hipblaslt_table("gfx1201", [], 100500, [pkg / "tuning"]))
        self.assertTrue(any("no hipBLASLt tuning table" in str(line) for line in seen))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_import_projector.py

"""Importing a model together with its picture reader (mmproj), and the plain words when a model type is not ours."""

import io
import json
import struct
import tempfile
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path

from unittest import mock

from strata_cli.cli import main
from strata_control import models
from tests.terminal.test_models import gguf_fixture


def projector_fixture(projector_type="qwen3vl_merger", architecture="clip") -> bytes:
    def string(value):
        raw = value.encode()
        return struct.pack("<Q", len(raw)) + raw

    pairs = [("general.architecture", 8, string(architecture)), ("clip.projector_type", 8, string(projector_type))]
    header = (b"GGUF" + struct.pack("<IQQ", 3, 1, len(pairs)) +
              b"".join(string(key) + struct.pack("<I", kind) + value for key, kind, value in pairs))
    header += string("v.blk.0.attn_q.weight") + struct.pack("<IQIQ", 1, 64, 1, 0)
    return header + b"\x00" * (-len(header) % 32) + b"\x00" * 128


class ImportProjectorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.source = Path(self.temp.name) / "model"
        self.source.mkdir()

    def plan(self, path):
        output = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(output):
            main(["models", "import", str(path), "--plan", "--output", "json"])
        return json.loads(output.getvalue())["plan"]

    def model(self, **kwargs):
        first = self.source / "Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00001-of-00001.gguf"
        first.write_bytes(gguf_fixture(**kwargs))
        return first

    def test_pinned_projector_next_to_a_model_means_pictures(self):
        self.model()
        file = self.source / "mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf"
        file.write_bytes(projector_fixture())
        with mock.patch.dict(models.PINNED_PROJECTORS, {file.name.lower(): file.stat().st_size}):
            plan = self.plan(self.source)
        self.assertTrue(plan["reads_pictures"])
        self.assertEqual(plan["projectors"][0]["status"], "ok")
        self.assertIn("pictures will work", plan["messages"][0])

    def test_same_name_but_another_size_is_not_called_official(self):
        self.model()
        (self.source / "mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf").write_bytes(projector_fixture())
        plan = self.plan(self.source)
        self.assertEqual(plan["projectors"][0]["status"], "other_name")

    def test_projector_beside_a_chosen_model_file_is_found(self):
        first = self.model()
        (self.source / "mmproj-F16.gguf").write_bytes(projector_fixture())
        plan = self.plan(first)
        self.assertEqual([p["name"] for p in plan["projectors"]], ["mmproj-F16.gguf"])
        self.assertTrue(plan["reads_pictures"])

    def test_projector_of_another_kind_is_not_used(self):
        self.model()
        (self.source / "mmproj-other.gguf").write_bytes(projector_fixture("mlp"))
        plan = self.plan(self.source)
        self.assertFalse(plan["reads_pictures"])
        self.assertEqual(plan["projectors"][0]["status"], "unsupported")
        self.assertIn("Custom model API", plan["projectors"][0]["plain"])

    def test_other_name_projector_of_our_kind_is_explained(self):
        self.model()
        (self.source / "mmproj-mine.gguf").write_bytes(projector_fixture())
        plan = self.plan(self.source)
        self.assertEqual(plan["projectors"][0]["status"], "other_name")
        self.assertTrue(plan["reads_pictures"])

    def test_unsupported_model_type_says_custom_api(self):
        first = self.source / "SmolVLM-256M-Q8_0.gguf"
        first.write_bytes(gguf_fixture(architecture="llama"))
        (self.source / "mmproj-SmolVLM-256M-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf").write_bytes(projector_fixture("idefics3"))
        plan = self.plan(self.source)
        self.assertEqual(plan["file_set_status"], "invalid_or_incomplete")
        self.assertFalse(plan["reads_pictures"])
        self.assertEqual(plan["messages"], ["This model type isn't supported by the Strata engine. "
                                            "Add it as a Custom model API (llama-server) instead."])

    def test_choosing_the_projector_itself_says_so(self):
        projector = self.source / "mmproj-F16.gguf"
        projector.write_bytes(projector_fixture())
        output = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(output):
            code = main(["models", "import", str(projector), "--plan", "--output", "json"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 5)
        self.assertIn("picture reader", json.dumps(json.loads(output.getvalue())))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_install_scripts_env.py

"""install.ps1 / install.sh: an ARM computer is refused with the reason and the way out; the Windows script survives the usual environment trouble."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PS1 = ROOT / "packaging" / "install.ps1"
SH = ROOT / "packaging" / "install.sh"


class Text(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ps1 = PS1.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.sh = SH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def test_arm_is_refused_with_a_reason_and_a_next_step(self):
        self.assertIn("Windows on ARM PC", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("no engine for ARM", self.ps1)
        self.assertNotIn("has no Strata Terminal yet", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("ARM processor", self.sh)
        self.assertIn("Apple silicon", self.sh)

    def test_tls12_proxy_sign_in_and_the_real_error_text(self):
        self.assertIn("Tls12", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("DefaultNetworkCredentials", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("$($_.Exception.Message)", self.ps1)

    def test_long_paths_junction_and_running_version(self):

        self.assertIn("STRATA_DATA_DIR to a short folder", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $current", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("a program is using it", self.ps1)
        self.assertIn("Windows did not say where your user folder is", self.ps1)
        self.assertNotIn("is the disk full?", self.ps1)

from __future__ import annotations

import json

class Issue3298MtpDepth(unittest.TestCase):
    """Qwen3.6 passes `--mtp 2` (a draft depth); it is not a folder."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)

    def test_doctor_does_not_look_for_a_folder_named_2(self):
        from strata_control import doctor
        engine = self.root / "engine"
        engine.write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        engine.chmod(0o700)
        tok = self.root / "tok"
        tok.mkdir()
        for n in ("vocab.json", "merges.txt", "token_type.json"):
            (tok / n).write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
        model = self.root / "m.gguf"
        model.write_bytes(b"x")
        cfg = self.root / "run.json"
        cfg.write_text(json.dumps({"exe": str(engine), "args": ["--native", str(model), "--mtp", "2", "--vision"],
                                   "cwd": str(self.root), "tokenizer": str(tok), "model_name": "q36", "port": 8095}),
                       encoding="utf-8")
        report = doctor.inspect(cfg)
        self.assertNotIn("mtp", [c["name"] for c in report["components"]])
        self.assertEqual([c["name"] for c in report["components"] if c["status"] not in ("ok",)
                          and c.get("required") and c["name"] in ("native", "mtp", "pack")], [])

    def test_doctor_still_checks_an_mtp_folder(self):
        from strata_control import doctor
        engine = self.root / "engine"
        engine.write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        engine.chmod(0o700)
        tok = self.root / "tok"
        tok.mkdir()
        for n in ("vocab.json", "merges.txt", "token_type.json"):
            (tok / n).write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
        cfg = self.root / "run.json"
        cfg.write_text(json.dumps({"exe": str(engine), "args": ["--mtp", str(self.root / "gone")],
                                   "cwd": str(self.root), "tokenizer": str(tok), "model_name": "x", "port": 8095}),
                       encoding="utf-8")
        report = doctor.inspect(cfg)
        mtp = [c for c in report["components"] if c["name"] == "mtp"]
        self.assertEqual(len(mtp), 1)
        self.assertEqual(mtp[0]["status"], "missing")

    def test_launch_files_present_ignores_a_depth_number(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import files_present
        model = self.root / "m.gguf"
        model.write_bytes(b"x")
        self.assertEqual(files_present({"args": ["--native", str(model), "--mtp", "2"]}), [])
        self.assertEqual(files_present({"args": ["--mtp", str(self.root / "gone")]}), [str(self.root / "gone")])


class Issue3403MacBuildTools(unittest.TestCase):
    """The Mac setup compiles without setup.cmake_build(), so cmake and ninja must be installed for it too."""

    def test_missing_build_tools_are_installed_before_the_mac_compile(self):
        from unittest import mock
        import setup
        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "metal"))
        import setup_mac as M
        installed = {"cmake": None, "ninja": None}

        def find(name):
            return installed[name]

        def pip(packages, what):
            self.assertTrue(all(p.split("==")[0] in ("cmake", "ninja") for p in packages), packages)
            for p in packages:
                installed[p.split("==")[0]] = "/venv/bin/" + p.split("==")[0]

        with mock.patch.object(setup, "find_tool", side_effect=find), mock.patch.object(setup, "pip_install", side_effect=pip) as pi:
            self.assertEqual(setup.ensure_build_tools(), ("/venv/bin/cmake", "/venv/bin/ninja"))
            self.assertEqual(pi.call_count, 1)
            setup.ensure_build_tools()                       # present now: nothing more is installed
            self.assertEqual(pi.call_count, 1)

    def test_both_mac_builds_ask_for_the_tools_first(self):
        import inspect
        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "metal"))
        import setup_mac as M
        for fn in (M.build_engine, M.build_vision):
            self.assertIn("S.ensure_build_tools()", inspect.getsource(fn), fn.__name__)


@unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "win32", "ACLs are Windows only")
class WindowsRuntimeFolderRefused(unittest.TestCase):
    """The owner's fresh Windows PC: `strata launch` stopped with "runtime directory must be owner-only" on a folder that was already
    there with another account in its ACL.  Fake SDDL strings for each way an ACL can look."""

    def setUp(self):
        from unittest import mock
        from strata_control import private_files as pf
        self.pf, self.mock = pf, mock
        self.me = "S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001"
        patch = mock.patch.object(pf, "current_user_sid", return_value=self.me)
        patch.start()
        self.addCleanup(patch.stop)

    def offenders(self, sddl):
        return self.pf.unshared_offenders(sddl)

    def test_the_usual_acls_are_fine(self):
        for sddl in ("D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)",
                     "D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)(A;OICI;FA;;;BA)(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)",
                     "D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)",               # the built-in Administrator's alias
                     "D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-18)(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-32-544)(A;OICIIO;GA;;;CO)(A;OICI;FA;;;OW)"):
            self.assertEqual(self.offenders(sddl), [], sddl)

    def test_another_account_is_named(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.offenders("D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)(A;OICI;FR;;;BU)"), ["BU"])
        self.assertEqual(self.offenders("D:PAI(A;;FA;;;WD)(A;;FA;;;AU)"), ["WD", "AU"])
        self.assertEqual(self.offenders("D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1002)"), ["S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1002"])

    def test_an_inherit_only_entry_is_not_for_the_folder_itself(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.offenders("D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)(A;OICIIO;FR;;;BU)(A;CIIO;GR;;;WD)"), [])
        # the same entry without the IO flag does apply
        self.assertEqual(self.offenders("D:PAI(A;OICI;FR;;;BU)"), ["BU"])

    def test_deny_entries_do_not_make_it_reachable(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.offenders("D:PAI(D;;FA;;;BU)(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)"), [])

    def test_plain_names(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.pf.account_name("BU"), "Users")
        self.assertEqual(self.pf.account_name("WD"), "Everyone")
        self.assertEqual(self.pf.account_name("S-1-5-32-545"), "Users")

    def test_runtime_dir_repairs_a_folder_that_names_other_accounts(self):
        from strata_control import runtime
        pf = self.pf
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            base = Path(tmp) / "runtime"
            base.mkdir()
            state = {"fixed": False}

            def sddl(_path):
                return "D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)" if state["fixed"] else \
                    "D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)(A;OICI;0x1200a9;;;BU)"

            def restrict(path, directory=None):
                state["fixed"] = True

            env = {"STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR": str(base)}
            with self.mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env), self.mock.patch.object(pf, "dacl_sddl", side_effect=sddl), \
                    self.mock.patch.object(pf, "restrict_to_current_user", side_effect=restrict) as r, \
                    self.mock.patch.object(pf, "private_mkdir"), self.mock.patch.object(runtime, "_private_mkdir"):
                self.assertEqual(runtime.runtime_dir(), base)
                self.assertEqual(r.call_count, 1)

    def test_runtime_dir_still_refuses_and_says_who_when_the_repair_fails(self):
        from strata_control import profiles, runtime
        pf = self.pf
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            base = Path(tmp) / "runtime"
            base.mkdir()
            with self.mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR": str(base)}), \
                    self.mock.patch.object(pf, "dacl_sddl", return_value="D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)(A;OICI;FR;;;BU)"), \
                    self.mock.patch.object(pf, "restrict_to_current_user", side_effect=OSError("denied")), \
                    self.mock.patch.object(runtime, "_private_mkdir"):
                with self.assertRaises(profiles.ProfileError) as cm:
                    runtime.runtime_dir()
            self.assertIn("Users", str(cm.exception))
            self.assertIn(str(base), str(cm.exception))
            self.assertIn("Properties", str(cm.exception))


@unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "win32", "ACLs are Windows only")
class WindowsRuntimeFolderMoreCases(unittest.TestCase):
    """The cases beyond the first repair (audit-refusals-022.md item 5): a data drive's inherited Users entries, an ACL that cannot be
    read, a folder made by an elevated run, a drive without permissions, and a message in plain words."""

    ME = "S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001"

    def run_dir(self, *, sddl, restrict=None, repair=None, acls=True):
        from unittest import mock
        from strata_control import private_files as pf, runtime
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            base = Path(tmp) / "runtime"
            base.mkdir()
            calls = {"restrict": 0, "repair": 0}

            def r(path, directory=None):
                calls["restrict"] += 1
                if restrict:
                    return restrict(calls)
            def rp(path, tree=True):
                calls["repair"] += 1
                return repair(calls) if repair else False
            with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR": str(base)}), \
                    mock.patch.object(pf, "current_user_sid", return_value=self.ME), \
                    mock.patch.object(pf, "dacl_sddl", side_effect=sddl), \
                    mock.patch.object(pf, "restrict_to_current_user", side_effect=r), \
                    mock.patch.object(pf, "repair_access", side_effect=rp), \
                    mock.patch.object(pf, "volume_has_acls", return_value=acls), \
                    mock.patch.object(runtime, "_private_mkdir"), mock.patch.object(runtime, "_NO_ACL_WARNED", set()), \
                    mock.patch("sys.stderr", new_callable=lambda: __import__("io").StringIO()) as err:
                try:
                    return runtime.runtime_dir(), calls, None, err.getvalue()
                except Exception as exc:     # noqa: BLE001 - the test looks at the ProfileError text
                    return None, calls, exc, err.getvalue()

    def test_a_data_drive_folder_with_users_and_authenticated_users_is_repaired_once(self):
        state = {"fixed": False}
        def sddl(_):
            return f"D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;{self.ME})" if state["fixed"] else \
                f"D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;{self.ME})(A;OICI;0x1301bf;;;AU)(A;OICI;0x1200a9;;;BU)"
        base, calls, exc, _ = self.run_dir(sddl=sddl, restrict=lambda c: state.update(fixed=True))
        self.assertIsNone(exc)
        self.assertEqual(calls["restrict"], 1)

    def test_an_acl_that_cannot_be_read_is_repaired_then_refused_in_plain_words(self):
        def sddl(_):
            raise OSError("access denied")
        base, calls, exc, _ = self.run_dir(sddl=sddl)
        self.assertIsNotNone(exc)
        self.assertEqual((calls["restrict"], calls["repair"]), (1, 1))      # tried both, once each
        self.assertIn("cannot read the permissions", str(exc))
        self.assertNotIn("0700", str(exc))

    def test_a_folder_made_by_an_elevated_run_gets_ownership_taken_back(self):
        state = {"fixed": False}
        def sddl(_):
            if not state["fixed"]:
                raise OSError("access denied")
            return f"D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;{self.ME})"
        def restrict(calls):
            raise PermissionError("denied")
        base, calls, exc, _ = self.run_dir(sddl=sddl, restrict=restrict, repair=lambda c: state.update(fixed=True) or True)
        self.assertIsNone(exc)
        self.assertEqual((calls["restrict"], calls["repair"]), (1, 1))

    def test_a_drive_without_permissions_is_used_with_one_warning(self):
        def sddl(_):
            raise AssertionError("FAT has no ACL to read")
        base, calls, exc, err = self.run_dir(sddl=sddl, acls=False)
        self.assertIsNone(exc)
        self.assertEqual((calls["restrict"], calls["repair"]), (0, 0))
        self.assertIn("no file permissions", err)

    def test_the_refusal_names_the_accounts_and_never_says_mode_0700(self):
        sddl = lambda _: f"D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;{self.ME})(A;OICI;FR;;;AU)(A;OICI;FR;;;WD)"   # noqa: E731
        base, calls, exc, _ = self.run_dir(sddl=sddl)
        text = str(exc)
        self.assertIn("Authenticated Users", text)
        self.assertIn("Everyone", text)
        self.assertNotIn("0700", text)
        self.assertEqual(calls["restrict"], 1)

    def test_the_real_system_drive_has_permissions(self):
        from strata_control import private_files as pf
        self.assertTrue(pf.volume_has_acls(os.environ.get("SystemRoot", "C:\\Windows")))


class Issue3410TrashIsNotAnInstall(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_trash_folders_are_recognised(self):
        from strata_control.discovery import in_trash
        for p in ("/home/u/.local/share/Trash/files/strata", "/mnt/d/.Trash-1000/files/Strata", "/Users/u/.Trash/Strata",
                  "C:\\$Recycle.Bin\\S-1-5-21\\$R123\\Strata", "/home/u/.local/share/trash/files/strata/x"):
            self.assertTrue(in_trash(p), p)
        for p in ("/home/u/bin/strata", "/home/u/Trash-talk/strata", "/home/u/trash/strata", "/opt/Strata",
                  "C:\\Users\\u\\Strata"):
            self.assertFalse(in_trash(p), p)

    def test_remembered_installs_in_the_trash_are_not_listed(self):
        from strata_control import discovery
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            good = Path(tmp) / "bin" / "strata"
            trash = Path(tmp) / ".local" / "share" / "Trash" / "files" / "strata"
            got = discovery._installs_in({"installs": [str(trash), str(good)]})
            self.assertEqual(got, [good])

    def test_setup_does_not_pass_a_trash_folder_on(self):
        import setup
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            trash = Path(tmp) / ".local" / "share" / "Trash" / "files" / "strata"
            trash.mkdir(parents=True)
            (trash / "setup.py").write_text("x")
            from unittest import mock
            nowhere = Path(tmp) / "none" / "none" / "home"            # no Strata* folders beside it on this PC
            with mock.patch.object(setup, "home", return_value=nowhere):
                self.assertEqual(setup.other_installs({"installs": [str(trash)]}), [])
                self.assertEqual(setup.other_installs({"installs": [str(trash)] + [str(trash.parent.parent)]}), [])


class Issue2971WebToolRowFitsPhones(unittest.TestCase):
    """A tool row widened the whole page on a phone (752 px page at a 412 px viewport, measured in Chrome). The three rules
    that keep it inside the viewport; a long tool name is cut with an ellipsis instead of pushing the page."""

    def test_the_rules_are_in_the_stylesheet(self):
        import re
        css = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "serve" / "web" / "app.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        def rule(selector):
            m = re.search(r"(?m)^" + re.escape(selector) + r"\s*\{([^}]*)\}", css)
            self.assertIsNotNone(m, selector)
            return m.group(1)

        self.assertIn("min-width: 0", rule(".view"))
        self.assertIn("overflow: hidden", rule(".tool-call > summary"))
        name = rule(".tool-call__name")
        for part in ("min-width: 0", "overflow: hidden", "text-overflow: ellipsis"):
            self.assertIn(part, name)


class Issue3188BenchStartsItsOwnServer(unittest.TestCase):
    """tools/strata_bench.py named `port` in the start-a-server branch without ever setting it."""

    def test_the_start_branch_runs_with_the_config_port(self):
        from unittest import mock
        from tools import strata_bench as sb
        import io
        from contextlib import redirect_stdout
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            cfg = Path(tmp) / "run.json"
            cfg.write_text(json.dumps({"port": 18999, "args": []}), encoding="utf-8")
            started = []
            with mock.patch.object(sb, "is_strata", return_value=False), \
                    mock.patch.object(sb, "try_json", return_value=None), \
                    mock.patch.object(sb, "start_server", side_effect=lambda c, p, g, log: started.append(p) or object()), \
                    mock.patch.object(sb, "wait_ready", return_value=False), \
                    mock.patch.object(sb, "stop_server"):
                out = io.StringIO()
                with redirect_stdout(out), mock.patch("sys.stderr", io.StringIO()):
                    code = sb.main(["--config", str(cfg)])
                self.assertEqual(code, 1)
                self.assertEqual(started, [18999])
                self.assertIn("on port 18999", out.getvalue())
                started.clear()
                with redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), mock.patch("sys.stderr", io.StringIO()):
                    sb.main(["--config", str(cfg), "--port", "18777"])
                self.assertEqual(started, [18777])


@unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "win32", "SDDL aliases exist on Windows only")
class Issue3302AdministratorAlias(unittest.TestCase):
    """SDDL prints the built-in Administrator (RID 500) as `LA`; the owner-only checks must still accept it."""

    def setUp(self):
        from unittest import mock
        from strata_control import private_files as pf
        self.pf = pf
        self.mock = mock
        # the built-in Administrator's string SID on this machine: resolve the alias the same way the fix does
        import ctypes
        from ctypes import wintypes
        pointer = ctypes.c_void_p()
        pf._advapi.ConvertStringSidToSidW("LA", ctypes.byref(pointer))
        text = wintypes.LPWSTR()
        pf._advapi.ConvertSidToStringSidW(pointer.value, ctypes.byref(text))
        self.admin_sid = text.value
        self.assertTrue(self.admin_sid.endswith("-500"))

    def test_alias_matches_the_account_it_names(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.pf._same_sid("LA", self.admin_sid))
        self.assertTrue(self.pf._same_sid(self.admin_sid, self.admin_sid))
        self.assertFalse(self.pf._same_sid("LA", "S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001"))
        self.assertFalse(self.pf._same_sid("WD", self.admin_sid))
        self.assertFalse(self.pf._same_sid("S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001", self.admin_sid))

    def test_private_and_unshared_hold_for_the_built_in_administrator(self):
        pf = self.pf
        with self.mock.patch.object(pf, "current_user_sid", return_value=self.admin_sid), \
                self.mock.patch.object(pf, "dacl_sddl", return_value="D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)"):
            self.assertTrue(pf.is_private("x"))
            self.assertTrue(pf.is_unshared("x"))
        with self.mock.patch.object(pf, "current_user_sid", return_value=self.admin_sid), \
                self.mock.patch.object(pf, "dacl_sddl", return_value="D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;S-1-5-21-1-2-3-1001)"):
            self.assertFalse(pf.is_private("x"))
            self.assertFalse(pf.is_unshared("x"))
        with self.mock.patch.object(pf, "current_user_sid", return_value=self.admin_sid), \
                self.mock.patch.object(pf, "dacl_sddl", return_value="D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)(A;OICI;FR;;;WD)"):
            self.assertFalse(pf.is_private("x"))
            self.assertFalse(pf.is_unshared("x"))



class Issue3488IntegrityRetry(unittest.TestCase):
    """A hash that reads wrong once (file just unpacked, or held by a virus scanner) must not stick."""

    def test_second_read_decides(self):
        from unittest import mock
        from strata_control import engine_component as ec
        path = Path("x")
        with mock.patch.object(ec, "_sha256", side_effect=["bad", "good"]) as sha, mock.patch.object(ec.time, "sleep"):
            self.assertEqual(ec._hash_settled(path, "good"), "good")
            self.assertEqual(sha.call_count, 2)
        with mock.patch.object(ec, "_sha256", side_effect=[PermissionError(), "good"]), mock.patch.object(ec.time, "sleep"):
            self.assertEqual(ec._hash_settled(path, "good"), "good")
        with mock.patch.object(ec, "_sha256", return_value="bad"), mock.patch.object(ec.time, "sleep"):
            self.assertEqual(ec._hash_settled(path, "good"), "bad")      # still wrong after the retry: refuse



class Issue3501TrashOnPosix(unittest.TestCase):
    """A Windows Recycle Bin path read on Linux: Path does not split backslashes there."""

    def test_windows_path_on_a_posix_path_class(self):
        from pathlib import PurePosixPath
        from unittest import mock
        from strata_control import discovery
        with mock.patch.object(discovery, "Path", PurePosixPath):
            self.assertTrue(discovery.in_trash(r"C:\$Recycle.Bin\S-1-5-21\$R123\Strata"))
            self.assertTrue(discovery.in_trash("/mnt/d/$RECYCLE.BIN/S-1/Strata"))
            self.assertFalse(discovery.in_trash(r"C:\Users\a\Strata"))



class Issue3504MultiValueArgs(unittest.TestCase):
    """Advanced settings: a two-value option is two argv entries, `off` removes all of its values, an empty value is no bare flag."""

    ARGS = ["--max-context", "131072", "--control-vector-layer-range", "4", "44", "--cvec-dir", "per-layer",
            "--conversation-cache-mib", "8192"]

    def test_two_values_are_two_entries(self):
        from strata_control import tune_knobs
        for typed in ("4,44", "4 44", "4-44"):
            out = tune_knobs.apply_to_argv(self.ARGS, {"--control-vector-layer-range": typed})
            i = out.index("--control-vector-layer-range")
            self.assertEqual(out[i + 1:i + 3], ["4", "44"], typed)
            self.assertEqual(out.count("--control-vector-layer-range"), 1)

    def test_off_removes_the_option_and_every_value(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import settings as S
        from strata_control import tune_knobs
        extra = {"--control-vector-layer-range": "off", "--cvec-dir": "off"}
        a, _ = S.as_argv_changes(extra, tune_knobs.BOOL_FLAGS)
        out = tune_knobs.apply_to_argv(self.ARGS, a)
        self.assertEqual(out, ["--max-context", "131072", "--conversation-cache-mib", "8192"])

    def test_an_empty_value_is_no_bare_flag(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import settings as S
        from strata_control import tune_knobs
        a, _ = S.as_argv_changes({"--cvec-dir": "", "--kv-grow": ""}, tune_knobs.BOOL_FLAGS)
        self.assertEqual(a, {"--kv-grow": True})
        self.assertEqual(tune_knobs.apply_to_argv(self.ARGS, a)[:-1].count("--cvec-dir"), 1)

    def test_set_flag_and_the_table_keep_both_values(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import params
        from strata_control import user_args
        self.assertEqual(user_args.set_flag([], "--control-vector-layer-range", "4,44"),
                         ["--control-vector-layer-range", "4", "44"])
        self.assertEqual(params.argv_to_dict(self.ARGS)["--control-vector-layer-range"], "4 44")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations
