                with zipfile.ZipFile(bundle) as archive:
                    self.assertIn(b"MIT License", archive.read("LICENSE"))
                    self.assertIn("strata_cli/dashboard.py", archive.namelist())
                if importlib.util.find_spec("textual") is not None:
                    import_check = subprocess.run(
                        [sys.executable, "-I", "-c",
                         "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, " + repr(str(bundle)) + "); "
                         "from strata_cli.monitor import MonitorApp; print(MonitorApp.__name__)"],
                        cwd=directory, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
                    self.assertEqual(import_check.stdout.strip(), "MonitorApp")
                url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}"
                source_output = io.StringIO()
                with redirect_stdout(source_output):
                    self.assertEqual(source_main(["monitor", "--once", "--json", "--url", url]), 0)
                clean_env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("PYTHONPATH", "PYTHONHOME")}
                clean_env["STRATA_CONNECTION_DIR"] = str(Path(directory) / "connections")
                portable = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-S", str(bundle), "monitor", "--once", "--json",
                                           "--url", url], cwd=directory, env=clean_env, check=True,
                                          capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(portable.stdout), json.loads(source_output.getvalue()))
                bare_source = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-S", str(ROOT / "strata.py"), "monitor",
                                              "--once", "--json", "--url", url], cwd=directory, env=clean_env,
                                             check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(bare_source.stdout), json.loads(portable.stdout))
                status = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-S", str(bundle), "status", "--json", "--url", url],
                                        cwd=directory, env=clean_env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(status.stdout)["snapshot"]["work"]["active"], 2)
                saved = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-S", str(bundle), "connection", "list", "--json"],
                                       cwd=directory, env=clean_env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(saved.stdout)["connections"], [])
                quiet_saved = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-S", str(bundle), "connection", "list", "--quiet"],
                                             cwd=directory, env=clean_env, check=True,
                                             capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual((quiet_saved.stdout, quiet_saved.stderr), ("", ""))
                quiet_json = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-S", str(bundle), "connection", "list",
                                             "--quiet", "--json"], cwd=directory, env=clean_env,
                                            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(quiet_json.stdout)["connections"], [])
                self.assertEqual(paths, ["/v1/telemetry"] * 4)
                data = bytearray(bundle.read_bytes())
                data[-1] ^= 1
                bundle.write_bytes(data)
                broken = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(BUILDER), "verify", str(bundle)],
                                        capture_output=True, text=True)
                self.assertEqual(broken.returncode, 1)
                self.assertIn("SHA-256 mismatch", broken.stderr)
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()
            thread.join(timeout=2)


## tests/terminal/test_monitor_classic.py

"""The monitor in the classic Windows console (Cascadia Mono switch, the solid look, the tip) and with several cards / CPUs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import time
import unittest
from unittest import mock

from rich.console import Console

from strata_cli import consoleinfo, monitor, overview
from tests.terminal.test_overview import GIB, metrics

TIP = "For the full look, use Windows Terminal (built into Windows 11)"


def draw(model, width=110, height=40, **kw) -> str:
    c = Console(width=width + 2, record=True, file=io.StringIO(), force_terminal=False, legacy_windows=False)
    c.print(overview.render(model, width=width, height=height, connection="http://127.0.0.1:8080", **kw))
    return c.export_text()


def three_cards(sockets=2):
    m = metrics("generating")
    cards = [{"index": i, "name": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090", "util": u, "mem_used": used * GIB, "mem_total": 24 * GIB, "temp": t, "power": p, "power_limit": 350}
             for i, (u, used, t, p) in enumerate(((88, 22.1, 61, 236), (71, 21.4, 58, 201), (64, 20.8, 55, 188)))]
    m["hardware"]["gpus"] = cards
    m["hardware_static"].update({"gpu_name": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090", "gpu_count": 3, "cores": 64, "threads": 128, "sockets": sockets, "numa_nodes": 2})
    return m


class WhichLook(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        consoleinfo.forget_style()
        self.addCleanup(consoleinfo.forget_style)

    def test_decide_style_by_the_facts(self):
        d = consoleinfo.decide_style(legacy=False, cascadia_ok=False, font=None)
        self.assertEqual((d["mode"], d["tip"]), ("none", None))                       # Windows Terminal, Linux, macOS: nothing changes
        d = consoleinfo.decide_style(legacy=True, cascadia_ok=True, font="Cascadia Mono")
        self.assertEqual((d["mode"], d["tip"]), ("full", TIP))                        # the font was switched: the full Unicode look, the tip anyway
        d = consoleinfo.decide_style(legacy=True, cascadia_ok=False, font="Consolas")
        self.assertEqual((d["mode"], d["bullet"], d["tip"]), ("solid", "●", TIP))
        d = consoleinfo.decide_style(legacy=True, cascadia_ok=False, font="Lucida Console")
        self.assertEqual((d["mode"], d["bullet"]), ("solid", "•"))                    # Lucida has no ●
        self.assertEqual(consoleinfo.decide_style(legacy=True, cascadia_ok=False, font=None)["bullet"], "•")

    def test_classic_style_switches_the_font_once_when_cascadia_is_installed(self):
        with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=True), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.os, "name", "nt"), \
                mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_GLYPHS": ""}), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "cascadia_installed", return_value=True), \
                mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "console_font", side_effect=["Consolas", "Cascadia Mono"]), \
                mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "switch_font", return_value=True) as sw:
            s = consoleinfo.classic_style()
            self.assertEqual(s["mode"], "full")
            sw.assert_called_once_with("Cascadia Mono")
            consoleinfo.classic_style()
            sw.assert_called_once()                                                   # cached: the font API is not called again

    def test_without_cascadia_or_when_the_switch_fails_the_solid_look_with_the_font_it_has(self):
        for installed, switched in ((False, False), (True, False)):
            consoleinfo.forget_style()
            with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=True), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.os, "name", "nt"), \
                    mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_GLYPHS": ""}), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "cascadia_installed", return_value=installed), \
                    mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "console_font", return_value="Lucida Console"), \
                    mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "switch_font", return_value=switched):
                s = consoleinfo.classic_style()
                self.assertEqual((s["mode"], s["bullet"]), ("solid", "•"))

    def test_never_in_windows_terminal_linux_or_mac(self):
        with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=False), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "switch_font") as sw:
            self.assertEqual(consoleinfo.classic_style()["mode"], "none")
            sw.assert_not_called()
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("WT_SESSION", "TERM_PROGRAM", "STRATA_GLYPHS")}
        env["WT_SESSION"] = "x"
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env, clear=True), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.os, "name", "nt"), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.sys, "platform", "win32"):
            self.assertFalse(consoleinfo.legacy_console())                            # Windows Terminal
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=True), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.os, "name", "posix"), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.sys, "platform", "linux"):
            self.assertFalse(consoleinfo.legacy_console())
        with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo.os, "name", "posix"):
            self.assertIsNone(consoleinfo.console_font())
            self.assertFalse(consoleinfo.switch_font())
            self.assertFalse(consoleinfo.cascadia_installed())

    def test_choose_glyphs(self):
        with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=True), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "classic_style", return_value={"mode": "full"}):
            self.assertEqual(monitor.choose_glyphs("auto", "utf-8", "xterm"), "unicode")
        with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=True), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "classic_style", return_value={"mode": "solid"}):
            self.assertEqual(monitor.choose_glyphs("auto", "utf-8", None), "solid")
            with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_GLYPHS": "ascii"}):
                self.assertEqual(monitor.choose_glyphs("auto", "utf-8", None), "ascii")      # forced ASCII stays ASCII
            self.assertEqual(monitor.choose_glyphs("unicode", "utf-8", None), "unicode")      # an explicit --glyphs wins
        with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=False):
            self.assertEqual(monitor.choose_glyphs("auto", "utf-8", "xterm"), "unicode")


class SolidLook(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_solid_blocks_only_no_dithered_shades_and_no_eighth_blocks(self):
        text = draw(overview.build(metrics("generating")), glyphs="solid")
        for ch in "░▒▓▁▂▃▅▆▇╭╮╰╯":
            self.assertNotIn(ch, text, ch)
        for ch in "█▄┌┐└┘":
            self.assertIn(ch, text, ch)

    def test_bars_use_a_thin_track_and_boxes_are_square(self):
        bar = overview.bar(0.25, 20, "solid", "bright_green")
        self.assertEqual(bar.plain, "█" * 5 + "▄" * 15)
        self.assertEqual(overview.bar(None, 4, "solid", "x").plain, "▄▄▄▄")
        self.assertEqual(overview.spark([0, 50, 100], 3, "solid", lo=0, hi=100).plain, "▄▄█")

    def test_the_16_palette_names_not_hex_colours(self):
        group = overview.render(overview.build(metrics("generating")), width=110, height=40, connection="x", glyphs="solid")
        c = Console(width=112, record=True, file=io.StringIO(), force_terminal=True, color_system="standard", legacy_windows=False)
        c.print(group)
        out = c.export_text(styles=True)
        self.assertNotIn("38;2;", out)                                          # no 24-bit colours: conhost maps them to cyan or black

    def test_the_bullet_follows_the_font(self):
        m = overview.build(metrics("generating"))
        self.assertIn("● Generating", draw(m, glyphs="solid", bullet="●"))
        self.assertIn("• Generating", draw(m, glyphs="solid", bullet="•"))

    def test_the_other_looks_are_unchanged(self):
        m = overview.build(metrics("generating"))
        self.assertIn("╭", draw(m, glyphs="unicode"))
        self.assertNotIn("╭", draw(m, glyphs="ascii"))


class SeveralCards(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_one_card_looks_exactly_as_before(self):
        base = metrics("generating")
        one = metrics("generating")
        one["hardware"]["gpus"] = [{"index": 0, "name": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070", "util": 88, "mem_used": 11.2 * GIB, "mem_total": 12 * GIB, "temp": 54, "power": 114}]
        for glyphs in ("unicode", "ascii", "solid"):
            self.assertEqual(draw(overview.build(base), glyphs=glyphs, now=1.0), draw(overview.build(one), glyphs=glyphs, now=1.0), glyphs)
        self.assertNotIn("Cards", draw(overview.build(base)))

    def test_the_tiles_say_it_for_the_whole_computer(self):
        m = overview.build(three_cards())
        g = m["gpu"]
        self.assertEqual((g["util"], g["temp"], g["count"]), (88.0, 61.0, 3.0))                  # the busiest, the hottest
        self.assertAlmostEqual(g["vram_used"], 64.3, places=1)
        self.assertEqual(g["vram_total"], 72.0)                                                    # all cards
        self.assertEqual((g["power"], g["power_limit"]), (625.0, 1050.0))
        text = draw(m)
        for want in ("busiest of 3 cards", "all 3 cards", "hottest card", "64.3 / 72 GB", "625 W", "of 1,050 W limit", "61 °C"):
            self.assertIn(want, text, want)
        self.assertNotIn("+2", text)                                                              # no more "RTX 3090 +2"

    def test_the_cards_strip_one_line_per_card(self):
        text = draw(overview.build(three_cards()))
        lines = [ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.startswith("GPU ")]
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 3)
        self.assertIn("Cards", text)
        for want, line in zip(("88 %", "71 %", "64 %"), lines):
            self.assertIn(want, line)
        self.assertIn("22.1 / 24 GB", lines[0])
        self.assertIn("61 °C", lines[0])
        self.assertIn("236 W", lines[0])
        self.assertIn("RTX 3090", lines[0])

    def test_up_to_four_cards_then_a_pointer_to_view_5(self):
        m = three_cards()
        m["hardware"]["gpus"] += [dict(m["hardware"]["gpus"][0], index=i) for i in (3, 4, 5)]
        text = draw(overview.build(m), height=44)
        self.assertEqual(len([ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.startswith("GPU ")]), 4)
        self.assertIn("+ 2 more cards: press 5", text)

    def test_the_cpu_tile_says_how_many_cpus(self):
        self.assertIn("2 CPUs · 64 cores", draw(overview.build(three_cards(sockets=2))))
        one = draw(overview.build(three_cards(sockets=1)))
        self.assertIn("64 cores · 128 threads", one)
        self.assertNotIn("CPUs", one)
        self.assertIn("6 cores · 12 threads", draw(overview.build(metrics("generating"))))     # no socket count reported: as before

    def test_a_missing_reading_stays_missing(self):
        m = three_cards()
        for c in m["hardware"]["gpus"]:
            c["temp"] = None
            c["power"] = None
        g = overview.build(m)["gpu"]
        self.assertIsNone(g["temp"])
        self.assertIsNone(g["power"])
        self.assertIn("-- °C", draw(overview.build(m)))

    def test_it_fits_the_width_and_the_classic_looks_too(self):
        for glyphs in ("unicode", "ascii", "solid"):
            for ln in draw(overview.build(three_cards()), glyphs=glyphs, width=100).splitlines():
                self.assertLessEqual(len(ln.rstrip()), 102, (glyphs, ln))


class FooterAndViews(unittest.TestCase):
    def screen_text(self, classic):
        import asyncio
        from tests.terminal.test_overview import Source

        async def go():
            consoleinfo.forget_style()
            style = consoleinfo.decide_style(legacy=bool(classic), cascadia_ok=classic == "full", font="Consolas")
            with mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "legacy_console", return_value=bool(classic)), mock.patch.object(consoleinfo, "classic_style", return_value=style):
                app = monitor.MonitorApp(Source(three_cards()), None, interval=30)
                async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
                    await pilot.pause(0.5)
                    return "\n".join(s.text for s in app.screen._compositor.render_strips())
        try:
            return asyncio.run(go())
        finally:
            consoleinfo.forget_style()

    def test_the_tip_is_in_the_classic_console_only(self):
        self.assertIn(TIP, self.screen_text("solid"))
        self.assertIn(TIP, self.screen_text("full"))                  # also when the font was switched: one line, always
        self.assertNotIn(TIP, self.screen_text(None))                  # Windows Terminal, Linux, macOS

    def test_the_monitor_draws_the_several_cards_in_every_look(self):
        for classic in ("solid", "full", None):
            shown = self.screen_text(classic)
            self.assertIn("busiest of 3 cards", shown, classic)
            self.assertIn("Cards", shown, classic)
            self.assertIn("2 CPUs", shown, classic)

    def test_view_5_shows_the_whole_card_name(self):
        from strata_cli.render import _device
        row = {"index": 1, "name": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090", "mem_used": 21.4 * GIB, "mem_total": 24 * GIB, "util": 71, "temp": 58, "power": 201}
        line = _device(row, 100)
        self.assertIn("RTX 3090", line)
        self.assertNotIn("NVIDIA", line)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_no_acquisition.py

"""Starting and serving never acquire anything.

The owner's rule: a user must never download random packages from the internet while starting or serving. Everything
that installs, downloads or compiles lives behind an explicit command (SETUP, UPDATE, `strata install`). Three layers
are checked here:

* the import graph of the start/serve entry points does not reach installer code;
* no module on the start/serve side runs pip, git, cmake, npm or a package manager, or opens a URL, outside a short
  list of request-time and loopback uses, each with its reason;
* a real start (setup.main with an installed model) with the network and every subprocess mocked makes no request and
  runs no installer, and a start that WOULD need one stops with a typed error that names the explicit command.
"""

import ast
import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

import setup
from strata_cli import cli
from strata_control import acquisition

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

#: Modules the start/serve entry points must never load.
INSTALLER_MODULES = {"setup", "pip", "ensurepip", "venv", "huggingface_hub", "modelscope", "metal.setup_mac",
                     "sycl.setup_intel"}
#: Files that may be loaded on the start/serve side besides the control, cli and serve packages.
ALLOWED_TOOLS = {"tools.strata_tokenizer", "tools.gguf_reader"}   # read-only: a tokenizer and a GGUF header reader

#: argv words that mean "acquire": a subprocess whose literal argv contains one of these is an installer.
INSTALL_WORDS = {"pip", "pip3", "git", "cmake", "ninja", "npm", "npx", "pnpm", "yarn", "winget", "apt-get", "apt",
                 "dnf", "pacman", "brew", "curl", "wget", "choco"}

#: (file, call) -> why a network call there is not an acquisition. Request-time and loopback only.
NETWORK_ALLOWED = {
    ("serve/server.py", "urlopen"): "an image_url a client sends in a chat request is fetched at request time",
    ("serve/mcp.py", "urlopen"): "the MCP servers the user configured, at request time",
    ("strata_control/tune_api.py", "urlopen"): "the loopback engine/server of a tuning job the user started",
    ("strata_control/tune_session.py", "urlopen"): "the loopback engine (127.0.0.1) the auto-tuner a user started measures",
    ("strata_control/loopback.py", "urlopen"): "the one opener for this computer's own servers (no proxy); any other address is passed on unchanged",
    ("strata_control/components.py", "urlopen"): "the component fetcher: only `strata install`/UPDATE call it",
}
#: Modules that import the installer on purpose, with the explicit command that reaches them.
INSTALLER_IMPORT_ALLOWED = {
    "strata_control/calibration.py": "`strata engine calibrate`: an explicit tuning command, imports setup lazily",
}

SERVING_DIRS = ("serve", "strata_cli", "strata_control")


def _sources():
    for d in SERVING_DIRS:
        for p in sorted((ROOT / d).glob("*.py")):
            if p.name.startswith("test_") or p.name == "__init__.py":
                continue
            yield p
    yield ROOT / "strata.py"


class ImportGraphTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_start_and_serve_modules_do_not_load_installer_code(self):
        script = (
            "import sys, os, json\n"
            "sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())\n"
            "import strata_cli.cli as c\n"
            "import serve.server\n"
            "from strata_control import runtime\n"
            "c.parser()\n"
            "root = os.getcwd()\n"
            "mods = {n: os.path.relpath(m.__file__, root).replace(os.sep, '/') for n, m in list(sys.modules.items())\n"
            "        if getattr(m, '__file__', None) and os.path.abspath(m.__file__).startswith(root)}\n"
            "print(json.dumps({'mods': mods, 'names': sorted(sys.modules)}))\n")
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", script], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr[-1000:])
        got = json.loads(r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
        loaded = set(got["names"])
        self.assertEqual(sorted(loaded & INSTALLER_MODULES), [])
        for name, rel in got["mods"].items():
            top = rel.split("/")[0]
            self.assertIn(top, ("serve", "strata_cli", "strata_control"),
                          f"{name} ({rel}) is loaded by starting/serving but is not part of it")
        self.assertNotIn("strata_control.calibration", got["mods"])
        self.assertNotIn("strata_control.components", got["mods"])

    def test_static_imports_of_the_installer_are_explicit_commands_only(self):
        found = {}
        for p in _sources():
            rel = p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
            tree = ast.parse(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            for node in ast.walk(tree):
                names = []
                if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                    names = [a.name for a in node.names]
                elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
                    names = [node.module]
                for n in names:
                    top = n.split(".")[0]
                    if top == "setup" or n.startswith(("tools.", "metal.", "sycl.")) and n not in ALLOWED_TOOLS:
                        found.setdefault(rel, []).append(n)
        for rel in found:
            self.assertIn(rel, INSTALLER_IMPORT_ALLOWED, f"{rel} imports installer code: {found[rel]}")

    def test_no_installer_subprocess_or_network_call_on_the_serving_side(self):
        bad = []
        for p in _sources():
            rel = p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
            tree = ast.parse(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            for node in ast.walk(tree):
                if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
                    continue
                fn = node.func
                name = fn.attr if isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) else fn.id if isinstance(fn, ast.Name) else ""
                if name in ("urlopen", "urlretrieve") and (rel, name) not in NETWORK_ALLOWED \
                        and (rel, "urlopen") not in NETWORK_ALLOWED:
                    bad.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} {name}")
                if name in ("run", "call", "Popen", "check_call", "check_output") and node.args:
                    argv = node.args[0]
                    words = []
                    if isinstance(argv, (ast.List, ast.Tuple)):
                        words = [e.value for e in argv.elts if isinstance(e, ast.Constant) and isinstance(e.value, str)]
                    elif isinstance(argv, ast.Constant) and isinstance(argv.value, str):
                        words = argv.value.split()
                    hit = INSTALL_WORDS & {Path(w).stem if w.endswith(".exe") else w for w in words}
                    if hit:
                        bad.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} subprocess {sorted(hit)}")
        self.assertEqual(bad, [])
        for key, why in NETWORK_ALLOWED.items():
            self.assertTrue(why)


class _Recorder:
    """Stands in for the network and for every way of starting a program; records what a start tries."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.network = []
        self.programs = []

    def urlopen(self, req, *a, **k):
        self.network.append(getattr(req, "full_url", str(req)))
        raise AssertionError("a start reached the network: " + self.network[-1])

    def program(self, argv, *a, **k):
        argv = [str(x) for x in (argv if isinstance(argv, (list, tuple)) else str(argv).split())]
        self.programs.append(argv)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, stdout="", stderr="")

    def installers(self):
        return [a for a in self.programs
                if INSTALL_WORDS & {Path(w).stem.lower() if w.lower().endswith(".exe") else w for w in a}
                or "pip" in a or "-m" in a and "pip" in a]


class StartNeverAcquiresTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name) / "Strata"
        self.root.mkdir()
        self.data = Path(self.tmp.name) / "Strata-data"
        (self.data / "models").mkdir(parents=True)
        self.gguf = self.data / "models" / "m.gguf"
        self.gguf.write_bytes(b"GGUF")
        eng = self.root / "engine"
        eng.mkdir()
        (eng / setup.EXE).write_bytes(b"engine")
        # an engine older than this Strata expects: a start used to download the new one
        (eng / "BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps({"version": "0.1.1", "source": "prebuilt", "backend": "cuda",
                                                    "archs": [86]}))
        self.cfg = self.root / "strata-q2_0.json"
        self.cfg.write_text(json.dumps({
            "exe": str(eng / setup.EXE), "args": ["--native", str(self.gguf), "--max-context", "8192"],
            "tokenizer": str(self.data / "tok.json"), "model_name": "Q2_0", "port": 8080}))
        self.settings_home = Path(self.tmp.name) / "appdata"
        self.settings_home.mkdir()
        env = {"APPDATA": str(self.settings_home), "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(self.settings_home)}
        patcher = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env)
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        setup.settings_path().parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        setup.settings_path().write_text(json.dumps({"data_dir": str(self.data), "installs": [str(self.root)]}))
        self.settings_before = setup.settings_path().read_bytes()
        # pip_install keeps its stamp in sys.prefix: never in the interpreter running the tests
        prefix = mock.patch.object(sys, "prefix", str(self.root))
        prefix.start()
        self.addCleanup(prefix.stop)

    def run_setup(self, rec, *argv, gpus=None):
        out = io.StringIO()
        started = []
        with contextlib.ExitStack() as st:
            st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(setup, "ROOT", self.root))
            st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(sys, "argv", ["setup.py", *argv]))
            st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(urllib.request, "urlopen", rec.urlopen))
            for n in ("run", "call", "Popen", "check_call", "check_output"):
                st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(subprocess, n, rec.program))
            st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(setup, "gpus", lambda: gpus or []))
            st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(setup, "call_server", create=True))
            st.enter_context(mock.patch.object(setup.subprocess, "call", lambda cmd, *a, **k: (
                started.append(cmd), setattr(self, "env_of_start", (k.get("env") or {}).get(acquisition.ENV)), 0)[-1]))
            st.enter_context(contextlib.redirect_stdout(out))
            try:
                code = setup.main()
            except SystemExit as e:
                code = e.code
            except acquisition.AcquisitionRefused as e:
                code = e
        return code, out.getvalue(), started

    def test_a_start_with_an_old_engine_makes_no_request_and_runs_no_installer(self):
        rec = _Recorder()
        code, text, started = self.run_setup(rec, "--yes", "--no-browser")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, text)
        self.assertEqual(rec.network, [])
        self.assertEqual(rec.installers(), [])
        self.assertEqual(len(started), 1, text)                        # the server was started
        self.assertIn("server.py", " ".join(started[0]))
        self.assertEqual(self.env_of_start, "1")                         # the server is told, too
        self.assertIn("is older than this Strata expects", text)
        self.assertTrue("UPDATE" in text or "update.sh" in text, text)     # UPDATE.bat on Windows, ./update.sh elsewhere

    def test_a_start_moves_copies_and_creates_nothing(self):
        before = sorted(p.relative_to(self.tmp.name).as_posix() for p in Path(self.tmp.name).rglob("*"))
        stamps = {p: p.stat().st_mtime_ns for p in Path(self.tmp.name).rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
        rec = _Recorder()
        code, text, _ = self.run_setup(rec, "--yes", "--no-browser")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, text)
        after = sorted(p.relative_to(self.tmp.name).as_posix() for p in Path(self.tmp.name).rglob("*"))
        self.assertEqual(before, after)
        self.assertEqual(setup.settings_path().read_bytes(), self.settings_before)
        for p, ns in stamps.items():
            if p != self.cfg:                                          # a start touches the config (most recently used)
                self.assertEqual(p.stat().st_mtime_ns, ns, p)

    def test_a_card_the_engine_has_no_code_for_is_a_typed_error_naming_the_command(self):
        rec = _Recorder()
        card = {"index": 0, "name": "RTX 5090", "arch": "120", "vram_gb": 32.0, "driver": "580.0"}
        with mock.patch.object(setup, "engine_runs_on", lambda g, tk=13: False), \
                mock.patch.object(setup, "old_gpus_opt_in", lambda *a, **k: []):
            code, text, started = self.run_setup(rec, "--yes", "--no-browser", gpus=[card])
        self.assertIsInstance(code, acquisition.AcquisitionRefused)
        self.assertIn("RTX 5090", str(code))
        self.assertIn("setup", str(code).lower())
        self.assertEqual((rec.network, rec.installers(), started), ([], [], []))

    def test_main_script_reports_the_refusal_and_exits_5(self):
        e = acquisition.AcquisitionRefused("an engine for sm_120")
        self.assertEqual(e.exit_code, 5)
        self.assertEqual(e.code, "acquisition_refused")
        self.assertIn("never install or download", str(e))

    def test_every_acquiring_primitive_refuses_while_a_model_starts(self):
        rec = _Recorder()
        calls = [
            lambda: setup.download("https://example.invalid/x.bin", self.root / "x.bin"),
            lambda: setup.download("file:///nonexistent", self.root / "y.bin"),
            lambda: setup.pip_install(["definitely-not-installed==1.0"], "a test package"),
            lambda: setup.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "x"]),
            lambda: setup._urlopen(urllib.request.Request("https://example.invalid/")),
            lambda: setup.reachable("https://example.invalid/"),
            lambda: setup.get_prebuilt("https://example.invalid/", {"arch": "86"}, "none"),
            lambda: setup.cmake_build(self.root, self.root / "b", "strata", [], None, ""),
            lambda: setup.pip_cuda_libs(13),
        ]
        with mock.patch.object(urllib.request, "urlopen", rec.urlopen), \
                mock.patch.object(subprocess, "run", rec.program), mock.patch.object(subprocess, "Popen", rec.program):
            with acquisition.forbidden():
                for i, call in enumerate(calls):
                    with self.subTest(i=i):
                        with self.assertRaises(acquisition.AcquisitionRefused) as cm:
                            call()
                        self.assertIn("Run:", str(cm.exception))
        self.assertEqual((rec.network, rec.programs), ([], []))

    def test_the_environment_switch_forbids_a_whole_process(self):
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {acquisition.ENV: "1"}):
            with self.assertRaises(acquisition.AcquisitionRefused):
                setup.pip_install(["definitely-not-installed==1.0"], "a test package")

    def test_update_still_installs(self):
        """The explicit commands keep working: outside a start, the install step runs."""
        installed = []
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as prefix, mock.patch.object(sys, "prefix", prefix),                 mock.patch.object(setup, "run", lambda cmd, **k: installed.append([str(c) for c in cmd])):
            setup.pip_install(["somepkg==1.0"], "a test package")
        self.assertEqual(len(installed), 1)
        self.assertIn("pip", installed[0])


class CliServeIsOfflineTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_serve_plan_reaches_no_network_and_runs_no_program(self):
        rec = _Recorder()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            cfg = Path(d) / "strata-x.json"
            gguf = Path(d) / "m.gguf"
            gguf.write_bytes(b"GGUF")
            tok = Path(d) / "t.json"
            tok.write_text("{}")
            exe = Path(d) / "strata.exe"
            exe.write_bytes(b"x")
            cfg.write_text(json.dumps({"exe": str(exe), "args": ["--native", str(gguf)], "tokenizer": str(tok)}))
            out = io.StringIO()
            with mock.patch.object(urllib.request, "urlopen", rec.urlopen), \
                    mock.patch.object(subprocess, "run", rec.program), mock.patch.object(subprocess, "Popen", rec.program), \
                    mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_PROFILE_DIR": str(Path(d) / "profiles")}), \
                    contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
                code = cli.main(["serve", "--profile", str(cfg), "--plan", "--output", "json"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out.getvalue())
        self.assertEqual((rec.network, rec.programs), ([], []))
        self.assertNotIn("setup", sys.modules.get("strata_cli.cli").__dict__.get("__name__", ""))

    def test_strata_install_without_the_installer_is_a_typed_error(self):
        err = io.StringIO()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d, \
                mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_INSTALL_DIR": d}), \
                mock.patch.object(cli, "ROOT", Path(d)), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            code = cli.main(["install"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 5)
        self.assertIn("installer", err.getvalue())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_overview.py

"""The monitor's Overview (view 1): numbers from /metrics, the drawing, glyph fallbacks, and the monitor showing it."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import io
import time
import unittest

from rich.console import Console

from strata_cli import overview
from strata_cli.monitor import MonitorApp

GIB = 2 ** 30


def metrics(state="reading", **over):
    now = time.time()
    hist = lambda base, amp: [base + amp * ((i * 7) % 5) / 4 for i in range(60)]     # noqa: E731
    m = {"time": now,
         "engine": {"model": "IQ3_S", "max_context": 131072, "expert_slots": 1644, "experts": 5120, "expert_cache_mib": 3280},
         "live": {"state": state, "queued": 0, "prompt_read": 35610 if state == "reading" else None, "prompt_total": 36742 if state == "reading" else None,
                  "prompt_tokens": 36742, "generated": 120 if state == "generating" else 0, "max_tokens": 4096,
                  "tok_s": 50.4 if state == "generating" else None, "prefill_tok_s_mean": 820.0},
         "hardware": {"gpu_util": 88, "gpu_mem_used": 11.2 * GIB, "gpu_mem_total": 12 * GIB, "gpu_temp": 54, "gpu_power": 114, "gpu_power_limit": 250,
                      "gpu_pcie_rx_mb": 18237, "gpu_pcie_gen": 4, "gpu_pcie_width": 16, "cpu": 14, "ram_used": 58.5 * GIB, "ram_total": 63 * GIB,
                      "disk_read_mb": 0.1, "disk_write_mb": 0.0},
         "hardware_static": {"gpu_name": "RTX 5070", "gpu_count": 1, "cores": 6, "threads": 12},
         "history": {"tok_s": hist(40, 10), "gpu_util": hist(80, 10), "gpu_mem_used": [11.2 * GIB] * 60, "gpu_temp": [54] * 60,
                     "gpu_power": hist(110, 10), "gpu_pcie_rx_mb": hist(10000, 9000), "cpu": hist(10, 8), "disk_read_mb": hist(0, 3)},
         "requests": [{"id": "a", "time": now - 5, "duration_s": 429.8, "finish_reason": "stop", "prompt_tokens": 17183, "reused": 0,
                       "output_tokens": 19511, "decode_ms": 386000},
                      {"id": "b", "time": now - 9, "duration_s": 4.0, "finish_reason": "stop", "prompt_tokens": 626, "reused": 0,
                       "output_tokens": 11, "decode_ms": 410}]}
    m.update(over)
    return m


def draw(model, width=110, height=30, **kw) -> str:
    c = Console(width=width + 2, record=True, file=io.StringIO(), force_terminal=False, legacy_windows=False)
    c.print(overview.render(model, width=width, height=height, connection="http://127.0.0.1:8080", **kw))
    return c.export_text()


class Build(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reading_state_and_progress(self):
        m = overview.build(metrics("reading"))
        self.assertEqual(m["state"], "Reading")
        self.assertEqual(m["progress"], (35610.0, 36742.0))
        self.assertEqual(m["context"], (36742.0, 131072.0))
        self.assertEqual(m["speed"][:2], (820.0, "reading the prompt"))

    def test_generating_uses_the_live_rate_and_prompt_plus_generated_for_context(self):
        m = overview.build(metrics("generating"))
        self.assertEqual(m["state"], "Generating")
        self.assertEqual(m["speed"][:2], (50.4, "now"))
        self.assertEqual(m["context"][0], 36742 + 120)
        self.assertEqual(m["progress"], (120.0, 4096.0))

    def test_idle_shows_the_last_request(self):
        m = overview.build(metrics("idle"))
        self.assertEqual(m["state"], "Idle")
        self.assertEqual(m["speed"][1], "last request")
        self.assertAlmostEqual(m["speed"][0], 50.5, places=1)               # 19511 tokens in 386 s
        self.assertEqual(m["context"][0], 17183 + 19511)
        self.assertEqual(m["progress"], (None, None))

    def test_queued_and_error(self):
        self.assertEqual(overview.build(metrics("idle", live={"state": "idle", "queued": 3}))["state"], "Queued")
        self.assertEqual(overview.build(metrics("idle", engine={"model": "x", "error": "boom"}))["state"], "Error")

    def test_hardware_in_gb(self):
        m = overview.build(metrics())
        self.assertAlmostEqual(m["gpu"]["vram_used"], 11.2)
        self.assertEqual(m["gpu"]["vram_total"], 12.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(m["ram"][0], 58.5)
        self.assertEqual(m["experts"], {"slots": 1644.0, "total": 5120.0, "gb": 3280 / 1024.0})

    def test_missing_numbers_stay_missing(self):
        m = overview.build({"live": {"state": "idle"}, "engine": {}, "hardware": {}, "requests": []})
        self.assertIsNone(m["gpu"]["util"])
        self.assertIsNone(m["speed"][0])
        text = draw(m)
        self.assertIn("-- tok/s", text)
        self.assertIn("No requests yet", text)
        self.assertNotIn("0 %", text.replace("-- %", ""))                    # no invented zero

    def test_a_server_without_metrics_gives_none(self):
        self.assertIsNone(overview.build(None))
        self.assertIsNone(overview.build({"engine": {}}))


class Draw(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_approved_layout(self):
        text = draw(overview.build(metrics("reading")), connect=True)
        for part in ("STRATA  Overview", "IQ3_S 128K", "Reading prompt · 97%", "[LIVE]", "[1 Overview]", "7 Connect",
                     "Model state", "[Reading]", "35,610 / 36,742 tokens · 97%",
                     "Speed", "GPU load", "VRAM", "GPU temp", "Power", "PCIe", "CPU", "Disk read",
                     "88 %", "RTX 5070", "11.2 / 12 GB", "1,644 experts cached", "54 °C", "114 W", "of 250 W limit", "Gen4 x16",
                     "to GPU 18,237 MB/s", "6 cores · 12 threads", "0.1 MB/s", "write 0.0 MB/s",
                     "Context fill", "36K / 128K", "Experts in VRAM", "1,644 · 3.2 GB", "System RAM", "58.5 / 63 GB",
                     "Recent requests", "TIME", "STATUS", "PROMPT", "REUSED", "OUTPUT", "TOK/S", "DURATION", "17,183", "19,511", "429.8 s",
                     "1-7 views", "b open in browser", "q quit"):
            self.assertIn(part, text, part)

    def test_without_connect_the_hint_says_six_views(self):
        text = draw(overview.build(metrics()), connect=False)
        self.assertIn("1-6 views", text)
        self.assertNotIn("7 Connect", text)

    def test_ascii_mode_has_no_glyphs_the_classic_windows_console_font_lacks(self):
        text = draw(overview.build(metrics()), glyphs="ascii", color=False)
        for bad in "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█░╭╮╰╯✓●":
            self.assertNotIn(bad, text, bad)
        self.assertIn("#", text)
        self.assertIn("54 C", text)

    def test_fits_the_width_it_is_given(self):
        for w in (80, 100, 120):
            text = draw(overview.build(metrics()), width=w - 2)
            self.assertTrue(all(len(line) <= w for line in text.splitlines()), w)

    def test_spark(self):
        self.assertEqual(len(overview.spark([1, 2, 3], 8, "unicode")), 8)
        self.assertEqual(overview.spark([None, None], 4, "unicode"), "    ")
        self.assertEqual(overview.spark([0, 100], 2, "unicode", lo=0, hi=100), "▁█")
        self.assertEqual(overview.spark([0, 100], 2, "ascii", lo=0, hi=100), ".@")


class Source:
    root = "http://127.0.0.1:8095"

    def __init__(self, raw):
        self.raw = raw
        self.base_url = self.root

    def get(self, path):
        if path == "/metrics":
            return self.raw
        raise AssertionError(path)

    def snapshot(self):
        return {"source": "fixture", "sampled_at": time.time(), "schema_version": 1, "instance": {"id": "x"},
                "model": {"id": "IQ3_S", "loaded": True}, "work": {}, "rates": {}, "devices": [], "recent": [], "totals": {},
                "topology": {}, "quality": {}}


class InTheMonitor(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_view_one_is_the_new_overview_and_the_others_stay(self):
        async def go():
            app = MonitorApp(Source(metrics("generating")), None, interval=30)
            async with app.run_test(size=(120, 36)) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.5)
                shown = "\n".join(s.text for s in app.screen._compositor.render_strips())
                self.assertIn("Model state", shown)
                self.assertIn("Generating", shown)
                await pilot.press("2")
                await pilot.pause(0.2)
                shown = "\n".join(s.text for s in app.screen._compositor.render_strips())
                self.assertNotIn("Model state", shown)
                self.assertIn("Serving", shown)
        asyncio.run(go())

    def test_an_older_server_without_metrics_keeps_the_earlier_overview(self):
        class Old(Source):
            def get(self, path):
                from strata_cli.client import ClientError
                raise ClientError("not found", http_status=404)

        async def go():
            app = MonitorApp(Old(None), None, interval=30)
            async with app.run_test(size=(120, 36)) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.5)
                shown = "\n".join(s.text for s in app.screen._compositor.render_strips())
                self.assertNotIn("Model state", shown)
                self.assertIn("MONITOR", shown)
        asyncio.run(go())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_own_files.py

"""0.2.2: "use my own model files" accepts every layout 0.1.45's `setup.py --gguf-dir` accepted (issues #3316 #3292 #3190 #3209 #3331).

The checker in front of setup (strata_control/models.plan_import) used to be stricter than setup itself: a split set whose first shard
holds only the metadata (Unsloth's), a link to the file (Hugging Face cache, Ollama), a folder holding several sizes, a folder above the
model folder (a whole repository, a 0.1.45 data folder), more than 128 files in a folder. Tiny GGUF files with the real shard names
stand for the real ones (the shard names and the expert types are what the table checks)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import struct
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from strata_control import gguf_preflight, models
from strata_control.profiles import ProfileError
from tools.gguf_reader import BLOCK_GEOMETRY

TYPE_IDS = {"Q8_0": 8, "IQ3_S": 21, "IQ4_NL": 20, "IQ4_XS": 23, "IQ3_XXS": 18, "Q2_0": 42, "IQ2_S": 22, "IQ2_XS": 17}


def string(value: str) -> bytes:
    raw = value.encode()
    return struct.pack("<Q", len(raw)) + raw


def gguf_bytes(experts: list[str], *, metadata: bool = True) -> bytes:
    """A tiny qwen4exp GGUF with one routed-expert tensor per type named; `experts=[]` is the metadata-only first shard of a split set."""
    pairs = [("general.architecture", 8, string("qwen4exp")), ("tokenizer.ggml.model", 8, string("gpt2")),
             ("tokenizer.ggml.tokens", 9, struct.pack("<IQ", 8, 1) + string("a")),
             ("tokenizer.ggml.merges", 9, struct.pack("<IQ", 8, 1) + string("a b"))] if metadata else []
    header = b"GGUF" + struct.pack("<IQQ", 3, len(experts), len(pairs)) + \
        b"".join(string(k) + struct.pack("<I", kind) + value for k, kind, value in pairs)
    offset = 0
    for i, name in enumerate(experts):
        block, size = BLOCK_GEOMETRY[name]
        header += string(f"blk.{i}.ffn_gate_exps.weight") + struct.pack("<IQIQ", 1, block, TYPE_IDS[name], offset)
        offset += -(-size // 32) * 32
    header += b"\x00" * (-len(header) % 32)
    return header + b"\x00" * offset


UNSLOTH_Q4 = ["Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-0000%d-of-00004.gguf" % i for i in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
UNSLOTH_IQ4 = ["Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-0000%d-of-00003.gguf" % i for i in (1, 2, 3)]
Q2 = ["Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-0000%d-of-00002.gguf" % i for i in (1, 2)]
IQ3XXS = ["Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-0000%d-of-00002.gguf" % i for i in (1, 2)]


class Base(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="strata-own-")
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.base = Path(self.tmp.name)

    def put(self, folder: Path, names: list[str], experts: list[str]) -> Path:
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for n in names:
            (folder / n).write_bytes(gguf_bytes(experts))
        return folder

    def gsq(self, folder: Path, names: list[str], kind: str) -> Path:
        return self.put(folder, names, [kind])

    def unsloth(self, folder: Path, names: list[str], kinds: list[str]) -> Path:
        """The first shard has only the metadata (what llama.cpp's gguf-split makes), the others carry tensors."""
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (folder / names[0]).write_bytes(gguf_bytes([]))
        for n in names[1:]:
            (folder / n).write_bytes(gguf_bytes(kinds, metadata=False))
        return folder


class MetadataOnlyFirstShard(Base):
    def test_unsloth_split_set_is_recognised(self):
        folder = self.unsloth(self.base / "u", UNSLOTH_Q4, ["IQ4_NL"])
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder))
        # the tiny files carry IQ4_NL experts, which UD-Q4_K_XL does not list: the set is found, the quantization is what is flagged
        self.assertNotIn("unsupported_or_missing_architecture", plan["issues"])
        self.assertNotIn("unsupported_or_incomplete_tokenizer_metadata", plan["issues"])
        self.assertNotIn("GGUF tensor or metadata count", " ".join(plan["issues"]))
        self.assertEqual((plan["candidate_selection"]["family"], plan["candidate_selection"]["model"]), ("unsloth", "UD-Q4_K_XL"))

    def test_unsloth_iq4_xs_passes_with_its_real_expert_types(self):
        folder = self.unsloth(self.base / "u", UNSLOTH_IQ4, ["IQ3_S", "IQ4_NL", "IQ4_XS", "Q8_0"])
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder))
        self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], [])
        self.assertEqual(plan["candidate_selection"]["model"], "UD-IQ4_XS")
        self.assertEqual(plan["model_dir"], str(folder))

    def test_a_shard_with_no_tensors_and_no_metadata_is_still_refused(self):
        f = self.base / "x.gguf"
        f.write_bytes(gguf_bytes([], metadata=False))
        plan = models.plan_import(str(f))
        self.assertIn("unsupported_or_missing_architecture", plan["issues"])


class Links(Base):
    def make_links(self):
        blobs = self.base / "blobs"
        snap = self.base / "snapshots" / "abc" / "Q2_0"
        blobs.mkdir()
        snap.mkdir(parents=True)
        for i, n in enumerate(Q2):
            (blobs / f"sha{i}").write_bytes(gguf_bytes(["Q2_0"]))
            try:
                os.symlink(blobs / f"sha{i}", snap / n)
            except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
                self.skipTest("this account cannot create symbolic links")
        return snap

    def test_a_hugging_face_cache_snapshot_is_used_through_its_links(self):
        snap = self.make_links()
        plan = models.plan_import(str(snap))
        self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], [])
        self.assertEqual(plan["candidate_selection"]["model"], "Q2_0")
        self.assertEqual(plan["file_count"], 2)

    def test_a_link_to_the_folder_is_followed(self):
        real = self.gsq(self.base / "real", Q2, "Q2_0")
        link = self.base / "link"
        try:
            os.symlink(real, link, target_is_directory=True)
        except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
            self.skipTest("this account cannot create symbolic links")
        self.assertEqual(models.plan_import(str(link))["issues"], [])

    def test_a_link_to_a_file_that_is_gone_says_so(self):
        snap = self.base / "s"
        snap.mkdir()
        try:
            os.symlink(self.base / "gone", snap / Q2[0])
        except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
            self.skipTest("this account cannot create symbolic links")
        with self.assertRaises(ProfileError) as ctx:
            gguf_preflight.real_model_file(snap / Q2[0])
        self.assertIn("link to a file that is not there", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_a_missing_file_is_missing_not_a_link(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ProfileError) as ctx:
            gguf_preflight.real_model_file(self.base / "nope.gguf")
        self.assertIn("is missing", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_run_configs_keep_the_no_link_rule(self):
        cfg = self.base / "real.json"
        cfg.write_text("{}")
        link = self.base / "strata-x.json"
        try:
            os.symlink(cfg, link)
        except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
            self.skipTest("this account cannot create symbolic links")
        with self.assertRaises(ProfileError) as ctx:
            models._read(link)                               # noqa: SLF001
        self.assertIn("symlink", str(ctx.exception))


class Folders(Base):
    def test_many_other_gguf_files_in_the_folder_do_not_refuse(self):
        folder = self.gsq(self.base / "m", Q2, "Q2_0")
        for i in range(140):
            (folder / f"other-{i:03d}.gguf").write_bytes(b"GGUF")
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder))
        self.assertEqual(plan["candidate_selection"]["model"], "Q2_0")
        self.assertEqual(plan["file_count"], 2)

    def test_several_sizes_in_one_folder_name_them_and_ask_for_one_file(self):
        folder = self.gsq(self.base / "many", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.gsq(folder, IQ3XXS, "IQ3_XXS")
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder))
        self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], ["multiple_model_groups"])
        self.assertIsNone(plan["candidate_selection"])
        self.assertEqual(sorted(h["model"] for h in plan["folder_holds"]), ["IQ3_XXS", "Q2_0"])
        self.assertTrue(any("holds 2 models" in m and "type the path of its .gguf file" in m for m in plan["messages"]))

    def test_one_known_size_among_other_files_is_used_and_the_rest_is_named(self):
        folder = self.gsq(self.base / "mix", Q2, "Q2_0")
        (folder / "some-other-model-Q4_K_M.gguf").write_bytes(gguf_bytes(["IQ3_S"]))
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder))
        self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], [])
        self.assertEqual(plan["candidate_selection"]["model"], "Q2_0")
        self.assertEqual(plan["file_count"], 2)
        self.assertTrue(any("some-other-model-Q4_K_M.gguf" in m and "leaves the others alone" in m for m in plan["messages"]))

    def test_a_shard_file_picks_its_set_out_of_a_folder_of_several(self):
        folder = self.gsq(self.base / "many", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.gsq(folder, IQ3XXS, "IQ3_XXS")
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder / IQ3XXS[1]))
        self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], [])
        self.assertEqual(plan["candidate_selection"]["model"], "IQ3_XXS")
        self.assertEqual(plan["model_dir"], str(folder))

    def test_a_folder_above_the_model_folder_is_searched(self):
        data = self.base / "Strata-data"
        self.gsq(data / "models" / "q2_0", Q2, "Q2_0")
        (data / "packs").mkdir()
        for start in (data, data / "models"):
            plan = models.plan_import(str(start))
            self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], [], start)
            self.assertEqual(plan["model_dir"], str(data / "models" / "q2_0"))
            self.assertTrue(any("The model files are in" in m for m in plan["messages"]))

    def test_a_whole_repository_with_one_folder_per_size_asks_which(self):
        repo = self.base / "repo"
        self.gsq(repo / "Q2_0", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.gsq(repo / "IQ3_XXS", IQ3XXS, "IQ3_XXS")
        plan = models.plan_import(str(repo))
        self.assertIn("multiple_model_groups", plan["issues"])
        self.assertEqual(sorted((Path(h["folder"]).name, h["model"]) for h in plan["folder_holds"]),
                         [("IQ3_XXS", "IQ3_XXS"), ("Q2_0", "Q2_0")])
        self.assertTrue(plan["file_set_status"] == "invalid_or_incomplete")

    def test_one_known_folder_next_to_unrelated_ones_is_used(self):
        top = self.base / "all"
        self.gsq(top / "models" / "q2_0", Q2, "Q2_0")
        (top / "stuff").mkdir()
        (top / "stuff" / "notes.txt").write_text("x")
        plan = models.plan_import(str(top))
        self.assertEqual(plan["candidate_selection"]["model"], "Q2_0")

    def test_a_folder_with_no_gguf_anywhere_says_so(self):
        (self.base / "empty" / "a" / "b").mkdir(parents=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ProfileError) as ctx:
            models.plan_import(str(self.base / "empty"))
        self.assertIn("no GGUF files found", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_a_folder_name_with_spaces_and_a_second_drive_style_path(self):
        folder = self.gsq(self.base / "my models" / "Qwen 3.8 files", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.assertEqual(models.plan_import(str(folder))["issues"], [])

    def test_a_missing_second_shard_is_one_plain_issue(self):
        folder = self.put(self.base / "half", Q2[:1], ["Q2_0"])
        plan = models.plan_import(str(folder))
        self.assertEqual(plan["issues"], ["incomplete_or_invalid_shard_set"])


class Launcher(Base):
    """`strata launch --model-path` and the TUI's "use my own files" (strata_cli/launch/runner.py, screens.py)."""

    def runner(self, **kw):
        from strata_cli.launch import settings as S
        from strata_cli.launch.catalog import Catalog
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import Runner
        from tests.terminal.launch_support import HW_12
        return Runner(S.LaunchSettings(**kw), catalog=Catalog(hardware=HW_12))

    def test_a_folder_above_the_model_is_resolved_to_the_model_folder(self):
        data = self.base / "Strata-data"
        self.gsq(data / "models" / "q2_0", Q2, "Q2_0")
        r = self.runner(model_path=str(data))
        r.resolve_own_files()
        self.assertEqual((r.s.family, r.s.model), ("qwen", "Q2_0"))
        self.assertEqual(Path(r.s.model_path), data / "models" / "q2_0")
        argv = r.setup_args()
        self.assertEqual(Path(argv[argv.index("--gguf-dir") + 1]), data / "models" / "q2_0")

    def test_a_named_model_in_a_folder_of_several_sizes_is_never_refused_here(self):
        folder = self.gsq(self.base / "many", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.gsq(folder, IQ3XXS, "IQ3_XXS")
        r = self.runner(model_path=str(folder), family="qwen", model="IQ3_XXS")
        r.resolve_own_files()
        self.assertEqual(Path(r.s.model_path), folder)               # setup picks the IQ3_XXS files by name, as in 0.1.45
        self.assertEqual((r.s.family, r.s.model), ("qwen", "IQ3_XXS"))

    def test_a_named_model_is_found_in_the_folder_that_holds_it(self):
        repo = self.base / "repo"
        self.gsq(repo / "Q2_0", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.gsq(repo / "IQ3_XXS", IQ3XXS, "IQ3_XXS")
        r = self.runner(model_path=str(repo), family="qwen", model="IQ3_XXS")
        r.resolve_own_files()
        self.assertEqual(Path(r.s.model_path), repo / "IQ3_XXS")

    def test_two_models_and_none_named_says_which_in_plain_words(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import LaunchError
        repo = self.base / "repo"
        self.gsq(repo / "Q2_0", Q2, "Q2_0")
        self.gsq(repo / "IQ3_XXS", IQ3XXS, "IQ3_XXS")
        r = self.runner(model_path=str(repo))
        with self.assertRaises(LaunchError) as ctx:
            r.resolve_own_files()
        text = str(ctx.exception)
        self.assertIn("more than one model", text)
        self.assertIn("holds 2 models", text)

    def test_a_linked_model_file_keeps_its_name(self):
        snap = Links.make_links(self)
        r = self.runner(model_path=str(snap / Q2[0]))
        r.resolve_own_files()
        self.assertEqual((r.s.family, r.s.model), ("qwen", "Q2_0"))
        self.assertEqual(Path(r.s.model_path).name, Q2[0])           # not the blob's hash name


class Words(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_file_problem_names_the_file_and_says_why(self):
        self.assertEqual(models.plain_issue("model-00002-of-00002.gguf: GGUF metadata is truncated"),
                         "model-00002-of-00002.gguf: the file is cut short (a download or copy that did not finish)")
        self.assertIn("shorter than its own header", models.plain_issue("a.gguf: GGUF tensor payload is shorter than its directory requires"))
        self.assertIn("old format (version 2)", models.plain_issue("a.gguf: Strata metadata preflight requires GGUF v3"))
        self.assertEqual(models.plain_issue("incomplete_or_invalid_shard_set"), "some parts of the model are missing")

    def test_the_plan_carries_the_words(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            f = Path(tmp) / Q2[0]
            f.write_bytes(gguf_bytes(["Q2_0"])[:60])
            plan = models.plan_import(str(f))
        self.assertTrue(plan["plain_issues"])
        self.assertTrue(any(x.startswith(Q2[0] + ":") or x.startswith(Q2[1] + ":") for x in plan["plain_issues"]), plan["plain_issues"])


class Table(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_size_setup_installs_is_in_the_table(self):
        """Setup can install it from --gguf-dir, so the checker in front of it must know it too (0.2.0 knew 7 of 10)."""
        import importlib.util
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("strata_setup_for_test", models.ROOT / "setup.py")
        setup = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(setup)
        table = json.loads((models.ROOT / "data" / "gguf_fingerprints.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        missing = []
        for family, fam in setup.FAMILIES.items():
            if fam.get("ready"):
                continue
            for model, row in setup.MODELS.items():
                if family not in row.get("families", ("qwen", "swift")):
                    continue
                names = {setup.model_file(fam, model, i) for i in range(1, setup.model_shards(fam, model) + 1)}
                key = f"{family}/{model}"
                have = {Path(n).name for n in (table.get(key) or {}).get("files", [])}
                if key not in models.SUPPORTED_SELECTIONS or have != names:
                    missing.append(key)
        self.assertEqual(missing, [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_owner_transport.py

"""Owner transport contract tests.

These run on every platform and assert the properties the runtime depends on, rather than asserting
that a particular syscall was used. The Windows path is exercised on POSIX too: the loopback-TCP
listener and the state-file validation are ordinary Python and can be tested anywhere, so the
platform branch is not left unverified until someone has a Windows machine.

What is NOT tested here, and cannot be, is whether a Windows named pipe with an owner-only ACL
behaves as intended — because that implementation does not exist yet. `docs/work/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`
records that as the honest difference between the platforms rather than pretending the loopback
transport is equivalent to it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import socket
import stat
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from strata_control import owner_transport as ot  # noqa: E402
from strata_control.private_files import restrict_to_current_user  # noqa: E402


class TestAddressing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_unix_address_fits_the_sun_path_limit(self):
        """A long home directory must not produce an address the kernel rejects."""
        long_dir = Path("/Users/someone-with-a-very-long-account-name/Documents/deepseek-harness/state")
        addr = ot.address_for(long_dir, "default")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(addr.encode()), 90)
        if ot.WINDOWS:
            self.assertTrue(addr.startswith("tcp:"))
        else:
            self.assertTrue(addr.endswith(".sock"))

    @unittest.skipIf(ot.WINDOWS, "the Windows address is a placeholder; the listener picks the port")
    def test_address_is_stable_for_the_same_inputs(self):
        d = Path("/tmp/strata-runtime")
        self.assertEqual(ot.address_for(d, "default"), ot.address_for(d, "default"))
        self.assertNotEqual(ot.address_for(d, "default"), ot.address_for(d, "other"))


@unittest.skipIf(ot.WINDOWS, "POSIX socket binding")
class TestPosixListener(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="strata-transport-"))

    def tearDown(self):
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_round_trip_and_private_permissions(self):
        addr = ot.address_for(self.tmp, "default")
        with ot.Listener(addr, timeout=2) as listener:
            mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(listener.address).st_mode)
            self.assertEqual(mode, 0o600, "the owner socket must not be reachable by other users")

            received: list[bytes] = []

            def server():
                conn = listener.accept()
                assert conn is not None, "the listener timed out"
                with conn:
                    received.append(conn.recv(4096))

            t = threading.Thread(target=server)
            t.start()
            with ot.connect(listener.address, timeout=2) as client:
                client.sendall(json.dumps({"hello": "owner"}).encode() + b"\n")
            t.join(timeout=5)
            self.assertEqual([json.loads(received[0])], [{"hello": "owner"}])

    def test_the_socket_path_is_removed_on_close(self):
        addr = ot.address_for(self.tmp, "default")
        listener = ot.Listener(addr)
        listener.bind()
        self.assertTrue(Path(listener.address).exists())
        listener.close()
        self.assertFalse(Path(listener.address).exists(),
                         "a stale socket path would block the next owner from binding")

    def test_accept_returns_none_on_timeout_rather_than_raising(self):
        """The owner polls, so a quiet channel must not look like an error."""
        addr = ot.address_for(self.tmp, "default")
        with ot.Listener(addr, timeout=0.2) as listener:
            self.assertIsNone(listener.accept())

    def test_connect_to_a_dead_address_raises_oserror(self):
        addr = ot.address_for(self.tmp, "nothing-here")
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            ot.connect(addr, timeout=1)


class TestLoopbackTransport(unittest.TestCase):
    """The Windows branch, exercised on every platform.

    This is the same code Windows runs; only the socket family differs, and `socket.AF_INET` works
    everywhere. Testing it here means the transport is verified rather than deferred.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="strata-transport-tcp-"))

    def tearDown(self):
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def _bind_loopback(self) -> ot.Listener:
        """Bind the way the Windows branch does, regardless of host platform."""
        original = ot.WINDOWS
        ot.WINDOWS = True
        try:
            listener = ot.Listener("tcp:127.0.0.1:0", timeout=2)
            listener.bind()
            return listener
        finally:
            ot.WINDOWS = original

    def test_loopback_binds_and_round_trips(self):
        listener = self._bind_loopback()
        try:
            self.assertTrue(listener.address.startswith("tcp:127.0.0.1:"),
                            "the owner must never bind a wildcard address")
            port = int(listener.address.rsplit(":", 1)[1])
            self.assertGreater(port, 0)
            got: list[bytes] = []

            def server():
                conn = listener.accept()
                assert conn is not None
                with conn:
                    got.append(conn.recv(1024))

            t = threading.Thread(target=server)
            t.start()
            original = ot.WINDOWS
            ot.WINDOWS = True
            try:
                with ot.connect(listener.address, timeout=2) as client:
                    client.sendall(b"token-check\n")
            finally:
                ot.WINDOWS = original
            t.join(timeout=5)
            self.assertEqual(got, [b"token-check\n"])
        finally:
            listener.close()

    def test_two_owners_cannot_share_the_port(self):
        """A second owner must fail to bind rather than silently share the channel."""
        listener = self._bind_loopback()
        try:
            port = int(listener.address.rsplit(":", 1)[1])
            clash = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            try:
                clash.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
                # If the platform allows the rebind, the port is not exclusively held, which would
                # let a second owner hijack the channel. Fail loudly.
                self.fail("a second listener bound the owner's port")
            except OSError:
                pass
            finally:
                clash.close()
        finally:
            listener.close()

    def test_it_binds_loopback_only(self):
        """The listener must not be reachable from another interface."""
        listener = self._bind_loopback()
        try:
            port = int(listener.address.rsplit(":", 1)[1])
            # Connecting to a non-loopback local address on that port must fail: nothing is bound
            # there. 203.0.113.0/24 is TEST-NET-3 and is never a local address.
            s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            s.settimeout(0.5)
            try:
                with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                    s.connect(("203.0.113.1", port))
            finally:
                s.close()
        finally:
            listener.close()


class TestStateFileValidation(unittest.TestCase):
    """A client must refuse a state file it cannot trust."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="strata-state-"))
        self.path = self.tmp / "default.json"
        self.path.write_text('{"token": "x"}')
        restrict_to_current_user(self.path)

    def tearDown(self):
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_a_private_regular_file_is_accepted(self):
        ot.check_state_file(self.path)

    @unittest.skipUnless(ot.WINDOWS, "NTFS ACLs")
    def test_a_state_file_with_an_inherited_acl_is_refused(self):
        other = self.tmp / "inherited.json"
        other.write_text("{}")  # a fresh file inherits the directory's entries (SYSTEM, Administrators)
        with self.assertRaises(ot.TransportError):
            ot.check_state_file(other)

    @unittest.skipIf(ot.WINDOWS, "POSIX permission bits")
    def test_a_world_readable_state_file_is_refused(self):
        os.chmod(self.path, 0o644)
        with self.assertRaises(ot.TransportError):
            ot.check_state_file(self.path)

    @unittest.skipIf(ot.WINDOWS, "POSIX symlinks")
    def test_a_symlink_is_refused(self):
        link = self.tmp / "link.json"
        link.symlink_to(self.path)
        with self.assertRaises(ot.TransportError):
            ot.check_state_file(link)

    def test_a_directory_is_refused(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ot.TransportError):
            ot.check_state_file(self.tmp)

    def test_an_implausibly_large_state_file_is_refused(self):
        big = self.tmp / "big.json"
        big.write_bytes(b"x" * (17 * 1024))
        os.chmod(big, 0o600)
        with self.assertRaises(ot.TransportError):
            ot.check_state_file(big)

    def test_a_missing_file_raises_oserror(self):
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            ot.check_state_file(self.tmp / "nope.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_pack_gguf_engram.py

"""pack_gguf must never take an Engram file's metadata for the model's: ISTA-DASLab's final Engram says general.architecture 'deepseek41-engram'
(the first release's said 'engram').  The fixture is the real header of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Engram-IQ4_NL.gguf (its 416 bytes: metadata and the tensor
directory, no data)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import struct
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "dsv41"))
import pack_gguf as PG  # noqa: E402

FIXTURE = ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures" / "dsv41" / "engram-final-header.gguf"


def tiny_gguf(path: Path, arch: str, extra: dict | None = None) -> Path:
    """A GGUF with only metadata (string and uint32 values), no tensors."""
    kv = {"general.architecture": arch, **(extra or {})}
    out = bytearray(b"GGUF" + struct.pack("<IQQ", 3, 0, len(kv)))
    for k, v in kv.items():
        out += struct.pack("<Q", len(k)) + k.encode()
        if isinstance(v, str):
            out += struct.pack("<I", 8) + struct.pack("<Q", len(v)) + v.encode()
        else:
            out += struct.pack("<I", 4) + struct.pack("<I", v)
    out += b"\0" * (-len(out) % 32)
    path.write_bytes(bytes(out))
    return path


class EngramHeader(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_real_final_engram_header_is_an_engram_file(self):
        g = PG.Gguf(FIXTURE)
        self.assertEqual(g.kv["general.architecture"], "deepseek41-engram")
        self.assertTrue(PG.is_engram_file(g))
        self.assertEqual(len(g.tensors), 2)
        self.assertEqual(g.data_start, 416)

    def test_it_is_never_the_group_the_model_metadata_comes_from(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            d = Path(d)
            shard = PG.Gguf(tiny_gguf(d / "model-00001-of-00004.gguf", "deepseek41", {"split.count": 4}))
            engram = PG.Gguf(FIXTURE)
            for order in ([engram, shard], [shard, engram]):
                kv = PG.model_kv(order)
                self.assertIsNotNone(kv)
                self.assertEqual(kv["general.architecture"], "deepseek41")
            self.assertIsNone(PG.model_kv([engram]))                    # an Engram alone is not a model

    def test_the_first_releases_engram_is_one_too(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            self.assertTrue(PG.is_engram_file(PG.Gguf(tiny_gguf(Path(d) / "e.gguf", "engram"))))
            self.assertFalse(PG.is_engram_file(PG.Gguf(tiny_gguf(Path(d) / "m.gguf", "deepseek41"))))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_packaging_pins.py

"""The terminal archive's pins: the interpreter digests, the hash-pinned wheel locks, and the launchers that prefer the
bundled runtime. Offline: nothing is downloaded (the build and the smoke test do that)."""

import re
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "packaging"))

import package_terminal as pt  # noqa: E402


def norm(name):
    return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()


class InterpreterPins(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_target_has_a_digest_and_a_matching_url(self):
        self.assertEqual(sorted(pt.PYTHON_PINS), ["darwin-arm64", "linux-x86_64", "windows-x86_64"])
        for target, pin in pt.PYTHON_PINS.items():
            with self.subTest(target):
                self.assertRegex(pin["sha256"], r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
                self.assertIn(pt.PYTHON_VERSION, pin["url"])
                self.assertIn(pt.PBS_RELEASE, pin["url"])
                self.assertTrue(pin["url"].startswith("https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/"))
                self.assertTrue(pin["url"].endswith("install_only.tar.gz"))
        self.assertEqual(len({p["sha256"] for p in pt.PYTHON_PINS.values()}), 3)

    def test_the_mac_pin_is_the_one_setup_sh_downloads(self):
        text = (ROOT / "setup.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn(pt.PYTHON_PINS["darwin-arm64"]["sha256"], text)
        self.assertIn(pt.PYTHON_PINS["darwin-arm64"]["url"].split("/")[-1], text)

    def test_fetch_refuses_a_download_that_does_not_match_its_pin(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            cache = Path(d)
            pin = pt.PYTHON_PINS["linux-x86_64"]
            (cache / pin["file"].replace("+", "_")).write_bytes(b"not the interpreter")
            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as cm:
                pt.fetch_python("linux-x86_64", cache)
            self.assertIn("does not match its pin", str(cm.exception))


class WheelLocks(unittest.TestCase):
    def locks(self):
        found = sorted((ROOT / "packaging" / "locks").glob("runtime-*-cp312.txt"))
        self.assertEqual([p.name for p in found], ["runtime-darwin-arm64-cp312.txt", "runtime-linux-x86_64-cp312.txt",
                                                    "runtime-windows-x86_64-cp312.txt"])
        return found

    def test_every_entry_is_pinned_and_hashed_and_nothing_else_is_in_the_file(self):
        for lock in self.locks():
            with self.subTest(lock.name):
                entries = {}
                current = None
                for line in lock.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                    if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)==([0-9][^\s\\]*) \\$", line)
                    if m:
                        current = norm(m.group(1))
                        entries[current] = {"version": m.group(2), "hashes": []}
                        continue
                    h = re.match(r"^\s+--hash=sha256:([0-9a-f]{64})( \\)?$", line)
                    self.assertTrue(h and current, f"unexpected line in {lock.name}: {line!r}")
                    entries[current]["hashes"].append(h.group(1))
                self.assertGreater(len(entries), 15)
                for name, e in entries.items():
                    self.assertTrue(e["hashes"], name)

    def test_the_locks_agree_with_requirements_txt(self):
        pins = {}
        for name in ("requirements.txt", "requirements-monitor.txt"):
            for line in (ROOT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)==([^\s;]+)(?:\s*;\s*(.*))?$", line.split(" #")[0].strip())
                if m:
                    pins.setdefault(norm(m.group(1)), []).append((m.group(2), m.group(3) or ""))
        for lock in self.locks():
            names = pt.lock_names(lock)
            with self.subTest(lock.name):
                for pkg, versions in pins.items():
                    if pkg == "colorama":
                        self.assertEqual(pkg in names, "windows" in lock.name)
                        continue
                    if pkg == "numpy":                       # python_version markers: the 3.12 line applies
                        self.assertEqual(names[pkg], "2.5.3")
                        continue
                    self.assertEqual(names.get(pkg), versions[0][0], pkg)
                self.assertNotIn("cmake", names)             # build tools never ship in the bundle
                self.assertNotIn("ninja", names)

    def test_the_build_installs_with_hash_checking_and_no_resolution(self):
        text = (ROOT / "packaging" / "package_terminal.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for flag in ("--require-hashes", "--no-deps", "--only-binary=:all:"):
            self.assertIn(flag, text)
        self.assertNotIn('"--upgrade"', text)               # pip itself is the interpreter's, not a fresh download


class Launchers(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_wrappers_prefer_the_bundled_runtime(self):
        cmd = (ROOT / "bin" / "strata.cmd").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        ps1 = (ROOT / "bin" / "strata.ps1").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        sh = (ROOT / "bin" / "strata").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertLess(cmd.index("python\\python.exe"), cmd.index("py -3"))
        self.assertLess(ps1.index("python\\python.exe"), ps1.index("'py', '-3'"))
        self.assertLess(sh.index("python/bin/python3"), sh.index("command -v python3"))
        for text in (cmd, ps1, sh):
            self.assertIn("PYTHONNOUSERSITE", text)

    def test_start_here_setup_and_update_use_it(self):
        bat = (ROOT / "START-HERE.bat").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertLess(bat.index('if exist "python\\python.exe" goto bundled'), bat.index("call :findpy"))
        self.assertIn("START-HERE.bat", (ROOT / "SETUP.bat").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertIn("START-HERE.bat", (ROOT / "UPDATE.bat").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        sh = (ROOT / "setup.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertLess(sh.index("exec python/bin/python3"), sh.index("if [ ! -x .venv/bin/python ]"))
        self.assertIn("setup.sh", (ROOT / "update.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_picture_reader_package.py

"""I1 / I2 (tools and images review, 2026-10-22): the picture reader in an engine package must run on every card and Mac the package does.

#3669: the Windows cuda12 package reused a strata-vision.exe built before Pascal support; the engine ran on a P100 and the reader stopped
with "device kernel image is invalid". #3697: a macOS package with no reader at all. These tests need no GPU and no toolkit."""

import json
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "packaging"))
import package_engine  # noqa: E402
