    def _ops(self, *args):
        output = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(output):
            code = main(["ops", *args, "--profile", "local", "--output", "json"])
        return code, json.loads(output.getvalue())

    @unittest.skipIf(WINDOWS, "SIGTERM to a Windows process is TerminateProcess: the hard-kill test below covers it")
    def test_terminating_owner_host_stops_its_child_and_removes_state(self):
        started = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
        self.assertTrue(started["ok"])
        os.kill(started["host_pid"], signal.SIGTERM)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 8
        while runtime._read_state("local") is not None and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.05)
        self.assertIsNone(runtime._read_state("local"))
        owned = runtime._STARTED_HOSTS.pop("local", None)
        if owned is not None:
            self.assertEqual(owned.wait(timeout=3), 0)

    def test_hard_killed_host_child_exits_and_next_start_recovers_private_state(self):
        started = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
        self.assertTrue(started["ok"])
        old_child = started["child_pid"]
        state = runtime._read_state("local")
        orphan = self.root / "runtime" / f"local-{state['token']}-{'a' * 32}.rollback.json"
        orphan.write_bytes(self.config.read_bytes())
        orphan.chmod(0o600)
        owned = runtime._STARTED_HOSTS.pop("local")
        if WINDOWS:
            owned.kill()                          # TerminateProcess: the host cannot clean up after itself
            owned.wait(timeout=3)
            # the job object ends the server tree with the host, no matter how the host ended
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
            while runtime._pid_exists(old_child) and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                time.sleep(0.1)
            self.assertFalse(runtime._pid_exists(old_child))
        else:
            os.kill(started["host_pid"], signal.SIGKILL)
            self.assertEqual(owned.wait(timeout=3), -signal.SIGKILL)
        stale = runtime.status("local")
        self.assertEqual((stale["state"], stale["error"]), ("stale", "owner_host_lost"))
        # The next start waits for the inherited-pipe guard to stop the old
        # process group; it never sends a signal to the saved child PID.
        replacement = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
        self.assertTrue(replacement["ok"])
        self.assertNotEqual(replacement["child_pid"], old_child)
        self.assertFalse(runtime._pid_exists(old_child))
        self.assertFalse(orphan.exists())

    def test_recovery_refuses_a_still_present_child(self):
        state_path, socket_path, _ = runtime._paths("local")
        token = "a" * 64
        state = {"schema_version": 1, "profile": "local",
                 "socket": "tcp:127.0.0.1:50000" if WINDOWS else str(socket_path),
                 "token": token, "host_pid": 999999}
        lease = runtime._write_new(state_path, (json.dumps(state) + "\n").encode())
        os.close(lease)
        marker = runtime._child_marker("local", token)
        marker.write_text(json.dumps({"host_token": token, "phase": "owned",
                                      "pid": os.getpid(),
                                      "ready": str(state_path.parent / "local-fake.ready.json")}), encoding="utf-8")
        marker.chmod(0o600)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(profiles.ProfileError, "still present"):
            runtime.start("local", wait=0, shutdown_timeout=2)
        self.assertTrue(state_path.exists())

    # ---- owner transport, attach and identity (POSIX socket and Windows loopback alike)

    def _stale_host(self, child_pid, *, started=None, token="a" * 64):
        """A state file whose host is gone, and the ownership marker naming `child_pid` as its server."""
        state_path, socket_path, _ = runtime._paths("local")
        state = {"schema_version": 1, "profile": "local",
                 "socket": "tcp:127.0.0.1:50000" if WINDOWS else str(socket_path),
                 "token": token, "host_pid": 999999}
        lease = runtime._write_new(state_path, (json.dumps(state) + "\n").encode())
        runtime._unlock_file(lease)
        os.close(lease)
        marker = runtime._child_marker("local", token)
        record = {"host_token": token, "phase": "owned", "pid": child_pid,
                  "ready": str(state_path.parent / "local-fake.ready.json")}
        if started is not None:
            record["started"] = started
        marker.write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8")
        marker.chmod(0o600)
        return state_path, marker

    def _send(self, state, token, command):
        client = owner_transport.connect(state["socket"], timeout=5)
        try:
            client.sendall((json.dumps({"token": token, "command": command}) + "\n").encode())
            return json.loads(client.recv(4096).split(b"\n")[0])
        finally:
            client.close()

    def test_a_second_client_attaches_from_another_process_and_shares_the_owner(self):
        started = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
        self.assertTrue(started["ok"])
        state = runtime._read_state("local")
        if WINDOWS:
            self.assertRegex(state["socket"], r"^tcp:127\.0\.0\.1:[1-9][0-9]*$")
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
        done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "strata.py", "runtime", "status", "--profile", "local",
                               "--output", "json"], cwd=root, env=os.environ.copy(), capture_output=True,
                              text=True, timeout=30)
        self.assertEqual(done.returncode, 0, done.stderr)
        other = json.loads(done.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((other["state"], other["owner_id"], other["instance_id"], other["host_pid"]),
                         ("ready", started["owner_id"], started["instance_id"], started["host_pid"]))
        self.assertEqual(runtime.status("local")["owner_id"], started["owner_id"])   # attaching took nothing over
        self.assertEqual(runtime.stop("local", timeout=12)["ok"], True)
        self.assertEqual(runtime.status("local")["state"], "stopped")

    def test_a_wrong_or_stale_token_cannot_stop_the_owner(self):
        started = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
        self.assertTrue(started["ok"])
        state = runtime._read_state("local")
        wrong_last = "0" if state["token"][-1] != "0" else "1"
        for bad in ("0" * 64, state["token"][:-1] + wrong_last, "", "x" * 10):
            with self.subTest(token=bad[:6]):
                answer = self._send(state, bad, "stop")
                self.assertEqual((answer["ok"], answer["error"]), (False, "unauthorized"))
        self.assertEqual(runtime.status("local")["instance_id"], started["instance_id"])
        self.assertTrue(self._send(state, state["token"], "status")["ok"])     # the real token is what authorises

    def test_a_recorded_pid_of_an_unrelated_live_process_is_never_signalled(self):
        victim = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(120)"])
        try:
            state_path, marker = self._stale_host(victim.pid)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(profiles.ProfileError, "still present"):
                runtime.start("local", wait=0, shutdown_timeout=2)
            with self.assertRaises(profiles.ProfileError):            # nothing answers on the recorded address
                runtime.stop("local", timeout=2)
            self.assertIsNone(victim.poll(), "an unrelated process was stopped")
            self.assertTrue(state_path.exists() and marker.exists())
        finally:
            victim.kill()
            victim.wait(timeout=10)

    @unittest.skipUnless(WINDOWS, "a creation time is recorded with the PID on Windows only")
    def test_a_reused_pid_with_another_creation_time_is_not_the_recorded_child(self):
        victim = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(120)"])
        try:
            real = runtime.winproc.process_started(victim.pid)
            self.assertTrue(runtime._pid_exists(victim.pid, real))
            self.assertFalse(runtime._pid_exists(victim.pid, real + 12345))
            self._stale_host(victim.pid, started=real + 12345)           # the number was reused by another process
            started = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
            self.assertTrue(started["ok"])                               # recovered: it was not the recorded child
            self.assertIsNone(victim.poll(), "the process that reused the PID was stopped")
        finally:
            victim.kill()
            victim.wait(timeout=10)

    def test_marker_without_creation_time_ignores_a_reused_pid_of_a_foreign_program(self):
        # #3488: the marker had no `started`, the number was reused by another program, every load said "still present".
        child = {"pid": 38552}
        with mock.patch.object(runtime, "WINDOWS", True), \
                mock.patch.object(runtime, "_pid_exists", return_value=True), \
                mock.patch.object(runtime.winproc, "process_image", create=True) as image:
            image.return_value = r"C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe"
            self.assertFalse(runtime._child_present(child))
            image.return_value = r"C:\Users\a\AppData\Local\Strata\python\python.exe"
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present(child))
            image.return_value = None                                    # unreadable: keep refusing, never guess
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present(child))
            image.return_value = r"C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe"
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present({"pid": 1, "started": 5}))   # a creation time decides by itself

    def test_a_process_created_after_the_marker_was_written_is_not_the_recorded_child(self):
        # 2026-10-22: the app was force-killed, its marker had no creation time, the number now belonged to another Python program, and every
        # load said "lost host child is still present" until the marker was deleted by hand. The child was started BEFORE its marker was written.
        child = {"pid": 4242}
        with mock.patch.object(runtime, "_pid_exists", return_value=True), \
                mock.patch.object(runtime.winproc, "process_image", create=True, return_value="C:\\Python\\python.exe"), \
                mock.patch.object(runtime.procs, "started_epoch") as created:
            created.return_value = 1000.0 + 60
            self.assertFalse(runtime._child_present(child, written=1000.0), "created a minute after the marker: another process")
            created.return_value = 1000.0 - 5
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present(child, written=1000.0), "created before the marker: could be the child, keep refusing")
            created.return_value = 1000.0 + 1.5
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present(child, written=1000.0), "inside the clock slack: keep refusing")
            created.return_value = None
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present(child, written=1000.0), "creation time unreadable: never guess")
            created.return_value = 1000.0 + 60
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present({"pid": 4242, "started": 7}, written=1000.0) is True, "a recorded creation time decides by itself")
            self.assertTrue(runtime._child_present(child), "no marker time: unchanged")

    def test_a_marker_left_by_a_killed_app_is_cleaned_up_when_its_number_belongs_to_a_later_program(self):
        victim = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(120)"])
        try:
            state_path, marker = self._stale_host(victim.pid)             # a marker with no creation time (Windows could not read it)
            old = time.time() - 3600
            os.utime(marker, (old, old))                                  # written an hour ago: the victim started after it
            started = runtime.start("local", wait=10, shutdown_timeout=2)
            self.assertTrue(started["ok"], started)
            self.assertFalse(marker.exists(), "the stale marker was removed")
            self.assertIsNone(victim.poll(), "the program that reused the number was left alone")
        finally:
            victim.kill()
            victim.wait(timeout=10)

    def test_started_epoch_reads_a_live_process_and_nothing_for_a_dead_number(self):
        victim = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(120)"])
        try:
            now = time.time()
            created = procs.started_epoch(victim.pid)
            self.assertIsNotNone(created)
            self.assertLess(abs(created - now), 60)
        finally:
            victim.kill()
            victim.wait(timeout=10)
        self.assertIsNone(procs.started_epoch(victim.pid))
        self.assertIsNone(procs.started_epoch(0))
        self.assertIsNone(procs.started_epoch(-5))

    @unittest.skipUnless(WINDOWS, "os.kill(pid, 0) ends a process on Windows; liveness is a handle query")
    def test_liveness_check_does_not_end_the_process_it_asks_about(self):
        victim = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(120)"])
        try:
            for _ in range(5):
                self.assertTrue(runtime._pid_exists(victim.pid))
            self.assertIsNone(victim.poll())
        finally:
            victim.kill()
            victim.wait(timeout=10)
        self.assertFalse(runtime._pid_exists(victim.pid))

    @unittest.skipUnless(WINDOWS, "ACLs stand in for mode 0700 on Windows")
    def test_runtime_directory_is_owner_only_and_a_shared_one_is_refused(self):
        from strata_control import private_files
        directory = runtime.runtime_dir()
        self.assertTrue(private_files.is_private(directory))
        shared = Path(self.temp.name) / "shared-runtime"
        shared.mkdir()
        done = subprocess.run(["icacls", str(shared), "/grant", "*S-1-1-0:(OI)(CI)R"], capture_output=True)
        if done.returncode != 0:
            self.skipTest("icacls could not widen the test directory")
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR": str(shared)}):
            # a folder that names Everyone is the user's own state folder: it is locked down once and used (never a stop)
            self.assertEqual(runtime.runtime_dir(), shared)
            self.assertTrue(private_files.is_unshared(shared))
        again = Path(self.temp.name) / "shared-runtime-2"
        again.mkdir()
        subprocess.run(["icacls", str(again), "/grant", "*S-1-1-0:(OI)(CI)R"], capture_output=True)
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR": str(again)}), \
                mock.patch.object(private_files, "restrict_to_current_user"), \
                mock.patch.object(private_files, "repair_access", return_value=False):
            # when the lock-down does not happen it still refuses, in plain words and naming who can open it
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(profiles.ProfileError, "Everyone"):
                runtime.runtime_dir()

    def test_ready_pid_may_be_a_child_of_the_launcher_on_windows_only(self):
        # #3683: a Windows venv's python.exe starts the real interpreter as its child, so the server that writes the ready file
        # is one process below the pid the host started. It must still match; a stranger or a distant process must not.
        parents = {200: 100, 300: 200, 400: 300, 500: 400}
        with mock.patch.object(runtime.procs, "parent_of", side_effect=lambda pid: parents.get(pid)):
            with mock.patch.object(runtime, "WINDOWS", True):
                self.assertTrue(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(100, 100))
                self.assertTrue(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(200, 100))
                self.assertTrue(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(300, 100))
                self.assertTrue(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(400, 100))
                self.assertFalse(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(500, 100))      # too far below
                self.assertFalse(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(999, 100))      # unrelated
                self.assertFalse(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(None, 100))
                self.assertFalse(runtime._ready_pid_is_child("200", 100))
                self.assertFalse(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(0, 100))
            with mock.patch.object(runtime, "WINDOWS", False):
                self.assertTrue(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(100, 100))
                self.assertFalse(runtime._ready_pid_is_child(200, 100))      # POSIX has no launcher in between

    @unittest.skipUnless(WINDOWS, "the venv launcher is a Windows thing")
    def test_server_started_through_a_launcher_process_becomes_ready(self):
        launcher = self.root / "launcher.cmd"
        launcher.write_bytes(f'@echo off\r\n"{sys.executable}" %*\r\n'.encode())
        host = runtime.Host("local", shutdown_timeout=2, startup_wait=20)
        plan, args, source, original = host._plan()
        with mock.patch.object(sys, "executable", str(launcher)):
            host._launch(args, source, original, plan["profile_revision"])
        try:
            result = host._wait_ready(30)
            self.assertTrue(result["ok"], result)
            self.assertTrue(result["generation_ready"])
            ready = json.loads(host.ready_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertNotEqual(ready["pid"], host.child.pid)               # the server is below the launcher
        finally:
            host._stop_child()

    def test_a_ready_file_that_is_not_ours_is_named_in_the_status_phase(self):
        host = runtime.Host("local", shutdown_timeout=2, startup_wait=10)
        host.child = mock.Mock(pid=111)
        host.child.poll.return_value = None
        host.ready_path = self.root / "ready.json"
        host.ready_path.write_text(json.dumps({"pid": 222, "instance_id": "a" * 32}), encoding="utf-8")
        with mock.patch.object(runtime.procs, "parent_of", return_value=None):
            self.assertEqual(host._status()["phase"], "ready_file_not_matched")
        host.ready_path.unlink()
        self.assertEqual(host._status()["phase"], "loading")

    def test_exclusive_lease_waits_for_shared_holders_and_shared_holders_coexist(self):
        first = runtime.acquire_activity_lease(shared=True)
        second = runtime.acquire_activity_lease(shared=True)
        try:
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(profiles.ProfileError, "engine lease"):
                runtime.acquire_activity_lease(shared=False)
        finally:
            for descriptor in (first, second):
                runtime._unlock_file(descriptor)
                os.close(descriptor)
        exclusive = runtime.acquire_activity_lease(shared=False)
        try:
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(profiles.ProfileError, "engine lease"):
                runtime.acquire_activity_lease(shared=True)
        finally:
            runtime._unlock_file(exclusive)
            os.close(exclusive)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_setup_failure_words.py

"""When setup.py stops with a Python error, `strata launch` says what it was and where the rest of the output is (#3613, #3467)."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from strata_cli.launch import runner
from strata_cli.launch.runner import LaunchError, Runner, missing_file, python_failure, setup_failure

TRACEBACK = [
    "  [..] Tuning Strata for this PC",
    "Traceback (most recent call last):",
    '  File "C:\\Strata\\setup.py", line 6414, in calibrate_config',
    "    import calibrate as CAL",
    "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'calibrate'",
]


class SetupFailureWords(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_last_line_of_a_traceback_is_found(self):
        self.assertEqual(python_failure(TRACEBACK), "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'calibrate'")
        self.assertIsNone(python_failure(["[X] Not enough disk space", "       Free some space"]))
        self.assertIsNone(python_failure(["Traceback (most recent call last):", '  File "x.py", line 1, in <module>']))
        # the last traceback wins, frames and blank lines are skipped
        two = TRACEBACK[:1] + ["Traceback (most recent call last):", "  frame", "ValueError: old"] + TRACEBACK[1:]
        self.assertEqual(python_failure(two), "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'calibrate'")

    def test_a_missing_module_is_said_as_a_missing_file_with_the_next_step_and_the_output_path(self):
        error = setup_failure(TRACEBACK, "", "", r"C:\Users\x\launch\a.setup.log", False)
        self.assertIsInstance(error, LaunchError)
        self.assertIn("The model could not be installed.", error.text)
        self.assertIn("missing from this Strata install", error.text)
        self.assertIn("No module named 'calibrate'", error.text)
        self.assertIn("strata update", error.next)
        self.assertIn(r"C:\Users\x\launch\a.setup.log", error.next)

    def test_another_python_error_keeps_its_line_and_the_path(self):
        error = setup_failure(["Traceback (most recent call last):", "  f", "KeyError: 'cuda'"], "", "", "/tmp/a.setup.log", True)
        self.assertIn("KeyError: 'cuda'", error.text)
        self.assertNotIn("missing", error.text)
        self.assertIn("/tmp/a.setup.log", error.next)

    def test_a_setup_error_line_still_wins_and_gets_the_details_path(self):
        error = setup_failure(TRACEBACK, "Not enough disk space", "Free some space.", "/tmp/a.setup.log", False)
        self.assertEqual(error.text, "The model could not be installed. Not enough disk space.")
        self.assertEqual(error.next, "Free some space. Details: /tmp/a.setup.log")
        plain = setup_failure([], "", "", None, False)
        self.assertEqual(plain.text, "The model could not be installed.")
        self.assertIn("a download continues where it stopped", plain.next)
        self.assertNotIn("Details", plain.next)

    def test_missing_file_kinds(self):
        self.assertTrue(missing_file("ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'x'"))
        self.assertTrue(missing_file("ImportError: cannot import name 'y'"))
        self.assertFalse(missing_file("ValueError: bad"))

    def test_the_setup_output_is_kept_in_the_launch_folder(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            run = Runner.__new__(Runner)
            with mock.patch.object(Runner, "name", new_callable=mock.PropertyMock, return_value="gyro-s-32k"),                     mock.patch.object(runner, "launch_dir", return_value=Path(folder)):
                kept = run.keep_setup_output([f"line {i}" for i in range(1000)] + TRACEBACK)
            self.assertEqual(Path(kept), Path(folder) / "gyro-s-32k.setup.log")
            text = Path(kept).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertIn("ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'calibrate'", text)
            self.assertEqual(len(text.splitlines()), 400)                 # the tail, not a runaway file
            with mock.patch.object(Runner, "name", new_callable=mock.PropertyMock, return_value="gyro-s-32k"),                     mock.patch.object(runner, "launch_dir", side_effect=OSError("read-only")):
                self.assertIsNone(run.keep_setup_output(["x"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_shared_models_folder.py

"""One models folder for the Terminal and the desktop app: the folder changed last wins, the other settings file is updated, nothing moves."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

import setup
from strata_control import discovery
from tests.terminal.test_discovery import GuiLayout


class SharedModelsFolder(GuiLayout):
    def files(self):
        mine = Path(os.environ["APPDATA"]) / "Strata" / "settings.json"
        mine.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return mine, discovery.app_settings_file()

    def put(self, file: Path, folder: Path, at: float) -> None:
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(json.dumps({"data_dir": str(folder), "data_dir_at": at, "installs": ["keep"]}))

    def read(self, file: Path) -> dict:
        return json.loads(file.read_text())

    def test_the_terminal_choice_made_last_wins_and_the_app_file_follows(self):
        mine, app = self.files()
        old, new = self.base / "on-c", self.base / "on-d"
        self.put(app, old, 1000)
        self.put(mine, new, 2000)
        self.assertEqual(discovery.data_dir(self.base / "default"), (new, "settings"))
        self.assertEqual(Path(self.read(app)["data_dir"]), new)
        self.assertEqual(self.read(app)["data_dir_at"], 2000)
        self.assertEqual(self.read(app)["installs"], ["keep"])        # merged, not replaced
        self.assertEqual(list(old.iterdir()), [])                     # nothing moved

    def test_the_app_choice_made_last_wins_and_the_terminal_file_follows(self):
        mine, app = self.files()
        old, new = self.base / "on-c", self.base / "on-d"
        self.put(mine, old, 1000)
        self.put(app, new, 3000)
        self.assertEqual(discovery.data_dir(self.base / "default")[0], new)
        self.assertEqual(Path(self.read(mine)["data_dir"]), new)
        self.assertEqual(self.read(mine)["data_dir_at"], 3000)
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog().data_dir().resolve(), new.resolve())

    def test_an_app_folder_on_a_disk_that_is_gone_is_not_adopted(self):
        mine, app = self.files()
        keep = self.base / "kept"
        self.put(mine, keep, 1000)
        gone = self.base / "unplugged"
        app.write_text(json.dumps({"data_dir": str(gone), "data_dir_at": 5000}))
        self.assertEqual(discovery.data_dir(self.base / "default"), (keep, "settings"))
        self.assertEqual(Path(self.read(app)["data_dir"]), gone)      # the app's file is left alone

    def test_the_same_folder_in_both_changes_nothing(self):
        mine, app = self.files()
        folder = self.base / "same"
        self.put(mine, folder, 1000)
        self.put(app, folder, 2000)
        before = app.read_bytes()
        self.assertEqual(discovery.data_dir(self.base / "default")[0], folder)
        self.assertEqual(app.read_bytes(), before)

    def test_files_without_a_time_use_the_file_time(self):
        mine, app = self.files()
        old, new = self.base / "a", self.base / "b"
        old.mkdir(), new.mkdir()
        app.write_text(json.dumps({"data_dir": str(old)}))
        os.utime(app, (time.time() - 500, time.time() - 500))
        mine.write_text(json.dumps({"data_dir": str(new)}))
        self.assertEqual(discovery.data_dir(self.base / "default")[0], new)

    def test_the_apps_own_processes_do_not_sync(self):
        mine, app = self.files()
        self.put(mine, self.base / "t", 9000)
        self.put(app, self.base / "a", 1000)
        os.environ["STRATA_SETTINGS_FILE"] = str(app)
        self.assertIsNone(discovery.sync_data_dir())
        self.assertEqual(Path(self.read(app)["data_dir"]), self.base / "a")

    def test_setup_stamps_a_changed_data_folder(self):
        mine, _ = self.files()
        setup.save_settings({"data_dir": str(self.base / "x")})
        first = self.read(mine)["data_dir_at"]
        self.assertGreater(first, 0)
        time.sleep(0.02)
        setup.save_settings({**self.read(mine), "installs": ["y"]})   # same folder: the time stays
        self.assertEqual(self.read(mine)["data_dir_at"], first)


## tests/terminal/test_state_paths.py

"""Per-user state locations: %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Strata on Windows, $XDG_STATE_HOME/strata elsewhere."""

import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from strata_cli.cli import main
from strata_control import paths, runtime


class StatePaths(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_windows_uses_localappdata(self):
        env = {"LOCALAPPDATA": "C:\\Users\\me\\AppData\\Local", "XDG_STATE_HOME": "/ignored"}
        self.assertEqual(paths.state_base(env, windows=True, home=Path("C:\\Users\\other")),
                         Path("C:\\Users\\me\\AppData\\Local") / "Strata")

    def test_windows_without_localappdata_falls_back_to_the_profile(self):
        self.assertEqual(paths.state_base({}, windows=True, home=Path("C:\\Users\\me")),
                         Path("C:\\Users\\me") / "AppData" / "Local" / "Strata")

    def test_posix_is_unchanged(self):
        self.assertEqual(paths.state_base({"XDG_STATE_HOME": "/x"}, windows=False), Path("/x") / "strata")
        self.assertEqual(paths.state_base({}, windows=False, home=Path("/home/me")),
                         Path("/home/me") / ".local" / "state" / "strata")

    def test_runtime_dir_default_lives_under_the_state_base(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            env = {"LOCALAPPDATA": d, "XDG_STATE_HOME": d}
            with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env):
                os.environ.pop("STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR", None)
                self.assertEqual(runtime.runtime_dir(), paths.state_base() / "runtime")
                self.assertEqual(runtime.runtime_dir().parent.parent, Path(d))

    def test_cli_defaults_for_tuning_and_timeskip_follow_the_same_base(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            env = {"LOCALAPPDATA": d, "XDG_STATE_HOME": d}
            with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env):
                for var in ("STRATA_TUNE_DIR", "STRATA_TIMESKIP_DIR"):
                    os.environ.pop(var, None)
                self.assertEqual(main(["tune", "list", "--output", "json"]), 0)
                self.assertEqual(main(["timeskip", "list", "--output", "json"]), 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_sycl_package.py

"""Intel Arc engine package (owner test round 8, track L3): the stable feed had no `linux-x86_64-sycl` package, so a clean Arc PC got a
Terminal that could not run a model and `strata update` kept saying the feed had no engine for it. The feed is whatever packages the release
builds (packaging/feed_tool.py takes every `*.entry.json`), so the gap was the missing build recipe, not the choice code. These tests keep the
choice honest once the package exists: an Arc PC (found by its PCI vendor, with no oneAPI tools installed) gets it by itself, nobody else does,
and the recipe that makes it carries the checks that a clean PC needs."""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from strata_control import engine_component as ec, feed as feedmod, updater

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "packaging"))
import package_engine  # noqa: E402

LINUX, WIN = "linux-x86_64", "windows-x86_64"


def entry(platform, backend, variant, archs, version="0.1.47"):
    return {"version": version, "platform": platform, "backend": backend, "variant": variant, "archs": list(archs), "min_driver": {},
            "min_runtime": None, "build_id": f"rel-{platform}-{backend}-{variant}", "format": "tar.gz",
            "url": f"strata-engine-{platform}-{backend}-{variant}.tar.gz", "size": 1000, "sha256": "a" * 64, "manifest_sha256": "b" * 64,
            "installed_bytes": 2000, "notes": ""}


FEED = [feedmod._engine_package(e) for e in (
    entry(LINUX, "cuda", "cuda13", ("sm_75", "sm_86", "sm_89", "sm_120", "compute_120")),
    entry(LINUX, "hip", "rx9070", ("gfx1200", "gfx1201")),
    entry(WIN, "cuda", "cuda13", ("sm_86",)),
    entry(LINUX, "sycl", "", ("intel-arc",)))]


def fake_drm(root: Path, *vendors: str) -> str:
    """A /sys/class/drm with one card per vendor id (plus a connector entry, which must be skipped)."""
    for i, vendor in enumerate(vendors):
        dev = root / f"card{i}" / "device"
        dev.mkdir(parents=True)
        (dev / "vendor").write_text(vendor + "\n")
        (root / f"card{i}-HDMI-A-1").mkdir()
    return str(root)


class ArcChoice(unittest.TestCase):
    def detect(self, *vendors, platform=LINUX, environ=None):
        """What `updater.detect_hardware` says on a PC with these display vendors and none of the vendor tools installed."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
            drm = fake_drm(Path(t), *vendors)
            real = ec._drm_vendor_backend
            with mock.patch.object(ec.shutil, "which", return_value=None), \
                    mock.patch.object(ec, "host_platform", return_value=platform), \
                    mock.patch.object(updater, "host_platform", return_value=platform), \
                    mock.patch.object(ec, "_drm_vendor_backend", lambda: real(drm)), \
                    mock.patch.object(ec, "windows_display_adapters", return_value=[]),                     mock.patch.object(ec, "_windows_vendor_backend", lambda: real(drm)):      # the test PC may be Windows: either probe answers
                return updater.detect_hardware(environ or {})

    def pick(self, hardware):
        best, reasons = feedmod.select_engine(FEED, hardware)
        return best, reasons

    def test_a_clean_arc_pc_without_oneapi_gets_the_sycl_package(self):
        hw = self.detect("0x8086")
        self.assertEqual((hw["platform"], hw["backend"]), (LINUX, "sycl"))
        best, _ = self.pick(hw)
        self.assertEqual((best.backend, best.platform, best.archs), ("sycl", LINUX, ("intel-arc",)))

    def test_nvidia_and_amd_pcs_never_get_it_even_with_an_intel_igpu_beside_the_card(self):
        for vendors, want in ((("0x10de",), "cuda"), (("0x8086", "0x10de"), "cuda"), (("0x8086", "0x1002"), "hip")):
            hw = self.detect(*vendors)
            best, _ = self.pick(hw)
            self.assertEqual(best.backend, want, vendors)

    def test_windows_has_no_intel_package_and_says_why(self):
        hw = self.detect("0x8086", platform=WIN)
        best, why = self.pick(hw)
        self.assertIsNone(best)
        self.assertTrue(any("sycl" in r and WIN in r for r in why), why)
        self.assertEqual(ec.backend_supported("sycl", WIN)[0], False)
        self.assertEqual(ec.backend_supported("sycl", LINUX)[0], True)

    def test_the_package_is_not_offered_to_a_mac_or_to_a_forced_other_backend(self):
        self.assertIsNone(self.pick({"platform": "macos-arm64", "backend": "metal", "runtime": "0.2.2"})[0])
        best, _ = self.pick(self.detect("0x8086", environ={ec.ENV_BACKEND: "cuda"}))
        self.assertEqual(best.backend, "cuda")

    def test_an_older_sycl_package_does_not_beat_the_new_one_and_a_newer_one_wins(self):
        packages = [feedmod._engine_package(entry(LINUX, "sycl", "", ("intel-arc",), v)) for v in ("0.1.45", "0.1.47", "0.1.46")]
        best, _ = feedmod.select_engine(packages, self.detect("0x8086"))
        self.assertEqual(best.version, "0.1.47")

    def test_no_package_at_all_gives_the_plain_no_engine_reason(self):
        best, why = feedmod.select_engine([p for p in FEED if p.backend != "sycl"], self.detect("0x8086"))
        self.assertIsNone(best)
        self.assertTrue(any("needs sycl" in r for r in why), why)


class Recipe(unittest.TestCase):
    SCRIPT = ROOT / "packaging" / "build_sycl_linux.sh"

    def test_the_recipe_exists_and_is_valid_shell(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.SCRIPT.is_file())
        sh = shutil.which("sh")
        if sh:
            self.assertEqual(subprocess.run([sh, "-n", str(self.SCRIPT)], capture_output=True).returncode, 0)

    def test_the_recipe_bundles_the_runtime_and_checks_a_clean_start(self):
        text = self.SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for needed in ("collect_libs.py", "libur_adapter_level_zero", "libur_adapter_opencl", "patchelf --set-rpath",
                       "package_engine.py --verify", "binary_deps.py", "env -i", "--version", "--backend sycl", "intel-arc"):
            self.assertIn(needed, text)
        self.assertNotIn("\r", text, "a shell script with CRLF endings does not run on Linux")

    def test_a_sycl_package_needs_an_arch_tag_and_only_linux(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                package_engine.build(Path(t), "sycl", "0.1.47", LINUX, Path(t) / "out")
        self.assertIn(LINUX, ec.BACKEND_MATRIX["sycl"])
        self.assertNotIn(WIN, ec.BACKEND_MATRIX["sycl"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def four_gpu_snapshot():
    metrics = {
        "time": 1_790_000_000.0,
        "engine": {"model": "test-model", "batch_groups": 4},
        "live": {"parallel": 8, "running": 6, "queued": 5, "waiting": 2,
                 "slots": [{"slot": i, "group": i // 2, "state": "decoding" if i < 6 else "idle",
                            "prompt_tokens": 400 + i, "generated": i * 10} for i in range(8)]},
        "hardware_static": {"gpu_count": 4, "gpu_name": "aggregate"},
        "hardware": {"gpu_mem_used": 1000,
                     "gpus": [{"index": i, "name": f"GPU-{i}", "mem_used": 12 * 2**30,
                               "mem_total": 24 * 2**30, "util": 50 + i, "temp": 60 + i,
                               "power": 200 + i} for i in range(4)]},
        "requests": [{"finish": "stop", "prompt_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 20}],
        "totals": {"requests": 1, "output_tokens": 20},
    }
    status = {"service": "strata", "model": "test-model", "loaded": True,
              "concurrency": {"serving": 8}, "started": 1_789_999_000}
    return normalize_legacy(metrics, status)


class ContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_replica_slots_and_requests_keep_identity_without_aggregate_batch_claim(self):
        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["topology"]["mode"] = "replicas (configured)"
        sample["topology"]["replica_devices"] = [{"replica": 0, "devices": [0, 1]},
                                                  {"replica": 1, "devices": [2, 3]}]
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        sample["work"]["groups"] = 2
        sample["work"]["effective_rows_window"] = None
        for slot in sample["work"]["slots"]:
            slot["replica"] = slot["slot"] // 4
            slot["group"] = slot["replica"]
        sample["work"]["requests"] = [{"id": "abcdef012345", "state": "reading", "slot": 5,
                                        "group": 1, "replica": 1, "prompt_tokens": 100, "prompt_read": 12}]
        clean = sanitize_telemetry(sample)
        self.assertEqual(clean["work"]["slots"][5]["replica"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(clean["work"]["requests"][0]["replica"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(clean["topology"]["replica_devices"][1]["devices"], [2, 3])
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, render_dashboard
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            clean, width=108, height=28, history=MonitorHistory(), color=False))
        self.assertIn("replicas 2", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("R1 G1", output.getvalue())
        self.assertRegex(output.getvalue(), r"GPU 2 R1")
        sample["work"]["replica_batches"] = [
            {"replica": 0, "batch_sample_windows": 2, "batch_sample_rows": 8,
             "batch_sample_active_rows": 4, "batch_sample_span_s": 1.0, "batch_sample_age_s": 0.5},

             "batch_sample_active_rows": 4, "batch_sample_span_s": 1.0, "batch_sample_age_s": 0.7}]
        sample["work"].update(batch_sample_windows=2, batch_sample_rows=8,
                              batch_sample_active_rows=4, batch_sample_span_s=1.0,
                              batch_sample_age_s=0.5)
        clean = sanitize_telemetry(sample)
        self.assertIsNone(clean["work"]["effective_rows_window"])
        self.assertEqual([row.get("effective_rows_window") for row in clean["work"]["replica_batches"]],
                         [4.0, 3.0])
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(

        self.assertIn("R1 3.0/2.0", output.getvalue())

        self.assertIn("Replica 1", render_view(clean, "serving", 80, 24,
                                               serving_pane="groups", selected=5, detail=True))
        self.assertIn("Replica 1", render_view(clean, "requests", 80, 24, selected=0, detail=True))
        self.assertIn("Replica R1 [configured cards 2,3", render_view(
            clean, "hardware", 80, 24, selected=2, detail=True))
        sample["topology"]["replica_stages"] = [
            {"replica": replica, "stages": [
                {"stage": stage, "layer_start": stage * 20, "layer_end": stage * 20 + 19,
                 "engine_ordinal": stage, "device_index": replica * 2 + stage}
                for stage in range(2)]} for replica in range(2)]

    def test_display_cells_preserve_wide_and_combining_clusters(self):
        self.assertEqual(safe("漢字", 3), "漢")
        self.assertEqual(display_width(safe("漢字", 3)), 2)
        self.assertEqual(safe("x\u0338Y", 1), "x\u0338")
        self.assertEqual(display_width(safe("x\u0338Y", 1)), 1)
        self.assertEqual(safe("🇭🇷next", 1), "")
        self.assertEqual(safe("🇭🇷next", 2), "🇭🇷")
        self.assertEqual(safe("👩‍💻next", 2), "👩‍💻")
        self.assertEqual(safe("\u202e漢", 2), "漢")
        self.assertEqual(display_width(field("漢A", 4)), 4)
        self.assertEqual(field("漢A", 4), "漢A ")
        snapshot = four_gpu_snapshot()
        snapshot["devices"][0]["name"] = "漢字GPUx\u0338"
        snapshot["work"]["requests"] = [{"id": "漢字reqx\u0338", "state": "decoding",
                                         "slot": 0, "group": 0, "generated": 3}]
        for width, height in ((110, 30), (80, 24), (60, 16), (40, 12)):
            with self.subTest(width=width):
                for name in ("hardware", "serving", "requests"):
                    view = render_view(snapshot, name, width, height)
                    self.assertTrue(all(display_width(line) <= width for line in view.splitlines()), name)

    def test_batch_telemetry_opt_in_and_explicit_disable_are_reversible(self):
        env = {"STRATA_BATCH_TELEMETRY": "1"}
        configure_batch_telemetry_env(env, {}, None)
        self.assertEqual(env["STRATA_BATCH_TELEMETRY"], "1")
        configure_batch_telemetry_env(env, {"batch_telemetry": False}, None)
        self.assertNotIn("STRATA_BATCH_TELEMETRY", env)
        configure_batch_telemetry_env(env, {"batch_telemetry": False}, True)
        self.assertEqual(env["STRATA_BATCH_TELEMETRY"], "1")
        configure_batch_telemetry_env(env, {"batch_telemetry": True}, False)
        self.assertNotIn("STRATA_BATCH_TELEMETRY", env)

    def test_batch_window_sample_distinguishes_processed_rows_from_active_slots(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_batch_window_sample("BSTAT 3 18 9 1000\n"),
                         {"windows": 3, "processed_rows": 18, "active_rows": 9, "elapsed_ms": 1000})
        for invalid in ("BSTAT 0 2 1 100", "BSTAT 1 9 1 100", "BSTAT 1 4 5 100", "BSTAT 2 2 0 100",
                        "BSTAT 1 1 1 0", "BSTAT 1 1 1 extra", "BSTAT " + "9" * 100):
            self.assertIsNone(parse_batch_window_sample(invalid))
        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["work"].update(batch_sample_windows=3, batch_sample_rows=18,
                              batch_sample_active_rows=9, batch_sample_span_s=1.0,
                              batch_sample_age_s=1.5,
                              effective_rows_window=999)
        sample["quality"]["batch_window_rows"] = "measured"
        clean = sanitize_telemetry(sample)
        self.assertEqual(clean["work"]["effective_rows_window"], 6.0)
        self.assertEqual(clean["work"]["batch_active_rows_window"], 3.0)
        self.assertEqual(clean["quality"]["batch_window_rows"], "measured")
        self.assertEqual(clean["quality"]["batch_window_source"], "engine_bstat")
        serving = render_view(clean, "serving", 110, 30)
        self.assertIn("6.0 processed / 3.0 active", serving)
        sample["work"]["batch_sample_rows"] = 25
        rejected = sanitize_telemetry(sample)
        self.assertIsNone(rejected["work"]["effective_rows_window"])
        self.assertEqual(rejected["quality"]["batch_window_rows"], "unavailable")

    def test_pipeline_stage_in_flight_sample_is_bounded_and_labelled_host_time(self):

        self.assertIn("q quit", engine)

        sample["work"]["stage_in_flight_us"] = [800000, 700000, 600000, 500000]
        sample["work"]["stage_in_flight_us"][1] = 1_000_001

        self.assertEqual(rejected["quality"]["stage_in_flight"], "unavailable")

    def test_engine_stage_log_is_bounded_and_reports_only_valid_final_ranges(self):
        line = ("strata serve: layer split: layers 0-11 (CUDA0), 12-23 (CUDA1), "
                "24-35 (CUDA2), 36-47 (CUDA3), one hand-off per window")
        self.assertEqual([row["layer_start"] for row in parse_engine_stage_line(line)], [0, 12, 24, 36])
        for bad in (line.replace("12-23", "13-23"), line.replace("CUDA3", "CUDA99"),
                    line.replace("0-11", "0" * 6000 + "-11"),
                    line.replace("one hand-off per window", "unverified")):
            self.assertIsNone(parse_engine_stage_line(bad))
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            path = Path(directory) / "engine.log"
            path.write_text(line + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            offset = path.stat().st_size
            self.assertEqual(read_engine_stage_log(str(path), offset), [])
            with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as target:
                target.write("INFO engine=0.1.42\n" + line + "\nREADY 4096 stop\n")
            self.assertEqual(len(read_engine_stage_log(str(path), offset)), 4)
            self.assertEqual(read_engine_stage_log(str(path), offset, limit=12), [])
        cuda_env = {"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "2,0,3,1", "CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER": "PCI_BUS_ID"}
        self.assertEqual(visible_device_order(cuda_env, "cuda"), [2, 0, 3, 1])
        self.assertEqual(visible_device_order({"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "2,0,3,1"}, "cuda"), [])
        self.assertEqual(visible_device_order({"HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "1,0"}, "hip"), [1, 0])
        self.assertEqual(visible_device_order({**cuda_env, "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "2,2"}, "cuda"), [])
        self.assertEqual(visible_device_order({**cuda_env, "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "9" * 6000}, "cuda"), [])
        self.assertEqual(visible_device_order({"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "2,0"}, "sycl"), [])

    def test_reported_stage_ranges_render_and_invalid_remote_map_is_rejected(self):
        s = four_gpu_snapshot()
        s["topology"] = {"mode": "layer split (engine reported)", "resolved": True,
                         "source": "engine_start_log", "stages": [
                             {"stage": i, "layer_start": i * 12, "layer_end": i * 12 + 11,
                              "engine_ordinal": i, "device_index": i} for i in range(4)]}
        clean = sanitize_telemetry(s)
        self.assertTrue(clean["topology"]["resolved"])
        engine = render_view(clean, "engine", 80, 24)
        device = render_view(clean, "hardware", 80, 24, selected=3, detail=True)
        wide = render_view(clean, "serving", 110, 30)
        self.assertIn("Stage 3  Engine GPU 3  Device 3  Layers 36-47", engine)
        self.assertIn("Stage/layers 3:36-47 [engine log]", device)
        self.assertIn("GPU 3: 36-47", wide)
        s["topology"]["stages"][1]["layer_start"] = 13
        rejected = sanitize_telemetry(s)
        self.assertEqual(rejected["topology"]["stages"], [])
        self.assertFalse(rejected["topology"]["resolved"])
        self.assertEqual(rejected["quality"]["placement"], "unavailable")

    def test_remote_url_requires_tls_and_no_embedded_credentials(self):
        for url in ("http://example.com:8080", "https://key@example.com", "https://example.com/v1",
                    "https://example.com/#fragment"):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError, msg=url):
                server_url(url)
        self.assertEqual(server_url("http://127.0.0.1:8080/"), "http://127.0.0.1:8080")

    def test_parallel_fields_do_not_invent_window_metrics(self):
        s = four_gpu_snapshot()
        self.assertEqual(len(s["devices"]), 4)
        self.assertEqual(s["work"]["groups"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(s["work"]["active"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(s["work"]["occupied_slots"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(s["work"]["queued"], 5)
        self.assertIsNone(s["work"]["effective_rows_window"])
        self.assertIsNone(s["work"]["slots_requested"])
        self.assertIsNone(s["topology"]["mode"])
        serving = render_view(s, "serving", 110, 30)
        self.assertIn("GPU 3", serving)

        s["work"]["requests"] = [{"id": "queued-1", "state": "queued", "queued_at": 1_790_000_000.0,
                                   "slot": None, "group": None, "prompt_tokens": 512}]

    def test_occupied_slot_count_requires_complete_report(self):
        metrics = {"live": {"slots": [{"slot": i, "state": "decoding" if i < 6 else "idle"}
                                         for i in range(8)]}}
        status = {"concurrency": {"serving": 8}}
        complete = normalize_legacy(metrics, status)
        self.assertEqual(complete["work"]["occupied_slots"], 6)
        complete["work"]["occupied_slots"] = 99
        self.assertEqual(sanitize_telemetry(complete)["work"]["occupied_slots"], 6)
        metrics["live"]["slots"] = metrics["live"]["slots"][:-1]
        partial = normalize_legacy(metrics, status)
        self.assertIsNone(partial["work"]["occupied_slots"])
        partial["work"]["occupied_slots"] = 6
        self.assertIsNone(sanitize_telemetry(partial)["work"]["occupied_slots"])
        metrics["live"]["slots"].append({"slot": 0, "state": "decoding"})
        self.assertIsNone(normalize_legacy(metrics, status)["work"]["occupied_slots"])
        metrics["live"]["slots"] = [{"slot": i, "state": "decoding"} for i in range(70)]
        status["concurrency"]["serving"] = 70
        self.assertEqual(len(normalize_legacy(metrics, status)["work"]["slots"]), 64)
        self.assertIsNone(normalize_legacy(metrics, status)["work"]["occupied_slots"])

    def test_parallel_prompt_progress_and_frozen_queue_age(self):
        s = four_gpu_snapshot()
        s["work"]["requests"] = [
            {"id": "reading-1", "state": "reading", "slot": 0, "group": 0,
             "queued_at": 1_789_999_998.0, "admitted_at": 1_789_999_999.0,
             "prompt_tokens": 1000, "prompt_read": 250, "generated": 0},
            {"id": "queued-2", "state": "queued", "slot": None, "group": None,
             "queued_at": 1_789_999_995.0, "admitted_at": None,
             "prompt_tokens": 900, "prompt_read": None, "generated": None},
        ]
        for width, height, pane in ((110, 30, "devices"), (80, 24, "requests"), (40, 12, "requests")):
            shown = render_view(s, "serving", width, height, serving_pane=pane)
            self.assertIn("read 250 new", shown)
            self.assertLessEqual(len(shown.splitlines()), height)
            self.assertTrue(all(len(line) <= width for line in shown.splitlines()))
        with mock.patch("strata_cli.render.time.time", return_value=1_800_000_000.0):
            shown = render_view(s, "serving", 80, 24, serving_pane="requests")
        self.assertIn("wait 5.0 s", shown)
        self.assertIn("wait 1.0 s", shown)
        small = render_view(s, "requests", 40, 12, selected=1)
        self.assertIn("queued-2", small)
        self.assertIn("Pre-admit 5", small)
        detail = render_view(s, "serving", 80, 24, serving_pane="requests", detail=True)
        self.assertIn("REQUEST DETAIL", detail)

        self.assertIn("First engine token --", detail)
        self.assertNotIn("prompt body", detail.lower())
        fitted = render_view(s, "serving", 78, 22, serving_pane="requests", detail=True)
        self.assertIn("First engine token --", fitted)
        self.assertIn("Sample age", fitted)
        self.assertIn("q quit", fitted)
        filtered = render_view(s, "serving", 110, 30, filter_text="queued-2")
        self.assertIn("queued-2", filtered)
        self.assertNotIn("reading-1", filtered)
        compact_detail = render_view(s, "serving", 60, 16, serving_pane="requests", selected=1, detail=True)
        self.assertIn("queued-2", compact_detail)
        self.assertIn("Wait 5.0 s", compact_detail)
        s["work"]["requests"][0]["first_engine_token_s"] = 1.234
        self.assertIn("First engine token 1.234 s", render_view(s, "serving", 80, 24,
                                                                serving_pane="requests", detail=True))
        s["recent"] = [{"finish": "stop", "first_engine_token_s": 1.234}]
        self.assertIn("First engine token 1.234 s", render_view(s, "overview", 80, 24))
        self.assertIn("First engine token 1.234 s", render_view(s, "serving", 110, 30))

    def test_device_and_slot_details_fit_standard_and_compact_views(self):

                                    "work": {"slots": [{"slot": 0, "state": "decoding",
                                                        "prompt": "private"}],
                                             "requests": [{"id": "req-1", "state": "queued",

    def test_activity_feed_is_bounded_redacted_and_visible_at_terminal_sizes(self):
        raw = four_gpu_snapshot()
        raw["activity"] = {"last_seq": 70, "events": [
            {"seq": i, "at": 1_790_000_000.0, "request_id": f"{i:012x}",
             "event": "finished", "outcome": "stop", "prompt": "private"}
            for i in range(1, 71)
        ]}
        raw["activity"]["events"][-1]["event"] = "\x1b[2Jforged"
        clean = sanitize_telemetry(raw)
        self.assertTrue(clean["activity"]["available"])
        self.assertLessEqual(len(clean["activity"]["events"]), 32)
        self.assertNotIn("private", json.dumps(clean))
        self.assertNotIn("forged", json.dumps(clean))
        self.assertEqual(clean["activity"]["events"][-1]["seq"], 69)
        for width, height in ((110, 30), (80, 24), (60, 16), (40, 12)):
            display = render_view(clean, "logs", width, height)
            self.assertIn("activity", display)
            self.assertIn("finished", display)
            self.assertNotIn("private", display)
            self.assertNotIn("\x1b", display)
            self.assertLessEqual(len(display.splitlines()), height)
            self.assertTrue(all(len(line) <= width for line in display.splitlines()))
        legacy = render_view(four_gpu_snapshot(), "logs", 80, 24)
        self.assertIn("unavailable", legacy)
        raw["activity"] = {"last_seq": [], "events": [{"event": []}]}
        self.assertFalse(sanitize_telemetry(raw)["activity"]["available"])

    def test_cli_rejects_invalid_serve_flags_before_loading_engine(self):
        with redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            self.assertEqual(main(["serve", "--profile", "missing.json", "--parallel", "0"]), 2)

    def test_offline_server_rejects_remote_image_before_fetch(self):
        from serve.server import ByteTokenizer, ChatTemplate, MockEngine, Service
        tok = ByteTokenizer()
        svc = Service(MockEngine(tok, "ok"), tok,
                      ChatTemplate(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "serve/chat_template.jinja"))
        svc.offline = True
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "source": "https://example.com/p.png"}]}]
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "offline mode cannot download"):
            svc.prepare(messages, [], {})

    def test_direct_server_remote_bind_without_key_reaches_engine_load(self):
        # no early exit over the key any more: every way of saying "no key" gets past the key check
        import serve.server as server
        cases = [('{"args":[]}', []), ('{"args":[],"api_key":"none"}', []), ('{"args":[]}', ["--no-api-key"]),
                 ('{"args":[]}', ["--api-key", "none"])]
        for body, extra in cases:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
                profile = Path(directory) / "model.json"
                profile.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
                err = io.StringIO()
                with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=True), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
                    with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                        server.main(["--engine", "strata", "--config", str(profile),
                                     "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "0", *extra])
                self.assertIn("tokenizer is missing", err.getvalue(), (body, extra))   # past the key check, stopped later

    def test_code_run_uses_missing_component_exit_until_shared_harness_arrives(self):
        output = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(output):
            code = main(["code", "run", "--prompt-file", "task.md", "--policy", "policy.json",
                         "--output", "jsonl"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 5)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(output.getvalue())["error"]["code"], 5)

    from strata_cli.monitor import MonitorApp, with_aggregate_rate
except ImportError:

@unittest.skipIf(MonitorApp is None, "optional Textual dependency absent")
class HeadlessMonitorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_live_monitor_marks_activity_gaps_after_freeze_and_resets_on_restart(self):
        from rich.console import Console

        def snapshot(instance, last, seqs):
            value = four_gpu_snapshot()
            value["sampled_at"] = time.time()
            value["instance"]["id"] = instance
            value["activity"] = {"available": True, "last_seq": last, "events": [
                {"seq": seq, "at": value["sampled_at"], "request_id": f"{seq:012x}",
                 "event": "queued", "outcome": None} for seq in seqs]}
            return value

        class Source:
            root = "http://127.0.0.1:8095"

            def snapshot(self):
                return self.snapshots.pop(0)

        Source.snapshots = [snapshot("a", 5, [2, 4, 5]), snapshot("b", 2, [1, 2])]

        async def exercise():
            app = MonitorApp(Source(), snapshot("a", 2, [1, 2]), interval=30)
            async with app.run_test(size=(80, 24)) as pilot:
                app.view = 5
                app.action_freeze()
                app._schedule_poll(force=True)
                await pilot.pause(0.1)
                self.assertIsNone(app.displayed_activity_continuity["gap"])
                app.action_freeze()
                await pilot.pause()
                self.assertEqual(app.displayed_activity_continuity["gap"],
                                 {"from_seq": 3, "to_seq": 3})
                shown = str(app.query_one("#content").render())
                self.assertIn("Missed activity #3-3", shown)
                app.view = 0
                app._paint()
                await pilot.pause()
                output = io.StringIO()
                Console(file=output, width=80, color_system=None).print(app.query_one("#content").content)
                self.assertIn("Missed activity #3-3", output.getvalue())
                app._schedule_poll(force=True)
                await pilot.pause(0.1)
                self.assertIsNone(app.displayed_activity_continuity["gap"])
                self.assertTrue(app.displayed_activity_continuity["restarted"])
                app.view = 5
                app._paint()
                await pilot.pause()
                self.assertIn("Serving restarted", str(app.query_one("#content").render()))
                await pilot.press("q")

        asyncio.run(exercise())

    def test_live_compact_screen_replaces_cached_work_on_disconnect(self):
        from rich.console import Console

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        sample["model"]["id"] = "cached-model"
        sample["work"]["requests"] = [{"id": "cached-request", "state": "decoding", "slot": 0}]

        class Source:
            root = "http://127.0.0.1:8095"

            def snapshot(self):
                return sample

        async def exercise(width, height, view):
            app = MonitorApp(Source(), sample, interval=30)
            async with app.run_test(size=(width, height)) as pilot:
                app.view = view
                app.connection_state = "disconnected"
                app._paint()
                await pilot.pause(0.05)
                output = io.StringIO()
                Console(file=output, width=width, color_system=None).print(app.query_one("#content").content)
                shown = output.getvalue()
                self.assertIn("CONNECTION LOST", shown)
                self.assertNotIn("cached-model", shown)
                self.assertNotIn("cached-request", shown)
                self.assertNotIn("GPU-0", shown)
                await pilot.press("q")

        asyncio.run(exercise(40, 12, 0))
        asyncio.run(exercise(80, 24, 1))

    def test_overview_uses_selected_cards_and_marks_missing_sensors(self):
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, render_dashboard

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        sample["topology"]["selected_devices"] = [2, 0, 3, 1, 2, -1, 1.5, True]
        extra = {**sample["devices"][0], "index": 5, "name": "unselected GPU"}
        sample["devices"] = [extra, sample["devices"][1], sample["devices"][2], sample["devices"][0]]
        sample = sanitize_telemetry(sample)
        self.assertEqual(sample["topology"]["selected_devices"], [2, 0, 3, 1])
        history = MonitorHistory()
        complete = four_gpu_snapshot()
        history.add(complete, ("id", "selected-cards"))
        history.add(sample, ("id", "selected-cards"))
        self.assertEqual(list(history.device_util[3]), [complete["devices"][3]["util"], None])
        self.assertEqual(list(history.device_vram[3]), [50.0, None])
        self.assertNotIn(5, history.device_util)
        self.assertNotIn(5, history.device_vram)
        for width, height in ((110, 30), (80, 24)):
            with self.subTest(width=width):
                output = io.StringIO()
                Console(file=output, width=width, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
                    sample, width=width - 2, height=height - 2, history=history,
                    color=False))
                shown = output.getvalue()
                positions = [shown.index(f"GPU {index}") for index in (2, 0, 3, 1)]
                self.assertEqual(positions, sorted(positions))
                self.assertRegex(shown, r"GPU 3[^\n]*--/--G")
                if width == 80:
                    self.assertRegex(shown, r"GPU 3[^\n]*--/--G[^\n]*--\s+--")
                    self.assertNotIn("vram", shown)
                else:
                    self.assertRegex(shown, r"GPU 2[^\n]*vram [^\s-]+")
                    self.assertRegex(shown, r"GPU 3[^\n]*vram --")
                self.assertNotIn("GPU 5", shown)
                self.assertEqual(len(shown.splitlines()), height - 1)

        duplicate = {**sample, "devices": sample["devices"] + [dict(sample["devices"][-1])]}
        history.add(duplicate, ("id", "selected-cards"))
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_util[0][-1])
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_vram[0][-1])
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=80, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            duplicate, width=78, height=22, history=history, color=False))
        self.assertRegex(output.getvalue(), r"GPU 0[^\n]*--/--G")
        self.assertRegex(output.getvalue(), r"GPU 0[^\n]*--/--G[^\n]*--\s+--")

    def test_monitor_history_bounds_device_indices_across_snapshots(self):
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, _output_trend

        history = MonitorHistory()
        for start in (0, 16, 32):
            history.add({"devices": [{"index": index, "util": 20}
                                     for index in range(start, start + 16)],
                         "rates": {"aggregate_output_tok_s": 42.0}}, ("id", "same"))
            self.assertEqual(set(history.device_util), set(range(start, start + 16)))
            self.assertEqual(set(history.device_vram), set(range(start, start + 16)))
        history.add({"devices": [{"index": 32, "util": 40}]}, ("id", "same"))
        self.assertEqual(set(history.device_util), {32})
        self.assertEqual(set(history.device_vram), {32})
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_vram[32][-1])
        self.assertEqual(list(history.output_rate)[-1], None)
        self.assertEqual(_output_trend(history.output_rate, "ascii", False), "Output trend  --")

    def test_vram_history_is_per_card_and_missing_values_are_not_zero(self):
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, render_dashboard

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()

        sample["devices"][1]["mem_used"] = 18 * 2**30

        self.assertEqual(history.device_vram[0][-1], 25.0)
        self.assertEqual(history.device_vram[1][-1], 75.0)
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        self.assertRegex(output.getvalue(), r"GPU 0[^\n]*vram :")
        self.assertRegex(output.getvalue(), r"GPU 1[^\n]*vram \*")

        sample["devices"][0]["mem_total"] = 0
        sample["devices"][1]["mem_used"] = 30 * 2**30
        history.add(sample, ("id", "memory-samples"))
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_vram[0][-1])
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_vram[1][-1])
        history.gap()
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_vram[0][-1])
        history.add(sample, ("id", "new-instance"))
        self.assertEqual(len(history.device_vram[0]), 1)
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_vram[0][-1])

        sample["devices"][0]["mem_used"] = 1e308
        sample["devices"][0]["mem_total"] = 1e308
        history.add(sample, ("id", "new-instance"))
        self.assertEqual(history.device_vram[0][-1], 100.0)
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        self.assertRegex(output.getvalue(), r"GPU 0[^\n]*vram\s+@")

    def test_overview_output_trend_is_bounded_and_resets_with_instance(self):
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, _output_trend, render_dashboard

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        history = MonitorHistory()

            with self.subTest(width=width):

    def test_batch_and_queue_histories_keep_replica_windows_separate(self):
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, render_dashboard

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        history = MonitorHistory(limit=3)
        for rows, queued in ((4.0, 1), (6.0, 5)):
            sample["work"].update(effective_rows_window=rows, batch_sample_age_s=0.5,
                                  queued=queued)
            history.add(sample, ("id", "one"))
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        shown = output.getvalue()
        self.assertIn("Rows trend", shown)
        self.assertIn("4.0-6.0/win", shown)
        self.assertIn("Pre-admit", shown)
        self.assertIn("1-5 req", shown)
        self.assertEqual(len(shown.splitlines()), 29)
        compact = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=compact, width=80, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=78, height=22, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        self.assertNotIn("Rows trend", compact.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("1 Over", compact.getvalue())
        history.gap()
        self.assertIsNone(history.batch_rows[-1])
        self.assertIsNone(history.pre_admit[-1])
        self.assertIsNone(history.device_util[0][-1])
        after_gap = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=after_gap, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        self.assertNotIn("Rows trend", after_gap.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("Pre-admit  ", after_gap.getvalue())

        sample["work"]["batch_sample_age_s"] = 5.1
        history.add(sample, ("id", "one"))
        old_single = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=old_single, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        self.assertIsNone(history.batch_rows[-1])
        self.assertIn("Rows/win -- processed", old_single.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("Rows trend", old_single.getvalue())

        replica = copy.deepcopy(sample)
        replica["topology"]["mode"] = "replicas (configured)"
        replica["topology"]["replica_devices"] = [{"replica": 0, "devices": [0, 1]},
                                                    {"replica": 1, "devices": [2, 3]}]
        replica["work"]["effective_rows_window"] = None
        for first, second in ((4.0, 3.0), (5.0, 4.0)):
            replica["work"]["replica_batches"] = [
                {"replica": 0, "effective_rows_window": first, "batch_active_rows_window": 2.0,
                 "batch_sample_age_s": 0.5},
                {"replica": 1, "effective_rows_window": second, "batch_active_rows_window": 2.0,
                 "batch_sample_age_s": 0.5}]
            history.add(replica, ("id", "two"))
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            replica, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        shown = output.getvalue()
        self.assertIn("R0 rows", shown)
        self.assertIn("4.0-5.0/win", shown)
        self.assertIn("R1 rows", shown)
        self.assertIn("3.0-4.0/win", shown)
        self.assertNotIn("Rows trend", shown)

        replica["work"]["replica_batches"][1]["batch_sample_age_s"] = 5.1
        history.add(replica, ("id", "two"))
        self.assertIsNone(history.replica_batch_rows[1][-1])
        old_sample = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=old_sample, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            replica, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="ascii", color=False))
        self.assertIn("R1 --/--", old_sample.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("R1 rows", old_sample.getvalue())

        replica["work"]["replica_batches"] = [replica["work"]["replica_batches"][0]]
        history.add(replica, ("id", "two"))
        self.assertIsNone(history.replica_batch_rows[1][-1])
        self.assertEqual(len(history.replica_batch_rows[0]), 3)
        history.add(replica, ("id", "three"))
        self.assertEqual(len(history.batch_rows), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(history.replica_batch_rows[0]), 1)

    def test_overview_slot_phases_require_complete_slot_report(self):
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, render_dashboard

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        sample["work"]["slots"][0]["state"] = "reading"
        self.assertIn("Occupied slots by group  G0 2/2", render_view(sample, "serving", 110, 30))
        for width, height in ((110, 30), (80, 24)):
            with self.subTest(width=width):
                output = io.StringIO()
                Console(file=output, width=width, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
                    sample, width=width - 2, height=height - 2, history=MonitorHistory(),
                    color=False))
                shown = output.getvalue()
                self.assertIn("read 1  decode 5  idle 2", shown)
                self.assertLessEqual(len(shown.splitlines()), height - 1)
                self.assertTrue(all(display_width(line) <= width for line in shown.splitlines()))

        incomplete = dict(sample["work"])
        incomplete["slots"] = incomplete["slots"][:-1]
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            {**sample, "work": incomplete}, width=108, height=28, history=MonitorHistory(), color=False))
        self.assertNotIn("Slot phases", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("Group occupancy --", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("Occupied slots by group -- (slot report incomplete)",
                      render_view({**sample, "work": incomplete}, "serving", 110, 30))

        duplicated = dict(sample["work"])
        duplicated["slots"] = [dict(row) for row in sample["work"]["slots"]]
        duplicated["slots"][1]["slot"] = duplicated["slots"][0]["slot"]
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            {**sample, "work": duplicated}, width=108, height=28, history=MonitorHistory(), color=False))
        self.assertNotIn("Slot phases", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("Group occupancy --", output.getvalue())

        invalid_group = dict(sample["work"])
        invalid_group["slots"] = [dict(row) for row in sample["work"]["slots"]]
        invalid_group["slots"][1]["group"] = None
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            {**sample, "work": invalid_group}, width=108, height=28, history=MonitorHistory(), color=False))
        self.assertIn("Slot phases", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("Group occupancy --", output.getvalue())

        invalid_group["slots"][1]["group"] = 9
        self.assertIn("Occupied slots by group -- (slot report incomplete)",
                      render_view({**sample, "work": invalid_group}, "serving", 110, 30))
        invalid_group["slots"][1]["group"] = 0
        invalid_group["slots"][1]["slot"] = 99
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            {**sample, "work": invalid_group}, width=108, height=28, history=MonitorHistory(), color=False))
        self.assertNotIn("Slot phases", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("Group occupancy --", output.getvalue())

    def test_overview_dashboard_keeps_parallel_work_and_four_devices_on_one_screen(self):
        from rich.console import Console
        from strata_cli.dashboard import MonitorHistory, _spark, render_dashboard
        from strata_cli.monitor import choose_glyphs

        self.assertEqual(choose_glyphs("auto", "utf-8", "xterm-256color"), "unicode")
        self.assertEqual(choose_glyphs("auto", "ascii", "xterm-256color"), "ascii")
        self.assertEqual(choose_glyphs("auto", "utf-8", "dumb"), "ascii")
        self.assertEqual(choose_glyphs("braille", "ascii", "dumb"), "braille")

        sample = four_gpu_snapshot()
        sample["sampled_at"] = time.time()
        sample["instance"]["id"] = "fixture-instance"
        sample["rates"].update(answer_tok_s=42.5, prefill_tok_s=180.0,
                               aggregate_output_tok_s=126.0)
        sample["work"].update(effective_rows_window=5.0, batch_active_rows_window=3.0,
                              batch_sample_age_s=0.5,
                              requests=[{"id": "queued-1", "state": "queued", "slot": None,
                                         "group": None, "queued_at": sample["sampled_at"] - 2},
                                        {"id": "running-1", "state": "decoding", "slot": 0,
                                         "group": 0, "generated": 18}])
        sample["activity"] = {"available": True, "events": [
            {"seq": 1, "at": sample["sampled_at"], "request_id": "running-1", "event": "admitted"}]}
        history = MonitorHistory()
        history.add(sample, ("id", "fixture-instance"))
        for width, height in ((110, 30), (80, 24), (110, 42)):
            with self.subTest(width=width):
                output = io.StringIO()
                Console(file=output, width=width, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
                    sample, width=width - 2, height=height - 2, history=history,
                    connection_state="connected", glyphs="ascii", color=False))
                shown = output.getvalue()
                self.assertLessEqual(len(shown.splitlines()), height - 1)
                self.assertTrue(all(display_width(line) <= width for line in shown.splitlines()))
                for expected in ("BATCHING / PARALLEL", "HARDWARE", "REQUESTS", "ACTIVITY",
                                 "5.0", "queued-1", "GPU 0", "GPU 1", "GPU 2", "GPU 3",
                                 "G0", "G3", "42.5 tok/s"):
                    self.assertIn(expected, shown)
                if width == 110:
                    self.assertIn("Stage host span", shown)
                if height == 42:
                    self.assertIn("SESSION", shown)
                    self.assertIn("ENGINE", shown)
                if width == 80:
                    self.assertIn("1 Over", shown)
                self.assertRegex(shown, r"queued-1[^\n]*wait")
                self.assertNotRegex(shown, r"queued-1[^\n]*out")

        history.add({"devices": [{"index": 0, "util": 90}]}, ("id", "restarted"))
        self.assertEqual(list(history.device_util[0]), [90])
        self.assertNotIn(1, history.device_util)
        self.assertTrue(all("\u2800" <= char <= "\u28ff" for char in _spark([25, 75, 50, 100], "braille")))
        self.assertEqual(_spark([None, None], "braille"), "--")
        self.assertEqual(len(_spark([25, 75, 50, 100], "unicode")), 4)
        sample["devices"][0]["name"] = "漢字 RTX 6000"
        sample["work"]["requests"][0]["id"] = "\x1b[2J漢字-queued\u202e"
        sample["work"]["slots"][0]["state"] = None
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=80, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=78, height=22, history=history, color=False))
        self.assertIn("Group occupancy --", output.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("\x1b", output.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("\u202e", output.getvalue())
        self.assertTrue(all(display_width(line) <= 80 for line in output.getvalue().splitlines()))

        sample["work"]["requests"].append({"id": "reading-1", "state": "reading", "slot": 2,
                                               "group": 1, "prompt_read": 250, "prompt_tokens": 1000})
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="unicode", color=False))
        self.assertIn("Reading reading-1", output.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("250/1,000", output.getvalue())
        self.assertTrue(all(display_width(line) <= 110 for line in output.getvalue().splitlines()))

        sample["model"]["loaded"] = False
        output = io.StringIO()
        Console(file=output, width=110, color_system=None).print(render_dashboard(
            sample, width=108, height=28, history=history, glyphs="unicode", color=False))
        self.assertIn("SLEEPING", output.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("42.5 tok/s", output.getvalue())
