## tests/terminal/test_tui_stress_launch.py

"""G04/E01 from the TUI stress test: a second launch while a model serves (same choices, other choices, no screens, --restart,
another context on the same port)."""

import os
import unittest
from unittest import mock

from strata_cli.launch import settings as S
from strata_cli.launch.catalog import Catalog
from strata_cli.launch.runner import LaunchError, Runner
from tests.terminal.launch_support import HW_12, Home, catalog, run_cli


class SecondLaunchTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)
        p = mock.patch.object(Catalog, "hardware", lambda self, fresh=False: dict(HW_12, disk_free_gb=500.0))
        p.start()
        self.addCleanup(p.stop)

    def runner(self, **kw):
        s = S.LaunchSettings(family="qwen", model="IQ3_XXS", context=32768, name="gyro")
        r = Runner(s, catalog=catalog(), **kw)
        r.said = []
        r.emit_cb = lambda e: r.said.append(e.text)
        return r

    @staticmethod
    def row(r, port=8080, name=None, choices=None):
        return [{"profile": "launch-" + (name or r.name), "name": name or r.name, "port": port,
                 "choices": r.choices() if choices is None else choices}]

    def test_same_choices_reuse_the_running_server(self):
        r = self.runner()
        rows = self.row(r)
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows), \
             mock.patch.object(Runner, "ensure_engine", side_effect=AssertionError("must not run")), \
             mock.patch("strata_control.runtime.stop", side_effect=AssertionError("must not stop")):
            res = r.run()
        self.assertTrue(res.reused)
        self.assertTrue(res.urls)
        self.assertTrue(any("nothing was restarted" in x for x in r.said))

    def test_other_choices_without_screens_refuse_in_one_line(self):
        r = self.runner()
        rows = self.row(r, choices={**r.choices(), "vision": "cpu", "context": 65536})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows):
            with self.assertRaises(LaunchError) as cm:
                r.run()
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.code, 6)
        self.assertIn("port 8080", cm.exception.text)
        self.assertIn("context 64K", cm.exception.text)
        self.assertIn("--restart", cm.exception.next)
        self.assertIn("strata launch --stop", cm.exception.next)

    def test_yes_alone_does_not_restart(self):
        r = self.runner(assume_yes=True)
        rows = self.row(r, choices={**r.choices(), "context": 65536})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows):
            with self.assertRaises(LaunchError):
                r.run()

    def test_screens_ask_once_and_cancel_leaves_it_running(self):
        asked = []
        r = self.runner(confirm_restart=lambda q, d: asked.append((q, d)) or False)
        rows = self.row(r, choices={**r.choices(), "context": 65536})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows), \
             mock.patch("strata_control.runtime.stop") as stop:
            with self.assertRaises(LaunchError) as cm:
                r.run()
        self.assertEqual(len(asked), 1)
        self.assertIn("Restart it with these settings?", asked[0][0])
        self.assertEqual(asked[0][1], "Answers in progress stop.")
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.code, 130)
        stop.assert_not_called()

    def test_screens_restart_goes_on(self):
        r = self.runner(confirm_restart=lambda q, d: True)
        rows = self.row(r, choices={**r.choices(), "context": 65536})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows), \
             mock.patch.object(Runner, "ensure_engine", side_effect=RuntimeError("went on")):
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                r.run()

    def test_restart_flag_goes_on_without_asking(self):
        r = self.runner(restart=True)
        rows = self.row(r, choices={**r.choices(), "context": 65536})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows), \
             mock.patch.object(Runner, "ensure_engine", side_effect=RuntimeError("went on")):
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                r.run()

    def test_a_changed_context_on_the_same_port_stops_the_old_profile_first(self):
        r = self.runner(restart=True)
        rows = self.row(r, name="gyro-s-32k", choices={"context": 32768})      # another profile name, same port 8080
        order = []
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows):
            self.assertIsNone(r.check_serving())
        self.assertEqual(r._stop_first, ["launch-gyro-s-32k"])
        with mock.patch("strata_control.runtime.stop", side_effect=lambda n, timeout=0: order.append(n)), \
             mock.patch("strata_cli.launch.access.stop_tunnel"):
            r.stop_others()
        self.assertEqual(order, ["launch-gyro-s-32k"])
        self.assertEqual(r._stop_first, [])

    def test_a_changed_context_without_restart_names_the_running_one(self):
        r = self.runner()
        rows = self.row(r, name="gyro-s-32k", choices={"context": 32768})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows):
            with self.assertRaises(LaunchError) as cm:
                r.check_serving()
        self.assertIn("gyro-s-32k", cm.exception.text)

    def test_a_different_port_runs_beside_with_a_memory_warning(self):
        r = self.runner()
        r.s.port = 8081
        rows = self.row(r, name="other", port=8080, choices={})
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows):
            self.assertIsNone(r.check_serving())
        self.assertEqual(r._stop_first, [])
        self.assertTrue(any("graphics memory" in n for n in r.notices))

    def test_command_line_refuses_restarts_and_yes_alone_does_not(self):
        rows = [{"profile": "launch-q2-0-32k", "name": "q2-0-32k", "port": 8080, "choices": {"context": 1}}]
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "serving_launches", lambda self: rows):
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0", "--context", "32k"])
            self.assertEqual(code, 6, err)
            self.assertIn("--restart", err)
            self.assertIn("q2-0-32k", err)
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--yes", "--model", "q2_0", "--context", "32k"])
            self.assertEqual(code, 6)
            seen = {}

            def go(self, *a, **k):
                seen["restart"] = self.restart
                from strata_cli.launch.runner import Result
                return Result("launch-x", ["http://127.0.0.1:8080"], None, None, [], "/x")

            with mock.patch.object(Runner, "run", go):
                code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--yes", "--restart", "--model", "q2_0", "--context", "32k"])
            self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
            self.assertTrue(seen["restart"])

    def test_restart_is_in_help_and_docs(self):
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["launch", "--help"])
        self.assertIn("--restart", out)
        root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
        with open(os.path.join(root, "docs", "TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            self.assertIn("--restart", f.read())


class ModelPathWins(unittest.TestCase):
    """C08: --model-path and --data-dir are honoured even when an installed copy with the same model and context exists."""

    def setUp(self):
        import json
        import tempfile
        from pathlib import Path
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)
        p = mock.patch.object(Catalog, "hardware", lambda self, fresh=False: dict(HW_12, disk_free_gb=500.0))
        p.start()
        self.addCleanup(p.stop)
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.base = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.installed = self.base / "dl-data"
        (self.installed / "models" / "Q2_0").mkdir(parents=True)
        self.gguf = self.installed / "models" / "Q2_0" / "m.gguf"
        self.gguf.write_bytes(b"x")
        self.pack = self.installed / "packs" / "q2_0"
        self.pack.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.cfg_path = self.base / "strata-q2_0.json"
        self.cfg_path.write_text(json.dumps({"args": ["--model", str(self.gguf), "--pack", str(self.pack), "--max-context", "32768"]}), encoding="utf-8")
        self.mine = self.base / "documents"
        self.mine.mkdir()
        (self.mine / "mine.gguf").write_bytes(b"y")

    def runner(self, **fields):
        s = S.LaunchSettings(family="qwen", model="Q2_0", context=32768, **fields)
        return Runner(s, catalog=catalog())

    def test_installed_copy_serves_when_nothing_was_given(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.runner().installed_serves_request(self.cfg_path))

    def test_a_model_path_elsewhere_is_not_served_by_the_installed_copy(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.runner(model_path=str(self.mine)).installed_serves_request(self.cfg_path))
        self.assertFalse(self.runner(model_path=str(self.mine / "mine.gguf")).installed_serves_request(self.cfg_path))

    def test_a_model_path_that_is_the_installed_folder_is_the_installed_copy(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.runner(model_path=str(self.installed / "models" / "Q2_0")).installed_serves_request(self.cfg_path))

    def test_a_data_dir_elsewhere_is_not_served_by_the_installed_copy(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.runner(data_dir=str(self.base / "c08-data")).installed_serves_request(self.cfg_path))
        self.assertTrue(self.runner(data_dir=str(self.installed)).installed_serves_request(self.cfg_path))

    def test_ensure_model_runs_setup_with_the_given_path_instead_of_reusing_the_profile(self):
        r = self.runner(model_path=str(self.mine))
        said = []
        r.emit_cb = lambda e: said.append(e.text)
        desc = {"context": 32768, "kv": "int8", "images": "off"}
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "check_own_files"), mock.patch.object(Runner, "resolved_vision"),              mock.patch.object(Runner, "installed_state", return_value=(self.cfg_path, desc)),              mock.patch.object(Runner, "_spawn", side_effect=RuntimeError("setup would run")):
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                r.ensure_model()
        self.assertFalse(any("already installed with these choices" in x for x in said))
        self.assertTrue(any("uses the folder you gave" in x for x in said))
        self.assertIn(str(self.mine), r.setup_args())

    def test_without_a_path_the_installed_copy_is_still_reused(self):
        r = self.runner()
        said = []
        r.emit_cb = lambda e: said.append(e.text)
        desc = {"context": 32768, "kv": "int8", "images": "off"}
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "check_own_files"), mock.patch.object(Runner, "resolved_vision"),              mock.patch.object(Runner, "installed_state", return_value=(self.cfg_path, desc)):
            self.assertEqual(r.ensure_model(), self.cfg_path)
        self.assertTrue(any("already installed with these choices" in x for x in said))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_tui_stress_screens.py

"""TUI stress test fixes on the screens: the Folder step (B05), the Save summary (B12), ctrl+c and Escape (B13), PermissionError words, setup guard."""

import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

import setup
from strata_control import folders
from strata_cli.launch import settings as S
from strata_cli.launch.runner import setup_failure
from tests.terminal.launch_support import run_cli
from tests.terminal.test_launch_tui import Base, FakeRunner, flat, press, text_of, typed


class FolderRules(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.base = Path(self.tmp.name)

    def test_usable_folders_pass_and_nothing_is_left_behind(self):
        self.assertIsNone(folders.problem(""))
        self.assertIsNone(folders.problem(self.base))
        self.assertIsNone(folders.problem(self.base / "new" / "deeper"))          # the parent exists and can be written: it can be created
        self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.base), [])                               # nothing was created, the test file is gone

    def test_a_file_is_not_a_folder(self):
        f = self.base / "a.txt"
        f.write_text("x")
        what, nxt = folders.problem(f)
        self.assertIn("is a file", what)
        self.assertTrue(nxt)

    def test_a_missing_parent_that_cannot_be_created_is_refused(self):
        f = self.base / "a.txt"
        f.write_text("x")
        self.assertIn("is a file", folders.problem(f / "inside")[0])
        with mock.patch.object(folders, "_can_write", return_value=False):
            what, nxt = folders.problem(self.base / "x" / "y")
        self.assertIn("cannot be created", what)

    def test_a_folder_that_cannot_be_written_is_refused(self):
        with mock.patch.object(folders, "_can_write", return_value=False):
            what, nxt = folders.problem(self.base)
        self.assertIn("cannot write", what)
        self.assertIn("Pick another folder", nxt)

    def test_the_write_test_creates_and_deletes_a_file(self):
        seen = []
        real = open

        def spy(path, *a, **k):
            seen.append(str(path))
            return real(path, *a, **k)

        with mock.patch("builtins.open", spy):
            self.assertTrue(folders._can_write(self.base))
        self.assertTrue(any(".strata-write-test-" in s for s in seen))
        self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.base), [])

    @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "nt", "Windows system folders")
    def test_system_folders_are_refused(self):
        for p in (r"C:\Windows\System32", r"C:\Windows", r"C:\Program Files\Strata", r"C:\Program Files (x86)\x"):
            with self.subTest(p=p):
                what, nxt = folders.problem(p)
                self.assertIn("system folder", what)

    @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "nt", "Windows path rules")
    def test_malformed_and_relative_paths_are_refused(self):
        for p in (r"C:\a C:\b", r"C:\models|x", r"D:\what?", "models", r"..\x"):
            with self.subTest(p=p):
                self.assertIsNotNone(folders.problem(p), p)

    def test_the_plain_words_carry_a_next_step(self):
        text = folders.words(("This is bad.", "Do that."))
        self.assertEqual(text, "This is bad. Do that.")


class FolderScreen(Base):
    def test_a_bad_folder_stays_on_the_screen_with_one_plain_line_and_is_not_kept(self):
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, "enter", "enter")
            f = app.screen.query_one("#folderpath")
            f.value = ""
            await typed(pilot, str(self.home.base / "afile.txt"))
            (self.home.base / "afile.txt").write_text("x")
            await press(pilot, "enter")
            t = flat(app)
            self.assertIn("Where should the model files be stored?", t)
            self.assertIn("is a file, not a folder", t)
            self.assertIn("Pick another folder", t)
            self.assertIsNone(ctx.settings.data_dir)
            f.value = ""
            await typed(pilot, str(self.home.base / "good"))
            await press(pilot, "enter")
            self.assertIn("How much text should it remember at once?", text_of(app))
            self.assertEqual(ctx.settings.data_dir, str(self.home.base / "good"))
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_the_save_summary_shows_the_chosen_storage_path(self):
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 7, "n", "enter")
            t = flat(app)
            self.assertIn("Storage", t)
            self.assertIn(str(ctx.default_folder()), t)
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_the_save_summary_shows_a_typed_folder(self):
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, "enter", "enter")
            f = app.screen.query_one("#folderpath")
            f.value = ""
            await typed(pilot, str(self.home.base / "mine"))
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 5, "n", "enter")
            self.assertIn("Step 9 of 9", flat(app))
            self.assertIn("mine", flat(app))
        self.run_app(case)


class QuitKeys(Base):
    def test_ctrl_c_quits_the_setup_screens_like_ctrl_q(self):
        for key in ("ctrl+c", "ctrl+q"):
            with self.subTest(key=key):
                async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
                    await press(pilot, "enter")                               # the Model screen
                    await press(pilot, key)
                    await pilot.pause(0.3)
                    self.assertTrue(app._exit)                                 # the app is closing
                self.run_app(case)

    def test_ctrl_c_in_the_folder_field_still_quits(self):
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, "enter", "enter")
            await press(pilot, "ctrl+c")
            await pilot.pause(0.3)
            self.assertTrue(app._exit)
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_escape_in_the_stop_dialog_only_closes_it(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import store
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            store.save(S.LaunchSettings(name="T", family="qwen", model="IQ3_XXS", context=32768))
            FakeRunner.behaviour = "wait"
            app.start_preset("T")
            await pilot.pause(0.4)
            await press(pilot, "ctrl+c")                                       # work would be lost: the dialog stays
            self.assertIn("Stop now?", text_of(app))
            await press(pilot, "escape")
            self.assertNotIn("Stop now?", text_of(app))
            self.assertTrue(app.running)                                       # still running, and no Back happened
            self.assertEqual(app.current, "run")
            app.cancel.set()
            await pilot.pause(0.5)
        self.run_app(case)


class PermissionWords(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_permission_error_names_the_folder_and_what_to_do(self):
        lines = ["Traceback (most recent call last):", "  f",
                 r"PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied: 'C:\Windows\System32\models'"]
        e = setup_failure(lines, "", "", r"C:\x\a.setup.log", False)
        self.assertIn(r"C:\Windows\System32", e.text)
        self.assertIn("access denied", e.text)
        self.assertNotIn("WinError", e.text + e.next)
        self.assertNotIn("Run it again", e.next)
        self.assertIn("--data-dir", e.next)

    def test_other_errors_keep_their_words(self):
        e = setup_failure(["Traceback (most recent call last):", "  f", "KeyError: 'cuda'"], "", "", None, True)
        self.assertIn("KeyError", e.text)


class SetupGuard(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.base = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.root = self.base / "Strata"
        self.root.mkdir()
        env = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"APPDATA": str(self.base / "appdata"), "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(self.base / "appdata")})
        env.start()
        self.addCleanup(env.stop)
        os.environ.pop("STRATA_SETTINGS_FILE", None)
        for patcher in (mock.patch.object(setup, "ROOT", self.root), mock.patch.object(setup, "_CONTROL_HOME", None)):
            patcher.start()
            self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        setup.settings_path().parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def test_a_bad_requested_folder_stops_with_plain_words_and_is_never_saved(self):
        setup.settings_path().write_text(json.dumps({"installs": []}), encoding="utf-8")
        afile = self.base / "afile"
        afile.write_text("x")
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()) as out, self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
            setup.data_folder(str(afile), yes=True)
        self.assertIn("is a file, not a folder", out.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("data_dir", json.loads(setup.settings_path().read_text(encoding="utf-8")))

    def test_a_bad_saved_folder_is_dropped_not_kept(self):
        afile = self.base / "afile"
        afile.write_text("x")
        setup.settings_path().write_text(json.dumps({"data_dir": str(afile), "installs": []}), encoding="utf-8")
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            dest, _ = setup.data_folder(None, yes=True)
        self.assertNotEqual(str(dest.resolve()), str(afile.resolve()))
        self.assertNotEqual(json.loads(setup.settings_path().read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("data_dir"), str(afile))


class DataDirFlag(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_launch_data_dir_with_a_bad_path_refuses_before_anything(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            afile = Path(tmp) / "afile"
            afile.write_text("x")
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--plan", "--model", "q2_0", "--data-dir", str(afile)])
        self.assertEqual(code, 2)
        self.assertIn("is a file, not a folder", err)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_tuiqa_browser.py

"""Owner rule 2026-10-18: the Terminal never opens a browser by itself; only an explicit --open does (the monitor's b key is also a request). The generic
start message promises a browser only when one will open."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from strata_cli.launch import cmd, settings as S
from strata_cli.launch.runner import Result, Runner, derive_config
from strata_control import tune_knobs
from tests.terminal.launch_support import Home, run_cli


def served() -> Result:
    return Result("launch-x", ["http://127.0.0.1:8081"], None, None, [], "/x")


class NoBrowserByItself(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)

    def test_the_launch_config_forbids_a_browser_and_drops_open_from_the_args(self):
        base = {"exe": "e", "args": ["--native", "x.gguf", "--open", "--max-context", "32768"], "open_browser": True}
        cfg = derive_config(base, S.LaunchSettings(), bool_flags=tune_knobs.BOOL_FLAGS)
        self.assertIs(cfg["open_browser"], False)
        self.assertNotIn("--open", cfg["args"])
        self.assertEqual(cfg["args"][:2], ["--native", "x.gguf"])

    def test_a_plain_launch_opens_no_browser(self):
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "run", return_value=served()), mock.patch("webbrowser.open") as opened:
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        opened.assert_not_called()

    def test_open_opens_the_local_page_once(self):
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "run", return_value=served()), mock.patch("webbrowser.open", return_value=True) as opened:
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0", "--open"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        opened.assert_called_once_with("http://127.0.0.1:8081")

    def test_the_screens_open_a_browser_only_for_open(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import app as launch_app
        from tests.terminal.launch_support import HW_12, catalog
        for flag, calls in ((False, 0), (True, 1)):
            with mock.patch.object(launch_app.LaunchApp, "run", lambda self, **kw: served()), \
                    mock.patch.object(launch_app, "run_monitor", lambda info, **kw: 0), mock.patch("webbrowser.open", return_value=True) as opened:
                with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
                    launch_app.run_tui(S.LaunchSettings(family="qwen", model="Q2_0", context=32768, vision="off"), catalog=catalog(HW_12),
                                       auto_run=True, open_page=flag)
            self.assertEqual(opened.call_count, calls, flag)

    def test_open_is_in_the_help(self):
        code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--help"])
        self.assertIn("--open", out)
        self.assertIn("nothing opens a browser without this", out.replace("\n", " ").replace("  ", " "))


class StartMessage(unittest.TestCase):
    def narrate(self, opens: bool) -> str:
        from serve import server
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        log = Path(d) / "engine.log"
        log.write_text("strata generate: expert arena: resident, 31.64 GiB\n", encoding="utf-8")
        done, out = threading.Event(), io.StringIO()
        with mock.patch.object(server, "OPENS_BROWSER", opens), contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
            t = threading.Thread(target=server.narrate_start, args=(str(log), 0, [], done))
            t.start()
            time.sleep(0.8)
            done.set()
            t.join(5)
        return out.getvalue()

    def test_the_browser_is_promised_only_with_open(self):
        self.assertNotIn("browser", self.narrate(False))
        self.assertIn("the server says when it is ready", self.narrate(False))
        self.assertIn("the browser opens when it is ready", self.narrate(True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_tuiqa_connect_cli.py

"""Tester report T07: `strata connect pi --check --output json` skipped the checks and said "ok": true with exit 0 even when nothing was
listening. It now runs the same two checks as the plain-words output, returns each result, and exits 1 when one failed or the server cannot be
reached."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import socket
import threading
import unittest
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from tests.terminal.launch_support import Home, run_cli


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    mode = "good"                                           # good | no-text | no-tool

    def log_message(self, *a) -> None:
        pass

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)) or b"{}")
        wants_tool = bool(body.get("tools"))
        message = {"role": "assistant", "content": "pong"}
        if Handler.mode == "no-text" and not wants_tool:
            message = {"role": "assistant", "content": None}
        if wants_tool:
            message = ({"role": "assistant", "content": "I cannot."} if Handler.mode == "no-tool" else
                       {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [
                           {"id": "1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": json.dumps({"city": "Paris"})}}]})
        data = json.dumps({"choices": [{"message": message}]}).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)


class ConnectCheckJson(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)
        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.port = self.server.server_address[1]
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.addCleanup(self.server.shutdown)
        Handler.mode = "good"

    def free_port(self) -> int:
        with socket.socket() as s:
            s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
            return s.getsockname()[1]

    def run_json(self, port: int, *extra: str):
        code, out, err = run_cli(["connect", "pi", "--url", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", "--context", "128k", "--check", "--output", "json", *extra])
        return code, json.loads(out), err

    def run_human(self, port: int):
        return run_cli(["connect", "pi", "--url", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", "--context", "128k", "--check"])

    def test_a_working_server_passes_both_checks_with_ok_true_and_exit_zero(self):
        code, data, _ = self.run_json(self.port)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIs(data["ok"], True)
        self.assertEqual([c["name"] for c in data["checks"]], ["prompt", "tool call"])
        self.assertTrue(all(c["ok"] for c in data["checks"]))
        self.assertIn("get_weather", data["checks"][1]["detail"])
        self.assertEqual(data["checked_server"], f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}")
        self.assertEqual(data["vendor_tested"], "pi 0.74.2")
        self.assertIn("files", data)                          # the rendered setup is still there

    def test_a_server_that_answers_wrongly_is_false_with_exit_one_and_says_which_check(self):
        for mode, failing in (("no-text", "prompt"), ("no-tool", "tool call")):
            Handler.mode = mode
            code, data, _ = self.run_json(self.port)
            self.assertEqual(code, 1, mode)
            self.assertIs(data["ok"], False)
            bad = [c["name"] for c in data["checks"] if not c["ok"]]
            self.assertEqual(bad, [failing], mode)
            self.assertIn(failing, data["error"]["message"])
            self.assertIn("answered", data["error"]["message"])

    def test_nothing_listening_is_false_with_exit_one_and_says_it_could_not_be_reached(self):
        port = self.free_port()
        code, data, _ = self.run_json(port)
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertIs(data["ok"], False)
        self.assertEqual([c["ok"] for c in data["checks"]], [False, False])
        self.assertIn("could not be reached", data["error"]["message"])

    def test_json_and_human_agree_on_the_exit_code(self):
        port = self.free_port()
        self.assertEqual(self.run_json(port)[0], self.run_human(port)[0])
        Handler.mode = "no-tool"
        self.assertEqual(self.run_json(self.port)[0], self.run_human(self.port)[0])
        Handler.mode = "good"
        self.assertEqual(self.run_json(self.port)[0], self.run_human(self.port)[0], 0)

    def test_without_check_json_is_unchanged_and_asks_nothing_of_the_server(self):
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["connect", "pi", "--url", f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.free_port()}", "--output", "json"])
        data = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertTrue(data["ok"])
        self.assertNotIn("checks", data)

    def test_the_list_says_vendor_tested_and_not_a_check_of_your_server(self):
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["connect"])
        self.assertIn("Vendor tested", out)
        self.assertIn("not a check of your server", out)
        code, out, _ = run_cli(["connect", "--output", "json"])
        rows = json.loads(out)["harnesses"]
        self.assertEqual(next(r for r in rows if r["id"] == "pi")["vendor_tested"], "pi 0.74.2")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_tuiqa_launch.py

"""Tester report 2026-10-18 (Terminal 0.1.45), T02: `strata launch` with flags opened the screens straight into the run, which crashed
(IndexError: pop from empty list in switch_screen) and exited 0. The run now opens on its own screen; an error of the screens ends non-zero."""

from __future__ import annotations

def flags_settings() -> S.LaunchSettings:
    """What `strata launch --model q2_0 --family qwen --context 128k --kv int8 --vision cpu --parallel 1 --tune skip --access local --port 8081` gives."""
    return S.LaunchSettings(name="QA flags", family="qwen", model="Q2_0", context=131072, kv="int8", vision="cpu", parallel=1, tune="skip",
                            access="local", port=8081)


class FlagsOpenTheRun(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)
        FakeRunner.instances.clear()
        FakeRunner.behaviour = "ok"
        FakeRunner.download = 0.0
        p = mock.patch("strata_cli.launch.app.Runner", FakeRunner)
        p.start()
        self.addCleanup(p.stop)

    def test_auto_run_shows_the_run_screen_and_finishes(self):
        app = LaunchApp(make_ctx(settings=flags_settings()), auto_run=True)

        async def go():
            async with app.run_test(size=SIZE) as pilot:
                for _ in range(60):
                    await pilot.pause(0.05)
                    if app.result is not None:
                        break
                return app.result

        result = asyncio.run(go())
        self.assertIsNotNone(result, "the run did not finish: the screens crashed instead of opening the run")
        self.assertEqual(result.urls, ["http://127.0.0.1:8081"])

    def test_auto_run_with_a_big_download_asks_first_and_then_runs(self):
        FakeRunner.download = 66.0
        app = LaunchApp(make_ctx(settings=flags_settings()), auto_run=True)

        async def go():
            async with app.run_test(size=SIZE) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.3)
                self.assertIn("Download about 66 GB?", text_of(app))
                await pilot.press("enter")                      # Download and start
                for _ in range(60):
                    await pilot.pause(0.05)
                    if app.result is not None:
                        break
                return app.result

        self.assertIsNotNone(asyncio.run(go()))

    def headless_run(self, app):
        return App.run(app, headless=True)

    def test_run_tui_with_flags_returns_zero_and_opens_the_monitor(self):
        calls = []
        with mock.patch.object(LaunchApp, "run", lambda self, **kw: App.run(self, headless=True)), \
                mock.patch.object(launch_app, "run_monitor", lambda info, **kw: calls.append(info) or 0), \
                mock.patch.object(launch_app, "Catalog", create=True):
            cat = catalog(HW_12)
            code = launch_app.run_tui(flags_settings(), catalog=cat, auto_run=True)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)

    def test_an_error_of_the_screens_ends_non_zero_with_a_plain_sentence(self):
        class Broken(FakeRunner):
            def __init__(self, *a, **kw):
                raise RuntimeError("boom")

        err = io.StringIO()
        with mock.patch.object(LaunchApp, "run", lambda self, **kw: App.run(self, headless=True)), \
                mock.patch.object(launch_app, "Runner", Broken), \
                contextlib.redirect_stderr(err), contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            code = launch_app.run_tui(flags_settings(), catalog=catalog(HW_12), auto_run=True)
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("nothing was started", err.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("--no-tui", err.getvalue())

    def test_the_command_turns_a_crash_into_exit_one(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import cmd
        err = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            code = cmd._tui(lambda *a, **k: (_ for _ in ()).throw(IndexError("pop from empty list")))
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertIn("unexpected problem", err.getvalue())
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", err.getvalue())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


class NoEngineFlow(unittest.TestCase):
    """Owner decision 2026-10-18: no usable engine is a warning, not a refusal; the model downloads and the end message names the problem."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)

    def served_nothing(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import Result, no_engine_final
        text = no_engine_final("The feed has no engine package for this PC.")
        return Result("launch-x", [], None, None, [text], "/x", serving=False, engine_problem="The feed has no engine package for this PC.",
                      final_text=text)

    def test_the_command_ends_with_exit_zero_and_the_engine_message(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import Runner
        from tests.terminal.launch_support import run_cli
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "run", return_value=self.served_nothing()):
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0", "--yes"])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        self.assertIn("The model is ready, but Strata can't start it yet", out)
        self.assertIn("The feed has no engine package for this PC", out)
        self.assertIn("Next step:", out)
        self.assertNotIn("Strata is serving", out)

    def test_json_says_not_serving(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import Runner
        from tests.terminal.launch_support import run_cli
        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "run", return_value=self.served_nothing()):
            code, out, err = run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0", "--output", "json"])
        data = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertTrue(data["ok"])
        self.assertFalse(data["serving"])
        self.assertIn("engine", data["engine_problem"])

    def test_yes_is_passed_to_the_runner_and_json_never_asks(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.runner import Runner
        from tests.terminal.launch_support import run_cli
        seen = []
        real = Runner.__init__

        def spy(self, *a, **kw):
            seen.append(kw.get("assume_yes"))
            real(self, *a, **kw)

        with mock.patch.object(Runner, "__init__", spy), mock.patch.object(Runner, "run", return_value=self.served_nothing()):
            run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0", "--yes"])
            run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0", "--output", "json"])
            run_cli(["launch", "--no-tui", "--model", "q2_0"])
        self.assertEqual(seen, [True, True, False])

    def test_the_question_default_is_yes(self):
        from strata_cli.launch import cmd
        with mock.patch("builtins.input", return_value=""), mock.patch.object(cmd.sys, "stdin") as sin, \
                mock.patch.object(cmd.sys, "stdout") as sout:
            sin.isatty.return_value = True
            sout.isatty.return_value = True
            self.assertTrue(cmd._ask_yes("t", "text"))
        with mock.patch("builtins.input", return_value="n"), mock.patch.object(cmd.sys, "stdin") as sin, \
                mock.patch.object(cmd.sys, "stdout") as sout:
            sin.isatty.return_value = True
            sout.isatty.return_value = True
            self.assertFalse(cmd._ask_yes("t", "text"))
        self.assertTrue(cmd._ask_yes("t", "text"))               # no keyboard: the person already named the model

    def test_the_screens_ask_with_a_dialog_and_enter_means_yes(self):
        FakeRunner.instances.clear()
        FakeRunner.behaviour = "ok"
        FakeRunner.download = 0.0
        answers = []

        class Asking(FakeRunner):
            def run(self, start=True):
                answers.append(self.confirm("No engine", "Strata couldn't find an engine for this computer (x). Download?"))
                return super().run(start)

            def __init__(self, *a, confirm=None, **kw):
                super().__init__(*a, **kw)
                self.confirm = confirm

        app = LaunchApp(make_ctx(settings=flags_settings()), auto_run=True)

        async def go():
            with mock.patch("strata_cli.launch.app.Runner", Asking):
                async with app.run_test(size=SIZE) as pilot:
                    await pilot.pause(0.4)
                    self.assertIn("Strata couldn't find an engine for this computer", text_of(app))
                    await pilot.press("enter")                  # Download anyway
                    for _ in range(60):
                        await pilot.pause(0.05)
                        if app.result is not None:
                            break
                    return app.result

        self.assertIsNotNone(asyncio.run(go()))
        self.assertEqual(answers, [True])

    def test_the_screens_show_the_end_message_and_exit_zero(self):
        from strata_cli.launch.app import LaunchApp as LA
        res = self.served_nothing()
        with mock.patch.object(LA, "run", lambda self, **kw: res), mock.patch.object(launch_app, "run_monitor", side_effect=AssertionError("no monitor")):
            out = io.StringIO()
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
                code = launch_app.run_tui(flags_settings(), catalog=catalog(HW_12), auto_run=True)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("The model is ready, but Strata can't start it yet", out.getvalue())


## tests/terminal/test_tuiqa_monitor.py

"""Tester report 2026-10-18, T06 / T08 / T10 and the smaller monitor items: one seven-view model in every view and at every width,
Connect that says what is vendor history and what is this server's live result, and a light theme the Connect view and its pop-ups follow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import re
import unittest
from unittest import mock

from strata_cli import nav
from strata_cli.launch import check, harness
from strata_cli.launch.monitor_ext import LaunchMonitor
from strata_cli.launch.widgets import DARK, LIGHT
from strata_cli.monitor import MonitorApp
from tests.terminal.launch_support import Home, text_of
from tests.terminal.test_launch_monitor import INFO
from tests.terminal.test_overview import Source, metrics

SIZES = ((120, 40), (80, 24), (60, 20), (40, 15))
NAMES = ["Overview", "Serving", "Requests", "Engine", "Hardware", "Logs", "Connect"]
SHORT = {"Overview": "Over", "Serving": "Serve", "Requests": "Reqs", "Engine": "Engine", "Hardware": "GPU", "Logs": "Logs", "Connect": "Conn"}


def tab_line(shown: str) -> str:
    """The row with the tab names: the one that has the marked tab."""
    for line in shown.splitlines():
        if re.search(r"\[\d [A-Za-z]+\]", line) and re.search(r"\b\d [A-Za-z]+", line.replace("[", " ")):
            return line
    return ""


def marked(line: str) -> str | None:
    m = re.search(r"\[(\d) ([A-Za-z]+)\]", line)
    return None if m is None else m.group(2)


class TabModel(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_all_names_when_there_is_room(self):
        self.assertEqual(nav.plain(1, 120, True), "1 Overview  [2 Serving]  3 Requests  4 Engine  5 Hardware  6 Logs  7 Connect")
        self.assertEqual(nav.plain(1, 120, False), "1 Overview  [2 Serving]  3 Requests  4 Engine  5 Hardware  6 Logs")

    def test_short_names_then_a_window_around_the_selected_tab_and_it_is_always_marked(self):
        for connect in (False, True):
            for current in range(nav.count(connect)):
                for width in (120, 90, 80, 60, 50, 40, 30, 24):
                    line = nav.plain(current, width, connect)
                    self.assertLessEqual(len(line), width, (current, width, connect))
                    name = NAMES[current]
                    self.assertTrue(f"[{current + 1} {name}]" in line or f"[{current + 1} {SHORT[name]}]" in line, (line, current, width))
                    if width >= 60 + (10 if connect else 0):
                        self.assertNotIn("<", line)                       # nothing hidden when the short names fit
        self.assertEqual(nav.plain(3, 40, True), "< 3 Reqs [4 Engine] 5 GPU 6 Logs 7 Conn")
        self.assertEqual(nav.plain(3, 34, True), "< 3 Reqs [4 Engine] 5 GPU 6 Logs >")

    def test_the_hint_matches_the_number_of_views(self):
        self.assertEqual((nav.keys(False), nav.keys(True)), ("1-6", "1-7"))

    def test_styled_marks_the_selected_tab_bold(self):
        t = nav.styled(2, 120, True, accent="#34d399")
        spans = [(t.plain[s.start:s.end], s.style) for s in t.spans if "bold" in str(s.style)]
        self.assertEqual([x for x, _ in spans], ["[3 Requests]"])


class MonitorViews(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_app(self, cls, size, coro, **kw):
        async def go():
            if cls is LaunchMonitor:
                app = LaunchMonitor(Source(metrics("idle")), None, info=dict(INFO), interval=30, **kw)
            else:
                app = MonitorApp(Source(metrics("idle")), None, interval=30, **kw)
            async with app.run_test(size=size) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.4)
                return await coro(app, pilot)
        with Home():
            return asyncio.run(go())

    def test_arrows_visit_all_seven_views_and_wrap_both_ways(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            seen = [app.view]
            for _ in range(7):
                await pilot.press("right")
                await pilot.pause(0.05)
                seen.append(app.view)
            self.assertEqual(seen, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 0])           # Logs -> Connect -> Overview
            await pilot.press("left")
            await pilot.pause(0.05)
            self.assertEqual(app.view, 6)                               # Overview <- Connect
            await pilot.press("left")
            await pilot.pause(0.05)
            self.assertEqual(app.view, 5)                               # Connect <- Logs: the previous tab, not a relative of the last ordinary view
        self.run_app(LaunchMonitor, (120, 40), case)

    def test_number_keys_and_arrows_agree(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            for n in range(1, 8):
                await pilot.press(str(n))
                await pilot.pause(0.05)
                self.assertEqual(app.view, n - 1)
        self.run_app(LaunchMonitor, (120, 40), case)

    def test_every_view_at_every_size_shows_the_tabs_the_hint_and_the_selection(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            for size in SIZES:
                await pilot.resize_terminal(*size)
                await pilot.pause(0.15)
                for index in range(7):
                    await pilot.press(str(index + 1))
                    await pilot.pause(0.08)
                    shown = text_of(app)
                    line = tab_line(shown)
                    name = marked(line)
                    self.assertIsNotNone(name, (size, index, shown[:400]))
                    self.assertIn(name, (NAMES[index], SHORT[NAMES[index]]), (size, index, line))
                    self.assertNotIn("1-6 views", shown, (size, index))           # the hint never disagrees with the tab line
                    self.assertIn("Overview" if index == 0 and size[0] >= 78 else NAMES[index][:3], shown.replace("[", " "), (size, index))
        self.run_app(LaunchMonitor, (120, 40), case)

    def test_the_plain_monitor_has_six_views_and_says_1_6(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            for size in SIZES:
                await pilot.resize_terminal(*size)
                await pilot.pause(0.15)
                shown = text_of(app)
                self.assertNotIn("Connect", shown)
                self.assertNotIn("1-7", shown)
            await pilot.press("7")
            await pilot.pause(0.05)
            self.assertEqual(app.view, 0)                                      # no seventh view here
            await pilot.press("left")
            await pilot.pause(0.05)
            self.assertEqual(app.view, 5)
        self.run_app(MonitorApp, (120, 40), case)

    def test_strata_monitor_is_the_same_seven_view_monitor_as_launchs(self):
        """`strata monitor --url ...` builds the launch monitor without the quit question: seven views, key 7, Connect points at that server."""
        from strata_cli import monitor_commands
        seen = {}

        class Fake:
            def __init__(self, endpoint, snapshot, **kw):
                seen.update(kw, endpoint=endpoint)

            def run(self):
                seen["ran"] = True

        args = monitor_commands.parser().parse_args(["monitor", "--url", "http://127.0.0.1:18765"])
        with mock.patch("strata_cli.launch.monitor_ext.LaunchMonitor", Fake), mock.patch("sys.stdout.isatty", return_value=True), Home():
            self.assertEqual(monitor_commands.run(args), 0)
        self.assertTrue(seen.get("ran"))
        self.assertFalse(seen["ask_quit"])                                   # q detaches: this command started nothing
        self.assertEqual(seen["info"]["url"], "http://127.0.0.1:18765")      # the Connect view's address is the --url server
        self.assertIn("seven views", " ".join(monitor_commands.parser().format_help().split()))

    def test_the_monitor_strata_monitor_opens_has_seven_views_and_connect_shows_the_server(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            shown = text_of(app)
            self.assertIn("7 Connect", shown)
            self.assertNotIn("1-6", shown)
            await pilot.press("7")
            await pilot.pause(0.2)
            self.assertEqual(app.view, 6)
            self.assertIn(INFO["url"], text_of(app))
            await pilot.press("escape")
            await pilot.pause(0.1)
            self.assertEqual(app.view, 0)
        async def go():
            app = LaunchMonitor(Source(metrics("idle")), None, info=dict(INFO), interval=30, ask_quit=False)
            async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.4)
                return await case(app, pilot)
        with Home():
            asyncio.run(go())

    def test_the_overview_is_titled_overview(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            self.assertIn("STRATA  Overview", text_of(app))
            self.assertNotIn("STRATA  Serving", text_of(app))
            await pilot.press("2")
            await pilot.pause(0.1)
            self.assertIn("Serving", text_of(app))
        self.run_app(LaunchMonitor, (120, 40), case)


class ConnectStatus(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_app(self, coro, size=(120, 40), **kw):
        async def go():
            app = LaunchMonitor(Source(metrics("idle")), None, info=dict(INFO), interval=30, **kw)
            async with app.run_test(size=size) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.4)
                return await coro(app, pilot)
        with Home():
            return asyncio.run(go())

    def test_vendor_history_and_this_servers_result_are_separate_columns(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            await pilot.press("7")
            await pilot.pause(0.2)
            shown = text_of(app)
            header = next(ln for ln in shown.splitlines() if "Vendor tested" in ln)
            self.assertIn("This server", header)
            for h in harness.HARNESSES:
                said = "built into Strata" if h.built_in else h.tested
                row = next(ln for ln in shown.splitlines() if h.title[:16] in ln and said[:23] in ln)
                self.assertIn("Not checked", row)                          # nothing has been tried against THIS server yet
                self.assertNotIn("tested ok", row)
                self.assertIn(said[:23], row)
            self.assertNotIn("Passed", shown)
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_a_check_turns_not_checked_into_passed_or_failed_for_that_app_only(self):
        good = [check.Check("prompt", True, "ok", 1.0), check.Check("tool call", True, "ok", 1.0)]
        bad = [check.Check("prompt", True, "ok", 1.0), check.Check("tool call", False, "no tool call", 1.0)]

        async def case(app, pilot):
            await pilot.press("7")
            for results, want in ((good, "Passed (2/2)"), (bad, "Failed (1/2)")):
                with mock.patch.object(check, "run_checks", return_value=results):
                    await pilot.press("h")
                    for _ in range(30):
                        await pilot.pause(0.1)
                        if want in text_of(app):
                            break
                self.assertIn(want, text_of(app))
                await pilot.press("down")
                await pilot.pause(0.1)
            shown = text_of(app)
            self.assertEqual(shown.count("Not checked"), 6)                # 8 apps, 2 checked
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_narrow_widths_keep_the_this_server_column(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            for width in (80, 60, 40):
                await pilot.resize_terminal(width, 24)
                await pilot.pause(0.15)
                await pilot.press("7")
                await pilot.pause(0.1)
                shown = text_of(app)
                self.assertIn("This server", shown, width)
                self.assertIn("Not checked", shown, width)
        self.run_app(case)


def luminance(hex_color: str) -> float:
    r, g, b = (int(hex_color[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5))
    f = lambda c: c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4          # noqa: E731
    return 0.2126 * f(r) + 0.7152 * f(g) + 0.0722 * f(b)


def contrast(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    la, lb = sorted((luminance(a), luminance(b)), reverse=True)
    return (la + 0.05) / (lb + 0.05)


class LightTheme(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_light_palette_is_readable_on_white_and_on_its_selection(self):
        for name in ("fg", "mute", "accent", "warn", "bad"):
            self.assertGreaterEqual(contrast(getattr(LIGHT, name), LIGHT.panel), 4.5, name)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(contrast(LIGHT.accent, LIGHT.sel), 4.5)
        self.assertLess(contrast(DARK.accent, "#ffffff"), 3.0)                  # the old dark colours are what the report measured (1.92:1)

    def run_app(self, coro, size=(120, 40)):
        async def go():
            app = LaunchMonitor(Source(metrics("idle")), None, info=dict(INFO), interval=30, theme="light", color="always")
            async with app.run_test(size=size) as pilot:
                await pilot.pause(0.4)
                return await coro(app, pilot)
        with Home():
            return asyncio.run(go())

    def test_connect_uses_the_light_colours_only(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            await pilot.press("7")
            await pilot.pause(0.2)
            t = app.connect_text(118)
            used = {str(s.style) for s in t.spans}
            joined = " ".join(used)
            for dark_only in ("#34d399", "#8e979f", "#f28b82", "#f5c56b", "#1f2a27"):
                self.assertNotIn(dark_only, joined)
            self.assertIn(LIGHT.accent, joined)
            self.assertIn(LIGHT.mute, joined)
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_the_dialog_opened_from_light_mode_is_light(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            self.assertTrue(app.has_class("theme-light"))
            await pilot.press("7")
            await pilot.pause(0.1)
            await pilot.press("w")
            await pilot.pause(0.3)
            dialog = app.screen.query_one("#dialog")
            self.assertEqual(str(dialog.styles.background.hex).lower()[:7], "#ffffff")
            await pilot.press("escape")
            await pilot.pause(0.1)
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_theme_cycling_moves_the_class_and_the_dialog_back_to_dark(self):
        async def case(app, pilot):
            self.assertTrue(app.has_class("theme-light"))
            await pilot.press("t")                                           # light -> terminal
            await pilot.pause(0.05)
            self.assertFalse(app.has_class("theme-light"))
            await pilot.press("t")                                           # terminal -> dark
            await pilot.press("7", "w")
            await pilot.pause(0.3)
            self.assertEqual(str(app.screen.query_one("#dialog").styles.background.hex).lower()[:7], "#161a1d")
        self.run_app(case)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_tuiqa_version.py

"""The Terminal tells people the app's version (0.2.3), and its README no longer contradicts itself."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import strata_cli

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "packaging"))
import package_terminal  # noqa: E402


class ProductVersion(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_it_is_the_apps_own_version_or_a_terminal_only_release_after_it(self):
        cargo = ROOT / "apps" / "desktop" / "src-tauri" / "Cargo.toml"
        if not cargo.is_file():
            self.skipTest("no app source in this tree")
        m = re.search(r'^version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', cargo.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.MULTILINE)
        # 0.2.3.1 is a Control-only hotfix: the Terminal says 0.2.3.1 while the app (and its updater entry) stay 0.2.3
        # 0.2.4 is a Terminal release: the app stays 0.2.3 (the Terminal is never older than the app)
        as_tuple = lambda v: tuple(int(p) for p in v.split("."))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(as_tuple(strata_cli.PRODUCT_VERSION), as_tuple(m.group(1)))
        self.assertEqual(as_tuple(strata_cli.PRODUCT_VERSION)[:2], as_tuple(m.group(1))[:2])

    def test_dash_dash_version_leads_with_it_and_keeps_the_build_number(self):
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "strata.py"), "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(f"strata {strata_cli.PRODUCT_VERSION} (build {strata_cli.version()};"), out)
        self.assertIn(sys.executable, out)                                  # the packaging smoke test reads the interpreter back from this line

    def test_the_build_number_stays_numeric_for_the_engine_compatibility_checks(self):
        self.assertRegex(strata_cli.version(), r"^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+$")


class Readme(unittest.TestCase):
    def readme(self, target: str) -> str:
        return package_terminal._readme("0.2.3", target)

    def test_it_does_not_say_nothing_downloads_and_then_that_launch_fetches(self):
        text = " ".join(self.readme("windows-x86_64").split())
        self.assertNotIn("Starting and serving never install or download anything", text)
        self.assertIn("Serving and watching", text)
        self.assertIn("Only two commands fetch files", text)
        self.assertIn("`strata launch`", text)

    def test_the_launch_doc_it_points_at_is_in_the_archive(self):
        self.assertIn("docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md", self.readme("linux-x86_64"))
        self.assertIn("docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md", package_terminal.PAYLOAD)
        self.assertTrue((ROOT / "docs" / "TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md").is_file())

    def test_free_memory_guidance_fits_the_system(self):
        win, lin, mac = (self.readme(t) for t in ("windows-x86_64", "linux-x86_64", "darwin-arm64"))
        self.assertNotIn("free -g", win)
        self.assertIn("FreePhysicalMemory", win)
        self.assertIn("Task Manager", win)
        self.assertIn("free -g", lin)
        self.assertNotIn("free -g", mac)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/terminal/test_tuiqa_wizard.py

"""Tester report T05, T09, T11 and the smaller wizard items, with Textual's pilot at 120x40, 80x24, 60x20 and 40x15: the Folder step knows an installed

class Base(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.home = Home().__enter__()
        self.addCleanup(self.home.__exit__, None, None, None)
        FakeRunner.instances.clear()
        FakeRunner.behaviour = "ok"
        FakeRunner.download = 0.0
        p = mock.patch("strata_cli.launch.app.Runner", FakeRunner)
        p.start()
        self.addCleanup(p.stop)

    def run_app(self, coro, ctx=None, size=(120, 40)):

class SaveChoices(Base):
    def test_the_three_choices_and_the_name_are_on_screen_at_every_size(self):
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 7, "n", "enter")
            for size in SIZES:
                await pilot.resize_terminal(*size)
                await pilot.pause(0.3)
                shown = text_of(app)
                for choice in ("Save as a preset and launch", "Launch without saving", "Save the preset and stop here"):
                    self.assertIn(choice, shown, (size, shown))
                body = app.screen.query_one("#body")
                menu = app.screen.menu()
                self.assertLessEqual(menu.region.bottom, body.region.bottom, size)               # the choices are inside the body, not below it
                self.assertGreaterEqual(menu.region.y, body.region.y, size)
                name = app.screen.query_one("#name")
                self.assertLessEqual(name.region.bottom, body.region.bottom, size)
                self.assertIn("Enter:", flat(app), size)                                           # the footer says which action Enter does
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_the_footer_names_the_action_enter_will_do(self):
        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 7, "n", "enter")
            self.assertIn("Enter: Save as a preset and launch", flat(app))
            await press(pilot, "down")
            self.assertIn("Enter: Launch without saving", flat(app))
            await press(pilot, "down")
            self.assertIn("Enter: Save the preset and stop here", flat(app))
        self.run_app(case)

    def test_the_full_layout_is_kept_when_it_fits(self):

            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 7, "n", "enter")
            shown = text_of(app)
            for part in ("Save as preset, then launch", "Context", "Pictures", "Parallel", "Tuning", "Access", "Storage"):
                self.assertIn(part, shown)
        self.run_app(case)


class AdvancedLayout(Base):
    HELP = "  --prefill N          prompt chunk size (default 2048)\n  --kv fp16|int8       KV storage\n"

    def ctx_with_engine(self, **choices):
        ctx = make_ctx()
        ctx.settings.family, ctx.settings.model = "qwen", "IQ3_XXS"
        for k, v in choices.items():
            setattr(ctx.settings, k, v)
        base = {"exe": "component:strata-engine", "vision": {"mmproj": "/x/mmproj.gguf", "gpu": False},
                "args": ["--native", "/very/long/path/to/the/models/folder/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Something-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf",
                         "--pack", "/very/long/path/to/the/data/packs/iq3_xxs", "--max-context", "131072", "--kv", "int8", "--prefill", "auto",
                         "--vision"]}
        for p in (mock.patch.object(Ctx, "base_config", lambda self: base), mock.patch.object(Ctx, "engine_exe", lambda self: "/engine/strata"),
                  mock.patch("strata_cli.launch.params.engine_help_text", return_value=self.HELP)):
            p.start()
            self.addCleanup(p.stop)
        return ctx

    def test_the_command_follows_the_wizard_choices(self):
        ctx = self.ctx_with_engine(context=102400, kv="q4_0", vision="off")
        cmd = ctx.command_text()
        self.assertIn("--max-context 102400", cmd)
        self.assertIn("--kv q4_0", cmd)
        self.assertNotIn("--vision", cmd)
        self.assertNotIn("131072", cmd)
        ctx2 = self.ctx_with_engine(context=65536, kv="int8", vision="cpu")
        cmd2 = ctx2.command_text()
        self.assertIn("--max-context 65536", cmd2)
        self.assertIn("--vision", cmd2)
        # and the "Same as" line agrees with it
        self.assertIn("--context 100k", S.flags_text(ctx.settings))
        self.assertIn("--kv q4_0", S.flags_text(ctx.settings))
        self.assertIn("--vision off", S.flags_text(ctx.settings))

    def test_the_preview_is_inside_its_own_scroll_area_at_every_size_and_the_next_key_is_visible(self):
        ctx = self.ctx_with_engine(context=102400, kv="q4_0", vision="off")

        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 7)
            self.assertEqual(app.current, "advanced")
            for size in SIZES:
                await pilot.resize_terminal(*size)
                await pilot.pause(0.3)
                body = app.screen.query_one("#body")
                box = app.screen.query_one("#cmdbox")
                self.assertGreaterEqual(box.region.y, body.region.y, size)
                self.assertLessEqual(box.region.bottom, body.region.bottom, size)                # the preview never leaves the body
                self.assertGreaterEqual(box.region.height, 3, size)
                self.assertIn("n next", flat(app), size)                                           # the key hints wrap instead of being cut off
                self.assertIn("Command that will run", text_of(app), size)
        self.run_app(case, ctx)

    def test_tab_scrolls_the_preview_and_esc_comes_back(self):
        ctx = self.ctx_with_engine(context=102400, kv="q4_0", vision="off")

        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 7)
            await pilot.resize_terminal(60, 20)
            await pilot.pause(0.3)
            await press(pilot, "tab")
            self.assertTrue(app.screen.query_one("#cmdbox").has_focus)
            await press(pilot, "down", "down")
            await press(pilot, "escape")
            self.assertFalse(app.screen.query_one("#cmdbox").has_focus)
            self.assertEqual(app.current, "advanced")                      # Esc only gave the focus back; it did not leave the step
            await press(pilot, "n")
            self.assertEqual(app.current, "access")
        self.run_app(case, ctx)

    def test_descriptions_use_plain_words(self):
        text = "  --expert-cache N   R4: experts held in VRAM (default auto)\n  --mystery N   R7 internal thing T2\n"
        rows = {p.name: p for p in P.parse_help(text)}
        self.assertNotIn("R4", rows["--expert-cache"].short)
        self.assertIn("graphics memory", rows["--expert-cache"].short)
        self.assertNotRegex(rows["--mystery"].short, r"\bR\d|\bT\d")

class InstalledModelFolder(Base):
    """The GUI's installation: weights, pack, picture reader there; the draft layer gone."""

    def build(self):
        base = Path(os.environ["LOCALAPPDATA"]).parent / "gui"
        docs = base / "Documents" / "Strata"
        gguf = docs / "Models" / "qwen-IQ3_XXS" / "Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf"
        gguf.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        gguf.write_bytes(b"x")
        pack = docs / "packs" / "iq3_xxs"
        pack.mkdir(parents=True)
        mm = docs / "Models" / "mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf"
        mm.write_bytes(b"x")
        install = Path(os.environ["STRATA_INSTALL_DIR"])
        install.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cfg = {"exe": "component:strata-engine", "tokenizer": str(pack), "args": ["--pack", str(pack), "--native", str(gguf), "--mtp", str(docs / "mtp" / "rt"),
                                                                                 "--max-context", "32768", "--kv", "int8"],
               "vision": {"mmproj": str(mm), "gpu": False}}
        (install / "strata-iq3_xxs.json").write_text(json.dumps(cfg))
        return docs

    def test_the_folder_starts_where_the_model_is_and_says_what_is_missing(self):
        docs = self.build()
        ctx = make_ctx()
        ctx.settings.family, ctx.settings.model, ctx.settings.vision = "qwen", "IQ3_XXS", "cpu"

        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, "enter", "up", "enter")                 # Start -> Model (up: IQ3_XXS, the 64 GB tier pre-selects IQ3_S) -> Folder
            self.assertEqual(app.current, "folder")
            field = app.screen.query_one("#folderpath")
            self.assertEqual(Path(field.value).resolve(), docs.resolve())
            shown = flat(app)
            self.assertIn("The model is already downloaded", shown)
            self.assertIn("Only the draft layer is missing (5.2 GB)", shown)
            self.assertNotIn("Needs about", shown)
            self.assertNotIn("download the model", shown.lower())
        self.run_app(case, ctx)

    def test_everything_there_says_already_downloaded(self):
        docs = self.build()
        (docs / "mtp" / "rt").mkdir(parents=True)
        (docs / "mtp" / "rt" / "experts.bin").write_bytes(b"x")
        ctx = make_ctx()
        ctx.settings.family, ctx.settings.model, ctx.settings.vision = "qwen", "IQ3_XXS", "cpu"

        async def case(app, pilot, ctx):
            await press(pilot, "enter", "up", "enter")                 # up: IQ3_XXS (IQ3_S is pre-selected)
            shown = flat(app)
            self.assertIn("Already downloaded", shown)
            self.assertIn("Nothing more to download", shown)
            # and the final screen does not warn about a download
            await press(pilot, *("enter",) * 5, "n", "enter")
            self.assertIn("Nothing needs to be downloaded", flat(app))
        self.run_app(case, ctx)

## tests/terminal/test_update_feed.py

"""The signed feed and its checks: a bad signature, a bad hash and a downgrade are all refused, and the choice of engine package
follows the hardware. No network and no engine here (the end-to-end flow is test_updater.py)."""

import base64
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from strata_control import feed as feedmod, signing, transfer
from tests.terminal import update_fixture as fx

SEED1 = bytes.fromhex("9d61b19deffd5a60ba844af492ec2cc44449c5697b326919703bac031cae7f60")
PUB1 = bytes.fromhex("d75a980182b10ab7d54bfed3c964073a0ee172f3daa62325af021a68f707511a")
SIG1 = bytes.fromhex("e5564300c360ac729086e2cc806e828a84877f1eb8e5d974d873e065224901555fb8821590a33bacc61e39701cf9b46bd25bf5f0595bbe24655141438e7a100b")
SEED2 = bytes.fromhex("4ccd089b28ff96da9db6c346ec114e0f5b8a319f35aba624da8cf6ed4fb8a6fb")
PUB2 = bytes.fromhex("3d4017c3e843895a92b70aa74d1b7ebc9c982ccf2ec4968cc0cd55f12af4660c")
SIG2 = bytes.fromhex("92a009a9f0d4cab8720e820b5f642540a2b27b5416503f8fb3762223ebdb69da085ac1e43e15996e458f3613d0f11d8c387b2eaeb4302aeeb00d291612bb0c00")


class Ed25519(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_rfc8032_vectors(self):
        self.assertEqual(signing.public_from_seed(SEED1), PUB1)
        self.assertEqual(signing.sign_raw(SEED1, b""), SIG1)
        self.assertTrue(signing.verify_raw(PUB1, b"", SIG1))
        self.assertEqual(signing.public_from_seed(SEED2), PUB2)
        self.assertEqual(signing.sign_raw(SEED2, b"\x72"), SIG2)
        self.assertTrue(signing.verify_raw(PUB2, b"\x72", SIG2))

    def test_tampering_is_refused(self):
        self.assertFalse(signing.verify_raw(PUB2, b"\x73", SIG2))
        self.assertFalse(signing.verify_raw(PUB1, b"\x72", SIG2))
        bad = bytearray(SIG2)
        bad[10] ^= 1
        self.assertFalse(signing.verify_raw(PUB2, b"\x72", bytes(bad)))
        self.assertFalse(signing.verify_raw(PUB2, b"\x72", SIG2[:63]))
        high_s = SIG2[:32] + (int.from_bytes(SIG2[32:], "little") + signing._L).to_bytes(32, "little")
        self.assertFalse(signing.verify_raw(PUB2, b"\x72", high_s), "a non-canonical s must be refused")

    def test_documents_and_key_ids(self):
        key = signing.generate_key()
        trusted = fx.trusted_of(key)
        signature = signing.sign_bytes(key, b"hello")
        self.assertEqual(signing.verify_bytes(trusted, b"hello", signature), key["key_id"])
        with self.assertRaises(signing.SignatureError):
            signing.verify_bytes(trusted, b"hellO", signature)
        other = signing.generate_key()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(signing.SignatureError, "does not trust"):
            signing.verify_bytes(fx.trusted_of(other), b"hello", signature)
        entry = signing.public_part(key)
        entry["key_id"] = "0" * 16
        with self.assertRaises(signing.SignatureError):
            signing.parse_public(entry)

    def test_minisign_app_signature(self):
        public, secret = fx.minisign_pair()
        blob = os.urandom(5000)
        sig = fx.minisign_sign(blob, secret)
        signing.minisign_verify(public, sig, [blob[:1000], blob[1000:]])
        with self.assertRaises(signing.SignatureError):
            signing.minisign_verify(public, sig, [blob + b"x"])
        other_public, _ = fx.minisign_pair()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(signing.SignatureError, "different key"):
            signing.minisign_verify(other_public, sig, [blob])
        text = base64.b64decode(sig).decode().replace("timestamp:1", "timestamp:2")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(signing.SignatureError, "comment was changed"):
            signing.minisign_verify(public, base64.b64encode(text.encode()).decode(), [blob])


def entry(version="0.1.46", backend="cuda", variant="cuda13", archs=("sm_86", "compute_89"), driver="580.65", **extra):
    base = {"version": version, "platform": "linux-x86_64", "backend": backend, "variant": variant, "archs": list(archs),
            "min_driver": {"nvidia": driver} if backend == "cuda" else {}, "min_runtime": None, "build_id": f"b-{version}-{variant}",
            "format": "tar.gz", "url": f"engine/e-{version}-{variant}.tar.gz", "size": 1000, "sha256": "a" * 64,
            "manifest_sha256": "b" * 64, "installed_bytes": 2000, "notes": ""}
    base.update(extra)
    return base


def document(**over):
    doc = {"schema_version": 1, "feed": "strata-updates", "channel": "stable", "sequence": 5,
           "generated_at": "2026-10-15T00:00:00Z", "expires_at": None, "engine": {"packages": [entry()]}}
    doc.update(over)
    return doc


def signed(doc, key):
    payload = (json.dumps(doc, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode()
    return payload, json.dumps(signing.sign_bytes(key, payload)).encode()


class FeedChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.key = signing.generate_key()
        self.trusted = fx.trusted_of(self.key)

    def load(self, payload, sig, **guards):
        return feedmod.verify_and_parse(payload, sig, source="/feeds/strata-feed.json", trusted=self.trusted, **guards)

    def test_a_good_feed_loads(self):
        feed = self.load(*signed(document(), self.key))
        self.assertEqual((feed.sequence, feed.channel, feed.key_id), (5, "stable", self.key["key_id"]))
        self.assertEqual(feed.engine[0].label, "0.1.46 linux-x86_64-cuda-cuda13")

    def test_a_bad_signature_is_refused(self):
        payload, sig = signed(document(), self.key)
        forged = json.loads(sig)
        raw = bytearray(base64.b64decode(forged["value"]))
        raw[3] ^= 0x40
        forged["value"] = base64.b64encode(bytes(raw)).decode()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "not trusted"):
            self.load(payload, json.dumps(forged).encode())

    def test_a_feed_changed_after_signing_is_refused(self):
        payload, sig = signed(document(), self.key)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "does not match the signed content"):
            self.load(payload.replace(b'"sequence": 5', b'"sequence": 6'), sig)

    def test_a_feed_signed_by_an_unknown_key_is_refused(self):
        payload, sig = signed(document(), signing.generate_key())
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "does not trust"):
            self.load(payload, sig)

    def test_no_trusted_keys_means_no_update(self):
        payload, sig = signed(document(), self.key)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "trusts no update key"):
            feedmod.verify_and_parse(payload, sig, source="x/strata-feed.json", trusted={})

    def test_an_older_feed_is_a_downgrade(self):
        payload, sig = signed(document(sequence=4), self.key)
        with self.assertRaises(feedmod.FeedDowngrade):
            self.load(payload, sig, last_sequence=5)
        self.assertEqual(self.load(*signed(document(sequence=5), self.key), last_sequence=5).sequence, 5)
        self.assertEqual(self.load(*signed(document(sequence=9), self.key), last_sequence=5).sequence, 9)

    def test_an_expired_feed_and_another_channel_are_refused(self):
        payload, sig = signed(document(expires_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"), self.key)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "expired"):
            self.load(payload, sig, now=dt.datetime(2026, 10, 15, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "channel"):
            self.load(*signed(document(channel="beta"), self.key), channel="stable")

    def test_malformed_entries_are_errors_not_defaults(self):
        for change in ({"sha256": "nothex"}, {"size": 0}, {"format": "rar"}, {"platform": "plan9"}, {"backend": "tpu"},
                       {"version": "latest"}, {"archs": []}, {"manifest_sha256": None}, {"size": True}):
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                with self.assertRaises(feedmod.FeedError):
                    self.load(*signed(document(engine={"packages": [entry(**change)]}), self.key))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(feedmod.FeedError, "twice"):
            self.load(*signed(document(engine={"packages": [entry(), entry()]}), self.key))
        with self.assertRaises(feedmod.FeedError):
            self.load(b"not json", signed(document(), self.key)[1])

    def test_versions_are_strict_and_ordered(self):
        self.assertLess(feedmod.version_key("0.1.9"), feedmod.version_key("0.1.10"))
        self.assertLess(feedmod.version_key("0.1.45"), feedmod.version_key("0.1.45.1"))
        with self.assertRaises(feedmod.FeedError):
            feedmod.version_key("0.1.x")


class Selection(unittest.TestCase):
    HW = {"platform": "linux-x86_64", "backend": "cuda", "runtime": "0.1.45", "nvidia_driver": "615.71", "cuda_archs": ["sm_86"], "gfx": []}

    def pick(self, packages, **hw):
        parsed = [feedmod._engine_package(p) for p in packages]
        return feedmod.select_engine(parsed, {**self.HW, **hw})

    def test_cuda_13_when_the_driver_is_new_enough_else_12(self):
        both = [entry(variant="cuda12", driver="575.51", archs=("sm_60", "sm_86", "compute_89")), entry(variant="cuda13")]
        self.assertEqual(self.pick(both)[0].variant, "cuda13")
        old = self.pick(both, nvidia_driver="576.02")
        self.assertEqual(old[0].variant, "cuda12")
        self.assertTrue(any("580.65" in r for r in old[1]))
        self.assertIsNone(self.pick(both, nvidia_driver="500.00")[0])

    def test_the_newest_version_wins_and_the_card_must_be_covered(self):
        newer = [entry("0.1.45"), entry("0.1.46")]
        self.assertEqual(self.pick(newer)[0].version, "0.1.46")
        pascal = self.pick([entry(archs=("sm_75", "sm_86", "compute_86"))], cuda_archs=["sm_61"])
        self.assertIsNone(pascal[0])
        self.assertIn("this PC's GPU is sm_61", pascal[1][0])
        self.assertIsNotNone(self.pick([entry(archs=("sm_75", "compute_75"))], cuda_archs=["sm_120"])[0], "PTX covers a newer card")

    def test_hip_by_gfx_sycl_and_metal_by_platform(self):
        hip = [entry(backend="hip", variant="", archs=("gfx1200", "gfx1201"))]
        self.assertIsNotNone(self.pick(hip, backend="hip", gfx=["gfx1201"])[0])
        self.assertIsNone(self.pick(hip, backend="hip", gfx=["gfx1100"])[0])
        self.assertIsNotNone(self.pick(hip, backend="hip", gfx=[])[0], "an unreadable gfx is not a refusal")
        self.assertIsNone(self.pick(hip, backend="cuda")[0], "a HIP package is not offered to an NVIDIA PC")
        sycl = [entry(backend="sycl", variant="", archs=("intel-arc",))]
        self.assertIsNotNone(self.pick(sycl, backend="sycl")[0])
        metal = dict(entry(backend="metal", variant="", archs=("apple-gpu",)), platform="macos-arm64")
        self.assertIsNone(self.pick([metal])[0], "wrong platform")
        self.assertIsNotNone(self.pick([metal], platform="macos-arm64", backend="metal")[0])

    def test_min_runtime(self):
        got = self.pick([entry(min_runtime="0.1.50")])
        self.assertIsNone(got[0])
        self.assertIn("needs control 0.1.50", got[1][0])


class References(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_references_stay_inside_the_feed(self):
        base = "http://127.0.0.1:9/feed/"
        self.assertEqual(transfer.resolve_ref(base, "engine/a.tar.gz"), "http://127.0.0.1:9/feed/engine/a.tar.gz")
