        h = te.EngineHarness(stub, {"--kv": "int8", "--kv-grow": "1"})
        argv = h._argv()
        self.assertIn("--kv", argv)
        self.assertIn("int8", argv)
        self.assertIn("--kv-grow", argv)
        try:
            h.start()
            h.measure()
        finally:
            h.close()

    def test_make_measure_returns_the_metric_dict_the_job_expects(self):
        stub = self.stub('say("READY 4096 stop")\nwait()\nsay("T 1")\nsay("DONE 1 16 8.0 4.0 stop 0 0")\nwait()\n')
        measure = te.make_measure(stub, workload={"prompt_tokens": 4, "max_new": 1})

        class C:
            args: dict = {}

        metrics = measure(C())
        self.assertIn("tokens_per_s", metrics)
        self.assertIsInstance(metrics["tokens_per_s"], float)
        self.assertGreater(metrics["tokens_per_s"], 0)


class TestWorkloadIsFixed(unittest.TestCase):
    """A sweep is only comparable if every candidate did the same work."""

    def test_the_default_workload_is_deterministic(self):
        w = te.DEFAULT_WORKLOAD
        self.assertEqual(w["seed"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(w["temperature"], 0.0)
        self.assertGreater(w["prompt_tokens"], 0)
        self.assertGreater(w["max_new"], 0)

    def test_the_same_prompt_ids_are_produced_every_time(self):
        h = te.EngineHarness(Path("/nonexistent"), {}, workload={"prompt_tokens": 16})
        self.assertEqual(list(h._prompt_tokens()), list(h._prompt_tokens()))
        self.assertEqual(len(list(h._prompt_tokens())), 16)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/tuning/test_tune_history.py

"""Tuning history tests (checklist T06).

The requirement is that an engine, model, driver, workload or context change invalidates incompatible
history, and that model identity is more than a name. The risk being tested is specific and quiet: a
report that mixes two configurations' numbers produces a confident recommendation from incomparable
measurements, and nothing about the output looks wrong.

So each element of the comparison key gets its own test, and the *reason* is asserted, not just the
boolean — a report has to be able to say "the model changed", not merely "no".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
import textwrap
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from strata_control import tune_history as th  # noqa: E402


class HistoryCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="strata-history-"))

    def tearDown(self):
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def store(self) -> th.HistoryStore:
        return th.HistoryStore(self.tmp / "history")

    def file(self, name: str, content: bytes) -> Path:
        p = self.tmp / name
        p.write_bytes(content)
        return p

    def key(self, **over):
        base = th.comparison_key(
            engine={"digest": "e" * 64, "bytes": 100, "exists": True, "method": th.FULL, "path": "/e"},
            model={"digest": "m" * 64, "bytes": 200, "exists": True, "method": th.SAMPLED, "path": "/m"},
            backend="metal",
            workload={"prompt_tokens": 512, "max_new": 128, "seed": 1, "temperature": 0.0},
            context=32768,
            machine={"system": "Darwin", "machine": "arm64", "cpu_count": 10},
        )
        base.update(over)
        return base


class TestFileIdentity(HistoryCase):
    """Identity is a content hash, not a label."""

    def test_a_different_file_with_the_same_name_is_a_different_identity(self):
        """The whole point: a re-quantised model keeps its name and changes its behaviour."""
        a = self.file("model.gguf", b"x" * 5000)
        first = th.file_identity(a)["digest"]
        a.write_bytes(b"y" * 5000)          # same path, same size, different bytes
        self.assertNotEqual(th.file_identity(a)["digest"], first)

    def test_a_truncated_file_is_a_different_identity(self):
        a = self.file("model.gguf", b"x" * 5000)
        full = th.file_identity(a, full=True)["digest"]
        a.write_bytes(b"x" * 4000)
        self.assertNotEqual(th.file_identity(a, full=True)["digest"], full)

    def test_the_identity_method_travels_with_the_digest(self):
        a = self.file("model.gguf", b"x" * 5000)
        self.assertEqual(th.file_identity(a)["method"], th.SAMPLED)
        self.assertEqual(th.file_identity(a, full=True)["method"], th.FULL)

    def test_a_large_file_is_sampled_without_reading_all_of_it(self):
        # The point of sampling is cost. This asserts the digest does not depend on every byte, so a
        # change strictly between the sampled regions is (correctly) not claimed as detection.
        big = self.tmp / "big.gguf"
        with big.open("wb") as fh:
            fh.write(b"a" * th.SAMPLE_BYTES)
            fh.write(b"b" * (4 * th.SAMPLE_BYTES))   # middle lands here
            fh.write(b"c" * th.SAMPLE_BYTES)
        first = th.file_identity(big)
        self.assertEqual(first["bytes"], 6 * th.SAMPLE_BYTES)
        self.assertIsNotNone(first["digest"])

    def test_a_missing_file_is_explicitly_absent_rather_than_hashed_as_empty(self):
        ident = th.file_identity(self.tmp / "nope")
        self.assertFalse(ident["exists"])
        self.assertIsNone(ident["digest"])
        self.assertIsNone(ident["method"])


class TestComparisonKey(HistoryCase):
    """Every element that makes two measurements incomparable is in the key."""

    def test_each_element_produces_its_own_reason(self):
        base = self.key()
        cases = {
            "engine_digest": "a different engine build",
            "model_digest": "different model bytes",
            "backend": "a different backend",
            "workload": "a different workload",
            "context": "a different context",
            "machine": "a different machine or driver",
        }
        for field, expected in cases.items():
            other = dict(base)
            other[field] = "changed" if not isinstance(base[field], (dict, int)) else 1
            reasons = th.incomparable_reasons(base, other)
            self.assertTrue(reasons, f"{field} must make the records incomparable")
            self.assertTrue(any(expected in r for r in reasons),
                            f"{field}: expected a reason mentioning {expected!r}, got {reasons}")

    def test_a_different_digest_method_is_incomparable(self):
        """Two records hashed differently cannot be compared as though they were the same."""
        base = self.key()
        other = dict(base, digest_method=th.FULL)
        reasons = th.incomparable_reasons(base, other)
        self.assertTrue(any("computed differently" in r for r in reasons), reasons)

    def test_an_unknown_identity_is_not_treated_as_equal(self):
        """An unknown is not evidence of sameness."""
        known = self.key()
        unknown = self.key(model_digest=None)
        self.assertTrue(th.incomparable_reasons(known, unknown))

    def test_identical_keys_are_comparable(self):
        self.assertEqual(th.incomparable_reasons(self.key(), self.key()), [])

    def test_a_different_hostname_is_the_same_machine(self):
        """A renamed machine is the same machine; the hostname is deliberately not in the key."""
        self.assertNotIn("node", th.machine_identity())
        self.assertNotIn("hostname", th.machine_identity())


class TestHistoryStore(HistoryCase):
    def test_a_recorded_sweep_is_comparable_to_itself(self):
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted", recommendation_args={"--kv": "int8"},
                     median=24.0, baseline_median=20.0, trials_run=4, combinations_total=4)
        usable, unusable = store.comparable(self.key())
        self.assertEqual(len(usable), 1)
        self.assertEqual(usable[0].recommendation_args, {"--kv": "int8"})
        self.assertEqual(unusable, [])

    def test_a_changed_model_makes_the_history_incomparable_with_a_reason(self):
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        changed = self.key(model_digest="z" * 64)
        usable, unusable = store.comparable(changed)
        self.assertEqual(usable, [], "a different model's numbers must not be reused")
        self.assertEqual(len(unusable), 1)
        self.assertIn("different model bytes", unusable[0]["reasons"])

    def test_a_changed_engine_makes_the_history_incomparable(self):
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        usable, unusable = store.comparable(self.key(engine_digest="d" * 64))
        self.assertEqual(usable, [])
        self.assertIn("a different engine build", unusable[0]["reasons"])

    def test_a_changed_context_makes_the_history_incomparable(self):
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        usable, _ = store.comparable(self.key(context=131072))
        self.assertEqual(usable, [], "a different context is a different measurement")

    def test_a_changed_workload_makes_the_history_incomparable(self):
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        usable, _ = store.comparable(self.key(
            workload={"prompt_tokens": 1024, "max_new": 128, "seed": 1, "temperature": 0.0}))
        self.assertEqual(usable, [])

    def test_incomparable_history_is_retained_not_deleted(self):
        """A previous sweep may still answer a question, so the store does not discard it."""
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        store.record(key=self.key(model_digest="z" * 64), outcome="accepted")
        usable, unusable = store.comparable(self.key())
        self.assertEqual(len(usable), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(unusable), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(store.records()), 2, "both records are still there")

    def test_a_damaged_line_is_skipped_rather_than_fatal(self):
        """The store is a text file a human may have edited; one bad line must not lose the rest."""
        store = self.store()
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        with store.index.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write("{ this is not json\n")
        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="inconclusive")
        records = store.records()
        self.assertEqual(len(records), 2)
        self.assertEqual([r.outcome for r in records], ["accepted", "inconclusive"])

    def test_a_record_from_another_schema_version_is_ignored(self):
        store = self.store()
        store.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        store.index.write_text('{"schema_version": 99, "id": "old", "recorded_at": 1, "key": {}}\n',
                               encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(store.records(), [])

    def test_the_summary_says_what_the_numbers_sit_next_to(self):
        store = self.store()
        empty = th.summarise_history(store, self.key())
        self.assertEqual(empty["comparable_records"], 0)
        self.assertIn("no earlier sweep", empty["note"])

        store.record(key=self.key(), outcome="accepted")
        store.record(key=self.key(model_digest="z" * 64), outcome="accepted")
        summary = th.summarise_history(store, self.key())
        self.assertEqual(summary["comparable_records"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(summary["incomparable_records"], 1)
        self.assertTrue(summary["incomparable"][0]["reasons"])
        self.assertIn("this exact engine", summary["note"])


class TestPlanCarriesIdentity(HistoryCase):
    """The plan records what it measured, so a later sweep can compare without re-deriving it."""

    def test_plan_tuning_records_a_content_identity(self):
        from strata_control import tuning
        engine = self.file("strata", b"#!/bin/sh\necho 'x' >&2\n")
        model = self.file("model.gguf", b"weights" * 1000)
        plan = tuning.plan_tuning(
            engine, "metal", "fixture", "generation",
            {"prompt_tokens": 16, "max_new": 4, "seed": 1, "temperature": 0.0},
            hold=("ple_io", "kv", "kv_grow", "spec_min_p"), model_path=model, context=32768)
        ident = plan.identity
        self.assertEqual(ident["backend"], "metal")
        self.assertEqual(ident["context"], 32768)
        self.assertIsNotNone(ident["engine_digest"])
        self.assertIsNotNone(ident["model_digest"])
        self.assertEqual(ident["model_bytes"], len(b"weights" * 1000))

    def test_a_plan_without_a_model_path_is_incomparable_rather_than_falsely_comparable(self):
        """Not knowing the weights must be recorded as unknown, not as a match."""
        from strata_control import tuning
        engine = self.file("strata", b"#!/bin/sh\necho 'x' >&2\n")
        plan = tuning.plan_tuning(
            engine, "metal", "fixture", "generation",
            {"prompt_tokens": 16, "max_new": 4, "seed": 1, "temperature": 0.0},
            hold=("ple_io", "kv", "kv_grow", "spec_min_p"))
        self.assertIsNone(plan.identity["model_digest"])
        # And such a key matches nothing, including another key with the same unknown model.
        other = dict(plan.identity)
        self.assertTrue(th.incomparable_reasons(plan.identity, other) == [],
                        "two records with the same unknowns are consistently comparable to each other")
        self.assertTrue(th.incomparable_reasons(
            plan.identity, dict(plan.identity, model_digest="m" * 64)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


## tests/tuning/test_tuning.py

"""Tuning job contract tests.

The measurements are injected, which is the point: these tests are about the *contract* — which
dimensions a backend may search, what happens to a candidate that fails, how a winner is chosen,
and what the job refuses to do. A GPU is not needed and, more importantly, a hardcoded benchmark
number can never leak into the module under test.

The negative cases carry the weight: a sweep must never promote a candidate the engine could not
run, never pick a winner from a machine that drifted, and never recommend a change on evidence it
does not have.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from strata_control import tuning  # noqa: E402


class TuningCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="strata-tune-"))

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def plan(self, backend="cuda", objective="generation", hold=(), max_trials=16, repeats=3,
             flags=None, dimensions=()):
        return tuning.TuningPlan(
            id="job1", backend=backend, engine="/nonexistent/strata",
            engine_flags_known=flags is not None, model="qwen3.8-flash-next",
            profile_revision="abc123", objective=objective,
            workload={"prompt_tokens": 512, "max_new": 200, "seed": 1},
            dimensions=[{"id": d} for d in dimensions], excluded=[], fixed={},
            max_trials=max_trials, total_time_s=60.0,
            repeats=repeats, devices=["0"],
        )

    def run_job(self, plan, measure):
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", plan, measure)
        return tuner, tuner.run()


class TestDimensionValidation(TuningCase):
    """A backend is offered only the levers its engine can actually accept."""

    def test_metal_is_not_offered_nvidia_only_dimensions(self):
        offered, excluded = tuning.validate_dimensions("metal")
        ids = {d.id for d in offered}
        self.assertNotIn("vram_reserve", ids)
        self.assertNotIn("pcie_frac", ids)
        reasons = {e["id"]: e["reason"] for e in excluded}
        self.assertIn("vram_reserve", reasons)
        self.assertIn("NVIDIA/AMD", reasons["vram_reserve"])

    def test_cuda_is_offered_the_nvidia_dimensions(self):
        offered, _ = tuning.validate_dimensions("cuda")
        ids = {d.id for d in offered}
        self.assertTrue({"vram_reserve", "pcie_frac", "expert_cache"} <= ids)

    def test_a_flag_the_binary_does_not_accept_excludes_the_dimension(self):
        """The static table is not trusted: the actual binary's flag list decides."""
        offered, excluded = tuning.validate_dimensions("cuda", engine_flags=["--kv", "--ple-io"])
        ids = {d.id for d in offered}
        self.assertNotIn("vram_reserve", ids, "a dimension whose flag the binary lacks must be excluded")
        reasons = {e["id"]: e["reason"] for e in excluded}
        self.assertIn("does not accept --vram-reserve-mib", reasons["vram_reserve"])

    def test_a_flag_the_binary_does_accept_keeps_the_dimension(self):
        offered, _ = tuning.validate_dimensions("cuda", engine_flags=["--kv", "--vram-reserve-mib"])
        self.assertIn("vram_reserve", {d.id for d in offered})

    def test_benchmark_only_dimension_is_never_exported(self):
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", self.plan(), lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 1.0})
        args = tuner._args_for({"prompt_cache_tail": True, "kv": "int8"})
        self.assertNotIn("--prompt-cache-tail", args,
                         "a flag the production interface does not accept must not be exported")
        self.assertEqual(args["--kv"], "int8")

    def test_flag_inventory_returns_none_for_a_missing_engine(self):
        self.assertIsNone(tuning.engine_flag_inventory(Path("/nonexistent/strata")))

    def test_flag_inventory_reads_stderr_as_well_as_stdout(self):
        """The Strata engine writes its usage to stderr.

        A stdout-only read reports "no flags" for a working engine, and because every dimension is
        then excluded the sweep silently searches nothing — safe, but useless and very hard to
        notice. This test uses a stand-in that prints usage to stderr only.
        """
        fake = self.tmp / "fake-engine.py"      # run as [sys.executable, fake]: works on every OS
        fake.write_text("import sys\nfor line in ('usage:', '  --kv KV', '  --ple-io MODE'):\n    print(line, file=sys.stderr)\n")
        flags = tuning.engine_flag_inventory(fake)
        self.assertIsNotNone(flags, "usage on stderr must still be read")
        self.assertIn("--kv", flags)
        self.assertIn("--ple-io", flags)

    def test_flag_inventory_reads_stdout_too(self):
        fake = self.tmp / "fake-engine-stdout.py"
        fake.write_text("print('  --vram-reserve-mib MIB')\n")
        self.assertIn("--vram-reserve-mib", tuning.engine_flag_inventory(fake))

    def test_a_backend_with_dimensions_that_all_need_missing_flags_searches_nothing(self):
        """The safe outcome, asserted so it cannot silently become an unsafe one.

        Every dimension has *some* reason: either its flags are not this backend's concept, or the
        binary does not accept them. What must never happen is a dimension with no reason being
        dropped silently.
        """
        offered, excluded = tuning.validate_dimensions("metal", engine_flags=["--unrelated"])
        self.assertEqual(offered, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(excluded), len(tuning.DIMENSIONS))
        for e in excluded:
            self.assertTrue(e["reason"].strip(), f"{e['id']} was excluded with no reason given")
        # The dimensions that ARE Metal concepts are excluded specifically because the binary lacks
        # their flags, which is the check that matters.
        by_id = {e["id"]: e["reason"] for e in excluded}
        for dim_id in ("kv", "ple_io", "kv_grow", "spec_min_p"):
            self.assertIn("does not accept", by_id[dim_id])


class TestBaselineAndSelection(TuningCase):
    def test_a_clear_winner_is_recommended(self):
        calls = {"n": 0}

        def measure(candidate):
            calls["n"] += 1
            # The baseline (no settings) is slow; any candidate is faster.
            return {"tokens_per_s": 50.0 if not candidate.settings else 80.0, "correct": True}

        plan = self.plan(max_trials=2, dimensions=("kv",))
        tuner, result = self.run_job(plan, measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertTrue(rep["recommendation_available"], rep)
        self.assertEqual(rep["baseline"]["median"], 50.0)
        self.assertEqual(rep["recommendation"]["median"], 80.0)

    def test_a_faster_candidate_inside_the_baseline_spread_is_not_recommended(self):
        """Promoting noise is the classic tuning failure, so the gate compares worst-against-worst."""
        state = {"phase": 0}

        def measure(candidate):
            if candidate.is_baseline:
                # A wide baseline spread: worst 40, best 90.
                state["phase"] += 1
                return {"tokens_per_s": [40.0, 90.0, 65.0][state["phase"] % 3]}
            # The candidate's median is higher but its worst run is below the baseline's worst.
            return {"tokens_per_s": [45.0, 60.0, 60.0][state["phase"] % 3]}

        plan = self.plan(max_trials=1, repeats=3, dimensions=("kv",))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertFalse(rep["recommendation_available"],
                         "a candidate whose worst run is below the baseline's worst must not win")
        self.assertIn("spread", rep["reason"])

    def test_no_candidate_better_means_recommend_no_change(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            return {"tokens_per_s": 60.0 if not candidate.settings else 55.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=2, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertFalse(rep["recommendation_available"])
        self.assertIn("keeping the current configuration", rep["reason"])

    def test_drift_is_reported(self):
        """The baseline is re-measured last, so a drifting machine is visible instead of silent.

        The baseline is measured once as a warmup plus `repeats` times, and then again after the
        sweep. This case makes the measured value a function of *which* baseline measurement it is,
        rather than of the call count, so the expectation does not depend on how repeats are
        scheduled.
        """
        state = {"baseline_measurements": 0}

        def measure(candidate):
            if candidate.kind == "baseline":
                state["baseline_measurements"] += 1
                # The first measurement is the warmup; the three counted repeats are 50, and the
                # recheck afterwards is 40 (below), simulating a machine that got slower.
                return {"tokens_per_s": 50.0}
            if candidate.kind == "recheck":
                return {"tokens_per_s": 40.0}
            return {"tokens_per_s": 45.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertEqual(rep["baseline"]["median"], 50.0)
        self.assertIsNotNone(rep["recheck"], "the baseline must be re-measured after the sweep")
        self.assertEqual(rep["recheck"]["median"], 40.0)
        self.assertIsNotNone(rep["drift"], "the drift between the two baseline measurements is reported")
        self.assertLess(rep["drift"]["relative"], 0,
                        "the report must show that the machine slowed, not hide it")

    def test_fewer_repeats_than_required_disqualifies_a_candidate(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            return {"tokens_per_s": 90.0 if candidate.settings else 50.0}

        plan = self.plan(max_trials=1, repeats=5, dimensions=("kv",))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, measure)
        best = [c for c in result["report"]["candidates"] if c["kind"] == "trial"][0]
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(best["metrics"]), 5)


class TestFailuresAreRecorded(TuningCase):
    """A candidate that could not run is evidence about the configuration, never a slow winner."""

    def test_a_boot_failure_is_recorded_and_excluded(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            if candidate.settings:
                raise RuntimeError("the engine failed to boot with these flags")
            return {"tokens_per_s": 50.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=2, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertEqual(rep["recommendation_available"], False)
        self.assertTrue(rep["failures"])
        self.assertEqual(rep["failures"][0]["status"], "FAIL_BOOT")
        self.assertIn("failed to boot", rep["failures"][0]["reason"])

    def test_a_timeout_is_recorded_as_a_timeout(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            if candidate.settings:
                raise RuntimeError("the measurement timed out after 120s")
            return {"tokens_per_s": 50.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        self.assertEqual(result["report"]["failures"][0]["status"], "TIMEOUT")

    def test_no_tokens_is_not_a_slow_configuration(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            return {"tokens_per_s": 0.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertFalse(rep["recommendation_available"])
        statuses = [c["status"] for c in rep["candidates"]]
        self.assertIn("NO_TOKENS", statuses)

    def test_a_correctness_failure_disqualifies_a_fast_candidate(self):
        """tokens/s alone is not acceptance."""
        def measure(candidate):
            if candidate.settings:
                return {"tokens_per_s": 500.0, "correct": False}
            return {"tokens_per_s": 50.0, "correct": True}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertFalse(rep["recommendation_available"],
                         "a fast but incorrect configuration must never be recommended")
        self.assertTrue(any(f["status"] == "INVALID" for f in rep["failures"]), rep["failures"])

    def test_a_baseline_that_cannot_be_measured_stops_the_sweep(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            raise RuntimeError("no engine here")

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=5, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertFalse(rep["recommendation_available"])
        self.assertIsNone(rep["baseline"])
        self.assertIn("could not be measured", rep["reason"])


class TestBounds(TuningCase):
    def test_the_trial_limit_is_respected(self):
        # Count *trials*, not measurement calls: each candidate is measured once as a warmup plus
        # `repeats` times, so counting calls would measure the wrong thing entirely.
        plan = self.plan(max_trials=3, dimensions=("ple_io", "kv"))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 60.0})
        self.assertEqual(result["report"]["trials_run"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(len([c for c in result["report"]["candidates"]
                              if c["kind"] == "trial"]), 3)
        self.assertLessEqual(result["report"]["baseline"] is not None, True)

    def test_the_time_bound_stops_new_trials(self):
        clock = {"t": 0.0}

        def measure(candidate):
            clock["t"] += 30.0
            return {"tokens_per_s": 60.0}

        plan = self.plan(max_trials=100, dimensions=("kv",))
        plan.total_time_s = 45.0
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", plan, measure, clock=lambda: clock["t"])
        result = tuner.run()
        self.assertTrue(any(e["state"] == "time_limit" for e in result["events"]),
                        "the displayed time bound must actually stop the sweep")

    def test_cancellation_keeps_evidence_and_recommends_nothing(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            if candidate.settings:
                tuner.request_cancel()
            return {"tokens_per_s": 90.0 if candidate.settings else 50.0}

        plan = self.plan(max_trials=10, dimensions=("kv",))
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", plan, measure)
        result = tuner.run()
        self.assertEqual(result["state"], "cancelled")
        self.assertFalse(result["report"]["recommendation_available"],
                         "a cancelled sweep must not produce a winner")
        self.assertTrue(result["report"]["candidates"], "evidence collected before the cancel is kept")


class TestSearchSpaceIsDisclosed(TuningCase):
    """A bounded sweep must not look like a complete one.

    This is the honesty property that decides whether "no candidate beat the baseline" can be read
    as a conclusion. With four trials out of ninety-six combinations, it cannot — and the report has
    to say so, or a reader will take a partial search for a full one.
    """

    def test_a_bounded_sweep_reports_the_size_of_the_space_it_sampled(self):
        plan = self.plan(max_trials=2, dimensions=("kv",))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 60.0})
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertEqual(rep["trials_run"], 2)
        # `kv` has four values, so the space is four and two trials is a prefix of it.
        self.assertEqual(rep["combinations_total"], 4)
        self.assertTrue(rep["trials_are_a_prefix"])

    def test_a_complete_sweep_is_not_labelled_a_prefix(self):
        plan = self.plan(max_trials=10, dimensions=("kv",))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 60.0})
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertEqual(rep["combinations_total"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(rep["trials_run"], 4, "the whole four-value space is enumerated")
        self.assertFalse(rep["trials_are_a_prefix"])

    def test_the_space_size_accounts_for_every_offered_dimension(self):
        plan = self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv", "kv_grow"))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 60.0})
        # kv has 4 values, kv_grow has 2 -> 8 combinations.
        self.assertEqual(result["report"]["combinations_total"], 8)

    def test_a_plan_with_no_dimensions_reports_no_space(self):
        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1), lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 60.0})
        self.assertEqual(result["report"]["combinations_total"], 0)


class TestDriftIsGraded(TuningCase):
    """A drift note is only warranted when the drift is material.

    Printing "the comparison is weaker than the repeat count suggests" at +0.0% trains the reader to
    ignore the warning, which is worse than not printing it.
    """

    def test_negligible_drift_is_not_flagged_as_material(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            return {"tokens_per_s": 50.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertIsNotNone(rep["drift"])
        self.assertAlmostEqual(rep["drift"]["relative"], 0.0)
        self.assertFalse(rep["drift_material"])

    def test_material_drift_is_flagged(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            return {"tokens_per_s": 40.0 if candidate.kind == "recheck" else 50.0}

        _, result = self.run_job(self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",)), measure)
        rep = result["report"]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(rep["drift"]["relative"], -0.2)
        self.assertTrue(rep["drift_material"])


class TestExclusiveLease(TuningCase):
    """Tuning must own its devices: a second job, or a serving load, must not share them."""

    def test_a_second_job_is_refused_while_the_lease_is_held(self):
        first = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", self.plan(), lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 50.0})
        first._acquire_lease()
        try:
            second = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", self.plan(), lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 50.0})
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as ctx:
                second._acquire_lease()
            self.assertIn("exclusive device lease", str(ctx.exception))
        finally:
            first._release_lease()

    def test_the_lease_is_released_even_when_the_job_fails(self):
        plan = self.plan()
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", plan, lambda c: (_ for _ in ()).throw(RuntimeError("boom")))
        tuner.run()
        self.assertFalse((tuner.root / "tuning.lease").exists(),
                         "a failed job must not leave the devices leased")

    def test_a_stale_lease_is_reported_rather_than_ignored(self):
        stale = self.tmp / "runs" / "job1"
        stale.mkdir(parents=True)
        (stale / "tuning.lease").write_text(json.dumps({"id": "dead", "pid": 1}))
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", self.plan(), lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 50.0})
        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as ctx:
            tuner._acquire_lease()
        self.assertIn("dead", str(ctx.exception))


class TestExportedRetest(TuningCase):
    """A winner is not qualified until the *exported* configuration is measured again."""

    def test_a_configuration_that_loses_its_advantage_on_export_is_withdrawn(self):
        def measure(args):
            # The benchmark-only lever carried the gain; without it the engine is at the baseline.
            return {"tokens_per_s": 90.0 if "--prompt-cache-tail" in args else 50.0}

        outcome = tuning.verify_exported(Path("/engine"), {"--kv": "int8"}, measure)
        self.assertTrue(outcome["verified"])
        self.assertEqual(outcome["median"], 50.0)

    def test_an_exported_configuration_that_fails_to_boot_is_not_verified(self):
        def measure(args):
            raise RuntimeError("the engine failed to boot")

        outcome = tuning.verify_exported(Path("/engine"), {}, measure)
        self.assertFalse(outcome["verified"])
        self.assertIn("failed to run", outcome["reason"])

    def test_an_incorrect_exported_configuration_is_not_verified(self):
        outcome = tuning.verify_exported(Path("/engine"), {}, lambda a: {"tokens_per_s": 100.0,
                                                                        "correct": False})
        self.assertFalse(outcome["verified"])
        self.assertIn("correctness", outcome["reason"])


class TestPersistenceAndReporting(TuningCase):
    def test_the_job_is_reloadable_with_its_report(self):
        def measure(candidate):
            return {"tokens_per_s": 70.0 if candidate.settings else 50.0}

        plan = self.plan(max_trials=1, dimensions=("kv",))
        _, result = self.run_job(plan, measure)
        saved = json.loads((self.tmp / "runs" / "job1" / "job.json").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(saved["state"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(saved["id"], "job1")
        self.assertTrue(saved["report"]["candidates"])
        self.assertIn("excluded_dimensions", saved["report"])
        self.assertIn("machine", json.dumps(tuning.machine_identity()))

    def test_the_report_names_what_was_excluded_and_why(self):
        plan = tuning.plan_tuning(Path("/nonexistent/strata"), "metal", "m", "generation",
                                  {"prompt_tokens": 128})
        self.assertIn("vram_reserve", {e["id"] for e in plan.excluded})
        self.assertFalse(plan.engine_flags_known,
                         "a plan must record that the engine could not be interrogated")

    def test_objective_selects_the_metric(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.plan(objective="generation").__class__.__name__, "TuningPlan")
        tuner = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs", self.plan(objective="prefill"),
                             lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 1.0})
        self.assertEqual(tuner._objective_metric(), "prefill_tokens_per_s")
        tuner2 = tuning.Tuner(self.tmp / "runs2", self.plan(objective="latency"),
                              lambda c: {"tokens_per_s": 1.0})
        self.assertEqual(tuner2._objective_metric(), "ttft_ms")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#ifndef __DPCT_ATOMIC_HPP__
#define __DPCT_ATOMIC_HPP__

#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>

namespace dpct {

/// Atomically add the value operand to the value at the addr and assign the
/// result to the value at addr.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The value to add to the value at \p addr.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The value at the \p addr before the call.
template <typename T,
          sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device>
inline T atomic_fetch_add(T *addr, T operand) {
  auto atm =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(addr[0]);
  return atm.fetch_add(operand);
}

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device,
          typename T1, typename T2>
inline T1 atomic_fetch_add(T1 *addr, T2 operand) {
  auto atm =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T1, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(addr[0]);
  return atm.fetch_add(operand);
}

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device>
inline sycl::half2 atomic_fetch_add(sycl::half2 *addr, sycl::half2 operand) {
  auto atm = sycl::atomic_ref<unsigned, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(
      *reinterpret_cast<unsigned *>(addr));

  union {
    unsigned i;
    sycl::half2 h;
  } old{0}, output{0};

  while (true) {
    old.i = atm.load();
    output.h = old.h + operand;
    if (atm.compare_exchange_strong(old.i, output.i))
      break;
  }

  return output.h;
}

/// Atomically add the value operand to the value at the addr and assign the
/// result to the value at addr.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The value to add to the value at \p addr.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The value at the \p addr before the call.
template <typename T, sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
                          sycl::access::address_space::global_space>
inline T atomic_fetch_add(T *addr, T operand,
                          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder) {
  switch (memoryOrder) {
  case sycl::memory_order::relaxed:
    return atomic_fetch_add<T, addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
                            sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr, operand);
  case sycl::memory_order::acq_rel:
    return atomic_fetch_add<T, addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::acq_rel,
                            sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr, operand);
  case sycl::memory_order::seq_cst:
    return atomic_fetch_add<T, addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::seq_cst,
                            sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr, operand);
  default:
    assert(false && "Invalid memory_order for atomics. Valid memory_order for "
                    "atomics are: sycl::memory_order::relaxed, "
                    "sycl::memory_order::acq_rel, sycl::memory_order::seq_cst!");
  }
}

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          typename T1, typename T2>
inline T1 atomic_fetch_add(T1 *addr, T2 operand,
                           sycl::memory_order memoryOrder) {
  atomic_fetch_add<T1, addressSpace>(addr, operand, memoryOrder);
}

  case sycl::memory_order::relaxed:
    return atomic_fetch_xor<T, addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
                            sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr, operand);
  case sycl::memory_order::acq_rel:
    return atomic_fetch_xor<T, addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::acq_rel,
                            sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr, operand);
  case sycl::memory_order::seq_cst:
    return atomic_fetch_xor<T, addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::seq_cst,
                            sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr, operand);
  default:
    assert(false && "Invalid memory_order for atomics. Valid memory_order for "
                    "atomics are: sycl::memory_order::relaxed, "
                    "sycl::memory_order::acq_rel, sycl::memory_order::seq_cst!");
  }
}

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          typename T1, typename T2>
inline T1 atomic_fetch_xor(T1 *addr, T2 operand,
                           sycl::memory_order memoryOrder) {
  atomic_fetch_xor<T1, addressSpace>(addr, operand, memoryOrder);
}

/// Atomically set \p operand to the value stored in \p addr, if old value stored in
/// \p addr is equal to zero or greater than \p operand, else decrease the value stored
/// in \p addr.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The threshold value.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The old value stored in \p addr.
template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace = sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device>
inline unsigned int atomic_fetch_compare_dec(unsigned int *addr,
                                             unsigned int operand) {
  auto atm = sycl::atomic_ref<unsigned int, memoryOrder, memoryScope,
                                  addressSpace>(addr[0]);
  unsigned int old;

	while (true) {
	  old = atm.load();
	  if (old == 0 || old > operand) {
		  if (atm.compare_exchange_strong(old, operand))
        break;
	  } else if (atm.compare_exchange_strong(old, old - 1))
      break;
	}

  return old;
}

/// Atomically increment the value stored in \p addr if old value stored in \p
/// addr is less than \p operand, else set 0 to the value stored in \p addr.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The threshold value.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The old value stored in \p addr.
template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device>
inline unsigned int atomic_fetch_compare_inc(unsigned int *addr,
                                             unsigned int operand) {
  auto atm = sycl::atomic_ref<unsigned int, memoryOrder, memoryScope,
                                  addressSpace>(addr[0]);
  unsigned int old;
  while (true) {
    old = atm.load();
    if (old >= operand) {
      if (atm.compare_exchange_strong(old, 0))
        break;
    } else if (atm.compare_exchange_strong(old, old + 1))
      break;
  }
  return old;
}

/// Atomically increment the value stored in \p addr if old value stored in \p
/// addr is less than \p operand, else set 0 to the value stored in \p addr.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The threshold value.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The old value stored in \p addr.
template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space>
inline unsigned int
atomic_fetch_compare_inc(unsigned int *addr, unsigned int operand,
                         sycl::memory_order memoryOrder) {
  switch (memoryOrder) {
  case sycl::memory_order::relaxed:
    return atomic_fetch_compare_inc<addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
                                    sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr,
                                                                   operand);
  case sycl::memory_order::acq_rel:
    return atomic_fetch_compare_inc<addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::acq_rel,
                                    sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr,
                                                                   operand);
  case sycl::memory_order::seq_cst:
    return atomic_fetch_compare_inc<addressSpace, sycl::memory_order::seq_cst,
                                    sycl::memory_scope::device>(addr,
                                                                   operand);
  default:
    assert(false && "Invalid memory_order for atomics. Valid memory_order for "
                    "atomics are: sycl::memory_order::relaxed, "
                    "sycl::memory_order::acq_rel, sycl::memory_order::seq_cst!");
  }
}

/// Atomically exchange the value at the address addr with the value operand.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The value to be exchanged with the value pointed by \p addr.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The value at the \p addr before the call.
template <typename T,
          sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device>
inline T atomic_exchange(T *addr, T operand) {
  auto atm =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(addr[0]);
  return atm.exchange(operand);
}

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device,
          typename T1, typename T2>
inline T1 atomic_exchange(T1 *addr, T2 operand) {
  auto atm =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T1, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(addr[0]);
  return atm.exchange(operand);
}

/// Atomically exchange the value at the address addr with the value operand.
/// \param [in, out] addr The pointer to the data.
/// \param operand The value to be exchanged with the value pointed by \p addr.
/// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
/// \returns The value at the \p addr before the call.
template <typename T, sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
                          sycl::access::address_space::global_space>
inline T atomic_exchange(T *addr, T operand,
                         sycl::memory_order memoryOrder) {
  switch (memoryOrder) {

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          typename T1, typename T2>
inline T1 atomic_exchange(T1 *addr, T2 operand,
                           sycl::memory_order memoryOrder) {
  atomic_exchange<T1, addressSpace>(addr, operand, memoryOrder);
}

/// Atomically compare the value at \p addr to the value expected and exchange
/// with the value desired if the value at \p addr is equal to the value expected.
/// Returns the value at the \p addr before the call.
/// \param [in, out] addr Multi_ptr.
/// \param expected The value to compare against the value at \p addr.
/// \param desired The value to assign to \p addr if the value at \p addr is expected.
/// \param success The memory ordering used when comparison succeeds.
/// \param fail The memory ordering used when comparison fails.
/// \returns The value at the \p addr before the call.
template <typename T,
          sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device>
T atomic_compare_exchange_strong(
    sycl::multi_ptr<T, addressSpace> addr, T expected, T desired,
    sycl::memory_order success = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
    sycl::memory_order fail = sycl::memory_order::relaxed) {
  auto atm = sycl::atomic_ref<T, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(*addr);

  atm.compare_exchange_strong(expected, desired, success, fail);
  return expected;
}

template <sycl::access::address_space addressSpace =
              sycl::access::address_space::global_space,
          sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
          sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = sycl::memory_scope::device,
          typename T1, typename T2, typename T3>
T1 atomic_compare_exchange_strong(
    sycl::multi_ptr<T1, addressSpace> addr, T2 expected, T3 desired,
    sycl::memory_order success = sycl::memory_order::relaxed,
    sycl::memory_order fail = sycl::memory_order::relaxed) {
  auto atm =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T1, memoryOrder, memoryScope, addressSpace>(*addr);
  T1 expected_value = expected;
  atm.compare_exchange_strong(expected_value, desired, success, fail);
  return expected_value;
}

/// Atomic extension to implement standard APIs in std::atomic
namespace detail{
template <typename T> struct IsValidAtomicType {
  static constexpr bool value =
      (std::is_same<T, int>::value || std::is_same<T, unsigned int>::value ||
       std::is_same<T, long>::value || std::is_same<T, unsigned long>::value ||
       std::is_same<T, long long>::value ||
       std::is_same<T, unsigned long long>::value ||
       std::is_same<T, float>::value || std::is_same<T, double>::value ||
       std::is_pointer<T>::value);
};
} // namespace detail

template <typename T,
          sycl::memory_scope DefaultScope = sycl::memory_scope::system,
#ifdef __AMDGPU__
          sycl::memory_order DefaultOrder = sycl::memory_order::acq_rel,
#else
          sycl::memory_order DefaultOrder = sycl::memory_order::seq_cst,
#endif
          sycl::access::address_space Space =
              sycl::access::address_space::generic_space>
class atomic {
  static_assert(
    detail::IsValidAtomicType<T>::value,
    "Invalid atomic type.  Valid types are int, unsigned int, long, "
      "unsigned long, long long, unsigned long long, float, double "
      "and pointer types");
  T __d;

public:
  /// default memory synchronization order
  static constexpr sycl::memory_order default_read_order =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space>::default_read_order;
  static constexpr sycl::memory_order default_write_order =
      sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space>::default_write_order;
  static constexpr sycl::memory_scope default_scope = DefaultScope;
  static constexpr sycl::memory_order default_read_modify_write_order =
      DefaultOrder;

  /// Default constructor.
  constexpr atomic() noexcept = default;
  /// Constructor with initialize value.
  constexpr atomic(T d) noexcept : __d(d){};

  /// atomically replaces the value of the referenced object with a non-atomic argument
  /// \param operand The value to replace the pointed value.
  /// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  void store(T operand, sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_write_order,
             sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {
    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    atm.store(operand, memoryOrder, memoryScope);
  }

  /// atomically obtains the value of the referenced object
  /// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns The value of the referenced object
  T load(sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_read_order,
         sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) const noexcept {
    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(
      const_cast<T &>(__d));
    return atm.load(memoryOrder, memoryScope);
  }

  /// atomically replaces the value of the referenced object and obtains the value held previously
  /// \param operand The value to replace the pointed value.
  /// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns The value of the referenced object before the call.
  T exchange(T operand,
             sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_read_modify_write_order,
             sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {

    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.exchange(operand, memoryOrder, memoryScope);
  }

  /// atomically compares the value of the referenced object with non-atomic argument 
  /// and performs atomic exchange if equal or atomic load if not
  /// \param expected The value expected to be found in the object referenced by the atomic_ref object
  /// \param desired  The value to store in the referenced object if it is as expected
  /// \param success The memory models for the read-modify-write
  /// \param failure The memory models for load operations
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns true if the referenced object was successfully changed, false otherwise.
  bool compare_exchange_weak(
      T &expected, T desired,
      sycl::memory_order success, sycl::memory_order failure,
      sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {
    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.compare_exchange_weak(expected, desired, success, failure, memoryScope);
  }
  /// \param expected The value expected to be found in the object referenced by the atomic_ref object
  /// \param desired  The value to store in the referenced object if it is as expected
  /// \param memoryOrder 	The memory synchronization ordering for operations
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns true if the referenced object was successfully changed, false otherwise.
  bool compare_exchange_weak(T &expected, T desired,
                  sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_read_modify_write_order,
                  sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {
    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.compare_exchange_weak(expected, desired, memoryOrder, memoryScope);
  }

  /// atomically compares the value of the referenced object with non-atomic argument 
  /// and performs atomic exchange if equal or atomic load if not
  /// \param expected The value expected to be found in the object referenced by the atomic_ref object
  /// \param desired  The value to store in the referenced object if it is as expected
  /// \param success The memory models for the read-modify-write
  /// \param failure The memory models for load operations
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns true if the referenced object was successfully changed, false otherwise.
  bool compare_exchange_strong(
      T &expected, T desired,
      sycl::memory_order success, sycl::memory_order failure,
      sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {

    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.compare_exchange_strong(expected, desired, success, failure, memoryScope);
  }
  /// \param expected The value expected to be found in the object referenced by the atomic_ref object
  /// \param desired  The value to store in the referenced object if it is as expected
  /// \param memoryOrder 	The memory synchronization ordering for operations
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns true if the referenced object was successfully changed, false otherwise.
  bool compare_exchange_strong(T &expected, T desired,
                    sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_read_modify_write_order,
                    sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {
    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.compare_exchange_strong(expected, desired, memoryOrder, memoryScope);
  }

  /// atomically adds the argument to the value stored in the atomic object and obtains the value held previously
  /// \param operand 	The other argument of arithmetic addition
  /// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns The value of the referenced object before the call.
  T fetch_add(T operand,
              sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_read_modify_write_order,
              sycl::memory_scope  memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {

    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.fetch_add(operand, memoryOrder,  memoryScope);
  }

  /// atomically subtracts the argument from the value stored in the atomic object and obtains the value held previously
  /// \param operand 	The other argument of arithmetic subtraction
  /// \param memoryOrder The memory ordering used.
  /// \param memoryScope The memory scope used.
  /// \returns The value of the referenced object before the call.
  T fetch_sub(T operand,
              sycl::memory_order memoryOrder = default_read_modify_write_order,
              sycl::memory_scope memoryScope = default_scope) noexcept {

    sycl::atomic_ref<T, DefaultOrder, DefaultScope, Space> atm(__d);
    return atm.fetch_sub(operand, memoryOrder, memoryScope);
  }
};

} // namespace dpct
#endif // __DPCT_ATOMIC_HPP__

/// The wrapper structure for external memory resource handle desc
class external_mem_handle_desc {
#ifdef _WIN32
  void *handle;
  const void *name;
#else
  int handle;
#endif // _WIN32
  sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::external_mem_handle_type handle_type;
  size_t size_in_bytes;
  int flags;

public:
  external_mem_handle_desc() {
#ifdef _WIN32
    handle = nullptr;
    name = nullptr;
#else
    handle = -1;
#endif // _WIN32
    handle_type =
        sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::external_mem_handle_type::opaque_fd;
    size_in_bytes = 0;
    flags = 0;
  }

#ifdef _WIN32
  /// handle setter
  /// \param [in] win32_handle The win32 NT handle of the external memory
  /// resource
  void set_win32_handle(void *win32_handle) { handle = win32_handle; }

  /// name setter
  /// \param [in] win32_obj_name The object of the external memory resource
  void set_win32_obj_name(const void *win32_obj_name) { name = win32_obj_name; }
#else
  /// fd setter
  /// \param [in] fd The file descriptor of the external memory resource
  void set_fd_handle(int fd) { handle = fd; }
#endif // _WIN32

  /// handle_type setter
  /// \param [in] type The type of the external memory resource handle
  void set_handle_type(
      sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::external_mem_handle_type type) {
    handle_type = type;
  }

  /// size setter
  /// \param [in] size The size (in bytes) of the external memory resource
  void set_res_size(unsigned long long size) { size_in_bytes = size; }

  /// flags setter
  /// \param [in] flags The flags used to handle importing of external memory
  /// resource
  void set_flags(int flags) { this->flags = flags; }

#ifdef _WIN32
  /// handle getter
  /// \param [out] handle The win32 NT handle of the external memory resource
  void *get_win32_handle() { return handle; }

  /// name getter
  /// \param [out] name The object of the external memory resource
  const void *get_win32_obj_name() { return name; }
#else
  /// fd getter
  /// \param [out] fd The file descriptor of the external memory resource
  int get_fd_handle() { return handle; }
#endif // _WIN32

  /// handle_type getter
  /// \param [out] handle_type The type of the external memory resource handle
  sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::external_mem_handle_type get_handle_type() {
    return handle_type;
  }

  /// size getter
  /// \param [out] size The size (in bytes) of the external memory resource
  unsigned long long get_res_size() { return size_in_bytes; }

  /// flags getter
  /// \param [out] flags The flags used to handle importing of external memory
  /// resource
  int get_flags() { return flags; }
};

/// The wrapper structure for external image memory desc
class external_mem_img_desc {
  sycl::range<3> size;
  image_channel channel;
  unsigned int num_levels;
  sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::image_type type;

public:
  external_mem_img_desc() {
    size = sycl::range<3>{0, 0, 0};
    channel = image_channel::create<float>();
    num_levels = 1;
    type = sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::image_type::standard;
  }

  /// size setter
  /// \param [in] img_dims The dimensions of the imported image resource
  void set_size(sycl::range<3> img_dims) {
    size = img_dims;

    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
      if (size[i] == 1) {
        size[i] = 0;
      }
    }
  }

  /// image_channel setter
  /// \param [in] img_ch The channel info of the imported image resource
  void set_image_channel(image_channel img_ch) { channel = img_ch; }

  /// num_levels setter
  /// \param [in] numLevels The no. of levels in the imported image resource
  void set_num_levels(unsigned int num_levels) {
    this->num_levels = num_levels;

    if (num_levels > 1) {
      set_image_type(sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::image_type::mipmap);
    }
  }

  /// type setter
  /// \param [in] img_type The type of the imported image resource
  void set_image_type(sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::image_type img_type) {
    type = img_type;
  }

  /// size getter
  /// \param [out] size The dimensions of the imported image resource
  sycl::range<3> get_size() { return size; }

  /// image_channel getter
  /// \param [out] image_channel The channel info of the imported image resource
  image_channel get_image_channel() { return channel; }

  /// num_levels getter
  /// \param [out] num_levels The no. of levels in the imported image resource
  unsigned int get_num_levels() { return num_levels; }

  /// type getter
  /// \param [out] type The image type of the imported image resource
  sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::image_type get_image_type() { return type; }
};

/// The wrapper structure for external buffer memory desc
class external_mem_buf_desc {
  uint64_t size_in_bytes;
  uint64_t offset;
  unsigned int flags;

public:
  external_mem_buf_desc() {
    size_in_bytes = 0;
    offset = 0;
    flags = 0;
  }

  /// size setter
  /// \param [in] size The size (in bytes) of the external buffer resource
  void set_res_size(uint64_t size) { size_in_bytes = size; }

  /// offset setter
  /// \param [in] offset The memory offset of the external buffer resource
  void set_mem_offset(uint64_t offset) { this->offset = offset; }

  /// flags setter
  /// \param [in] flags The flags used to import external buffer resource
  void set_flags(unsigned int flags) { this->flags = flags; }

  /// size getter
  /// \param [out] size_in_bytes The size (in bytes) of the external buffer res
  uint64_t get_res_size() { return size_in_bytes; }

  /// offset getter
  /// \param [out] offset The memory offset of the external buffer resource
  uint64_t get_mem_offset() { return offset; }

  /// flags getter
  /// \param [out] flags The flags used to import external buffer resource
  unsigned int get_flags() { return flags; }
};
